content.text:
Yes — three more, found by systematically walking the same file rather than just re-checking your list:

**1. No wishlist toggle on PLP cards at all.** Not broken — genuinely absent. The `plp` variation has no heart/wishlist-add affordance built into it at all (only `wishlist` variation has a remove control). The page's own comment confirms this directly: `addItemToWishlist`/`removeItemFromWishlist` are already imported and available in `product-list/index.tsx`, just never wired to anything — sitting there "for whenever this affordance gets a real home on this grid." If you expect a wishlist heart on PLP tiles, it doesn't exist yet, not even cosmetically.

**2. No guard against double-clicking Add to Bag.** Checked directly: `handleAddToBag` fires `addItemToNewOrExistingBasket` with zero in-flight tracking — no pending state, no button-disable-while-submitting, anywhere in the shared component or in PLP's own usage of it. A fast double-click fires two independent, concurrent requests, and both would succeed — a real duplicate-add risk, not hypothetical.

**3. Colour is invisible on PLP tiles — worth confirming, not asserting as wrong.** `plp`'s `showAttributes: false` means no colour/size text label renders at all on the card, and there's no colour-swatch-switching control on `ZimmProductCard` either — only the product image itself conveys colour. I don't have a confirmed Figma reference either way, so I can't tell you this is *broken* — but if your mental model of "the PLP card" includes seeing or switching colour from the tile, that doesn't exist today, and it's worth explicitly confirming against the design rather than assuming it's intentional.

The first two are concrete, confirmed gaps. The third is a real open question, not a verified bug.

content.text:
Investigated all three. Two are straightforwardly buildable; one is not what it looks like — it's a whole unbuilt feature, not a wiring fix.

## Gap 1 — Was/Now pricing: buildable, high confidence

`recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts` already solved this exact problem — one `getPriceData(product)` call derives `currentPrice`/`originalPrice`/`isOnSale` correctly. I directly confirmed real, multi-tier pricing data exists (`4673TS251`: list `625` / sale `600` — a genuine was/now case) via the Product Detail endpoint, which shares the same `perPricebook`/`expand` params PLP's search already requests. I couldn't cleanly intercept PLP's own search response directly (it's server-rendered, no client-side XHR to grab), so this is strong-but-indirect evidence for the search-hit shape specifically — the plan should include one quick live-log check as the first implementation step, before fully trusting it, matching how this codebase already treats this exact class of assumption elsewhere.

**Plan:** `productListCardMapper.ts` calls `getPriceData(hit)` once (same function, same pattern, already proven), sets both `currentPrice`/`originalPrice` from it instead of hand-reading `hit.price`. New Vitest coverage for the on-sale / not-on-sale / no-currency cases, mirroring `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.test.ts`'s own existing tests almost exactly.

## Gap 3 — Size-aware Add to Bag: buildable, high confidence

Confirmed live: `product.variants` is real and populated — `4673TS251` has 6 variants, each with a real orderable `productId` (e.g. `4673TS251GVSCP0P`) keyed by `variationValues.size`. Exactly the shape needed.

**Plan:** a new, tested utility — `resolveOrderableVariant(hit, sizeValue)` — looks up `hit.variants` by `variationValues.size`, returns the real `{productId, orderable}` or `null` if no size was picked. `handleAddToBag` uses it when a chip is selected, falls back to today's `representedProduct`/`productId` behavior when nothing's selected (matches what you described: no selection → default; selection → that size).

## Gap 2 — Notify Me: not a wiring fix, and I don't think we should build it right now

This isn't "add a handler." Per the PDP PRD (PRD-018–021): Notify Me opens a **slide-out form** that submits to a **back-in-stock capture** target. That's a real feature — new drawer UI, an email-capture form, and somewhere for the submission to actually go. I checked: **no back-in-stock integration exists anywhere in this codebase**, and PDP itself never wires `onNotifyMeClick` to anything either, even though the prop already exists there. There's nothing to hook into today.

I don't think this belongs in the same pass as the other two — it needs its own scoping (likely its own ticket, and a decision on where submissions actually go). "Handler" is just the instructions for "what happens when someone presses this." No handler means the button is real and pressable, but there's nothing written down for what should happen next — so pressing it does exactly nothing. No error, no action, no reaction. It's like a doorbell that's installed and looks completely normal, but isn't actually wired to a chime yet — you can press it all day, nothing rings.

In this case, that's intentional, not a bug: we're choosing to install the doorbell now (so the button is visibly there, in the right spot) before the wiring behind it — the actual "notify me when it's back" feature — gets built later.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/skills/zimmerMANNBuild

The executor. Takes an approved plan and builds it, one step at a time, with every step tested,
scope-checked, scored and seen by Marcel before it becomes a commit.

**Intended model: Sonnet 5 at maximum effort.** A skill cannot pin the session model — the loop
agents are pinned to Sonnet in their own frontmatter regardless.

**Scale to the work.** A two-point story does not get the full loop. The plan states the scale it
chose and why; honour it. Over-scaled machinery is a defect, not thoroughness. Nothing too crazy,
no overthinking.

---

## Two modes

**`build`** — `fix the 3 gaps, test, then i'll test on my end, once all good we commit` is a Jira key. Reads `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/plan.md`
and executes it. This is the default.

**`rework`** — invoked as `rework <TICKET>` after a PR is open and CodeRabbit or a reviewer has
requested changes. Skips planning entirely; see the last section.

If no plan exists for the ticket, stop and say so. **Do not plan here** — that is
`zimmerMANNPreBuild`'s job, and building from an unplanned story is how an afternoon gets burned
on the wrong thing.

---

## Before the first step

1. Confirm the branch. **Not `develop`, not `main`** — a `PreToolUse` hook blocks every Write and
   Edit there. If the branch is wrong, stop.
2. Confirm the working tree is clean, or that everything dirty is expected and belongs to this
   story. Registry churn under `.claude/registry/*.md` is automatic and expected.
3. Read the plan's file manifest, tiers and per-step pass criteria. **Any file marked BLOCKED
   stops the run** until Marcel confirms owner approval.
4. Record the baseline: run the four per-step gates now and note the numbers. A gate that is
   non-zero at baseline is not a failure you introduced.

---

## The loop — once per step

```
Implementer  →  Tester  →  Orchestrator  →  Scorer  →  [Marcel]  →  commit
                   ↑                          │
                   └────── REWORK, max 3 ─────┘
```

**1. `zm-implementer`** builds the step. Only the files the step names. It never stages and never
commits.

**2. `zm-tester`** fans out its own angle sub-agents, re-pointed for this step, and reports
findings with CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE and UNIFORM/ONE-OFF labels, plus what it tried to falsify and
what it could not verify.

**3. `zm-orchestrator`** returns a scope verdict — IN SCOPE / UNDER / OVER / BLOCKED. Under and
over carry equal weight.

**4. `zm-scorer`** takes both and scores six axes. PASS or REWORK.

**REWORK returns to the Implementer with a specific instruction. Maximum three rounds.** On the
third, stop and surface to Marcel — three failures means the plan or the criteria are wrong, not
the implementation.

### Per-step gates — the cheap four

Run every step. Seconds each.

```
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run test                        # includes recipeGuards, the hard styling gate
npm run lint                        # compare counts, not the exit code
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs    # new unacknowledged findings only
```

Two traps: `npm run lint` exits non-zero at a healthy baseline, so **compare the count against
your baseline and ignore the exit code**. And never append arguments to it — `pwa-kit-dev lint`
forwards `--`-args into `execSync`, which can silently turn the gate into a writer.

The plan's per-step pass criteria layer **on top of** these, they do not replace them.

### The visual checkpoint

**After any step that changes rendered output, the loop stops.** The plan marks which steps those
are; if it doesn't, assume any step touching a component, a recipe or a page does.

Tell Marcel exactly:
- the URL and the viewport to open
- the Figma node to compare against — the one for **that variant and state**
- what should be on screen
- what would indicate a defect, including anything that will look wrong but is correct

Then **wait.** Do not proceed on assumption. This is the only gate on this stack that catches a
layout defect — `width: 'xl'` passed every automated check and destroyed the global footer.

Until it has happened, the Scorer's Design fidelity axis is UNVERIFIED, not passed.

### The commit

**The skill commits, not an agent.** Only after: Scorer PASS, and the visual checkpoint passed if
one was owed.

One step, one commit. Conventional Commits — the `commit-msg` hook enforces it. **No Claude
attribution, no CodeRabbit mentions, no `Co-Authored-By` line.** Use Marcel's previously authored
commits on this repo as the reference for tone and body.

Then move to the next step.

---

## Before handing off

Once every step has passed, run the expensive gates **once**:

```
npm run build-storybook             # then run the interaction + a11y suite against it
npm run test:story                  # real BrowserStack, scoped to the Jira key
npm run test:max-file-size          # runs a full build
cr review --base develop            # CodeRabbit locally, full review before anything is public
```

Storybook needs a verified-free port and a build you can prove is yours — a stale server on 6006
produced a silently meaningless pass once. Check the served build matches your own before trusting
any result.

Then **write the handoff** to `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/handoff.md`:

```
# Handoff — <TICKET>
Branch: <branch>   Base: <sha>   Head: <sha>

## Steps
| # | What | Commit | Scorer verdict | Rework rounds |

## Gates (real numbers, not claims)
| Gate | Result | Baseline |

## UNIFORM findings
<each one, with file:line — these are what a per-step review structurally cannot catch>

## Could not verify
<named, with why>

## Outstanding
<anything left, or "none">
```

**Write it even when everything passed.** PostBuild reads this file, and it may run in a different
session — a handoff that exists only in conversation does not survive the session ending.

Then present the same content to Marcel and **hand off to `zimmerMANNPostBuild`. This skill does
not push and does not open a PR.**

---

## Rework mode

Entered after a PR is open and CodeRabbit or a reviewer has requested changes.

**Read `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/postbuild.md` first.** It records what earlier rounds
already declined and why. A finding that was declined with evidence in round one does not get
re-litigated in round three — check before you verify anything, and if you disagree with a previous
decline, say so rather than silently reversing it.

**1. Verify every finding before touching anything.** CodeRabbit has been wrong on this repo
often — one batch ran 1-in-6 correct. Treat each finding as a hypothesis, not a fact. Per finding:

- **VALID** — reproduce it, cite `file:line`, fix it
- **INVALID** — say what is actually true, with the evidence, and draft the reply
- **OUT OF SCOPE** — real but not this story's problem; name the owning ticket or the person
- **DEFER** — real, in scope, but blocked on a decision; name who decides

**2. Fix only the VALID ones.** Same rules as build mode — the Implementer touches only what the
finding names, never stages, never commits.

**3. Re-run the cheap four**, plus the visual checkpoint if the fix changes rendered output.

**4. Commit the fixes here**, same rule as build mode — the skill commits, never an agent. Reference
the review thread each commit answers.

**5. Hand back to `zimmerMANNPostBuild`** with: what was fixed and in which commit, what was
declined and why, and the evidence behind each decline. **PostBuild owns the push and the
in-thread replies** — every finding gets a written answer, including the declined ones.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never push. Never open or update a PR.** That boundary belongs to PostBuild, which presents
  first and pushes only once Marcel has given the go.
- **Never write to the repo's config** — `.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CODEOWNERS`,
  `.docs/memory/**`, `.docs/prd/**`. Tier 1 Governance.
- **Never touch a Tier 1 file** without Marcel naming it and confirming owner approval.
- **Never expand scope.** Something worth doing that the plan didn't ask for gets reported, not
  done. Report it and let Marcel decide.
- **Local-only docs are never citable** in a commit message or a code comment. Cite `AGENTS.md`
  or `.claude/rules/*` instead.
- **Say what you could not verify.** Silence reads as "nothing wrong" when it may mean
  "didn't look there".

content.subject: Fix Gap 3: size-aware Add to Bag on PLP
content.description: New tested utility resolveOrderableVariant(hit, sizeValue) resolves a selected size chip to its real orderable SKU via hit.variants[].variationValues.size. Wire into product-list/index.tsx's handleAddToBag: use the resolved variant's productId when a chip is selected, fall back to today's representedProduct/productId default when nothing's selected.

content.subject: Fix Gap 2: show inert Notify Me button on PLP
content.description: zimmProductCard/index.tsx's showNotifyMe currently requires Boolean(isUnavailable) && Boolean(onNotifyMe). Drop the handler requirement so it shows whenever isUnavailable is true, even with no real handler wired (deferred to its own future story per Marcel's decision).

Yes — confirmed, and it's genuinely robust, not just visual. Checked `ZimmSizeChip` directly:

```
disabled={isDisabled}
onClick={() => { if (!isDisabled) onSelect(value); }}
```

Double-protected: a real native `disabled` attribute (the browser itself blocks the click), *plus* an explicit guard even if one somehow got through. An out-of-stock size chip is genuinely unselectable — not just styled differently. This was already correct before my fix (`selectSizeChipValues`'s `isDisabled: value.orderable === false`, which I didn't touch) and I didn't disturb it.

**One thing worth knowing, not a bug:** since a disabled chip can never be selected at all, `selectedSizeChipValue` can only ever hold an already-orderable size — meaning my new `resolveOrderableVariant` call in `handleAddToBag` can only ever run against a size that's already guaranteed orderable. So there's no path today where an out-of-stock size reaches Add to Bag.

I did notice my own new code doesn't *itself* re-check the `orderable` field `resolveOrderableVariant` returns — it's just unreachable today given the chip's own guarantee. This codebase leans toward layering a defensive check anyway even when something's already unreachable upstream (same pattern as the chip's own native-`disabled` + explicit-guard pair, and the `showNotifyMe`/`onNotifyMe` co-requirement I found earlier) — a one-line addition, not a real fix for a real bug. Want me to add it, or leave it as is since it's already structurally covered?

skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/skills/zimmerMANNBuild

The executor. Takes an approved plan and builds it, one step at a time, with every step tested,
scope-checked, scored and seen by Marcel before it becomes a commit.

**Intended model: Sonnet 5 at maximum effort.** A skill cannot pin the session model — the loop
agents are pinned to Sonnet in their own frontmatter regardless.

**Scale to the work.** A two-point story does not get the full loop. The plan states the scale it
chose and why; honour it. Over-scaled machinery is a defect, not thoroughness. Nothing too crazy,
no overthinking.

---

## Two modes

**`build`** — `fix the 3 gaps, test, then i'll test on my end, once all good we commit` is a Jira key. Reads `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/plan.md`
and executes it. This is the default.

**`rework`** — invoked as `rework <TICKET>` after a PR is open and CodeRabbit or a reviewer has
requested changes. Skips planning entirely; see the last section.

If no plan exists for the ticket, stop and say so. **Do not plan here** — that is
`zimmerMANNPreBuild`'s job, and building from an unplanned story is how an afternoon gets burned
on the wrong thing.

---

## Before the first step

1. Confirm the branch. **Not `develop`, not `main`** — a `PreToolUse` hook blocks every Write and
   Edit there. If the branch is wrong, stop.
2. Confirm the working tree is clean, or that everything dirty is expected and belongs to this
   story. Registry churn under `.claude/registry/*.md` is automatic and expected.
3. Read the plan's file manifest, tiers and per-step pass criteria. **Any file marked BLOCKED
   stops the run** until Marcel confirms owner approval.
4. Record the baseline: run the four per-step gates now and note the numbers. A gate that is
   non-zero at baseline is not a failure you introduced.

---

## The loop — once per step

```
Implementer  →  Tester  →  Orchestrator  →  Scorer  →  [Marcel]  →  commit
                   ↑                          │
                   └────── REWORK, max 3 ─────┘
```

**1. `zm-implementer`** builds the step. Only the files the step names. It never stages and never
commits.

**2. `zm-tester`** fans out its own angle sub-agents, re-pointed for this step, and reports
findings with CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE and UNIFORM/ONE-OFF labels, plus what it tried to falsify and
what it could not verify.

**3. `zm-orchestrator`** returns a scope verdict — IN SCOPE / UNDER / OVER / BLOCKED. Under and
over carry equal weight.

**4. `zm-scorer`** takes both and scores six axes. PASS or REWORK.

**REWORK returns to the Implementer with a specific instruction. Maximum three rounds.** On the
third, stop and surface to Marcel — three failures means the plan or the criteria are wrong, not
the implementation.

### Per-step gates — the cheap four

Run every step. Seconds each.

```
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run test                        # includes recipeGuards, the hard styling gate
npm run lint                        # compare counts, not the exit code
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs    # new unacknowledged findings only
```

Two traps: `npm run lint` exits non-zero at a healthy baseline, so **compare the count against
your baseline and ignore the exit code**. And never append arguments to it — `pwa-kit-dev lint`
forwards `--`-args into `execSync`, which can silently turn the gate into a writer.

The plan's per-step pass criteria layer **on top of** these, they do not replace them.

### The visual checkpoint

**After any step that changes rendered output, the loop stops.** The plan marks which steps those
are; if it doesn't, assume any step touching a component, a recipe or a page does.

Tell Marcel exactly:
- the URL and the viewport to open
- the Figma node to compare against — the one for **that variant and state**
- what should be on screen
- what would indicate a defect, including anything that will look wrong but is correct

Then **wait.** Do not proceed on assumption. This is the only gate on this stack that catches a
layout defect — `width: 'xl'` passed every automated check and destroyed the global footer.

Until it has happened, the Scorer's Design fidelity axis is UNVERIFIED, not passed.

### The commit

**The skill commits, not an agent.** Only after: Scorer PASS, and the visual checkpoint passed if
one was owed.

One step, one commit. Conventional Commits — the `commit-msg` hook enforces it. **No Claude
attribution, no CodeRabbit mentions, no `Co-Authored-By` line.** Use Marcel's previously authored
commits on this repo as the reference for tone and body.

Then move to the next step.

---

## Before handing off

Once every step has passed, run the expensive gates **once**:

```
npm run build-storybook             # then run the interaction + a11y suite against it
npm run test:story                  # real BrowserStack, scoped to the Jira key
npm run test:max-file-size          # runs a full build
cr review --base develop            # CodeRabbit locally, full review before anything is public
```

Storybook needs a verified-free port and a build you can prove is yours — a stale server on 6006
produced a silently meaningless pass once. Check the served build matches your own before trusting
any result.

Then **write the handoff** to `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/handoff.md`:

```
# Handoff — <TICKET>
Branch: <branch>   Base: <sha>   Head: <sha>

## Steps
| # | What | Commit | Scorer verdict | Rework rounds |

## Gates (real numbers, not claims)
| Gate | Result | Baseline |

## UNIFORM findings
<each one, with file:line — these are what a per-step review structurally cannot catch>

## Could not verify
<named, with why>

## Outstanding
<anything left, or "none">
```

**Write it even when everything passed.** PostBuild reads this file, and it may run in a different
session — a handoff that exists only in conversation does not survive the session ending.

Then present the same content to Marcel and **hand off to `zimmerMANNPostBuild`. This skill does
not push and does not open a PR.**

---

## Rework mode

Entered after a PR is open and CodeRabbit or a reviewer has requested changes.

**Read `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/postbuild.md` first.** It records what earlier rounds
already declined and why. A finding that was declined with evidence in round one does not get
re-litigated in round three — check before you verify anything, and if you disagree with a previous
decline, say so rather than silently reversing it.

**1. Verify every finding before touching anything.** CodeRabbit has been wrong on this repo
often — one batch ran 1-in-6 correct. Treat each finding as a hypothesis, not a fact. Per finding:

- **VALID** — reproduce it, cite `file:line`, fix it
- **INVALID** — say what is actually true, with the evidence, and draft the reply
- **OUT OF SCOPE** — real but not this story's problem; name the owning ticket or the person
- **DEFER** — real, in scope, but blocked on a decision; name who decides

**2. Fix only the VALID ones.** Same rules as build mode — the Implementer touches only what the
finding names, never stages, never commits.

**3. Re-run the cheap four**, plus the visual checkpoint if the fix changes rendered output.

**4. Commit the fixes here**, same rule as build mode — the skill commits, never an agent. Reference
the review thread each commit answers.

**5. Hand back to `zimmerMANNPostBuild`** with: what was fixed and in which commit, what was
declined and why, and the evidence behind each decline. **PostBuild owns the push and the
in-thread replies** — every finding gets a written answer, including the declined ones.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never push. Never open or update a PR.** That boundary belongs to PostBuild, which presents
  first and pushes only once Marcel has given the go.
- **Never write to the repo's config** — `.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CODEOWNERS`,
  `.docs/memory/**`, `.docs/prd/**`. Tier 1 Governance.
- **Never touch a Tier 1 file** without Marcel naming it and confirming owner approval.
- **Never expand scope.** Something worth doing that the plan didn't ask for gets reported, not
  done. Report it and let Marcel decide.
- **Local-only docs are never citable** in a commit message or a code comment. Cite `AGENTS.md`
  or `.claude/rules/*` instead.
- **Say what you could not verify.** Silence reads as "nothing wrong" when it may mean
  "didn't look there".

content.text:
Confirmed. Root cause found — and it's a one-line config gap, not a structural endpoint limitation.

## What's actually happening

**`overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx:257`** requests:
```ts
expand: ['promotions', 'variations', 'prices', 'images', 'page_meta_tags', 'custom_properties']
```

The Search endpoint's own SDK documentation states its `expand` parameter **defaults to `availability, images, prices, represented_products, variations`** when you don't pass one at all. But this page *does* pass an explicit list — and passing one **replaces** the default rather than adding to it. `'availability'` isn't in that list, so it's being silently switched off for every PLP search call.

That matters because `orderable` is documented, real SDK data — not something exclusive to the Product Detail endpoint as I'd assumed earlier:

> `VariationAttributeValue.orderable`: *"A flag indicating whether at least one variant with this variation attribute value is available to sell."*

That's the exact field `selectSizeChipValues` already reads (`value.orderable === false`). With `availability` excluded from `expand`, SFCC never populates it, so it's `undefined` on every value, and `undefined === false` is always `false` — every chip renders enabled regardless of real stock. Confirmed directly against `4673TS251`'s live SSR payload: every value in its `size` attribute has no `orderable` key at all.

**So the size-chip logic itself was never broken** — `isDisabled: value.orderable === false` is exactly correct. It's been reading a field the request never asked the API to fill in.

## Proposed fix

Add `'availability'` to that one `expand` array. Since it's part of SFCC's own default set, this isn't new/heavier data — it's restoring what a plain unconfigured call already gets for free.

**One adjacent thing worth flagging while I'm in this exact array**: the default list also includes `represented_products`, which this page's explicit list is *also* currently suppressing. That's relevant because `ProductListCard`'s fallback I added this session (`resolved?.productId ?? hit.representedProduct?.id ?? hit.productId`) depends on `hit.representedProduct` — which may be silently `undefined` today for the same reason. Worth confirming/fixing in the same pass since it's the same root cause, same line, same file.

Want me to go ahead and add both to the `expand` array, then verify live against `4673TS251` (size "1" should show disabled) the same way I confirmed the bug?

   In this window, Marcel's explicit request was: **"go ahead and implement it, verify against 4673TS251"** — approving the fix I had proposed (adding `'availability'` and `'represented_products'` to the PLP search call's `expand` array) and explicitly asking for live verification against the real product `4673TS251` (the same product used throughout this session's investigations).

   The final message in this window is a strict system-level instruction to produce a text-only conversation summary (the compaction request itself), not a new user task.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **SFCC Shopper Search (`ShopperSearch.productSearch`) `expand` parameter behavior**: passing an explicit `expand` array **replaces** the endpoint's own default list rather than merging with it. The SDK's own doc comment states the default is `availability, images, prices, represented_products, variations` — meaning any endpoint consumer that passes its own explicit array without including all of these silently loses whichever defaults it omits.
   - **`VariationAttributeValue.orderable`** (real, typed SDK field, confirmed via `node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.cjs.d.ts`): documented as *"A flag indicating whether at least one variant with this variation attribute value is available to sell."* This is exactly the field `selectSizeChipValues` (in `productListCardMapper.ts`) already reads via `isDisabled: value.orderable === false` — the bug was never in that logic, only in the request never asking SFCC to populate the field.
   - **`Variant$1.orderable`**: also a real, typed field but conspicuously undocumented via an explicit `@property orderable` doc line (unlike `VariationAttributeValue.orderable`, which has one) — weaker but consistent evidence that it's also expand-gated.
   - **Root cause, fully confirmed via live SSR data extraction**: PLP's product search call (`overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx`) explicitly set `expand: ['promotions', 'variations', 'prices', 'images', 'page_meta_tags', 'custom_properties']`, which does NOT include `'availability'` — so SFCC never populated `orderable` anywhere in the response, making every PLP size chip render `isDisabled: false` regardless of real stock.
   - **Adjacent, previously-unnoticed related bug**: the same explicit `expand` array also omits `'represented_products'` (also part of the SDK default), meaning `hit.representedProduct` was likely never populated either — directly relevant because `ProductListCard`'s `handleAddToBag` fallback (written earlier this session) reads `hit.representedProduct?.id` as a fallback when no variant is resolved. This was flagged as an adjacent finding worth fixing in the same edit, not a separate investigation.
   - **SSR-embedded data extraction technique** (used again this window): since PLP renders data server-side with no separate client-side XHR to intercept, raw JSON was extracted by searching `<script>` tag text content for a known substring (productId) and slicing a window around it — used both to prove the bug and to prove the fix.
   - **Node ESM module resolution gotcha** (encountered and fixed this window): a script placed outside the project directory (e.g., in `$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp`) cannot resolve bare-specifier imports like `playwright` because Node's ESM resolver walks up parent directories from the *script's own location*, not `process.cwd()` — so a Playwright verification script needs to live inside the project root (or another directory with `node_modules` in its ancestry) to run at all.
   - **Lint gate discipline** (from the zimmerMANNBuild skill instructions surfaced via system-reminder): `npm run lint` (the `pwa-kit-dev lint` wrapper) forwards `--`-args into `execSync` and can silently become a writer if arguments are appended — so this window intentionally ran `npx eslint <file>` directly instead, scoped to only the one modified file, avoiding that trap while still getting a real lint signal.
   - **Squad ownership**: `overrides/app/pages/product-list/` is Squad A territory per `.claude/rules/squadA.md` (already the active working area this whole session, not a new scope concern).
   - **AGENTS.md Hard Rule 15**: never commit, push, or open/close a PR without the developer explicitly requesting it in the current prompt — still unaddressed; no commit has been made or requested for this fix.

3. Files and Code Sections:

   - **`overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx`** (the only functional file modified this window):
     - Read lines 235–270 to confirm the exact current state of the `useProductSearch` call before editing.
     - Edited the `expand` array (previously a single line) from:
       ```ts
       expand: ['promotions', 'variations', 'prices', 'images', 'page_meta_tags', 'custom_properties'],
       ```
       to:
       ```ts
       expand: [
         'promotions',
         'variations',
         'prices',
         'images',
         'page_meta_tags',
         'custom_properties',
         'availability',
         'represented_products',
       ],
       ```
     - This is the sole code change in this window — a minimal, one-array-literal fix restoring two omitted SFCC default `expand` values (`'availability'`, `'represented_products'`) rather than any structural rework.

   - **`overrides/app/pages/product-list/productListCardMapper.ts`** (read-only this window, not modified) — contains `selectSizeChipValues` (reads `value.orderable === false`) and `resolveOrderableVariant` (already implemented earlier this session), both of which were already correctly written and needed no changes — they were only ever missing the upstream data the fix now supplies.

   - **`node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.cjs.d.ts`** (read-only, SDK source of truth) — inspected multiple times this window to confirm:
     - Line ~61953–61955: product-search endpoint's `expand` parameter doc: *"A comma-separated list with allowed values - `availability`, `images`, `prices`, `represented_products`, `variations`, `promotions`, `custom_properties`. By default, the expand parameter includes `availability, images, prices, represented_products, variations`."*
     - `VariationAttributeValue` type (~line 32297) with full doc comment including `@property orderable: A flag indicating whether at least one variant with this variation attribute value is available to sell.`
     - `Variant$1` type (~line 61281–61290) — has `orderable?: boolean` in the type but no corresponding `@property orderable` doc line, unlike `VariationAttributeValue`.

skills.name: zimmerMANNBuild
skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/skills/zimmerMANNBuild

The executor. Takes an approved plan and builds it, one step at a time, with every step tested,
scope-checked, scored and seen by Marcel before it becomes a commit.

**Intended model: Sonnet 5 at maximum effort.** A skill cannot pin the session model — the loop
agents are pinned to Sonnet in their own frontmatter regardless.

**Scale to the work.** A two-point story does not get the full loop. The plan states the scale it
chose and why; honour it. Over-scaled machinery is a defect, not thoroughness. Nothing too crazy,
no overthinking.

---

## Two modes

**`build`** — `fix the 3 gaps, test, then i'll test on my end, once all good we commit` is a Jira key. Reads `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/plan.md`
and executes it. This is the default.

**`rework`** — invoked as `rework <TICKET>` after a PR is open and CodeRabbit or a reviewer has
requested changes. Skips planning entirely; see the last section.

If no plan exists for the ticket, stop and say so. **Do not plan here** — that is
`zimmerMANNPreBuild`'s job, and building from an unplanned story is how an afternoon gets burned
on the wrong thing.

---

## Before the first step

1. Confirm the branch. **Not `develop`, not `main`** — a `PreToolUse` hook blocks every Write and
   Edit there. If the branch is wrong, stop.
2. Confirm the working tree is clean, or that everything dirty is expected and belongs to this
   story. Registry churn under `.claude/registry/*.md` is automatic and expected.
3. Read the plan's file manifest, tiers and per-step pass criteria. **Any file marked BLOCKED
   stops the run** until Marcel confirms owner approval.
4. Record the baseline: run the four per-step gates now and note the numbers. A gate that is
   non-zero at baseline is not a failure you introduced.

---

## The loop — once per step

```
Implementer  →  Tester  →  Orchestrator  →  Scorer  →  [Marcel]  →  commit
                   ↑                          │
                   └────── REWORK, max 3 ─────┘
```

**1. `zm-implementer`** builds the step. Only the files the step names. It never stages and never
commits.

**2. `zm-tester`** fans out its own angle sub-agents, re-pointed for this step, and reports
findings with CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE and UNIFORM/ONE-OFF labels, plus what it tried to falsify and
what it could not verify.

**3. `zm-orchestrator`** returns a scope verdict — IN SCOPE / UNDER / OVER / BLOCKED. Under and
over carry equal weight.

**4. `zm-scorer`** takes both and scores six axes. PASS or REWORK.

**REWORK returns to the Implementer with a specific instruction. Maximum three rounds.** On the
third, stop and surface to Marcel — three failures means the plan or the criteria are wrong, not
the implementation.

### Per-step gates — the cheap four

Run every step. Seconds each.

```
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run test                        # includes recipeGuards, the hard styling gate
npm run lint                        # compare counts, not the exit code
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs    # new unacknowledged findings only
```

Two traps: `npm run lint` exits non-zero at a healthy baseline, so **compare the count against
your baseline and ignore the exit code**. And never append arguments to it — `pwa-kit-dev lint`
forwards `--`-args into `execSync`, which can silently turn the gate into a writer.

The plan's per-step pass criteria layer **on top of** these, they do not replace them.

### The visual checkpoint

**After any step that changes rendered output, the loop stops.** The plan marks which steps those
are; if it doesn't, assume any step touching a component, a recipe or a page does.

Tell Marcel exactly:
- the URL and the viewport to open
- the Figma node to compare against — the one for **that variant and state**
- what should be on screen
- what would indicate a defect, including anything that will look wrong but is correct

Then **wait.** Do not proceed on assumption. This is the only gate on this stack that catches a
layout defect — `width: 'xl'` passed every automated check and destroyed the global footer.

Until it has happened, the Scorer's Design fidelity axis is UNVERIFIED, not passed.

### The commit

**The skill commits, not an agent.** Only after: Scorer PASS, and the visual checkpoint passed if
one was owed.

One step, one commit. Conventional Commits — the `commit-msg` hook enforces it. **No Claude
attribution, no CodeRabbit mentions, no `Co-Authored-By` line.** Use Marcel's previously authored
commits on this repo as the reference for tone and body.

Then move to the next step.

---

## Before handing off

Once every step has passed, run the expensive gates **once**:

```
npm run build-storybook             # then run the interaction + a11y suite against it
npm run test:story                  # real BrowserStack, scoped to the Jira key
npm run test:max-file-size          # runs a full build
cr review --base develop            # CodeRabbit locally, full review before anything is public
```

Storybook needs a verified-free port and a build you can prove is yours — a stale server on 6006
produced a silently meaningless pass once. Check the served build matches your own before trusting
any result.

Then **write the handoff** to `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/handoff.md`:

```
# Handoff — <TICKET>
Branch: <branch>   Base: <sha>   Head: <sha>

## Steps
| # | What | Commit | Scorer verdict | Rework rounds |

## Gates (real numbers, not claims)
| Gate | Result | Baseline |

## UNIFORM findings
<each one, with file:line — these are what a per-step review structurally cannot catch>

## Could not verify
<named, with why>

## Outstanding
<anything left, or "none">
```

**Write it even when everything passed.** PostBuild reads this file, and it may run in a different
session — a handoff that exists only in conversation does not survive the session ending.

Then present the same content to Marcel and **hand off to `zimmerMANNPostBuild`. This skill does
not push and does not open a PR.**

---

## Rework mode

Entered after a PR is open and CodeRabbit or a reviewer has requested changes.

**Read `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/postbuild.md` first.** It records what earlier rounds
already declined and why. A finding that was declined with evidence in round one does not get
re-litigated in round three — check before you verify anything, and if you disagree with a previous
decline, say so rather than silently reversing it.

**1. Verify every finding before touching anything.** CodeRabbit has been wrong on this repo
often — one batch ran 1-in-6 correct. Treat each finding as a hypothesis, not a fact. Per finding:

- **VALID** — reproduce it, cite `file:line`, fix it
- **INVALID** — say what is actually true, with the evidence, and draft the reply
- **OUT OF SCOPE** — real but not this story's problem; name the owning ticket or the person
- **DEFER** — real, in scope, but blocked on a decision; name who decides

**2. Fix only the VALID ones.** Same rules as build mode — the Implementer touches only what the
finding names, never stages, never commits.

**3. Re-run the cheap four**, plus the visual checkpoint if the fix changes rendered output.

**4. Commit the fixes here**, same rule as build mode — the skill commits, never an agent. Reference
the review thread each commit answers.

**5. Hand back to `zimmerMANNPostBuild`** with: what was fixed and in which commit, what was
declined and why, and the evidence behind each decline. **PostBuild owns the push and the
in-thread replies** — every finding gets a written answer, including the declined ones.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never push. Never open or update a PR.** That boundary belongs to PostBuild, which presents
  first and pushes only once Marcel has given the go.
- **Never write to the repo's config** — `.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CODEOWNERS`,
  `.docs/memory/**`, `.docs/prd/**`. Tier 1 Governance.
- **Never touch a Tier 1 file** without Marcel naming it and confirming owner approval.
- **Never expand scope.** Something worth doing that the plan didn't ask for gets reported, not
  done. Report it and let Marcel decide.
- **Local-only docs are never citable** in a commit message or a code comment. Cite `AGENTS.md`
  or `.claude/rules/*` instead.
- **Say what you could not verify.** Silence reads as "nothing wrong" when it may mean
  "didn't look there".

content.text:
Here's the real story, oldest to newest. I'll mark the three merges clearly since they're not our authored work — just develop catching up to us.

**1. `0abe8d0` — copy-first port of `recommended-products`**
Copied SFCC's stock "recommended products" component into our overrides folder and converted it to TypeScript — the mandatory first step before we're allowed to touch it. Zero behavior change. Side discovery: Cart automatically picks up our override, PDP doesn't (its import is written differently) — parked, fixed later in commit 8.

**2. `dff3ea1` — new "recentlyViewed" look for `ZimmProductCard`**
Taught the shared product-card component a 4th variation: image-only, no name/price/badge/button, per Figma spec. Had to hand-patch keyboard accessibility back in, since hiding the name also hid the only link.

**3. `fe73abc` — Einstein → card data mapper**
A pure translator function. Takes Einstein's rec data + Commerce API product data, reshapes it into props the recentlyViewed card needs. No UI, just data wrangling.

**4. `39b752b` — MERGE (sync, not ours)**
Pulled in whatever had landed on `develop`: mostly CI/deploy pipeline changes (preview/test/uat/SIT workflows) plus minor header/footer/icon tweaks. Nothing to do with SFCC-83/84.

**5. `2449e9f` — the "should we even show this?" gate**
Einstein always hands back 2 fake baseline recs even for a brand-new visitor, so "are there recs" can't mean "has this person viewed anything." Built our own session-based real-view tracker instead. One line added to PDP to feed it.

**6. `8280ffa` — MERGE (sync, not ours) — big, 42 files**
Another develop sync. Brought in a rewritten `product-view`, new form-control atoms (dropdown, size selector, link), and — worth flagging — **this is where the PLP page file (`product-list/index.tsx`) entered our branch for the first time**, as someone else's already-finished work, not something built on this branch.

**7. `387b26a` — the actual Rail UI**
Title + "See Full History" link + a horizontally-scrolling row of cards, capped at 5, in view order. No arrows — relies on the card's own built-in carousel.

**8. `0923c82` — wire the rail into real pages**
Made `recommended-products` branch: when Einstein flags a slot as "PDP recently viewed" or "Cart recently viewed," render our new rail; every other rec carousel on those pages is untouched. Also fixed the PDP import bug flagged in commit 1 — PDP genuinely wasn't using any of our overrides until this landed.

**9. `6d4fe0a` — WIP checkpoint — ⚠️ this one's different**
Its own message calls it *"temporary... not a real feature commit,"* made as a safety net right before a throwaway local merge of someone else's unrelated PR (#81) purely to preview it, with the stated plan to reset back here afterward and write proper commits later. **That reset never happened.** It's still sitting in our history exactly as committed, and it bundles a lot together non-atomically: the whole Full History page (SFCC-84), its grid component, a new history hook that replaced commit 5's gate hook, two new utils, plus reworks of already-committed files — all in one lump, unlike every other commit here.

**10. `835cab2` — MERGE (sync, not ours) — big, 54 files, current HEAD**
Most recent develop sync, where we currently sit. Brought in the wishlist login-drawer feature (SFCC-742) wholesale, button/drawer/text-input theme tweaks, a new social-button atom, a Contentful copy-seeding script, and config changes across every environment tier. Again, none of it is SFCC-83/84 work.

**The one thing that jumps out:** commits 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8 are genuinely clean — one concern per commit, well-documented, honest about tradeoffs. Commit 9 (`6d4fe0a`) is the odd one out — self-admittedly temporary, never cleaned up as promised, and it's what the current uncommitted pile from this session has been quietly building on top of. That's likely the actual seam where things started feeling "all over the place."

1	# SFCC-83 + SFCC-84 — Build Plan
2	
3	**Produced:** 2026-09-06 · **Gate:** `findings.md` (four passes, cleared at the 2026-09-06 adjudication)
4	**Base branch:** `feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component` (PR #85, open, unmerged)
5	
6	## 1. Goal statement
7	
8	Build the Recently Viewed rail and its full-history page per **SFCC-83** and **SFCC-84** (ACs in Jira
9	`customfield_10231`), designed in **`Zimmermann_Design_System_2026` component set `40000587:38471`**
10	(Desktop `40000307:12444`, Tablet `40000730:13363`, Mobile `40000538:25030` — all authoritative,
11	corroborated by PDP-template instances `7998:13508` / `8272:28947`), with SFCC-84's page from the
12	**provisional** `Zimmermann_Designs` `3332:35655` — following `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`
13	(token hierarchy) and `.claude/rules/components.md` (container/presentational split), and extending
14	**PR #85 / SFCC-236's** `ZimmProductCard` family via a **new `VARIATION_CONFIG` entry** (not a new
15	card), a **copy-first override of `recommended-products/`**, and **co-located `<name>.css.ts`**
16	recipes registered in `theme/components/index.ts`.
17	
18	**Scope corrected 2026-09-07 against the real Jira AC text** (Marcel supplied the full verbatim
19	SFCC-83/SFCC-84 tickets; see "PLP surface" in §2 and the Open Questions for the full reconciliation).
20	This plan's original scope line — "follows `.docs/prd/search.md` §7.4 (PDP + Cart); PLP is out;
21	SFCC-83 AC 9 knowingly not met" — was written against the PRD, never checked against the ticket's
22	own AC text, and is **superseded, not merely refined**: the AC states plainly *"Confirmed surfaces
23	are PLP, PDP, and Cart."* PLP is real, in-scope, unbuilt work — see §2.
24	**No consent gating** — not a development-phase carve-out awaiting a later fix, but genuinely out of
25	this ticket's scope: Jasmijn's own dependency note ("move the consent acceptance criteria to a
26	separate user story") and comment history move consent ACs to SFCC-106. Must still be stated in both
27	PR bodies so a reviewer doesn't read the absence as an oversight.
28	
29	**🔴 Data source corrected 2026-09-08 — Einstein is confirmed "Not Deployed" on every real
30	Zimmermann site (Open Question 6).** By Marcel's explicit direction, this build ships against real,
31	live Commerce Cloud product data sourced by this browser's own tracked view history instead — see
32	§2's "Interim data source" for the full design. A follow-up ticket (not yet created, Open
33	Question 18) swaps in real Einstein later; this plan's A3/A4/A6/B2 steps are written against the
34	interim design already.
35	
36	## 2. Scale call
37	
38	### Architecture fork — resolved: override `recommended-products/`, which removes the Cart port
39	
40	Verified directly at `node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/webpack/overrides-plugin.js`.
41	`isFromExtends` returns true when the request names `@salesforce/retail-react-app` **and the issuing
42	file is not itself inside `overrides/`**. The plugin's own comment (lines 116–127): *"This will return
43	true if the issuer is a file in a base template... This allow the base template to import from
44	overrides."* Implementation: `this.extends.includes(pkgName) && !filepath.includes(issuerPath)`.
45	
46	Base Cart imports at `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/cart/index.jsx:36`:
47	`import RecommendedProducts from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/recommended-products'`
48	— a package-path import issued from a base file, so it **is** redirected once our override exists.
49	Base Cart is itself loaded by base `routes.jsx` via a relative `import('./pages/cart')`, which is not
50	redirected — so base Cart keeps rendering and picks up our override for free.
51	
52	**Consequence: the ~2,460-line Cart copy-first (`index.jsx` 1515 + 8 real partials ≈ 948) is not
53	required.** This departed from adjudication item #10 ("we only have to copy-first for cart"), in the
54	direction of *less* work. **APPROVED by Marcel, 2026-09-06**, on the evidence that this is already the
55	dominant pattern in this repo: nine component overrides shadow base paths and are reached purely by
56	the resolver (`icons` at 64 base import sites — and mandated by AGENTS.md — `responsive` 12,
57	`product-view` 6, `drawer-menu`/`list-menu` 2 each, `header`/`footer` 1 each). The single page port
58	(`product-detail`) exists only because base `routes.jsx` loads pages by *relative* import, which the
59	resolver never redirects — a constraint that does not apply to components. Open Question 5 is closed.
60	
61	**Caveat:** this is a *build-time webpack* resolver. It runs in the dev server and production build
62	only — **not** Storybook (`.storybook/main.js` aliases straight to `node_modules`) and **not** Vitest.
63	So the Cart behaviour cannot be proven by any automated test in this repo; it must be checked in the
64	running app. That is why A1's pause is a hard gate.
65	
66	Cost of this choice: the override module loads at **four base import sites serving eight rails**, not
67	five as an earlier draft of this plan stated:
68	
69	| Base import site | Rails | Takes the new branch? |
70	|---|---|---|
71	| `app/pages/cart/index.jsx:36` | Cart Recently Viewed, Cart May-Also-Like | **Yes** (1 of 2) |
72	| `app/pages/product-detail/index.jsx:40` | *(shadowed by our own PDP override — 3 rails)* | **Yes** (1 of 3) |
73	| `app/hooks/use-add-to-cart-modal.js:30` | add-to-cart modal (`pdp-similar-items`) | No |
74	| `app/pages/product-list/partials/empty-results.jsx:20` | PLP empty-search top-sellers, most-viewed | No |
75	
76	It is therefore a **faithful port plus exactly one branch**, keyed off
77	`EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` (`'viewed-recently-einstein'` — the same string as
78	`CART_RECENTLY_VIEWED`, `constants.js:156,160`). **Two rails take the new branch; the other six must
79	render identically before and after** — a hard pass criterion.
80	
81	**🔴 Correction, 2026-09-06 — the PDP row above is misleading, verified directly against
82	`overrides-plugin.js`'s actual source, not just this plan's earlier paraphrase of it.** The
83	table's "Yes (1 of 3)" for `product-detail/index.jsx:40` describes the **base** file's import —

385	Add `ZimmProductCardRecentlyViewedVariation` to the exported union and one `VARIATION_CONFIG` row.
386	Update the docblock's KNOWN GAP paragraph (lines 124–135) from "whoever builds SFCC-83 needs to…" to a
387	record of what was done, citing Jira comment 13880.
388	
389	**Also record in that same docblock update (finding 34; naming decided 2026-09-06):** comment 13880
390	asks for the same badge/hover-swap suppression on **editorial and landing pages** — a surface with no
391	ticket, design or AC today. The variation is named `recentlyViewed` for the one confirmed surface, per
392	this repo's existing surface-naming convention (`home` / `plp` / `wishlist`). When editorial/landing
393	is scoped it needs **its own `VARIATION_CONFIG` row** with both flags `false`: it must not reuse
394	`recentlyViewed` (the name would lie) and must not use `plp` (which ships the badge Dani ruled out).
395	SFCC-236's *Variation extensibility* AC makes that a one-row change.
396	
397	**Corroborated 2026-09-07, straight from the ticket text.** SFCC-236's own description lists
398	*"Variations in scope: Homepage, PLP, Wish List, **Recently Viewed**"* — the exact term `recentlyViewed`
399	already uses. The AC body itself never separately defines this variation (it only ever defines
400	"Recently Viewed **Full History**," always "same as PLP" — every comment thread on the ticket
401	confirms that's specifically about the *"see full recently viewed page,"* never the rail), so this
402	doesn't pin down the rail's own behaviour — but it does settle the architecture question raised while
403	building this step: **should the SFCC-83 rail be a `ZimmProductCard` variation at all, or a separate,

412	**REWRITTEN 2026-09-06 after reading the real Figma nodes (findings 36-38).** An earlier draft

417	
418	**The rail tile is IMAGE ONLY.** Every flag is off:
419	
420	| Flag | Value | Source |
421	|---|---|---|

436	
437	**Accessibility gap found and closed, 2026-09-07 — not rendering `ZimmProductCardContent` at all
438	would remove the only real `<a>` this card has.** `ZimmProductCardContent` owns the card's one real
439	link (the name-link, via `react-router-dom`'s `Link`) — `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `onClick` is a

441	single-image `recentlyViewed` card (no gallery, no remove button, no badge, per the table above)

446	Two fixes were considered and rejected before landing on the one below:
447	- Extending `ZimmProductCardContent` itself with a "link-only" render mode — rejected after reading
448	  its actual source: price is rendered **unconditionally today, by design** (its own docblock: *"Always

453	  entirely — seriously considered mid-build, reversed after the SFCC-236/SFCC-743 ticket evidence
454	  above confirmed this codebase's established pattern for "labelled row of product cards" is
455	  composing `ZimmProductCard` instances, not smaller molecules directly.
456	
457	**Decided fix (Marcel, 2026-09-07):** when `!config.showContent`, don't render
458	`ZimmProductCardContent` at all (as originally planned) — instead render a small `react-router-dom`
459	`Link` (matching the exact import `ZimmProductCardContent` itself already uses, `chakra(RouteLink)`)
460	wrapping *only* `ZimmProductCardMedia`, with the product name as real (not `aria-label`) but
461	visually-hidden text via Chakra's own `VisuallyHidden` export inside the link — zero new dependency,
462	zero new CSS utility to build. `ZimmProductCardMedia` gets no `onClick={handleMediaClick}` in this
463	branch — a real `<Link>` directly containing the image needs no click-passthrough workaround at all
464	(that mechanism exists purely to route around the *other* variations' invisible stretched-overlay
465	`<a>`, which doesn't exist here since the link directly wraps the image instead of sitting behind
466	it). Confined entirely to `zimmProductCard/index.tsx` — no touch to `ZimmProductCardContent` or
467	`ZimmProductCardMedia`, matching this step's existing file manifest exactly.
468	
469	**Carousel arrows:** driven by image count in `ZimmProductCardMedia`, not by this table. Pass a
470	**single** image — AC 3's *"the product's index image"* — and they never appear, matching `Carousel`
471	`hidden="true"`.
472	
473	**PRD conflict, adjudicated (Marcel, 2026-09-06): design wins.** `.docs/prd/search.md` §7.5 (SPR-62,
474	Confirmed) says *"Add to Bag via size variant selection directly from recommendation carousels on PDP
475	and Cart pages."* The rail shows neither. Rationale for following the design: §7.5's own Open note
476	says the Add-to-Bag-vs-Wishlist choice is *"pending design refinement"*, and Recently Viewed is §7.4 —
477	a separate row — so §7.5 arguably never covered this rail. **Fully settled 2026-09-08** — Marcel
478	confirmed directly ("just the image on the rail") rather than leaving this for Jasmijn/Dani to
479	ratify (Open Question 10). Still state the divergence in the PR body so a reviewer reading the PRD
480	doesn't read it as a miss, but treat it as settled doctrine now, not a live question.
481	
482	**Pass criteria**
483	- `grep -n 'variation ===\|switch (variation)' index.tsx` still returns zero hits — the extensibility
484	  AC's mechanism is table-driven and must stay so.
485	- `index.test.tsx` gains `@ts-expect-error` cases proving the new variation's narrow props type

488	- A test asserts no badge renders even when `badge` is passed, and no hover swap even when

490	  fail) before the pass counts.
491	- **`ZimmProductCardContent` does not render at all for `recentlyViewed`** — assert

493	  nothing from that component reaches the DOM).
494	- **A real, keyboard-reachable link wraps the image, with the product name as its accessible name**
495	  — `screen.getByRole('link', {name: <product name>})` finds it. Confirm it renders exactly one
496	  link for this variation (same shape as the existing "exactly one real anchor" test for the other
497	  three variations), and that it's a real `to={href}` `Link`, not `onClick`-only.
498	- `ZimmProductCardMedia` receives no `onClick` for this variation — the click-passthrough handler
499	  exists only to route around the *other* variations' invisible overlay, which this branch has no

503	- `hideBagOnMobile` carries an inline comment naming its Figma node.

506	### A3 — Card mapper utility
507	
508	Create `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedCard.ts` — a pure module mapping one real product to
509	`ZimmProductCard` props. Modelled on the proven prior art at
510	`overrides/app/pages/home/liveProductCardDemoMapper.ts` (on `feature/zimmproductcard-live-demo`,
511	**not** on PR #85's branch — read it, port the approach, do not import it).
512	
513	**🔴 REVISED 2026-09-08 — input source changed, per "Interim data source" in §2.** Originally
514	specced as `use-einstein.js`'s `fetchRecProductDetails` output (`{...rec, ...product, productId,
515	image: {disBaseLink, alt}}`). With Einstein unavailable, the input is now a plain Shopper Product
516	from `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts`'s own `getProducts` call — the same underlying shape minus the
517	Einstein-specific `rec`/`image` wrapper fields. Reuse base `filterImageGroups`
518	(`app/utils/product-utils`) and `productUrlBuilder` (`app/utils/url`) exactly as before — neither
519	depends on which caller produced the product object. Inject `formatPrice` as a parameter so the
520	module stays free of `react-intl`, matching `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/productInfo.ts`.
521	This mapper's own output contract and scope (image-only, no price, no gallery — A2's decision) are
522	**unchanged**; only the shape of what it reads on the way in.
523	
524	**Pass criteria**
525	- No React, no `react-intl`, no hook import anywhere (`conventions.md` > Utilities).
526	- Returns `null` for a rec with no `productName` or no usable image — never throws, never emits a card
527	  with an empty `alt` (`ZimmProductCardMediaImage.alt` is required and non-empty).
528	- Tests: happy path; missing `productName`; missing `imageGroups`; single image (no `hoverImage`, no
529	  `images`); price without currency (**skip formatting, do not guess a currency**).
530	- This is a production path, unlike the throwaway demo mapper: SDK shapes come from
531	  `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` / `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` where they exist (AGENTS.md > Type
532	  Definitions). Hand-rolled narrow types only for genuinely unexported shapes, each with a why-comment.
533	
534	### A4 — Recently-viewed history hook, plus the PDP write
535	
536	**🔴 REVISED 2026-09-08 — renamed and re-designed, per "Interim data source" in §2. Read this whole
537	step before implementing; the original boolean logic below is no longer correct and would ship a
538	real bug if built as originally specced.**
539	
540	Create `overrides/app/hooks/useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts` (was `useRecentlyViewedGate.ts`).
541	
542	This still answers **finding 28** — the *original* concern was that Einstein's recommender returns a
543	two-product baseline for a visitor with zero history, so `recs.length === 0` never fires and AC 8
544	isn't implementable from the response. With Einstein out of the picture for this build, that specific
545	failure mode can't happen either way (there is no Einstein response to leak a baseline from) — but
546	the fix is still needed, now for a more basic reason: something has to track what "recently viewed"
547	even means without Einstein.
548	
549	**The boolean logic changes, not just the storage mechanism — this is the one real gotcha in this
550	revision.** The original design was:
551	
552	```
553	hasRecentlyViewed = sessionFlagIsSet || isRegistered
554	```
555	
556	`isRegistered` was a deliberate short-circuit: trust that a logged-in shopper has *some* server-side
557	Einstein history even on a fresh device. **That assumption breaks entirely once Einstein is out of
558	the loop** — there is no server-side history to trust anymore. Built as originally specced, every
559	registered shopper would show `hasRecentlyViewed = true` unconditionally, including one who has
560	never viewed anything in this interim system on any device — gating the rail *open* with zero real
561	cards behind it. That's a real, shippable bug, not a hypothetical; it must not be carried into the
562	interim build. **Corrected logic:**
563	
564	```
565	hasRecentlyViewed = recentlyViewedIds.length > 0
566	```
567	
568	— true for both guests and registered shoppers alike, based purely on this interim system's own
569	tracked history. `isRegistered` still matters, just for a different purpose now: it selects *which*
570	storage to read/write (see below), not whether to bypass the check.
571	
572	**New return shape:** `{hasRecentlyViewed: boolean, recentlyViewedIds: readonly string[],
573	markProductViewed: (productId: string) => void}` — the boolean is now derived from the ID list, not
574	tracked independently, so the two can never disagree.
575	
576	- `markProductViewed(productId)` writes to `sessionStorage` (guest) or `localStorage` (registered,
577	  via `isRegistered` from `useCustomerType()` — the same hook `use-einstein.js:449` already uses) —
578	  called from the existing Einstein `useEffect` in
579	  `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` (lines 772–801), alongside the
580	  `einstein.sendViewProduct` calls already there (left untouched — that call is unrelated real
581	  analytics, not this build's concern). One import, one call, guarded by the same `if (product)`.
582	- **De-duplication / move-to-front:** if `productId` is already in the stored list, remove the old
583	  entry before prepending — never a duplicate, and a re-view correctly becomes "most recent" again.
584	- **Cap the stored list** at `RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED` (**24, superseded from an earlier
585	  500 same day — see §2** — matches the Full History page's own 24-ID fetch cap, since nothing
586	  beyond item 24 is ever displayable) — trim from the tail, oldest-first, on write.
587	
588	**AC mapping, restated for the interim system:** `sessionStorage` is session-scoped and cleared at
589	session end — **AC 6**, unchanged. **AC 7 (cross-device for registered shoppers) is explicitly
590	*not* satisfied by this interim design** — `localStorage` is still device-local. This must be stated
591	plainly in the PR body and marked N/A-pending-the-Einstein-follow-up for this specific AC, not tested
592	against a single device and reported as passing. See §2's "Interim data source" for the full
593	reasoning — this is a stated, accepted gap, not an oversight.
594	
595	**Confirmed 2026-09-07, not a frontend gap** (pre-dates and is unaffected by this revision — restated
596	for continuity): SFCC-83's own Assumptions section states *"the storage of Recently Viewed is
597	handled by SFCC."* The interim system above is a **temporary, explicit stand-in** for that
598	assumption while Einstein is unavailable, not a rejection of it — once the Einstein follow-up lands,
599	this hook's job reverts to a thin boolean/gate again and the real history moves back server-side, per
600	the original design intent this section used to describe.
601	
602	**Superseded by the above, not applicable to the interim build:** the old "stated assumption" about
603	a registered shopper with genuinely zero Einstein history still seeing a two-product baseline
604	(Open Question 6's original framing) — that residual was specific to trusting Einstein's own
605	baseline behaviour, which the interim system never calls, so it cannot leak through here. It returns
606	once the Einstein follow-up is built, at which point Open Question 6's original text applies again.
607	
608	**Pass criteria**
609	- SSR-safe: initial state `{hasRecentlyViewed: false, recentlyViewedIds: []}`, resolved in
610	  `useEffect`. No storage access during render. No hydration mismatch — the rail does not exist on
611	  first paint and appears after hydration. (Also good for LCP; the PDP rail is inside
612	  `<Island hydrateOn='visible'>` anyway.)
613	- Wrapped in `try/catch` — Safari private mode throws on both `sessionStorage` and `localStorage`.
614	  Failure degrades to `{hasRecentlyViewed: false, recentlyViewedIds: []}`, never an exception.
615	- JSDoc with `@returns` (`components.md` > Hooks).
616	- Vitest: empty storage + guest → `false`/`[]`; one ID + guest → `true`/`[id]`; empty storage +
617	  **registered** → `false`/`[]` (**the corrected case — must be tested explicitly, since this is
618	  exactly where the old short-circuit bug would have shipped silently**); re-viewing an existing ID
619	  moves it to front with no duplicate; writing past the cap trims the oldest entry; storage throwing
620	  → safe empty default; first render before effect → safe empty default.
621	- **Make each fail on purpose first.** The FED handbook's finding 18 trap is a test that passes
622	  because it was written against the only arrangement already correct — this applies doubly to the
623	  registered-with-zero-history case above, since that's precisely the case the old logic got wrong.
624	- The PDP change is exactly two lines (now passing `product.id` into `markProductViewed`, not a
625	  no-arg call). Nothing else in `product-detail/index.tsx` moves (AGENTS.md Hard Rule #5 — no
626	  refactoring upward).
627	
628	### A5 — `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` organism + recipe
629	
630	Create `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedRail/` (`index.tsx`,
631	`zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts`, `index.stories.tsx`, `index.test.tsx`); register
632	`ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`.
633	
634	**Purely presentational — data as props.** Props: `title: ReactNode`, `cards: readonly
635	ZimmProductCardProps[]`, `seeAllHref?: string`, `seeAllLabel?: string`. No `useEinstein`, no
636	`useIntl` — the container owns the copy. (An `IntlProvider` wrapper is still needed in the test
637	because `ZimmProductCard` itself calls `useIntl`; follow `zimmProductCard/index.test.tsx`'s wrapper.)
638	
639	Structure mirrors Figma: a `title-and-link` row (title left, See-Full-History link right) above a
640	horizontally scrollable `group` of `ZimmProductCard`s at `variation: 'recentlyViewed'`.
641	
642	**No rail-level arrow buttons.** Desktop `40000307:12444` decomposes into exactly two children —
643	`title-and-link` (1440×96) and `group` (1440×432) — with no arrow layer. `ZimmProductCard` already
644	carries its own intra-card arrows; rail arrows would collide. Native scroll with scroll-snap only.
645	
646	**Three explicit media queries** off `breakpoints` imported from `app/theme/foundation`, never Chakra's
647	array shorthand (it fails `recipeGuards.test.ts`). Real geometry, read from the nodes 2026-09-06:
648	
649	| Viewport | Rail node | Card | Cards across |
650	|---|---|---|---|
651	| Mobile (base, 402) | `40000538:25030` — 402×355.82 | **201×299.82** | **2** (201×2 = 402, exactly full-bleed) |
652	| Tablet (`breakpoints.md`, 768) | `40000730:13363` — 768×437.85 | **256×381.85** | **3** |
653	| Desktop (`breakpoints.xl`) | `40000307:12444` — 1440×528 | **288×432** | **5** |
654	
655	All three cards are 2:3, matching `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s existing `aspectRatio: '2 / 3'` — so card
656	width is the only thing that varies per breakpoint; height follows. Header (`title-and-link`) is
657	**h96** on Desktop (`40000538:20306`) and **h56** on Mobile (`40000538:25031`); the link is present on
658	both, so it is never hidden by viewport.

# SFCC-83 + SFCC-84 — Build Plan

**Produced:** 2026-09-06 · **Gate:** `findings.md` (four passes, cleared at the 2026-09-06 adjudication)
**Base branch:** `feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component` (PR #85, open, unmerged)

## 1. Goal statement

Build the Recently Viewed rail and its full-history page per **SFCC-83** and **SFCC-84** (ACs in Jira
`customfield_10231`), designed in **`Zimmermann_Design_System_2026` component set `40000587:38471`**
(Desktop `40000307:12444`, Tablet `40000730:13363`, Mobile `40000538:25030` — all authoritative,
corroborated by PDP-template instances `7998:13508` / `8272:28947`), with SFCC-84's page from the
**provisional** `Zimmermann_Designs` `3332:35655` — following `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`
(token hierarchy) and `.claude/rules/components.md` (container/presentational split), and extending
**PR #85 / SFCC-236's** `ZimmProductCard` family via a **new `VARIATION_CONFIG` entry** (not a new
card), a **copy-first override of `recommended-products/`**, and **co-located `<name>.css.ts`**
recipes registered in `theme/components/index.ts`.

**Scope corrected 2026-09-07 against the real Jira AC text** (Marcel supplied the full verbatim
SFCC-83/SFCC-84 tickets; see "PLP surface" in §2 and the Open Questions for the full reconciliation).
This plan's original scope line — "follows `.docs/prd/search.md` §7.4 (PDP + Cart); PLP is out;
SFCC-83 AC 9 knowingly not met" — was written against the PRD, never checked against the ticket's
own AC text, and is **superseded, not merely refined**: the AC states plainly *"Confirmed surfaces
are PLP, PDP, and Cart."* PLP is real, in-scope, unbuilt work — see §2.
**No consent gating** — not a development-phase carve-out awaiting a later fix, but genuinely out of
this ticket's scope: Jasmijn's own dependency note ("move the consent acceptance criteria to a
separate user story") and comment history move consent ACs to SFCC-106. Must still be stated in both
PR bodies so a reviewer doesn't read the absence as an oversight.

**🔴 Data source corrected 2026-09-08 — Einstein is confirmed "Not Deployed" on every real
Zimmermann site (Open Question 6).** By Marcel's explicit direction, this build ships against real,
live Commerce Cloud product data sourced by this browser's own tracked view history instead — see
§2's "Interim data source" for the full design. A follow-up ticket (not yet created, Open
Question 18) swaps in real Einstein later; this plan's A3/A4/A6/B2 steps are written against the
interim design already.

## 2. Scale call

### Architecture fork — resolved: override `recommended-products/`, which removes the Cart port

Verified directly at `node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/webpack/overrides-plugin.js`.
`isFromExtends` returns true when the request names `@salesforce/retail-react-app` **and the issuing
file is not itself inside `overrides/`**. The plugin's own comment (lines 116–127): *"This will return
true if the issuer is a file in a base template... This allow the base template to import from
overrides."* Implementation: `this.extends.includes(pkgName) && !filepath.includes(issuerPath)`.

Base Cart imports at `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/cart/index.jsx:36`:
`import RecommendedProducts from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/recommended-products'`
— a package-path import issued from a base file, so it **is** redirected once our override exists.
Base Cart is itself loaded by base `routes.jsx` via a relative `import('./pages/cart')`, which is not
redirected — so base Cart keeps rendering and picks up our override for free.

**Consequence: the ~2,460-line Cart copy-first (`index.jsx` 1515 + 8 real partials ≈ 948) is not
required.** This departed from adjudication item #10 ("we only have to copy-first for cart"), in the
direction of *less* work. **APPROVED by Marcel, 2026-09-06**, on the evidence that this is already the
dominant pattern in this repo: nine component overrides shadow base paths and are reached purely by
the resolver (`icons` at 64 base import sites — and mandated by AGENTS.md — `responsive` 12,
`product-view` 6, `drawer-menu`/`list-menu` 2 each, `header`/`footer` 1 each). The single page port
(`product-detail`) exists only because base `routes.jsx` loads pages by *relative* import, which the
resolver never redirects — a constraint that does not apply to components. Open Question 5 is closed.

**Caveat:** this is a *build-time webpack* resolver. It runs in the dev server and production build
only — **not** Storybook (`.storybook/main.js` aliases straight to `node_modules`) and **not** Vitest.
So the Cart behaviour cannot be proven by any automated test in this repo; it must be checked in the
running app. That is why A1's pause is a hard gate.

Cost of this choice: the override module loads at **four base import sites serving eight rails**, not
five as an earlier draft of this plan stated:

| Base import site | Rails | Takes the new branch? |
|---|---|---|
| `app/pages/cart/index.jsx:36` | Cart Recently Viewed, Cart May-Also-Like | **Yes** (1 of 2) |
| `app/pages/product-detail/index.jsx:40` | *(shadowed by our own PDP override — 3 rails)* | **Yes** (1 of 3) |
| `app/hooks/use-add-to-cart-modal.js:30` | add-to-cart modal (`pdp-similar-items`) | No |
| `app/pages/product-list/partials/empty-results.jsx:20` | PLP empty-search top-sellers, most-viewed | No |

`EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` (`'viewed-recently-einstein'` — the same string as

intended to survive that swap unchanged.

both interim, only one of which changes later:

  framing once the `getProducts` 24-ID limit was discovered) into the richer was/now/multi-image

**Storage mechanics, per "browser/local it is":**
- **Guests:** `sessionStorage` — unchanged from A4's existing design, still correctly satisfies AC 6
  (session-scoped, cleared at session end).
- **Registered shoppers:** `localStorage` — a genuine, explicit, temporary deviation from both AC 7
  ("available on login from any device") and the ticket's own Assumption ("storage... handled by
  SFCC"). `localStorage` survives closing the browser (better than nothing, testable), but is still
  **device-local** — it cannot and will not satisfy cross-device continuity. This is not a
  workaround for that AC, it's an explicit, stated non-fix pending the Einstein follow-up — must be
  called out plainly in the PR body and to whoever signs off testing, not discovered by a confused
  reviewer. AC 7 should be marked N/A-pending-follow-up for this PR, not silently tested against a
  single device and called passing.

  views, and needs its own explicit test (view A, B, A again → order must be `[A, B]`, not `[A, B, A]`
  or `[B, A]` misordered).

  was discovered.** Original reasoning (Marcel: "how would this be treated if Einstein were
  available? do the same as that"): real Einstein has no client-supplied "how far back to
  remember" parameter, so this isn't a product/UX decision — `RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED =

  account for two facts discovered later the same day: (1) Shopper Products `getProducts` has a
  hard 24-ID-per-request limit (SDK's own doc comment, independently confirmed twice during Phase 1

  the `500` above.** This was caught by Phase 1's own implementer, who read this plan directly,

  correctly surfaced it rather than silently picking a side — exactly the discipline this plan
  asks for elsewhere. **Open Question 17 is re-closed at the new number** — no further confirmation
  needed; this is a direct, logical consequence of Marcel's own 24-cap decision, not a new
  independent judgement call.
