Create `overrides/app/hooks/useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts` (was `useRecentlyViewedGate.ts`).

This still answers **finding 28** — the *original* concern was that Einstein's recommender returns a
two-product baseline for a visitor with zero history, so `recs.length === 0` never fires and AC 8
isn't implementable from the response. With Einstein out of the picture for this build, that specific
failure mode can't happen either way (there is no Einstein response to leak a baseline from) — but
the fix is still needed, now for a more basic reason: something has to track what "recently viewed"
even means without Einstein.

**The boolean logic changes, not just the storage mechanism — this is the one real gotcha in this
revision.** The original design was:

```
hasRecentlyViewed = sessionFlagIsSet || isRegistered
```

`isRegistered` was a deliberate short-circuit: trust that a logged-in shopper has *some* server-side
Einstein history even on a fresh device. **That assumption breaks entirely once Einstein is out of
the loop** — there is no server-side history to trust anymore. Built as originally specced, every
registered shopper would show `hasRecentlyViewed = true` unconditionally, including one who has
never viewed anything in this interim system on any device — gating the rail *open* with zero real
cards behind it. That's a real, shippable bug, not a hypothetical; it must not be carried into the
interim build. **Corrected logic:**

```
hasRecentlyViewed = recentlyViewedIds.length > 0
```

— true for both guests and registered shoppers alike, based purely on this interim system's own
tracked history. `isRegistered` still matters, just for a different purpose now: it selects *which*
storage to read/write (see below), not whether to bypass the check.

**New return shape:** `{hasRecentlyViewed: boolean, recentlyViewedIds: readonly string[],
markProductViewed: (productId: string) => void}` — the boolean is now derived from the ID list, not
tracked independently, so the two can never disagree.

- `markProductViewed(productId)` writes to `sessionStorage` (guest) or `localStorage` (registered,
  via `isRegistered` from `useCustomerType()` — the same hook `use-einstein.js:449` already uses) —
  called from the existing Einstein `useEffect` in
  `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` (lines 772–801), alongside the
  `einstein.sendViewProduct` calls already there (left untouched — that call is unrelated real
  analytics, not this build's concern). One import, one call, guarded by the same `if (product)`.
- **De-duplication / move-to-front:** if `productId` is already in the stored list, remove the old
  entry before prepending — never a duplicate, and a re-view correctly becomes "most recent" again.
- **Cap the stored list** at `RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED` (**24, superseded from an earlier
  500 same day — see §2** — matches the Full History page's own 24-ID fetch cap, since nothing
  beyond item 24 is ever displayable) — trim from the tail, oldest-first, on write.

**AC mapping, restated for the interim system:** `sessionStorage` is session-scoped and cleared at
session end — **AC 6**, unchanged. **AC 7 (cross-device for registered shoppers) is explicitly
*not* satisfied by this interim design** — `localStorage` is still device-local. This must be stated
plainly in the PR body and marked N/A-pending-the-Einstein-follow-up for this specific AC, not tested
against a single device and reported as passing. See §2's "Interim data source" for the full
reasoning — this is a stated, accepted gap, not an oversight.

**Confirmed 2026-09-07, not a frontend gap** (pre-dates and is unaffected by this revision — restated
for continuity): SFCC-83's own Assumptions section states *"the storage of Recently Viewed is
handled by SFCC."* The interim system above is a **temporary, explicit stand-in** for that
assumption while Einstein is unavailable, not a rejection of it — once the Einstein follow-up lands,
this hook's job reverts to a thin boolean/gate again and the real history moves back server-side, per
the original design intent this section used to describe.

**Superseded by the above, not applicable to the interim build:** the old "stated assumption" about
a registered shopper with genuinely zero Einstein history still seeing a two-product baseline
(Open Question 6's original framing) — that residual was specific to trusting Einstein's own
baseline behaviour, which the interim system never calls, so it cannot leak through here. It returns
once the Einstein follow-up is built, at which point Open Question 6's original text applies again.

**Pass criteria**
- SSR-safe: initial state `{hasRecentlyViewed: false, recentlyViewedIds: []}`, resolved in

  first paint and appears after hydration. (Also good for LCP; the PDP rail is inside

- Wrapped in `try/catch` — Safari private mode throws on both `sessionStorage` and `localStorage`.

**Pass criteria**
- **Every value is `textStyle`, `var(--zimm-*)`, or a named constant with a `provisional`/`pending`
  comment.** Zero raw hex/px/rem/em, zero bare Chakra token strings. `npm run audit:tokens` reports no
  new finding here; `recipeGuards.test.ts` passes (namespacing + bare-token guards).
- Recipe key namespaced `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` — an unnamespaced key deep-merges with any same-named
  SFCC base recipe.
- `ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts` passes — declared `parts` cover every part read off
  `useMultiStyleConfig`.
- **Cap is client-side.** At most `RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_MAX_ITEMS` (5, matching the Desktop
  composition) regardless of input length. Finding 29: the API ignores `limit`, so the cap cannot live
  in the request. Named constant, never a literal.
- **Order preserved verbatim** — renders `cards` in received order, most-recent-first, left to right
  (AC 2). Test with an input whose correct and incorrect orderings are distinguishable (**not** a list
  already order-independent — that is exactly the encoded-bug trap). Make it fail by reversing.
- Renders `null` when `cards` is empty — a second guard behind A4's gate.
- **See-Full-History link states — RESOLVED FROM REGISTERED TOKENS 2026-09-06, not from the

Good news first: the first six steps are in genuinely great shape. Then I'll show exactly where it comes apart.

## On-plan (A1–A6) — clean, matches, committed correctly

| Plan step | Commit | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| A1 — copy-first `recommended-products` | `0abe8d0` | ✅ matches exactly, including the Cart-works/PDP-doesn't finding the plan calls out |
| A2 — `recentlyViewed` variation | `dff3ea1` | ✅ matches exactly — table-driven, `showContent` flag, the accessibility Link+VisuallyHidden fix, all as spec'd |
| A3 (original) — Einstein-based mapper | `fe73abc` | ✅ matches the *original* plan text (built before the pivot below) |
| A4 (original) — boolean gate hook | `2449e9f` | ✅ matches the *original* plan text (same caveat) |
| A5 — Rail organism | `387b26a` | ✅ matches exactly — header row, group, 3 explicit media queries, cap |
| A6 — wire the branch, fix PDP import | `0923c82` | ✅ matches exactly, including the exact PDP relative-import fix the plan calls a real ship-blocking gap |

Six atomic commits, one plan step each, well-documented, in order. This part was done right.

## Where it comes apart

**1. The "interim data source" pivot (2026-09-08) is legitimate — how it landed isn't.**
Einstein turned out to be undeployed on every real site, so Marcel directed: ship against real browser-tracked view history instead. Good call, clearly documented in the plan. But that pivot **revises A3 and A4** — and the plan says the A4 revision fixes *"a real, shippable bug, not hypothetical"* (the old logic showed the rail to every logged-in shopper regardless of real history). That fix, plus **all of B1 (Grid) and B2 (Page+Route)**, landed inside `6d4fe0a` — the commit whose own message calls it *"a temporary local checkpoint... not a real feature commit... to be discarded via git reset... real commit history organized separately later."* That reset never happened. Three planned steps' worth of work, including a real bug fix, is sitting in one unscored, uncheckpointed lump instead of three separate Implementer→Tester→Scorer passes with commits.

**2. PLP surface — decision was made, the required gate wasn't visibly cleared.**
Plan's Open Question 13 says plainly: *"Owner: Marcel — decide whether this folds in... before any PLP file is created."* Marcel did decide ("we're doing PLP as well"), but the plan is equally explicit that this adds a third protection tier (Squad A pages) and needs its own **Hard Rule #10 stop** plus **Squad A Lead notification** per `squadA.md` before `product-list/` gets touched. I have no evidence either happened — `product-list/index.tsx` entered the branch via a develop merge (someone else's already-existing work), got reworked inside the `6d4fe0a` lump, and was touched again by this session's size-chip fix. Not necessarily wrong, but untracked against what the plan requires.

**3. This session's five bug fixes aren't in the plan at all.**
Image fallback, Notify Me, was/now pricing, size-aware Add-to-Bag, size-chip disabled-state — none are named steps. They read as real defects Marcel found live-testing the PLP/rail work, fixed one at a time as reported. Possibly all correct fixes, but none went through the plan's loop, none are committed, and there's no scoring or visual checkpoint behind any of them.

## Still open, straight from the plan, untouched by anything above

- **Open Question 18** — the Einstein follow-up ticket "does not exist yet." Owner: Marcel, due before this PR merges.
- **Open Question 19** — how AC 7 (cross-device continuity) gets represented to QA is undecided. Owner: Marcel, due before this reaches QA.
- **GATES step** — the consolidated pre-PR pass (`build` + `tsc` + `lint` + `test` + `audit:tokens` + a real `cr review`) has never run as its own single pass. This session ran the cheap three per individual fix, which isn't the same thing.
- **The PR-body disclosure list** — 14 separate items (a)–(n) the plan requires stated explicitly (Einstein not deployed, AC7 gap, PLP AC9 now in-scope, interim data source, provisional design source, etc.). None of this exists yet because no PR is open.

That's the full picture. Where do you want to start pulling this back together?

lastPrompt: since the last commit that's aligned to the plan, what are the changes that we've made/done - including the changes we have sitting uncommitted

content.text:
Here's the complete accounting from `0923c82` (last plan-aligned commit) to right now.

## Timeline anchor (covered last turn, restated briefly)

Two commits sit between A6 and today: `6d4fe0a` (self-labelled "WIP checkpoint... not a real feature commit") and `835cab2` (a `develop` sync, not our work). Everything below is what's sitting **uncommitted** on top of those — 27 files, +2287/−203.

## The uncommitted pile, grouped by what it actually does

**A. B3 delivered — the See-Full-History link, for real** (`recommended-products/index.tsx`+test)
This is a genuine plan step landing: `showSeeAllLink = cards.length > visibleCardCount`, threshold read via `useBreakpointValue(RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS)` (viewport-relative, matching the plan's reopened Open Question 1), href site-prefixed via `useMultiSite().buildUrl`. Matches the plan's B3 spec closely. *Status: plan-mapped, correctly designed — just never run through its own step/commit/checkpoint.*

**B. Rail cap changed from soft to hard** (`constants/index.ts`, `zimmRecentlyViewedRail/*`)
`RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_MAX_ITEMS` (flat 5) is **deleted** and replaced by `RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS = {base: 2, md: 3, xl: 5}`. More than a rename: the docs now state this is *"a real, hard per-breakpoint limit... not a 'fits before scrolling' soft limit,"* confirmed directly with you. That's a real UX decision reversal on already-shipped A5 — a mobile shopper can no longer scroll the rail to see a 3rd card, ever. *Status: retroactive change to already-committed, already-scored work.*

**C. Grid gains a real Tablet tier** (`zimmRecentlyViewedGrid/*`)
Was 2-tier (2-up mobile+tablet combined / 4-up desktop) with an explicitly-flagged "unconfirmed placeholder" for the missing tablet reading. Now 3-tier (2/3/4), with the tablet figure sourced as *"Marcel's own direct figure... not a re-derived Figma reading."* Also fixes a real Storybook bug where the grid demo's size chips looked unselectable (no-op handler) even though the click worked. *Status: retroactive design change to already-shipped B1, correctly sourced/labelled as a direct instruction rather than a Figma reading.*

**D. Notify Me now ships visible-but-inert** (`zimmProductCardContent`, `zimmProductCard`)
Reverses `showNotifyMe && Boolean(onNotifyMe)` → `showNotifyMe` alone. An out-of-stock card now always shows the button, even with no real handler wired (the actual feature doesn't exist yet — clicking does nothing). Documented as your explicit call. *Status: retroactive behavior change to already-shipped, already-tested A2 code.*

**E. Cascading image fallback — a real live defect, well-fixed** (`zimmProductCardMedia`, `zimmProductCard`, `recentlyViewedCard.ts`, `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts` + all four tests)
Real find: product `4673TS251`'s medium image group has 9 images, and index 0 specifically 404s. New `primaryImageFallbacks` prop cascades to the next candidate on a real `onError`, threaded from `ZimmProductCardMedia` up through both card mappers. Thorough, well-tested. *Status: legitimate bug fix, but touches four already-shipped files across two components and two utils, none of it planned or scored as its own step.*

**F. Was/now pricing wired into PLP** (`productListCardMapper.ts`)
`selectProductListCard` now calls real `getPriceData` instead of hardcoding `originalPrice: undefined`. **This is the one item I'd flag hardest** — the plan's own Open Question 16 explicitly says this exact change is *"not done... a bigger, separate call than 'fix the inaccurate comment'... left as a genuine fast-follow if wanted, not assumed."* It's been done anyway, with no visible sign that decision was revisited.

**G. Size-aware Add to Bag + the size-chip disabled-state fix** (`productListCardMapper.ts`, `product-list/index.tsx`)
New `resolveOrderableVariant` resolves the actually-selected size chip to its real SKU/price before adding to bag (previously always added the default variant regardless of chip selection). Bundled in the same file: the `expand` array fix (`availability` + `represented_products`) from earlier this session. Both real, both verified against live product `4673TS251`. *Status: new functionality on Squad A's `product-list/` — the plan's Open Question 13 required Squad A Lead notification before this territory was touched; no evidence that happened.*

**H. PLP rail title fix** (`product-list/index.tsx`)
Small, real correction — PLP's rail was rendering with no title at all; a stale comment claimed that was deferred to a "not yet built" step. Now fixed, comment corrected.

**I. Translation files — mixed signal** (`translations/en-*.json` + compiled)
+102 new keys in each source file. Some are directly ours (`recently_viewed.*`, `recommended_products.link.see_full_history`, PLP toast/title). Many are **not** — `product_detail.drawer_trigger.*`, `zimm_dropdown_item.*`, `zimm_size_selector.*`, `slide_indicator.*` belong to the dropdown/size-selector work that rode in via the `8280ffa` merge, not this branch's own output. Looks like a full-repo translation-extraction sweep, not a scoped one. Worth knowing this file is noisier than "our" diff.

## The pattern across B–G

Five of nine items (B, C, D, E, and arguably F) aren't new work — they're **revisions to components that were already implemented, tested, and in B's/D's case already visually reviewed**, discovered via live testing and fixed in place, with no step re-opened, no re-score, and no fresh visual checkpoint despite several changing what actually renders. G is genuinely new functionality in territory the plan flagged as needing a specific stop that doesn't look like it happened.

That's the full inventory. What do you want to do with it?

**The variant is genuinely done and shipped:**

143	 * browser-tracked stand-in `RecommendedProducts`' own Recently-Viewed branch already uses -- see

146	 * further to cap here), maps each result through `selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard` (filtering
147	 * the hard `null` gate every mapper in this codebase uses), and renders `ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid` --

151	 * `badge` field is always `undefined` -- the plain `getProducts` endpoint this build reads from has
152	 * no confirmed `c_productBadges` field (see that mapper's own docblock's "Badge" section). A card
153	 * rendered by this page will never show a badge yet; this is a pre-existing, out-of-scope gap for
154	 * this step, not a bug in this file.
155	 *
156	 * **Empty-state gate: `hasRecentlyViewed` (`recentlyViewedIds.length > 0`), not
157	 * `cards.length === 0`.** The two are equivalent for a shopper who has never viewed anything, but
158	 * diverge while `useRecentlyViewedProductFetch`'s own request is still in flight for a shopper who

Checked directly, same way as the rail. Solid foundation, but there's one real gap I hadn't surfaced before.

**Page + route — ✅ solid**
`/recently-viewed`, positioned correctly in `routes.tsx` (after `..._routes`, before the `/:slug` catch-all, with a comment explaining why), `getTemplateName = () => 'recently-viewed'` matching every other page. Has its own `index.test.tsx` (11.7KB, committed in `6d4fe0a`).

**Grid organism — ✅ solid, and the layout gap from last turn is now closed**
3-tier responsive columns confirmed: 2-up Mobile, 3-up Tablet (your own directly-supplied figure), 4-up Desktop (the one real Figma reading). Title + item-count header row, both `textStyle="heading3"`, cross-checked against the actual Figma node (`3332:37131`) and matches exactly.

**Data pipeline — ✅ real, wired correctly**
`useRecentlyViewedHistory` → `useRecentlyViewedProductFetch` (capped at 24) → `selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard`, producing real `variation: 'plp'`-shaped cards — real was/now pricing via `getPriceData`, real multi-image galleries, and the same cascading image-fallback fix as the rail. Matches SFCC-236's "same behaviour as PLP card" AC.

**Empty state + SEO — ✅ both built correctly**
Empty state ported from `EmptyCart`'s real precedent, `isRegistered`-branched copy/CTAs, gated on `hasRecentlyViewed` specifically (not `cards.length`) to avoid flashing empty-state copy while the fetch is still in flight. SEO uses `noindex, nofollow` via `Seo`'s `children`, correctly avoiding the `noIndex` prop's `nofollow`-less bug.

**One already-known, self-documented gap:** badge always renders `undefined` — the `getProducts` endpoint this page reads from has no confirmed badge field. Flagged in the page's own docblock, not new, not hidden.

**🔴 One gap I hadn't surfaced yet — Add to Bag and size-chip selection don't work on this page at all.**
Cards render at `variation: 'plp'`, which means the bag button and size chips both render (per SFCC-236's own AC). But I grepped the page, the grid, and the mapper for `onAddToBag`/`onSizeChipSelect`/`selectedSizeChipValue` — **zero matches, anywhere.** Both props are optional on `ZimmProductCard`, so nothing crashes — it just means:
- Add to Bag renders but clicking it does literally nothing (no handler at all — worse than PLP's old bug, which at least added *something*).
- Size chips render but can't be selected — no state, no handler.

Worth noting: the Storybook story *did* get a fix for exactly this look (`LiveSizeSelectionGrid`, from last turn's accounting) — but that fix only lives in the story file. The real page container never got the equivalent wiring PLP's own page now has (`ProductListCard` + `resolveOrderableVariant`). This isn't in the plan's B1/B2 pass criteria either, so it's not a "planned but skipped" item — it looks like something the plan never actually considered.

That's the full picture for SFCC-84: strong on page/layout/data/empty-state/SEO, but the interactive card behaviour needs real work before this page can ship.

25	 * (the closest existing precedent producing this exact `plp`-variation output shape from a real
26	 * product). Ported, not imported, from both — a genuinely separate, self-contained module with
27	 * its own local type aliases, the same relationship `recentlyViewedCard.ts` already has to
28	 * `productListCardMapper.ts` (see that file's own docblock).
29	 *
30	 * **What's ported near-verbatim from `productListCardMapper.ts`, and what changed:**
31	 * `selectGalleryImages`/`selectSizeChipValues` are re-pointed at `product.imageGroups`/
32	 * `product.variationAttributes` directly (the plain `Product` shape) in place of a
33	 * `ProductSearchHit`'s own same-named fields — the underlying `ImageGroup`/`Image`/
34	 * `VariationAttribute` shapes are the same `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` types either way (confirmed
35	 * directly against `node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts`), so the
36	 * picking/mapping logic itself needed no change, only the input type.
37	 *
38	 * **Primary-image resolution is NOT ported from `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own
39	 * `toCardImage(hit.image)`** — a plain `getProducts` `Product` has no equivalent flat `image`
40	 * field; that is a Search-hit-only convenience field. Instead this mirrors `recentlyViewedCard.ts`
41	 * `selectPrimaryImage` (`viewType: 'medium'` `imageGroups` lookup, required non-empty `alt`) — the
42	 * already-established, correct approach for this exact input shape.
43	 *
44	 * **Price handling is deliberately NOT copied from `productListCardMapper.ts`.** That mapper reads
45	 * the flat `hit.price` field for `currentPrice` while leaving `originalPrice` unset entirely — had
46	 * it called `getPriceData(hit).listPrice` for `originalPrice` while keeping `hit.price` for
47	 * `currentPrice`, the two would risk disagreeing on a multi-variant product, since `getPriceData`
48	 * internally sources its own `currentPrice` from `findLowestPrice()`, not from a flat `price`
49	 * field. Both `currentPrice` and `originalPrice` here come from one `getPriceData(product)` call
50	 * (base SFCC, `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils.js:123-170`,
51	 * confirmed by reading it directly) so the two halves can never disagree. `originalPrice` is only
52	 * ever set when that same call's `isOnSale` is `true` — a not-on-sale product must not render a
53	 * crossed-out price identical to its current one.
54	 *
55	 * **Badge — a real, found gap, not silently papered over.** `productListCardMapper.ts` reads
56	 * `hit.c_productBadges?.[0]?.productBadge` off a Search hit's custom index field. Checked directly
57	 * against `commerce-sdk-isomorphic`'s own type declaration for the plain `Product` shape
58	 * (`node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts:59783-59835`, the exact block backing
59	 * `ShopperProductsTypes.Product`): there is no typed `c_productBadges` field there — only a
60	 * generic `{[key: string]: any}` index signature, which would let `product.c_productBadges`
61	 * compile without error but proves nothing about whether the real `getProducts` endpoint (a
62	 * hydration endpoint, not the search-index endpoint `c_productBadges` is confirmed on) actually
63	 * populates this custom, index-only attribute. `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts`'s own `getProducts`
64	 * call requests no expand parameter that obviously corresponds to custom attributes either.
65	 * Rather than read a field with no confirmed backing, `badge` is left `undefined` below — see that
66	 * assignment's own comment. This is a real, unresolved gap, not a design choice: if Full History
67	 * needs badges to actually render, confirming whether `getProducts` carries this field needs a
68	 * live check against a real badged product in a running environment, the same "verify in the
69	 * running app" caveat the build plan's own B2 discussion already states for was/now pricing.
70	 */
71	import type { ShopperProductsTypes } from 'commerce-sdk-isomorphic';
72	import { getPriceData, filterImageGroups } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils';
73	import { productUrlBuilder } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/url';
74	import type {
75	  ZimmProductCardBaseProps,
76	  ZimmProductCardPlpVariation,
77	  ZimmProductCardImage,
78	} from '../components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard';
79	import type { ZimmSizeChipValue } from '../components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSizeChipGroup';

81	/**
82	 * The real Commerce API `Product` this mapper reads — the same `ShopperProductsTypes.Product`
83	 * `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts` produces and `recentlyViewedCard.ts` also consumes. Named
84	 * locally (rather than importing `RecentlyViewedProduct` from that sibling module) so this stays
85	 * a genuinely separate, self-contained module — matching how this whole file is itself "ported,
86	 * not imported" from its own two precedents.
87	 */
88	export type RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct = ShopperProductsTypes.Product;
89	
90	/** Formats a bare amount for the storefront. Injected so this module stays free of react-intl —
91	 *  same shape as `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s own `FormatPrice`, redeclared locally for the same
92	 *  separate-module reason as `RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct` above. */
93	export type FormatPrice = (amount: number, currency: string) => string;
94	
95	/**
96	 * The full `plp`-variation `ZimmProductCard` props this mapper produces — badge, size chips,
97	 * was/now pricing, multi-image gallery, heading level and variation all included. Mirrors
98	 * `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `ProductListCardResult` (unexported from that file, so
99	 * redeclared here rather than imported) — this mapper's output is meant to be spread straight
100	 * into `<ZimmProductCard>` by its page container (SFCC-84's Full History page, not yet built)
101	 * with nothing left to add, the same convenience that shape already gives PLP's own page.
102	 */
103	export type RecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard = ZimmProductCardBaseProps & ZimmProductCardPlpVariation;
104	
105	/** The correctly-sized product image view for the required `primaryImage` slot — same constant,
106	 *  same reasoning, as `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s own `MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE`: never serve an
107	 *  arbitrary-sized image at thumbnail size (AGENTS.md's image-sizing guidance). */
108	const MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE = 'medium';
109	
110	/** The variation-attribute id this mapper reads for size chips — named per conventions.md's
111	 *  no-magic-strings rule. `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `selectSizeChipValues`, which this is
112	 *  ported from, uses the literal inline; named here instead since this is a fresh file. */
113	const SIZE_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID = 'size';
114	
115	/**
116	 * `getPriceData`'s own return shape (base SFCC, `product-utils.js:123-170`, confirmed by reading
117	 * it directly), narrowed to the three fields this mapper reads. `@salesforce/retail-react-app`
118	 * ships no TypeScript types — this subpath falls through `overrides/app/types/vendor.d.ts`'s
119	 * catch-all `declare module '@salesforce/retail-react-app/*'`, a shorthand ambient module
120	 * declaration that types the whole module `any`, so `getPriceData`'s real return is implicitly
121	 * `any`. Declaring a local, narrow type for the fields actually read — rather than letting that
122	 * `any` propagate into this module's own types — matches `variantScopedPrice.ts`'s own
123	 * narrow-local-type pattern for the same untyped function (typescript.md's no-`any` rule). This
124	 * is a type annotation documenting an assumed shape, not a runtime guarantee: TypeScript allows
125	 * assigning `any` to any narrower type with no check, so the real correctness proof is the test
126	 * file's own direct comparison against a real `getPriceData` call, not this annotation alone.
127	 */
128	type SfccPriceData = {
129	  /** `findLowestPrice()`'s own `minPrice` — never `product.price` directly. This is the field
130	   *  `productListCardMapper.ts` does not use for its own `currentPrice` (it reads the flat
131	   *  `hit.price` field instead) — see this module's own docblock for why that risks disagreeing
132	   *  with a `getPriceData`-derived `originalPrice` on a multi-variant product. */
133	  currentPrice: number;
134	  /** The highest tiered price found — "was" price. `undefined` when the product has no
135	   *  `tieredPrices` at all (there is then no maximum to compute). */
136	  listPrice: number | undefined;
137	  /** `currentPrice < listPrice` — always `false`, never `true`, when `listPrice` is `undefined`
138	   *  (a numeric comparison against `undefined` evaluates to `false` in JS, never throws). */
139	  isOnSale: boolean;
140	};
141	
142	/** The real `imageGroups[].images[]` element shape (`commerce-sdk-isomorphic`'s own
143	 *  `ShopperProductsTypes.Image`) — named `RawImage` to match `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own
144	 *  local name for the equivalent concept, but pointed at the real SDK type rather than that
145	 *  file's hand-rolled shape (AGENTS.md > Type Definitions: don't re-declare a type the SDK
146	 *  already exports). */
147	type RawImage = ShopperProductsTypes.Image;
148	
149	const toCardImage = (image: RawImage | undefined, productName: string): ZimmProductCardImage | undefined => {
150	  const src = image?.disBaseLink ?? image?.link;
151	  const alt = image?.alt?.trim() || productName.trim();
152	  if (!src || !alt) return undefined;
153	  return { src, alt };
154	};
155	
156	/**
157	 * Picks the image group with the most images as this product's gallery. Ported near-verbatim from
158	 * `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `selectGalleryImages` — viewpoint-agnostic on purpose, for the
159	 * same reason that file states: this catalog's real `viewType` naming was not confirmed for that
160	 * quick-test integration, so "most images" is used as a simple, real-data-driven proxy for "the
161	 * full gallery" rather than guessing a specific viewType string. Re-pointed at
162	 * `product.imageGroups` (the plain `getProducts` shape) in place of a `ProductSearchHit`'s own
163	 * same-named field — the underlying `ImageGroup`/`Image` types are identical either way, so only
164	 * the input type annotation changed. Returns `undefined` for 0 or 1 resulting images, matching
165	 * `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own "no gallery" contract for that case.
166	 */
167	export const selectGalleryImages = (product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct): ZimmProductCardImage[] | undefined => {
168	  const groups = product.imageGroups ?? [];
169	  if (groups.length === 0) return undefined;
170	
171	  const largest = groups.reduce((best, group) =>
172	    (group.images?.length ?? 0) > (best.images?.length ?? 0) ? group : best,
173	  );
174	  const images = (largest.images ?? [])
175	    .map((image) => toCardImage(image, product.name ?? ''))
176	    .filter((img): img is ZimmProductCardImage => Boolean(img));
177	
178	  return images.length > 1 ? images : undefined;
179	};

181	/**
182	 * Resolves the required `primaryImage` slot. Not ported from `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own
183	 * `toCardImage(hit.image)` — a plain `getProducts` `Product` carries no equivalent flat `image`
184	 * field, that's a Search-hit-only convenience. Mirrors `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s own
185	 * `selectPrimaryImage` instead: `viewType: 'medium'` (a real, correctly-sized product image),
186	 * first matching group, first image, required non-empty `alt` (falls back to the product name) —
187	 * the already-established, correct approach for this exact input shape. `ZimmProductCardMedia`
188	 * ignores `primaryImage` entirely whenever `images` carries more than one entry (confirmed
189	 * directly in that component's own source — `slideImages = gallery ?? [primaryImage]`), so this
190	 * value never conflicts with `selectGalleryImages`'s independent, viewpoint-agnostic pick above
191	 * even on the rare product where the two would otherwise disagree on which image comes first.
192	 *
193	 * **Also returns `fallbacks` (2026-09-08, live defect)** — see `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s own
194	 * `selectPrimaryImage` for the full story (confirmed live against product `4673TS251`: a real
195	 * catalog image group can have a broken image ahead of working ones). Only actually matters for
196	 * a product with no multi-image `selectGalleryImages` result above (0 or 1 images in the `large`
197	 * group) — `ZimmProductCardMedia` ignores `primaryImage`/`primaryImageFallbacks` entirely once a
198	 * real gallery is active, per this file's own docblock two paragraphs up.
199	 *
200	 * @returns `null` when there is no usable `src` — `ZimmProductCardMediaImage.alt` is required and
201	 *   non-empty, so there is no safe placeholder card to build without a real image, the same
202	 *   hard-gate contract `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s own `selectPrimaryImage` documents.
203	 */
204	const selectPrimaryImage = (
205	  product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct,
206	  productName: string,
207	): { image: ZimmProductCardImage; fallbacks: ZimmProductCardImage[] } | null => {
208	  const filteredGroups = filterImageGroups(product.imageGroups ?? [], {
209	    viewType: MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE,
210	    variationValues: {},
211	  }) as ShopperProductsTypes.ImageGroup[];
212	  const groupImages = filteredGroups[0]?.images ?? [];
213	  const [groupImage, ...remainingGroupImages] = groupImages;
214	  if (!groupImage) return null;
215	
216	  const src = groupImage.disBaseLink || groupImage.link;
217	  if (!src) return null;
218	
219	  const alt = groupImage.alt?.trim() || productName;
220	  const fallbacks = remainingGroupImages
221	    .map((fallbackImage) => {
222	      const fallbackSrc = fallbackImage.disBaseLink || fallbackImage.link;
223	      if (!fallbackSrc) return null;
224	      return { src: fallbackSrc, alt: fallbackImage.alt?.trim() || productName };
225	    })
226	    .filter((fallbackImage): fallbackImage is ZimmProductCardImage => Boolean(fallbackImage));
227	
228	  return { image: { src, alt }, fallbacks };
229	};
230	
231	/**
232	 * Reads the "size" variation attribute (if this product has one) into the shape
233	 * `ZimmSizeChipGroup` expects. Ported near-verbatim from `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own
234	 * `selectSizeChipValues`, re-pointed at `product.variationAttributes` directly — `orderable` on
235	 * each value already reflects real stock for that specific size, so it maps directly to
236	 * `isDisabled` with no extra lookup needed.
237	 */
238	export const selectSizeChipValues = (product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct): ZimmSizeChipValue[] => {
239	  const sizeAttribute = product.variationAttributes?.find((attr) => attr.id === SIZE_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID);
240	  return (sizeAttribute?.values ?? []).map((value) => ({
241	    value: value.value,
242	    label: value.name ?? value.value,
243	    isDisabled: value.orderable === false,
244	  }));
245	};
246	
247	/**
248	 * Derives `currentPrice`/`originalPrice` from a single `getPriceData(product)` call — see this
249	 * module's own docblock for why both must come from the same call rather than mixing a flat
250	 * `product.price` field for one and `getPriceData` for the other. No `opts` passed — the default
251	 * `quantity: 1` is correct for a single-unit card display (matches `variantScopedPrice.ts`'s own
252	 * no-opts calls for the same reason). No hardcoded fallback currency — if either the price or the
253	 * currency is absent, formatting is skipped rather than guessed, matching `productInfo.ts`'s and
254	 * `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s own "no hardcoded fallback currency" rule.
255	 */
256	const selectPriceFields = (
257	  product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct,
258	  formatPrice: FormatPrice,
259	): Pick<RecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard, 'currentPrice' | 'originalPrice'> => {
260	  const priceData: SfccPriceData = getPriceData(product);
261	
262	  const currentPrice =
263	    typeof priceData.currentPrice === 'number' && product.currency
264	      ? formatPrice(priceData.currentPrice, product.currency)
265	      : undefined;
266	
267	  // Only set when isOnSale is true -- a not-on-sale product must not render a crossed-out price
268	  // identical to its current one.
269	  const originalPrice =
270	    priceData.isOnSale && typeof priceData.listPrice === 'number' && product.currency
271	      ? formatPrice(priceData.listPrice, product.currency)
272	      : undefined;
273	
274	  return { currentPrice, originalPrice };
275	};
276	
277	/**
278	 * @param product - A plain Commerce API product from `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts`'s own
279	 *   `getProducts` call, or `undefined`/`null` while that data is not yet available.
280	 * @param formatPrice - Currency formatter, normally `intl.formatNumber`.
281	 * @returns Props for the `plp`-variation `ZimmProductCard`, or `null` when the product has no
282	 *   usable name or no usable image — never a broken card, never a throw. Same hard-gate contract
283	 *   as `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s own `selectRecentlyViewedCard`.
284	 */
285	export const selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard = (
286	  product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct | undefined | null,
287	  formatPrice: FormatPrice,
288	): RecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard | null => {
289	  if (!product?.name) return null;
290	
291	  const selectedImage = selectPrimaryImage(product, product.name);
292	  if (!selectedImage) return null;
293	
294	  const { currentPrice, originalPrice } = selectPriceFields(product, formatPrice);
295	
296	  return {
297	    id: product.id,
298	    href: productUrlBuilder({ id: product.id }),
299	    name: product.name,
300	    headingLevel: 'h3',
301	    primaryImage: selectedImage.image,
302	    primaryImageFallbacks: selectedImage.fallbacks,
303	    images: selectGalleryImages(product),
304	    currentPrice,
305	    originalPrice,
306	    // Real, found gap -- see this module's own docblock's "Badge" section. ShopperProductsTypes.
307	    // Product carries no typed c_productBadges field, and there is no confirmation the plain
308	    // getProducts endpoint (as opposed to Product Search) populates this custom, index-only
309	    // attribute at all. Left unset rather than guessed at.
310	    badge: undefined,
311	    variation: 'plp',
312	    sizeChipValues: selectSizeChipValues(product),
313	  };
314	};

1	/**
2	 * The "given IDs, fetch real product data" half of SFCC-83/84's interim Recently Viewed data
3	 * source (build plan §2, "Interim data source" — Einstein is "Not Deployed" on every real
4	 * Zimmermann site, so this build ships against a browser-tracked view-history stand-in instead).
5	 * The companion piece is `useRecentlyViewedHistory`
6	 * (`overrides/app/hooks/useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts`), which supplies the `ids` this hook
7	 * consumes — every product this hook returns is real, live Commerce Cloud data; only the list of
8	 * *which* IDs to fetch is sourced from this browser's own tracked history rather than Einstein.
9	 *
10	 * Wraps `useProducts` (`@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`, confirmed real export at
11	 * `node_modules/@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react/hooks/ShopperProducts/query.js`, re-exported from
12	 * the package root — the same hook already used at
13	 * `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:334`), which calls the Shopper Products
14	 * `getProducts` endpoint. Parameters (`allImages: true`, `perPricebook: true`, `expand: [
15	 * 'prices', 'promotions', 'images', 'variations']`) match the combination already confirmed
16	 * correct three independent times this build (Einstein's own `fetchRecProductDetails`
17	 * — `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-einstein.js:465-505` — the PLP quick-test mapper,
18	 * and the `zimmproductcard-live-demo` branch's real-product search call).
19	 *
20	 * **The 24-ID cap is a real, hard API limit, not a preference.** Confirmed directly in the SDK's
21	 * own doc comment: `node_modules/@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react/hooks/ShopperProducts/query.js:29`
22	 * — *"The maximum number of productIDs that can be requested are 24."* — restated independently
23	 * in `commerce-sdk-isomorphic`'s own type-declaration prose
24	 * (`node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts:58802`: *"hydrate a list of products
25	 * (max 24)"*). Marcel's explicit decision: cap to the first `GET_PRODUCTS_MAX_IDS_PER_REQUEST`
26	 * ids, don't batch into multiple requests — a shopper with more than 24 tracked IDs simply never
27	 * gets the tail of their history fetched by this hook.
28	 *
29	 * **SDK param widening for `ids`.** `getProductsQueryParameters.ids` types as `Array<string>`
30	 * throughout `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` (confirmed at `index.esm.d.ts:57797` and `:58753`), but the
31	 * real, working base SFCC call this build models (`use-einstein.js`'s `fetchRecProductDetails`)
32	 * passes a comma-joined string (`ids.join(',')`) straight through — the SDK forwards it verbatim
33	 * into the query string regardless of the declared array type. This file follows the exact same
34	 * precedent already used elsewhere in this codebase for this exact field:
35	 * `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:339`
36	 * (`ids: childVariantIds.join(',') as unknown as string[]`, commented there as "SDK param
37	 * widening").
38	 */
39	import { useProducts } from '@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react';
40	import type { ShopperProductsTypes } from 'commerce-sdk-isomorphic';
41	
42	/**
43	 * Hard per-request limit on the Shopper Products `getProducts` endpoint — see this file's own
44	 * docblock above for the two independent SDK citations confirming this number. Not a UX/product
45	 * choice, and not adjustable client-side.
46	 */
47	const GET_PRODUCTS_MAX_IDS_PER_REQUEST = 24;
48	
49	export type RecentlyViewedProductFetchResult = {
50	  /**
51	   * Real Shopper Products data for as many of the requested (capped) `ids` as the API actually
52	   * returned, **re-ordered to match `ids`'s own order** — the API's own response order is not
53	   * documented or guaranteed to match request order, so this hook does the re-ordering rather
54	   * than assume it. An id the API didn't return at all (e.g. offline or deleted since it was
55	   * viewed) is silently dropped, not left as a hole in the array.
56	   */
57	  products: readonly ShopperProductsTypes.Product[];
58	  /** `true` only while a real fetch is in flight for a non-empty id list — deliberately `false`,
59	   *  not the underlying query's own (potentially permanently-pending) loading state, when there
60	   *  are no ids to fetch at all, since no request is ever made in that case. */
61	  isLoading: boolean;
62	};
63	
64	/**
65	 * Given a list of product IDs (most-recent-first, per `useRecentlyViewedHistory`), fetches real,
66	 * live Commerce Cloud product data for them.
67	 *
68	 * @param ids - Product IDs to fetch, most-recent-first. A list longer than
69	 *   `GET_PRODUCTS_MAX_IDS_PER_REQUEST` is truncated to the first N (Marcel's cap-don't-batch
70	 *   decision) — the endpoint itself has no way to serve more in a single call.
71	 * @returns `products` — real product data for the requested ids, re-ordered to match `ids` and
72	 *   with any id the API didn't return dropped. `isLoading` — whether a real fetch is in flight.
73	 */
74	export const useRecentlyViewedProductFetch = (ids: readonly string[]): RecentlyViewedProductFetchResult => {
75	  const cappedIds = ids.slice(0, GET_PRODUCTS_MAX_IDS_PER_REQUEST);
76	
77	  const { data, isLoading: queryIsLoading } = useProducts(
78	    {
79	      parameters: {
80	        // SDK param widening -- see this file's own docblock for why a comma-joined string is
81	        // correct here despite the declared `Array<string>` type.
82	        ids: cappedIds.join(',') as unknown as string[],
83	        allImages: true,
84	        perPricebook: true,
85	        expand: ['prices', 'promotions', 'images', 'variations'],
86	      },
87	    },
88	    {
89	      // Matches the existing precedent at product-detail/index.tsx:347 for this same hook: don't
90	      // fire a request at all when there's nothing to ask for.
91	      enabled: cappedIds.length > 0,
92	    },
93	  );
94	
95	  const productsById = new Map((data?.data ?? []).map((product) => [product.id, product] as const));
96	  const products = cappedIds
97	    .map((id) => productsById.get(id))
98	    .filter((product): product is ShopperProductsTypes.Product => product !== undefined);
99	
100	  return {
101	    products,
102	    // A disabled query (no ids) never transitions out of its initial loading state on some
103	    // TanStack Query versions/configurations -- AND against `cappedIds.length > 0` so "loading"
104	    // never lies about a fetch that was never actually started.
105	    isLoading: cappedIds.length > 0 && queryIsLoading,
106	  };
107	};

Same component, same variation — but not identical, and I found one more real gap while comparing the two mappers side by side.

**Yes — literally the same `ZimmProductCard` at `variation: 'plp'`.** Both mappers (`productListCardMapper.ts` for PLP, `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts` for Full History) produce the exact same TypeScript output shape (`ZimmProductCardBaseProps & ZimmProductCardPlpVariation`), and `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts` was deliberately written as a near-verbatim port of PLP's mapper for this reason — same gallery-picking logic, same size-chip logic, same was/now pricing logic, all ported line-for-line.

**But real differences exist, because the two pages read from different SFCC endpoints** (PLP hits Shopper **Search**; Full History hits Shopper **Products** `getProducts`) — not by design intent, just because those endpoints return different data:

1. **Badge never shows on Full History** (already self-documented in the file itself) — `getProducts` has no confirmed badge field the way a Search hit does. Same product, badge on PLP, no badge here.

2. **🔴 `isUnavailable` is never set on Full History at all — this one wasn't flagged anywhere.** PLP's mapper sets `isUnavailable: hit.orderable === false`. I just read `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts`'s full return object line-by-line — there's no `isUnavailable` field in it, period. That flag drives real behavior on `ZimmProductCard`: the whole disabled/dimmed recipe state, and (since this session's Notify-Me change) whether the Notify Me button shows at all. A genuinely out-of-stock product would look and behave as fully available on this page, while the identical product on PLP would show correctly. Individual size chips still correctly show per-size disabled state (that part *is* wired via `sizeChipValues[].isDisabled`) — it's specifically the card-level unavailability that's missing.

3. **Add to Bag does nothing** (found last turn) — button renders, click has no handler.

4. **Size chips aren't selectable** (found last turn) — chips render with correct per-size availability, but there's no state/handler to select one.

5. **No size-aware variant resolution exists for this page at all.** PLP's mapper exports `resolveOrderableVariant` (resolves a selected size to its real SKU/price). `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts` has no equivalent — so fixing #3/#4 isn't just "wire up the same handler PLP uses," that resolution logic would need building here too. The raw data may well be there already (`recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts` does request `expand: ['variations']`), just nothing reads it yet.

Everything else — price (was/now via `getPriceData`), gallery images, size-chip disabled states, the image-fallback cascade — is genuinely identical logic between the two, verified directly, not just assumed from the port.

So: same card, same look, but three real behavioral gaps (badge, unavailability, and the two interactive pieces) between what a shopper sees on PLP versus what they'd see for the identical product on Full History.

51	  // textTransform: 'uppercase') — `linkSm` was corrected to `textTransform: 'uppercase'` to

61	/**
62	 * `ZimmProductName`'s own heading-level prop, read off the atom's real signature via a utility
63	 * type rather than a hand-typed duplicate union (typescript.md: "prefer utility types over
64	 * hand-rolled duplicate shapes... a hand-copied type silently drifts from its source when the
65	 * original changes"). Its type param is `'h1' | 'h2' | 'h3'` — note this is NOT `'h2' | 'h3' |
66	 * 'h4'` as an earlier sketch of this component's contract assumed; see `headingLevel` below.

70	export type ZimmProductCardContentProps = {
71	  /** The product's display name, rendered as the card's heading and link text. */
72	  name: string;
73	  /**
74	   * Heading level for the composed `ZimmProductName`, forwarded to it as `as`. Named
75	   * `headingLevel` here (rather than `as`) because this component is not itself polymorphic —
76	   * it always renders the same fixed element tree, it just hands the one real heading a level.
77	   * Typed as `ZimmProductNameHeadingLevel` (`'h1' | 'h2' | 'h3'`) to exactly match what that atom
78	   * actually accepts — a prior sketch of this contract assumed `'h2' | 'h3' | 'h4'`, which is

92	  originalPrice?: string;
93	  /** Passed straight through to `ZimmProductPrice`'s own `isLoading`. */
94	  isPriceLoading?: boolean;
95	
96	  /**
97	   * Wishlist-only attributes line (colour + size as plain text), per the organism's
98	   * VARIATION_CONFIG (Step 6, not built yet) — this component only ever sees the resolved
99	   * boolean, never a variation name. When false the row is absent from the DOM entirely, not
100	   * merely visually hidden.
101	   */
102	  showAttributes: boolean;
103	  /**
104	   * Rendered only when `showAttributes` is true. Pass the plain colour value ("Ivory", not
105	   * "Ivory,") — the component itself appends the trailing comma when rendering, matching
106	   * Figma's own text-node structure (confirmed via get_design_context on node 40002187:58446:
107	   * the colour text node's own content literally includes the trailing comma, e.g. "Lilac
108	   * Sand,", not a separate punctuation node). See the `colourWithComma` derivation below.
109	   */
110	  colour?: string;
111	  /** Rendered only when `showAttributes` is true. */
112	  size?: string;

141	 * Molecule — the product-card text-content block: heading/link, bag action, wishlist-only
142	 * colour/size attributes, price, PLP-only size-chip picker, and an out-of-stock notify-me CTA.
143	 * Figma "Card-content" component set, node 40002109:26908 (Desktop 40002109:26906 / Mobile
144	 * 40002163:37103).
145	 *
146	 * Deliberately has NO remove/close button — that action lives entirely in
147	 * `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `close` overlay (Step 4), positioned on the image, not here.
148	 *
149	 * Also deliberately has no badge slot, despite the SFCC-236 AC mentioning one for PLP/Wishlist.
150	 * An earlier revision of this paragraph claimed no Figma design existed for it at all — that
151	 * was wrong: the badge (Figma "Tag") does exist, confirmed present and identical across every
152	 * Size/Type variant checked. It just lives inside "Image Group", which is
153	 * `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s domain, not this component's — so it was built there instead. See
154	 * that component's own docblock for the confirmed spec, and the organism's own docblock
155	 * ("Badge" note) for which variations actually show it.
156	 *
157	 * Composes `ZimmProductPrice` with `isLive={false}` unconditionally — this is the entire reason
158	 * that prop exists (SFCC-236 Step 3): a grid of these on a PLP must not mount dozens of
159	 * `aria-live` regions whose price never changes post-mount.
160	 */
161	export const ZimmProductCardContent = ({
162	  name,
163	  headingLevel,
164	  href,
165	  currentPrice,
166	  originalPrice,
167	  isPriceLoading,
168	  showAttributes,
169	  colour,
170	  size,
171	  showBag,
172	  isUnavailable,
173	  onAddToBag,
174	  showSizeChips,
175	  sizeChipValues,
176	  selectedSizeChipValue,
177	  onSizeChipSelect,
178	  showNotifyMe,
179	  onNotifyMe,
180	}: ZimmProductCardContentProps) => {
181	  const intl = useIntl();
182	  // `disabled`, not `isUnavailable` — matches `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s own `DEFAULT_STYLE_PROPS`
183	  // key so that guard's exhaustive prop-combination walk actually exercises both the true and
184	  // false branch of `bagButton`'s disabled styling (see zimmProductCardContent.css.ts's own
185	  // comment, and `zimmSizeChip.css.ts`'s identical `disabled` naming for the same reason).
186	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_PRODUCT_CARD_CONTENT_RECIPE, { disabled: isUnavailable });
187	
188	  // Was `showNotifyMe && Boolean(onNotifyMe)` — changed 2026-09-08, Marcel's explicit decision.
189	  // The real Notify Me feature (PRD-018–021: a slide-out form submitting to a back-in-stock
190	  // capture target) doesn't exist anywhere in this codebase yet, including on PDP where this
191	  // same prop concept already exists unused — building it is its own future story, not this
192	  // change. Until then, the button ships visible and genuinely inert: `onClick={onNotifyMe}`
193	  // below is a plain prop reference, and `onNotifyMe` stays optional on this component's own
194	  // props — React treats an `undefined` event handler as "no handler attached" (not an error),
195	  // so a click with none supplied safely does nothing.
196	  const showNotifyMeButton = showNotifyMe;
197	
198	  // Figma renders the colour/size attributes line as ONE continuous phrase, not two independent
199	  // labels: the comma is baked into the colour text node's own content ("Lilac Sand,"), not a
200	  // separate punctuation element — confirmed via get_design_context on node 40002187:58446 (the
201	  // real Wishlist Card-content instance). Reproduced the same way here, on the colour value's own
202	  // rendered string (never as a static comma JSX node between the two spans), paired with
203	  // attributesRow's 2px gap (zimmProductCardContent.css.ts) for the "Ivory, M" breathing room —
204	  // verified by rendering the real Futura Round Medium caption style at actual size: the glyph
205	  // ink-to-ink gap the 2px flex gap produces here reads as a genuine (if slightly tighter than
206	  // full-prose) space, not as "Ivory,M" touching. Guarded against `colour` being falsy so a
207	  // caller omitting it (a contract violation, but not this component's job to enforce) still
208	  // renders nothing, rather than the literal string "undefined,".
209	  const colourWithComma = colour ? `${colour},` : colour;
210	
211	  return (
212	    <chakra.div __css={styles.root} data-card-slot={CARD_SLOT.content}>
213	      <chakra.div __css={styles.nameRow}>
214	        <ProductNameLink to={href} __css={styles.nameLink}>
215	          <ZimmProductName name={name} as={headingLevel} />
216	        </ProductNameLink>
217	
218	        {showBag && (
219	          <chakra.div __css={styles.bagWrapper} data-card-slot={CARD_SLOT.bag}>
220	            <chakra.button
221	              type="button"
222	              __css={styles.bagButton}
223	              aria-label={intl.formatMessage(messages.addToBag)}
224	              disabled={isUnavailable}
225	              onClick={() => {
226	                // Belt-and-braces: the native `disabled` attribute already prevents the browser
227	                // from ever dispatching this click, but stating the invariant explicitly means a
228	                // reader doesn't have to recall that fact to trust onAddToBag can't fire while
229	                // unavailable. Same idiom as ZimmSizeChip's own onClick guard.
230	                if (isUnavailable) return;
231	                onAddToBag?.();
232	              }}
233	            >
234	              <ZimmIcon type="bag" aria-hidden />
235	            </chakra.button>
236	          </chakra.div>
237	        )}
238	      </chakra.div>
239	
240	      {showAttributes && (
241	        <chakra.div __css={styles.attributesRow} data-testid="card-content-attributes">
242	          <chakra.span __css={styles.colourText}>{colourWithComma}</chakra.span>
243	          <chakra.span __css={styles.sizeText}>{size}</chakra.span>
244	        </chakra.div>
245	      )}
246	
247	      <chakra.div __css={styles.priceWrapper} data-card-slot={CARD_SLOT.price}>
248	        <ZimmProductPrice
249	          currentPrice={currentPrice}
250	          originalPrice={originalPrice}
251	          isLoading={isPriceLoading}
252	          isLive={false}
253	        />
254	      </chakra.div>
255	
256	      {showSizeChips && (
257	        <chakra.div __css={styles.sizeChipWrapper} data-card-slot={CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}>
258	          <ZimmSizeChipGroup
259	            values={sizeChipValues ?? []}
260	            selectedValue={selectedSizeChipValue}
261	            onSelect={onSizeChipSelect}
262	          />
263	        </chakra.div>
264	      )}
265	
266	      {showNotifyMeButton && (
267	        <chakra.button
268	          type="button"
269	          __css={styles.notifyMeButton}
270	          onClick={onNotifyMe}
271	          data-card-slot={CARD_SLOT.notifyMe}
272	        >
273	          {intl.formatMessage(messages.notifyMe)}
274	        </chakra.button>
275	      )}
276	    </chakra.div>
277	  );
278	};
279	
280	export default ZimmProductCardContent;

281	 *          reveal pair. This is NOT the same case as `sizeSelectorUnavailable`'s permanent hide or
282	 *          `hideBagOnMobile`'s mobile hide elsewhere in the style object below — neither of THOSE
283	 *          has any `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)` reveal counterpart anywhere in this file at
284	 *          all, so there is no paired rule for either of them to silently dead-code, and both stay
285	 *          exactly as `display: 'none'`/`'flex'`, unconverted, on purpose: separate, correct,
286	 *          Figma-confirmed, non-regressed decisions, not part of the defect this fix addresses.
287	 *
288	 *      **Belt-and-braces addition (carousel only):** `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s `carousel`
289	 *      part sets `pointerEvents: 'none'` on the wrapper, with `arrowButton` individually
290	 *      re-enabling `pointerEvents: 'auto'` (so a click in the empty centre of the band passes
291	 *      through to the image beneath). While the wrapper was `display: 'none'` by default, that
292	 *      per-button override was harmless — `display: none` removes the entire subtree from
293	 *      hit-testing regardless of any descendant's own `pointerEvents`. Now that the wrapper's
294	 *      hidden state is expressed via `clipPath` instead, its arrow buttons are no longer
295	 *      unconditionally un-hittable purely by virtue of the wrapper being hidden, so this recipe
296	 *      adds an explicit `[data-card-slot="carousel"] button` rule below: `pointerEvents: 'none'`
297	 *      by default (unconditional, alongside the other unconditional lift rules in point 2 above),
298	 *      `'auto'` again only inside the same two revealed selectors — rather than relying on
299	 *      `clipPath`'s own hit-testing suppression alone. Price/the size-selector/notify-me need no
300	 *      equivalent: none of them sets `pointerEvents` anywhere in this file or in
301	 *      `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`.
302	 *
303	 * Parts: only `root` is declared. Everything above is a nested descendant selector inside
304	 * `root`'s own style object (targeting the composed children's `data-card-slot` attributes), not
305	 * a separate Chakra part — `index.tsx` never reads anything off `useMultiStyleConfig` but
306	 * `styles.root`, so `recipeParts.test.ts`'s declared-vs-read reconciliation needs nothing more.
307	 *
308	 * `zIndex: 1` below is this file's one deliberately unnamed magic number — accepted per
309	 * .claude/rules/conventions.md's own exception ("0, 1, -1 in obvious idiomatic uses"): it is the
310	 * standard "one level above the default/auto stacking layer" value, used identically at each of
311	 * the four lift points, and the stretched-link overlay is deliberately left with no z-index of
312	 * its own rather than pinned to a specific lower number — so the two sides only ever need to be
313	 * *some* value vs a *higher* one, never a specific pair.
314	 */
315	export const ZimmProductCard = {
316	  parts: ['root'],
317	
318	  baseStyle: ({
319	    hoverHidesPrice,
320	    hoverRevealsPrice,
321	    hoverRevealsSizeSelector,
322	    hoverRevealsNotifyMe,
323	    sizeSelectorUnavailable,
324	    hideBagOnMobile,
325	  }: ZimmProductCardStyleProps): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => ({
326	    root: {
327	      position: 'relative',
328	      width: '100%',
329	
330	      // 1. Stretched-link overlay — see docblock point 1. Deliberately no z-index of its own
331	      // (stays at the default/auto stacking layer), so every control lifted in point 2 below
332	      // reliably paints above it regardless of DOM order.
333	      [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] a::after`]: {
334	        content: '""',
335	        position: 'absolute',
336	        inset: 0,
337	      },
338	
339	      // 2. Every genuinely-interactive control sits above the stretched overlay. A plain `button`
340	      // type-selector under the relevant data-card-slot root reaches every control uniformly —
341	      // none of them declare their own data-card-slot, and none needs one: Content's bag button,
342	      // its notify-me button, and every ZimmSizeChip button nested inside its own sizeChips
343	      // wrapper are all real <button> descendants of [data-card-slot="content"].
344	      // Fix 1 (Scorer rework round 1): NO position value here. ZimmProductCardMedia's own
345	      // `close` recipe part already sets `position: 'absolute', top: 0, right: 0` on this exact
346	      // element (that's how the remove button pins to the image's top-right corner). This rule's
347	      // `.css-root [data-card-slot="close"]` descendant+attribute selector has HIGHER
348	      // specificity than Media's own single-class rule, so a competing `position` value declared
349	      // here would win the cascade and knock the button out of its pinned position into normal
350	      // flow — which is exactly what shipped here before this fix. The element is already
351	      // positioned (by Media's own recipe), which is all `zIndex` needs to take effect; no
352	      // `position` re-declaration was ever necessary. See index.test.tsx's "Fix 1" describe
353	      // blocks for the object-shape and real-DOM/getComputedStyle proof.
354	      [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.close}"]`]: {
355	        zIndex: 1,
356	      },
357	      // Fix 3 — zIndex only, on the carousel WRAPPER, not on each arrow `button` inside it. See
358	      // docblock point 2 above for why lifting the buttons individually left them unclickable in

360	      // zIndex) despite passing every jsdom test.
361	      [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
362	        zIndex: 1,
363	      },
364	      // Fix J — belt-and-braces (see docblock point 6's own Fix J note): the carousel wrapper's
365	      // arrow buttons carry their own `pointerEvents: 'auto'` unconditionally
366	      // (`zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s own `arrowButton` part) — harmless while the wrapper was
367	      // `display: 'none'` by default (that alone removed the whole subtree from hit-testing), but
368	      // no longer guaranteed once the wrapper's hidden state is `clipPath`-based instead (below,
369	      // and in `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s own `carousel` part). Re-enabled only inside the
370	      // same two revealed selectors, alongside the existing carousel reveal further below.
371	      [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"] button`]: {
372	        pointerEvents: 'none',
373	      },
374	      [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] button`]: {
375	        position: 'relative',
376	        zIndex: 1,
377	      },
378	      // Fix I — the media/gallery scroll region itself, lifted the same way `close`/`carousel`
379	      // already are (docblock point 2's new bullet has the full narrative). `zIndex` is all
380	      // that's needed: ZimmProductCardMedia's own root recipe already sets `position: 'relative'`.
381	      // `cursor: 'pointer'` is added alongside it — this element is no longer inside the overlay
382	      // `<a>` that used to convey that affordance via the browser's default link cursor, and
383	      // index.tsx's own new `onClick` (see that file's docblock) makes it genuinely clickable
384	      // again.
385	      [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.media}"]`]: {
386	        zIndex: 1,
387	        cursor: 'pointer',
388	      },
389	
390	      // 3. Hover-reveal swap — see docblock point 3. The unconditional (outside-media-query)
391	      // half of each flag below is what makes a touch/no-hover pointer see the *default* state
392	      // permanently: it never matches HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY at all, so whichever rule fired outside
393	      // it (or the total absence of one) is the only state that pointer type ever sees.
394	      //
395	      // `hoverRevealsPrice` (Home) is deliberately NOT here, unlike `hoverRevealsSizeSelector`
396	      // below it — see Fix E in the [HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY] block: Home's price must stay visible
397	      // unconditionally on a touch pointer, the opposite of what an unconditional hide here would
398	      // do.
399	      ...(hoverRevealsSizeSelector && {
400	        // PLP/Wishlist: size-selector starts hidden at every breakpoint/pointer type. Fix K
401	        // (CodeRabbit finding on PR #85, verified correct before fixing): Fix J converted this to
402	        // `position`/`clipPath` alongside its reveal pair, but this rule is UNCONDITIONAL — unlike
403	        // the other four Fix J sites, whose hidden state only ever applies while a hover-capable
404	        // pointer hasn't revealed the content YET (a state every such pointer can escape), this
405	        // one also applies on a pointer type that can NEVER escape it: `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` never
406	        // matches touch, so there is no reveal path on that pointer type at all (the original,
407	        // Figma-confirmed design — PLP/Wishlist's size picker is a hover-capable-only affordance).
408	        // Keeping this clip-path'd on touch, as Fix J shipped it, left a real `<button>` (each
409	        // `ZimmSizeChip`'s own roving tabindex) permanently in the tab order with no way for that
410	        // pointer type to ever reveal it — reachable by Tab (e.g. a tablet with an external
411	        // keyboard) but invisible and inert forever. Reverted to `display: 'none'` here — the
412	        // hover-capable override, where a reveal genuinely is possible, lives inside
413	        // [HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY] below instead (see that block's own Fix K note).
414	        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: {
415	          display: 'none',
416	        },
417	      }),
418	      // Fix C — see docblock point 4. Unconditional and permanent, on every device: an
419	      // out-of-stock item never gets the size-selector, in any state, so this is the only rule
420	      // for it at all when `sizeSelectorUnavailable` is true (no corresponding reveal exists
421	      // anywhere, inside or outside the media query below). Not part of Fix J's conversion — see
422	      // docblock point 6's own note: this has no reveal counterpart to dead-code, so it correctly
423	      // stays `display: 'none'`.
424	      ...(sizeSelectorUnavailable && {
425	        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: { display: 'none' },
426	        // Fix F (full-sweep follow-up audit): mobile-only price hide. Figma's Mobile PLP/Wishlist
427	        // Unavailable references hide price and show notify-me in its place — a genuine swap,
428	        // unlike Desktop's own additive treatment (price stays, notify-me is simply added on
429	        // hover, handled by hoverRevealsNotifyMe below). Hidden by default (mobile-first, matching
430	        // this file's own hideBagOnMobile direction); the DESKTOP_QUERY reveal lives in the single
431	        // shared [DESKTOP_QUERY] block below, NOT a second one here — see that block's own comment
432	        // for why a second `[DESKTOP_QUERY]` object key at this level would silently clobber it.
433	        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: { display: 'none' },
434	      }),
435	
436	      [HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]: {
437	        ...(hoverRevealsPrice && {
438	          // Fix E (full-sweep follow-up audit): the "hidden by default" half moved IN HERE from
439	          // the unconditional block above, where it used to live — Home's Mobile reference
440	          // (40000223:2821) shows price plainly, and Mobile has no Hover variant at all to ever
441	          // reveal a price hidden unconditionally like the original shape did. Confirmed live as
442	          // a real, shipped bug (the Home story showed no price whatsoever at mobile widths), not
443	          // just a Figma reading. Same shape Fix C already established for notify-me, applied
444	          // here for the same underlying reason: a touch pointer must never see this half at all.
445	          // Fix J: was `display: 'none'` — this is the paired hidden state for the two reveal
446	          // rules immediately below and converts along with them (see docblock point 6's own Fix

448	          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {
449	            position: 'absolute',
450	            clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
451	          },
452	          // ...and is only revealed here, once a hover-capable pointer actually hovers the card.
453	          [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {
454	            position: 'static',
455	            clipPath: 'none',
456	          },
457	          // Fix 2 (Scorer rework round 1): `display: none` removes an element from the tab
458	          // order entirely, so a keyboard-only user on a hover-capable device (tabbing, not
459	          // hovering) could never reveal this via `:hover` alone. Originally `:focus-within` on
460	          // this same root — scoped here, not on the price/size-chip wrapper itself, so that
461	          // focus landing on ANY descendant control (name link, bag button, size chip) triggers
462	          // the reveal — mirroring zimmSearchInput.css.ts's container/zimmFormRow's own
463	          // `_focusWithin` sibling to `_hover`.
464	          // Fix H (live-browser check after the arrow reveal shipped): plain `:focus-within`

469	          // stuck open, until focus moved elsewhere entirely (e.g. a click outside the card) —
470	          // moving the mouse back out was not enough. `:has(:focus-visible)` fixes this: it only
471	          // matches when the browser's own focus-visible heuristic says a *keyboard* focus ring

473	          // engine but still matches genuine Tab navigation — so the keyboard case Fix 2 exists
474	          // for keeps working, and the mouse-click case that produced the stuck-open bug does

476	          // this project's own browserslist (`iOS >= 17`, `Android >= 14`, `last 4 ChromeAndroid
477	          // versions`), all far past `:has()`'s 2022/2023 shipping baseline. Expressed as a
478	          // separate string key (not a comma-joined `'&:hover, &:has(:focus-visible) ...'`
479	          // selector) to match this file's own established idiom; raw selector strings are used
480	          // throughout rather than a Chakra shorthand prop because the descendant-combinator
481	          // path has to be baked into the selector itself, and Chakra has no `:has()` shorthand.
482	          // Fix J: was `display: 'block'` — converted alongside the `&:hover` entry above; see
483	          // docblock point 3/6 for why `display` no longer expresses this at all.
484	          [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {
485	            position: 'static',
486	            clipPath: 'none',
487	          },
488	        }),
489	        ...(hoverHidesPrice && {
490	          // PLP/Wishlist: price is visible by default (no unconditional rule needed above) and
491	          // hides only here, in favour of the size-selector reveal alongside it. Fix J: both
492	          // entries below were `display: 'none'` — see docblock point 3/6.
493	          [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {
494	            position: 'absolute',
495	            clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
496	          },
497	          // Fix 2 / Fix H — see the hoverRevealsPrice block above for the full rationale.
498	          // Keyboard focus anywhere in the card must hide price in favour of the size-selector
499	          // exactly as hover does, so a keyboard user sees the identical revealed state, not a
500	          // different partial one; `:has(:focus-visible)` keeps that true while no longer
501	          // sticking open after a mouse click.
502	          [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {
503	            position: 'absolute',
504	            clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
505	          },
506	        }),
507	        ...(hoverRevealsSizeSelector && {
508	          // Fix K (see the unconditional block above for the full narrative): a hover-capable
509	          // pointer overrides the `display: 'none'` above with the Fix J clip-path technique —
510	          // this pointer type genuinely CAN reveal the content below, so it needs to stay in the
511	          // DOM/tab order while merely not-yet-revealed, for the same VoiceOver/AT reason Fix J
512	          // exists at all. `display: 'flex'` matches ZimmSizeChipGroup's own natural root display
513	          // (zimmSizeChipGroup.css.ts's `radiogroup`/`oneSize` parts) — `position`/`clipPath` are
514	          // the only properties the reveal pair below needs to toggle.
515	          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: {
516	            display: 'flex',
517	            position: 'absolute',
518	            clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
519	          },
520	          // ...and is only revealed here, matching the price swap alongside it. Fix J: both
521	          // entries below were `display: 'block'` — see docblock point 3/6.
522	          [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: {
523	            position: 'static',
524	            clipPath: 'none',
525	          },
526	          // Fix 2 / Fix H — see the hoverRevealsPrice block above for the full rationale.
527	          [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: {
528	            position: 'static',
529	            clipPath: 'none',
530	          },
531	        }),
532	        // Fix C — see docblock point 4. Both the "hidden by default" declaration AND its reveal
533	        // live inside this same media-query block (unlike price/the size-selector above, whose
534	        // "hidden by default" half is unconditional): a touch pointer never matches this query at
535	        // all, so it never sees the hidden rule below either, leaving notify-me at its natural
536	        // (visible) default — exactly the unconditional visibility every Mobile Unavailable
537	        // reference confirms. Fix J: all three declarations below were `display: 'none'`/
538	        // `'block'` — converted together, same reasoning as the price/size-selector pair above.
539	        ...(hoverRevealsNotifyMe && {
540	          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.notifyMe}"]`]: {
541	            position: 'absolute',
542	            clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
543	          },
544	          [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.notifyMe}"]`]: {
545	            position: 'static',
546	            clipPath: 'none',
547	          },
548	          // Fix 2 / Fix H — see the hoverRevealsPrice block above for the full rationale.
549	          [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.notifyMe}"]`]: {
550	            position: 'static',
551	            clipPath: 'none',
552	          },
553	        }),
554	
555	        // 6. Carousel arrow reveal — see docblock point 6. Unconditional (no
