567	        // See docblock point 6's own Fix J note for why: this part needs `display: flex` for its
568	        // own `justifyContent`/`alignItems` layout, and nothing else asserts that once
569	        // `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s own unconditional `display: 'none'` is replaced by
570	        // `clipPath`. `position` is deliberately absent from both entries below, also unlike the
571	        // other four sites: this part is `position: 'absolute'` unconditionally already (Media's
572	        // own vertical-centring rule), and toggling it to `'static'` here would break that
573	        // centring the instant the arrows are revealed.
574	        //
575	        // Fix K (CodeRabbit finding on PR #85, verified correct before fixing): a hover-capable
576	        // pointer needs its OWN not-yet-revealed base state here — `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s
577	        // own `carousel` part reverted to an unconditional `display: 'none'` (Fix K there), which a
578	        // hover-capable pointer must override to `flex`/clipped before `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)`
579	        // below can reveal it at all; without this, the arrows never render even on desktop. Touch
580	        // pointers never enter this media query, so they correctly keep the unconditional
581	        // `display: 'none'` and never become tab stops for a control they can never reveal.
582	        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
583	          display: 'flex',
584	          clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
585	        },
586	        [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
587	          display: 'flex',
588	          clipPath: 'none',
589	        },
590	        // Fix J belt-and-braces (see docblock point 6 and the new lift-adjacent rule in point 2
591	        // above): re-enables the arrow buttons' hit-testing only once genuinely revealed.
592	        [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"] button`]: {
593	          pointerEvents: 'auto',
594	        },
595	        [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
596	          display: 'flex',
597	          clipPath: 'none',
598	        },
599	        [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"] button`]: {
600	          pointerEvents: 'auto',
601	        },
602	      },
603	
604	      // 5. PLP-only bag-icon mobile hide — see docblock point 5. A separate, sibling media-query
605	      // key from HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY above (a viewport-width gate, not a pointer-capability one).
606	      // Mobile-first: hidden by default, shown again from the shared [DESKTOP_QUERY] block below.
607	      ...(hideBagOnMobile && {
608	        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.bag}"]`]: { display: 'none' },
609	      }),
610	
611	      // Fix F+D's shared desktop-reveal block — deliberately ONE `[DESKTOP_QUERY]` object key,
612	      // not two. A first version of this recipe gave `sizeSelectorUnavailable` and
613	      // `hideBagOnMobile` each their OWN separate `...(condition && { [DESKTOP_QUERY]: {...} })`
614	      // spread (mirroring how every other flag in this file gets its own independent spread) —
615	      // which silently broke, because both spreads produce a property with the exact same
616	      // *computed key string* (`'@media (min-width: 48em)'`) on the same `root` object. Object
617	      // spread is a SHALLOW merge: it does not deep-merge two spreads that happen to share a key,
618	      // it just lets whichever spread comes LAST overwrite the earlier one's value entirely. With
619	      // `hideBagOnMobile`'s spread positioned after `sizeSelectorUnavailable`'s in this file, its
620	      // `[DESKTOP_QUERY]` object silently replaced the other's, and the price-reveal-on-desktop
621	      // rule vanished from the actual emitted CSS — confirmed for real via
622	      // `document.styleSheets` in a live browser (price stayed `display: none` at 1280px width
623	      // despite `window.matchMedia('(min-width: 48em)').matches` correctly reporting `true`);
624	      // every jsdom test still passed, because each one only ever sets ONE of the two colliding
625	      // flags at a time, never the realistic combination a genuine unavailable PLP card produces.
626	      // `[HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]` above never had this problem because it was always written as a
627	      // single key with every contributing condition spread INSIDE it — this block now follows
628	      // that same shape.
629	      [DESKTOP_QUERY]: {
630	        ...(sizeSelectorUnavailable && {
631	          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: { display: 'block' },
632	        }),
633	        ...(hideBagOnMobile && {
634	          // 'flex', not 'block': ZimmProductCardContent's own `bagWrapper` part sets
635	          // `display: 'flex'` (it centres the icon inside via alignItems/justifyContent) — this
636	          // organism's `[data-card-slot="content"] [data-card-slot="bag"]` selector has higher
637	          // specificity (a class + two attribute selectors vs. Content's own single class) and
638	          // would win the cascade either way, so restoring the actual display type Content uses
639	          // matters here, not just "anything visible" — 'block' would silently flatten that
640	          // wrapper's centering.
641	          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.bag}"]`]: { display: 'flex' },
642	        }),
643	      },
644	    },
645	  }),
646	};

import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';
import { CARD_SLOT, HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY, DESKTOP_QUERY } from '../../zimmProductCardShared';

/**
 * Same hover-capable-pointer gate `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts` already establishes for its own
 * arrows/indicator split — now a shared import from `zimmProductCardShared.ts` rather than each
 * file's own module-private copy, so the two can't silently drift. Governs the price <->
 * size-selector swap below, so both composed children's hover treatments engage together off the
 * exact same media feature, on this shared root.
 */

/**
 * A viewport-width gate, unrelated to `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` above — governs the PLP-only bag-icon
 * mobile hide (Fix D, SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit) below. Also a shared import from

          // wrapper's centering.
          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.bag}"]`]: { display: 'flex' },

      },
    },
  }),

Traced through the actual recipe CSS (`zimmProductCard.css.ts`) and the organism's own flag derivation — this one's fully built and Figma-confirmed already, not a gap. Here's exactly what shows, for an out-of-stock PLP card on Desktop:

**Default state (before you hover):**
- Product name
- Price — stays visible (out-of-stock gets an "additive" treatment on Desktop, not a swap)
- Bag icon — visible, but disabled/greyed out, cursor `not-allowed`
- Size chips — **never shown**, in any state, on any device, once a product is unavailable (`sizeSelectorUnavailable`'s own unconditional hide — there's nothing to pick a size *for* when nothing's in stock)

**On hover, the one thing that changes:**
- **"Notify me" appears** — it's hidden by default and only reveals once you actually hover (or keyboard-focus) the card. Everything else above stays exactly as it was — price doesn't hide, the bag icon doesn't change.

So to answer directly: **product name + price + a disabled bag icon are already showing before you even hover — hovering only adds "Notify me."** No size-selector swap happens at all for an out-of-stock item (that's reserved for an available product, which swaps price → size chips on hover instead).

This is all deliberate and already fixed correctly — it went through several named fix rounds (Fix C, F, G, J, K) each tied to a specific Figma reference (Desktop/Hover/Unavailable node `40002163:41468`), including catching and fixing a real accessibility regression along the way (`display: none` removing these from the tab order, since replaced with a `position`/`clipPath` technique that keeps them keyboard-reachable). Unlike the hover-image-swap gap from a couple turns ago, this one isn't something we need to add — it's solid.

| Size chips | `sizeSelectorUnavailable` hides it unconditionally — no `[DESKTOP_QUERY]` override exists for this one | **Never shown, in any state** |

| Notify Me | `hoverRevealsNotifyMe: true` → hidden by default (`clipPath: inset(50%)`) inside `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`, revealed only on `&:hover`/`&:has(:focus-visible)` | **Hidden until hover, then appears** |

So yes — exactly as stated: **name + price + a disabled bag icon are already on screen before you even touch the card; hovering adds only "Notify me."** Nothing else moves. That's what's actually configured right now, not just what should be — traced from the real derivation logic, not assumed from the CSS alone.

content.text:
Not quite — there are two, not one. Both are image-related and both come from the same root cause (PLP's mapper doesn't supply certain image fields), but they're functionally different gaps:

1. **Hover-to-model-image swap** (the one you just named) — `hoverImage` is never populated by `productListCardMapper.ts`, so `swapOnHover` always evaluates `false` regardless of the `showHoverImageSwap: true` config.

2. **Broken-image fallback cascade** (found a few turns earlier, before the hover-swap one) — `primaryImageFallbacks` was built and wired into the Rail's and Full History's own mappers, but never into PLP's. Same underlying defect we found live on `4673TS251` (a 404'd image sitting ahead of working ones) is still unprotected on PLP specifically.

Both trace back to the exact same file never being updated — `productListCardMapper.ts` — just for two different props (`hoverImage` vs `primaryImageFallbacks`). Everything else we checked for PLP (size-chip disabled state, size-aware Add to Bag, Notify Me, was/now pricing, badge, `isUnavailable`, the whole hover-reveal state machine) is confirmed correctly wired and shipped.

So: two open items on PLP's product card, both in the same mapper file, not just the hover swap alone.

content.text:
Both confirmed, with hard evidence. Here's each.

## 1. Hover-image-swap — the demo branch's approach

`overrides/app/pages/home/liveProductCardDemoMapper.ts` on `feature/zimmproductcard-live-demo` (read directly via `git show`, without switching branches):

```ts
const groups = filterImageGroups(hit.imageGroups ?? [], {
  viewType: 'medium',
  variationValues: variant.colourCode ? { color: variant.colourCode } : {},
});
const groupImages = groups?.[0]?.images ?? [];

primaryImage: groupImages[0] ? toCardImage(groupImages[0]) : ...,
hoverImage: groupImages[1] ? toCardImage(groupImages[1]) : undefined,
images: groupImages.length > 1 ? groupImages.map(toCardImage) : undefined,
```

**The approach is purely positional, not semantic.** `hoverImage` isn't resolved via any special "model shot" viewType or tag — it's just **the second image (index 1) in the same medium-viewType image group** that also supplies `primaryImage` (index 0) and the full gallery. One filtered array feeds all three.

One real difference from PLP's current mapper, worth flagging before porting this: the demo scopes that filter to the **resolved variant's own colour** (`variationValues: {color: ...}`) — PLP's own `selectGalleryImages` today picks "whichever image group has the most images," with no viewType or colour filter at all. So porting this exact approach isn't just "add one field" — it'd also mean aligning PLP's image-group selection to be colour/viewType-aware the way the demo's is.

## 2. Why PLP renders 4673TS251 fine but the Rail doesn't

Pulled the live SSR JSON properly (parsed `#mobify-data`'s actual JSON, not a text-window grep — my first attempt at this literally bled into a neighboring product's data and gave a wrong answer, caught and redone correctly) and compared the two fields side by side:

| Source | Field read | Filename |
|---|---|---|
| **PLP** (`hit.image`, flat Search-hit field) | image index **9** | `9.4673ts251.gvscp.guava-seascape.jpg` |
| **Rail/Full-History** (`imageGroups.medium[0]`) | image index **1** | `1.4673ts251.gvscp.guava-seascape.jpg` |

**They're different images, from two different fields entirely** — and index 1 of the medium group is the specific one already confirmed broken. Real, important gap in the demo's own approach — worth flagging directly: **the demo branch didn't actually solve this.** Its own hand-rolled type (`LiveDemoSourceHit`) has no `representedProduct` field at all, and its `resolveDemoVariant` just picks "first orderable variant, or variants[0]" — an arbitrary pick, not anything SFCC marked as default. So copying that approach as-is wouldn't answer your question; it would just grab *some* variant, not necessarily the one SFCC treats as representative.

**Is there a real SFCC "default variant" signal? Sort of — but only for a Search hit, and not a guaranteed typed contract.**

I checked the actual SDK type for `representedProduct` (what a `ProductSearchHit` carries): it's typed as `{id: string} & {[key: string]: any}` — just an ID, plus an open-ended catch-all. But in the **live data** I pulled from PLP last turn, that object actually carried real extra fields:
```

```
So for this catalog, `representedProduct` does look like SFCC's own pick of "the one variant that represents this hit" — colour included, via `c_color`. That's exactly the kind of default-variant marker you're asking about. Two honest caveats:

1. **This lives on the Search endpoint only.** `getProducts` (what Rail/Full-History's own fetch uses) returns a master `Product` with a `master` field (`masterId`, `orderable`, `price`/`priceMax`) — no equivalent "here's the representative variant" pointer at all. So even if PLP used this, it wouldn't transfer to Rail/Full-History — different endpoint, no such signal exists there.
2. **I've only confirmed `c_color` is populated for this one product's live data**, not that it's reliably there for every hit across the catalog — since it falls through an untyped index signature, it's whatever this catalog's search-index config happens to expose, not an SDK guarantee.

**One more thing worth noticing:** PLP's `hit.image` (the flat field it already uses today) is almost certainly already built by SFCC from that same representative variant — so PLP is already implicitly showing "the default colour's photo" without any code on our side choosing it. The real missing piece for a hover image isn't "figure out the default colour" — SFCC's already doing that for the primary shot — it's getting a **second** photo for that same already-resolved variant, which would mean scoping `filterImageGroups` by `representedProduct.c_color` (if it holds up across more products) rather than inventing a separate "first orderable" pick the way the demo did.

content.text:
Checked with real live data — found a genuine two-colour product on the current PLP results (`ZWNEWPRD04`, BLK/TAN) and traced through exactly what happens.

**Short answer: it's decided entirely server-side, before our code ever sees the data — and there's no client-side colour logic in this card at all, which matches what you noticed.**

For `ZWNEWPRD04`:
- `representedProduct.id` = `ZWNEWPRD04BLK0`, `representedProduct.c_color` = **`BLK`** — SFCC's search index has already picked Black as "the" representative colour for this one search hit, before it ever reaches the frontend.
- `hit.image` (the flat field PLP's mapper reads for the primary image) is filename `ZWNEWPRD04.BLK.PZ.jpg` — consistent with that same BLK pre-selection. So the primary photo you see is always whatever colour SFCC itself decided was representative — we have zero input into that choice, same as you observed there's no selector to give a shopper that input either.

**But here's a real, new gap this surfaced.** I dug into `imageGroups` for this product and each colour has its own separate, explicitly-tagged group:

```
medium group 1: variationAttributes: [{id: "color", values: [{value: "BLK"}]}] → BLK photos
medium group 2: variationAttributes: [{id: "color", values: [{value: "TAN"}]}] → TAN photos
```

PLP's own `selectGalleryImages` (the function that builds the swipeable multi-image gallery) does **not** filter by colour, or even by viewType — it just picks "whichever image group across the entire array has the most images." With BLK and TAN groups both sitting in that same array, it's picking essentially at random which colour's photos populate the gallery — it could easily show TAN images in the gallery on a card whose primary photo (and represented colour) is BLK. That's inconsistent with SFCC's own colour pre-selection, and it's a different, arguably bigger problem than the missing hover-image swap — a real mismatch a shopper could actually see, not just a missing feature.

So to tie this back to your original question: since there's no colour selector on our card, the honest picture is "we fully defer to SFCC's pick for the *primary* image, but the *gallery* logic ignores that pick entirely and can disagree with it."

content.text:
Given that, here's what I'd recommend — and I verified the mechanism against the same live product before proposing it, not just theorizing.

**The core fix: resolve the representative colour from data already on the hit, then scope the gallery to it.**

I checked `ZWNEWPRD04` again, specifically whether `hit.variants` can be matched against `hit.representedProduct.id` to get the colour SFCC already picked:

```
representedProduct.id: ZWNEWPRD04BLK0
variants: ZWNEWPRD04BLK0 -> {color: 'BLK', size: '0'}   ← exact match
```

It resolves cleanly and deterministically — no guessing, no reliance on the `c_color` custom attribute (which is untyped and catalog-specific), no string-parsing an ID. This is actually more reliable than what the demo branch does (its `resolveDemoVariant` picks "first orderable variant" as a heuristic, because it has no `representedProduct` to anchor against) — PLP's hit already tells us exactly which variant is representative.

**So the fix, concretely:**
1. Find the matching variant: `hit.variants?.find(v => v.productId === hit.representedProduct?.id)`.
2. Read its `variationValues?.color`.
3. Pass that into `filterImageGroups(hit.imageGroups, {viewType: 'medium', variationValues: {color: representativeColour}})` — the same base-SFCC utility, same shape, the demo branch already proved works.
4. Build the gallery from *that* filtered group only, not "whichever group anywhere has the most images."

**One thing worth calling out — this fixes two bugs at once, not one.** Today's `selectGalleryImages` has no `viewType` filter either, so it isn't just risking the wrong colour — it could just as easily pull from a `large` or `small` group instead of `medium`, if that group happens to have more images. Adding the `viewType: 'medium'` filter (which `selectPrimaryImage` on the Rail/Full-History side already does correctly) needs to happen regardless of the colour fix.

**Fallback for when this can't resolve** (single-colour product, or a hit with no `variants`/`representedProduct` data): degrade to today's "biggest group" heuristic, but at least scoped to `viewType: 'medium'` first — never fully unfiltered.

**One open question I can't answer from this data alone:** `hit.image` (the primary photo) already happened to agree with the representative colour for both products I checked — but I don't have confirmation that's a guaranteed SFCC behavior versus a coincidence of this test catalog. Worth keeping in mind, though I have no counter-evidence to suggest fixing the primary image too.

content.text:
Good question — and the honest answer is: it doesn't come for free, because there's a real conflict in the component itself that the demo's approach papers over.

**The part that IS free:** the same colour+viewType-scoped array (`groupImages`) that fixes the gallery is exactly the raw material hover-swap needs too — no separate resolution work, same lookup.

**The part that isn't free — a real conflict I need to flag before this becomes an implementation.** I went back and re-checked `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s actual logic:

```ts
const gallery = images && images.length > 1 ? images : undefined;
const showHoverSwap = swapOnHover && Boolean(hoverImage) && !gallery;
```

**Gallery mode and hover-swap are mutually exclusive by design** — the instant `images.length > 1`, `gallery` is truthy, and `!gallery` forces `showHoverSwap` to `false` regardless of whether `hoverImage` is populated.

Now look at what the demo mapper actually does: `hoverImage = groupImages[1]`, `images = groupImages.length > 1 ? groupImages : undefined`. Both conditions trigger off the exact same thing — "is there a 2nd image." **Which means: any time `hoverImage` gets populated, `images` gets populated too, with the same length, and gallery mode wins every time.** Hover-swap can never actually fire from that construction — it's live data, but functionally dead code, for any product with 2+ images (which was most of them — 4673TS251 alone had 9).

This actually lines up with something in the original AC I read earlier: Jasmijn's comment separately calls out "swaps to a model photo" and "shows carousel arrows for multi-image" as two distinct things — not one behavior. That reads like the real intent was never "always do both," it's "pick one, per product": a genuine multi-angle gallery gets the carousel treatment; a product with just a flat-lay + one model shot gets the hover-swap instead.

**So the actual decision needed once the gallery fix lands:** given the correctly-scoped `groupImages` for a product, we need a rule for which mode it gets — my instinct, matching the AC's own split, would be something like: exactly 2 images → hover-swap (primary + model shot, no gallery); 3+ images → gallery/carousel, skip `hoverImage` entirely so it doesn't quietly go dead. That's a real product decision though, not mine to default silently — want me to check how many images a few real multi-colour products actually have in their scoped group, to see how often each case would even come up before you decide?

content.text:
Confirmed directly from the SDK's own doc comment on `ProductSearchHit.image`:

> **"The first image of the product hit for the configured viewtype."**

So "official" means: **whichever image viewtype SFCC's Search configuration is set to use for search results, first image in that group** — a Business Manager setting, not anything visible or controllable from our frontend code.

**And it's not even a fixed viewtype across every product — I checked two real ones and got two different answers:**
- **4673TS251**: `hit.image` (photo "9") exactly matches this product's `hi-res` viewtype's own first image.
- **ZWNEWPRD04**: `hit.image` matches its `large` viewtype's first image — because this product has **no `hi-res` group at all**, so search evidently falls back to the next available viewtype.

So "official" isn't one consistent thing we could replicate — it's SFCC's own resolved answer, per-product, based on whatever viewtypes exist for that specific item. That's exactly why trying to guess/reconstruct it ourselves would be fragile — better to just keep trusting it as the primary source, like your proposal.

**Your proposed approach is the right one, and it ties together everything else we found today.** Keep `hit.image` as-is for the primary photo (fully respecting whatever SFCC decided is official — no change needed there), and populate `primaryImageFallbacks` from the **same colour + `medium`-viewtype-scoped group** we already need to correctly resolve for the gallery/hover-swap fix. If the official pick ever 404s, it falls back to a real, correctly-scoped photo from that product's own medium gallery — the exact mechanism already proven on Rail/Full-History.

That means one piece of resolution logic (colour-scoped, `medium`-viewtype images) now feeds **three** things: the gallery fix, the hover-swap image, and PLP's fallback safety net — not three separate problems.

Here's the full picture for the PLP product card — what's done, and what's left with a real plan behind it now.

## Already fixed (uncommitted, but implemented + verified)

| # | Finding | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Size chips showed enabled even when actually out of stock | Added `availability`/`represented_products` to PLP's search `expand` array |
| 2 | Add to Bag always added the default variant, ignoring the selected size | New `resolveOrderableVariant` + `ProductListCard` now owns real per-card selection state |
| 3 | Notify Me button wouldn't render at all (required a handler that doesn't exist yet) | Ships visible-but-inert now — your explicit call |
| 4 | Was/now pricing was hardcoded off | Wired real `getPriceData` into the mapper |

## Open, now with a concrete plan — three gaps, one shared fix

**The root problem behind all three:** `productListCardMapper.ts` never resolves *which colour* it's looking at for a multi-colour product. That single gap is what's causing all of the below.

**The fix:** resolve the representative colour deterministically — match `hit.representedProduct.id` against `hit.variants[]`, read that variant's `variationValues.color` (verified working on real live data, no guessing). Feed that colour into `filterImageGroups(imageGroups, {viewType: 'medium', variationValues: {color}})` — the same call the `feature/zimmproductcard-live-demo` branch already proved out. **That one resolved array now feeds three separate fixes:**

| # | Finding | How this fix closes it |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | Gallery images (`selectGalleryImages`) aren't scoped by colour *or* viewtype — can show a mix of the wrong colour's photos, or pull from `large`/`small` instead of `medium` | Rebuild it from the colour+viewtype-scoped array instead of "whichever group has the most images" |
| 6 | No hover-to-model-photo swap on PLP (`hoverImage` never populated) | Populate `hoverImage` from the same scoped array |
| 7 | No fallback if the primary photo 404s (PLP never got this, unlike Rail/Full History) | Keep `hit.image` ("the official picture," confirmed to be a backend-configured viewtype pick — not something we should try to replicate) as primary, but supply `primaryImageFallbacks` from that same scoped array as backup candidates |

**One more piece, and it's a real code change, not just data-wiring:** you've confirmed the hover behaviour should show the model-photo swap **and** activate the gallery arrows together — but `ZimmProductCardMedia` today has a rule (`&& !gallery`) that only ever allows one or the other. That rule itself needs to change for #6 to actually be visible whenever a real gallery exists (which real data shows is common — 5 of 7 sampled products had exactly 2 images once correctly scoped, 2 had 6–9).

**Bottom line:** 4 fixed, 3 open — and the 3 open ones aren't 3 separate investigations anymore, they're one shared data-resolution fix plus one small component-level rule change.

content.text:
Here's the build plan — framed as an addendum to the existing SFCC-83+84 plan (PLP surface was already folded into that plan; this is bug-fix work on what it delivered, not a new ticket). Presenting for your confirmation before anything gets written or touched, per the usual plan-then-pause step.

# Addendum: PLP Product Card — Image Resolution & Hover Behaviour

**Two steps.** Both small, both well-understood from this session's own live verification — no new research needed, everything below is already confirmed against real data.

## File manifest

| File | Action | Tier | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| `overrides/app/pages/product-list/productListCardMapper.ts` | MODIFY | Tier 3 (Squad A page) | `pwa-squad-a` |
| `overrides/app/pages/product-list/productListCardMapper.test.ts` | MODIFY | Tier 3 | as above |
| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx` | MODIFY | Tier 3 | `pwa-squad-a` + `pwa-squad-b` (shared component) |
| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/index.test.tsx` | MODIFY | Tier 3 | as above |

**Same open item as the original plan's PLP fold-in, not newly introduced here:** `product-list/` is Squad A territory per `squadA.md` — I don't have confirmation the Squad A Lead was ever notified when PLP work first folded into this build. Worth closing that loop before C1 lands, not just noting it again.

## Step C1 — Colour-aware image resolution in the PLP mapper

Rebuild `productListCardMapper.ts`'s image handling around one new resolver:

```ts
resolveRepresentativeColour(hit): string | undefined
// hit.variants?.find(v => v.productId === hit.representedProduct?.id)?.variationValues?.color
```

Then feed that into `filterImageGroups(hit.imageGroups, {viewType: 'medium', variationValues: colour ? {color: colour} : {}})` — replacing today's "whichever group has the most images" logic. One resolved array supplies three things:
- **`selectGalleryImages`** — rebuilt from this scoped array instead of the unscoped one.
- **`hoverImage`** — the array's `[1]`.
- **`primaryImageFallbacks`** — the rest of the array, as backup candidates if `hit.image` (kept as-is, unchanged — still the primary source) fails to load.

**Fallback when colour can't be resolved** (single-colour product, or no `variants`/`representedProduct`): still scope to `viewType: 'medium'`, just without the colour filter — never fall all the way back to today's fully-unscoped behaviour.

**Pass criteria**
- Colour resolves correctly against a real multi-colour fixture (mirrors `ZWNEWPRD04`'s BLK/TAN shape verified live this session).
- Gallery images never mix colours when a colour resolves — test with a fixture where the wrong-colour group has more images than the right one, and assert the *right* one wins. Make it fail first by reverting to "most images" to prove the test actually catches it.
- `hoverImage` and `primaryImageFallbacks` populated correctly from the same scoped array; both empty/undefined gracefully when the array has 0–1 images.
- No change to how `hit.image` itself is resolved — it stays the primary source untouched.
- `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run test`, `npm run lint` clean.

*No visual checkpoint owed here — pure data resolution, nothing rendered changes shape.*

## Step C2 — Let hover-swap and gallery mode run together

`ZimmProductCardMedia`'s `showHoverSwap = swapOnHover && Boolean(hoverImage) && !gallery` currently makes the two mutually exclusive. Here's the full chain — every investigation that fed into C1 and C2, in the order it happened.

**1. Two gaps found on a routine PLP audit.** Working through the consolidated PLP gap list, two came up with no fix yet: no fallback if the primary image 404s, and no hover-to-model-photo swap — both traced to `productListCardMapper.ts` never touching certain image fields.

**2. Your own catch: "isn't the hover swap a missed spec?"** Verified directly — `VARIATION_CONFIG.plp.showHoverImageSwap` was correctly `true`, but `hoverImage` was never populated anywhere in the mapper (confirmed via grep, zero matches). Config was right; data was missing.

**3. Correcting "is that the only thing missing?"** — no, two gaps, not one: the missing hover-swap *and* the missing fallback cascade, both stemming from the same file never being updated.

**4. You sent me to check two things at once:** the `feature/zimmproductcard-live-demo` branch's own hover-swap approach, and *why* PLP renders `4673TS251`'s photo fine while Recently Viewed doesn't.
- **Demo branch** (`liveProductCardDemoMapper.ts`): proved a working, colour-scoped `filterImageGroups` pattern already exists in this codebase — `primaryImage=[0]`, `hoverImage=[1]`, gallery=the rest, all from one filtered array.
- **The discrepancy**: parsed the real SSR JSON properly (my first attempt actually bled into a neighbouring product's data and gave a wrong answer — caught and redone correctly) and found PLP's `hit.image` and Recently Viewed's `imageGroups.medium[0]` are **two structurally different fields**, not the same data read two ways. PLP wasn't safer — it was looking somewhere else entirely, by coincidence.

**5. Your question about multi-colour products with no colour selector** pushed this further: found a real two-colour product (`ZWNEWPRD04`, BLK/TAN) in live data and discovered a **third, previously-unknown bug** — `selectGalleryImages` has zero colour or viewtype filtering at all, so it can pull gallery photos from the wrong colour entirely. This is what elevated the scope from "add a missing field" to "fix how images get selected, structurally."

**6. Resolving how to fix it, precisely:** found that `hit.representedProduct.id` matches an exact entry in `hit.variants[]`, whose `variationValues.color` gives the real answer — verified live, deterministic, no guessing. Better than the demo's own "first orderable variant" heuristic, because PLP's hit already tells us exactly which variant SFCC picked.

**7. "Once fixed, what does this mean for hover-swap?"** — tracing `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s actual gating logic surfaced the real architectural finding: gallery mode and hover-swap are **mutually exclusive by code today** (`!gallery` in the condition). The demo's own approach would make `hoverImage` functionally dead the moment a real gallery exists.

**8. Your clarification that the AC wants both together** — this is what turned "design tension to think about" into "a real code change is required," splitting the work into a data fix and a separate behaviour fix.

**9. Checking real products before committing to the plan** (your ask) — 5 of 7 real products had exactly 2 images once correctly scoped, 2 had 6–9. This confirmed the "both at once" case is the *common* case, not a rare one — worth getting right.

**10. What "official" actually means** — the SDK's own doc comment ("first image... for the configured viewtype") plus live confirmation that it resolves to a *different* viewtype per product (`hi-res` when it exists, falling back to `large` when it doesn't) settled that `hit.image` should stay untouched and trusted, just wrapped in a fallback — exactly your proposal.

**How it maps to the plan:** items 1–6 and 10 all converge on **C1** (one colour+viewtype-scoped resolution, reused for gallery, hover-image, and fallback candidates). Items 7–9 are what produced **C2** as a distinct step — a real component-level rule change, not a data-wiring fix, which is also why C2 (not C1) carries the visual-checkpoint requirement.

Here's the chain, in order — each finding is what actually pushed us to the next question.

1. **We first locked down that the "recently viewed" card itself was solid** — image-only, links to the PDP, keyboard-reachable, same at every screen size. Good foundation, nothing to fix there.

2. **Then we checked the rail's other pieces** (the "RECENTLY VIEWED" heading, the "SEE FULL HISTORY" link, and how it sits on PDP/Cart/PLP) — all present and correct, just still sitting uncommitted.

3. **Comparing Full History's cards to PLP's cards** (since they're supposed to be the identical card) turned up real behavior differences — an out-of-stock product looks fine on Full History when it shouldn't, Add to Bag does nothing there, size chips can't be picked. That was a Full History problem specifically, so we set it aside and narrowed to PLP only.

4. **Listing PLP's own gaps**, we had 4 already fixed (size chips, add to bag, notify me, pricing) and 1 still open (no backup photo if the main one breaks).

5. **You then noticed something separate** — PLP's supposed to swap to a model photo on hover, and it doesn't. Checked it: the mechanism exists, but nobody ever gave PLP a photo to swap *to*. Second open gap.

6. **We double- and triple-checked the out-of-stock hover state too**, since it's related — turned out that one's actually built correctly already, so nothing to add there.

7. **You pointed me at your old demo branch** to see how you'd solved the hover-photo problem before, and separately asked why PLP shows this one specific product's photo fine while Recently Viewed shows it broken. Digging into real live data (and catching myself misreading it once, then redoing it properly) showed: **they're not even looking at the same photo** — PLP uses one field, Recently Viewed uses a completely different one, and for this one product, Recently Viewed's happened to be the broken one. Pure coincidence, not PLP being smarter.

8. **That led to the bigger question**: for a product with more than one colour, how do we even know which colour's photos to show? Turns out **the store's backend already decides that for us** — we found a real 2-colour product and proved it. But digging into *that* uncovered a brand new bug: **our photo-gallery picker doesn't care about colour or photo-type at all**, so it can grab the wrong colour's pictures entirely.

9. **We worked out how the gallery-picker should behave instead** — read the colour the backend already chose, and only use that colour's photos.

10. **Then we asked what that means for the hover-swap fix from step 5** — and found a real conflict: the card's own code has a rule that says "if there's a real photo gallery, don't also do the hover-swap." You confirmed both should happen at once, which means that rule itself has to change, not just work around it.

11. **Checked real products to see how often this even comes up** — most only have 2 photos once correctly sorted by colour, a couple have a lot more (6–9). Useful to know before deciding how the fix should behave.

12. **Finally, you asked what that "official" photo from step 7 actually is** — turned out it's the store's own pre-picked photo type, and it's not even the same type for every product. Your call: keep trusting that one as the main photo, but now also give it a backup plan using the same colour-sorted photos from step 9.

**That's the full chain** — one small observation (the hover swap) kept unraveling into a bigger, connected picture (colour handling, the "official" photo, a hidden gallery bug, a rule that blocks two things from happening together), and all of it converged into the 2-step plan: fix the photo-picking logic once, and change the one rule blocking hover-swap and gallery from working together.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/skills/zimmerMANNBuild

The executor. Takes an approved plan and builds it, one step at a time, with every step tested,
scope-checked, scored and seen by Marcel before it becomes a commit.

**Intended model: Sonnet 5 at maximum effort.** A skill cannot pin the session model — the loop
agents are pinned to Sonnet in their own frontmatter regardless.

**Scale to the work.** A two-point story does not get the full loop. The plan states the scale it
chose and why; honour it. Over-scaled machinery is a defect, not thoroughness. Nothing too crazy,
no overthinking.

---

## Two modes

**`build`** — `` is a Jira key. Reads `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/plan.md`
and executes it. This is the default.

**`rework`** — invoked as `rework <TICKET>` after a PR is open and CodeRabbit or a reviewer has
requested changes. Skips planning entirely; see the last section.

If no plan exists for the ticket, stop and say so. **Do not plan here** — that is
`zimmerMANNPreBuild`'s job, and building from an unplanned story is how an afternoon gets burned
on the wrong thing.

---

## Before the first step

1. Confirm the branch. **Not `develop`, not `main`** — a `PreToolUse` hook blocks every Write and
   Edit there. If the branch is wrong, stop.
2. Confirm the working tree is clean, or that everything dirty is expected and belongs to this
   story. Registry churn under `.claude/registry/*.md` is automatic and expected.
3. Read the plan's file manifest, tiers and per-step pass criteria. **Any file marked BLOCKED
   stops the run** until Marcel confirms owner approval.
4. Record the baseline: run the four per-step gates now and note the numbers. A gate that is
   non-zero at baseline is not a failure you introduced.

---

## The loop — once per step

```
Implementer  →  Tester  →  Orchestrator  →  Scorer  →  [Marcel]  →  commit
                   ↑                          │
                   └────── REWORK, max 3 ─────┘
```

**1. `zm-implementer`** builds the step. Only the files the step names. It never stages and never
commits.

**2. `zm-tester`** fans out its own angle sub-agents, re-pointed for this step, and reports
findings with CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE and UNIFORM/ONE-OFF labels, plus what it tried to falsify and
what it could not verify.

**3. `zm-orchestrator`** returns a scope verdict — IN SCOPE / UNDER / OVER / BLOCKED. Under and
over carry equal weight.

**4. `zm-scorer`** takes both and scores six axes. PASS or REWORK.

**REWORK returns to the Implementer with a specific instruction. Maximum three rounds.** On the
third, stop and surface to Marcel — three failures means the plan or the criteria are wrong, not
the implementation.

### Per-step gates — the cheap four

Run every step. Seconds each.

```
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run test                        # includes recipeGuards, the hard styling gate
npm run lint                        # compare counts, not the exit code
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs    # new unacknowledged findings only
```

Two traps: `npm run lint` exits non-zero at a healthy baseline, so **compare the count against
your baseline and ignore the exit code**. And never append arguments to it — `pwa-kit-dev lint`
forwards `--`-args into `execSync`, which can silently turn the gate into a writer.

The plan's per-step pass criteria layer **on top of** these, they do not replace them.

### The visual checkpoint

**After any step that changes rendered output, the loop stops.** The plan marks which steps those
are; if it doesn't, assume any step touching a component, a recipe or a page does.

Tell Marcel exactly:
- the URL and the viewport to open
- the Figma node to compare against — the one for **that variant and state**
- what should be on screen
- what would indicate a defect, including anything that will look wrong but is correct

Then **wait.** Do not proceed on assumption. This is the only gate on this stack that catches a
layout defect — `width: 'xl'` passed every automated check and destroyed the global footer.

Until it has happened, the Scorer's Design fidelity axis is UNVERIFIED, not passed.

### The commit

**The skill commits, not an agent.** Only after: Scorer PASS, and the visual checkpoint passed if
one was owed.

One step, one commit. Conventional Commits — the `commit-msg` hook enforces it. **No Claude
attribution, no CodeRabbit mentions, no `Co-Authored-By` line.** Use Marcel's previously authored
commits on this repo as the reference for tone and body.

Then move to the next step.

---

## Before handing off

Once every step has passed, run the expensive gates **once**:

```
npm run build-storybook             # then run the interaction + a11y suite against it
npm run test:story                  # real BrowserStack, scoped to the Jira key
npm run test:max-file-size          # runs a full build
cr review --base develop            # CodeRabbit locally, full review before anything is public
```

Storybook needs a verified-free port and a build you can prove is yours — a stale server on 6006
produced a silently meaningless pass once. Check the served build matches your own before trusting
any result.

Then **write the handoff** to `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/handoff.md`:

```
# Handoff — <TICKET>
Branch: <branch>   Base: <sha>   Head: <sha>

## Steps
| # | What | Commit | Scorer verdict | Rework rounds |

## Gates (real numbers, not claims)
| Gate | Result | Baseline |

## UNIFORM findings
<each one, with file:line — these are what a per-step review structurally cannot catch>

## Could not verify
<named, with why>

## Outstanding
<anything left, or "none">
```

**Write it even when everything passed.** PostBuild reads this file, and it may run in a different
session — a handoff that exists only in conversation does not survive the session ending.

Then present the same content to Marcel and **hand off to `zimmerMANNPostBuild`. This skill does
not push and does not open a PR.**

---

## Rework mode

Entered after a PR is open and CodeRabbit or a reviewer has requested changes.

**Read `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/postbuild.md` first.** It records what earlier rounds
already declined and why. A finding that was declined with evidence in round one does not get
re-litigated in round three — check before you verify anything, and if you disagree with a previous
decline, say so rather than silently reversing it.

**1. Verify every finding before touching anything.** CodeRabbit has been wrong on this repo
often — one batch ran 1-in-6 correct. Treat each finding as a hypothesis, not a fact. Per finding:

- **VALID** — reproduce it, cite `file:line`, fix it
- **INVALID** — say what is actually true, with the evidence, and draft the reply
- **OUT OF SCOPE** — real but not this story's problem; name the owning ticket or the person
- **DEFER** — real, in scope, but blocked on a decision; name who decides

**2. Fix only the VALID ones.** Same rules as build mode — the Implementer touches only what the
finding names, never stages, never commits.

**3. Re-run the cheap four**, plus the visual checkpoint if the fix changes rendered output.

**4. Commit the fixes here**, same rule as build mode — the skill commits, never an agent. Reference
the review thread each commit answers.

**5. Hand back to `zimmerMANNPostBuild`** with: what was fixed and in which commit, what was
declined and why, and the evidence behind each decline. **PostBuild owns the push and the
in-thread replies** — every finding gets a written answer, including the declined ones.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never push. Never open or update a PR.** That boundary belongs to PostBuild, which presents
  first and pushes only once Marcel has given the go.
- **Never write to the repo's config** — `.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CODEOWNERS`,
  `.docs/memory/**`, `.docs/prd/**`. Tier 1 Governance.
- **Never touch a Tier 1 file** without Marcel naming it and confirming owner approval.
- **Never expand scope.** Something worth doing that the plan didn't ask for gets reported, not
  done. Report it and let Marcel decide.
- **Local-only docs are never citable** in a commit message or a code comment. Cite `AGENTS.md`
  or `.claude/rules/*` instead.
- **Say what you could not verify.** Silence reads as "nothing wrong" when it may mean
  "didn't look there".

Build step C1 of the SFCC-83+84 plan addendum. Read `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-83+84/plan.md`, section "## 7. Addendum (2026-09-09) — PLP product card: image resolution & hover behaviour", specifically step "#### C1 — Colour-aware image resolution in the PLP mapper" and its Pass criteria. Ignore every other section of that file (A1–B3/GATES) — those are a different, already-completed part of this same larger ticket, not part of this step.

**Touch only these two files:**
- `overrides/app/pages/product-list/productListCardMapper.ts`
- `overrides/app/pages/product-list/productListCardMapper.test.ts`

**The core requirement, restated so there's no ambiguity even if the plan file is large:**

1. Add `resolveRepresentativeColour(hit)`: finds the entry in `hit.variants` whose `productId` matches `hit.representedProduct?.id`, and returns that entry's `variationValues?.color` (or `undefined` if no match / no variants / no representedProduct).
2. Rebuild `selectGalleryImages` to use `filterImageGroups(hit.imageGroups ?? [], {viewType: 'medium', variationValues: colour ? {color: colour} : {}})` (from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils`, already imported elsewhere in this codebase — check `recentlyViewedCard.ts` or `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts` for the exact import) — replacing the current "whichever image group has the most images across every viewType/colour" logic entirely.
3. From that same colour+viewType-scoped array, also populate two currently-missing fields on the mapper's output: `hoverImage` (the array's index `[1]`, or `undefined` if it doesn't exist) and `primaryImageFallbacks` (the rest of that array, as an ordered list of backup image candidates).
4. `hit.image` (used for `primaryImage`) is NOT touched by this step — it stays exactly as it resolves today. `primaryImageFallbacks` exists purely so `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s existing cascading-fallback mechanism (`primaryImageFallbacks` prop, already built and already used by the Rail/Full-History mappers — see `recentlyViewedCard.ts` for the exact pattern to follow for constructing `ZimmProductCardImage` objects with `src`/`alt`) has real candidates to try if `hit.image` ever fails to load.
5. When colour can't be resolved (single-colour product, or no matching variant), still scope to `viewType: 'medium'` alone (empty `variationValues: {}`) — never fall back to the old fully-unscoped "biggest group anywhere" behaviour.

**Tests to add** (in `productListCardMapper.test.ts`), matching this codebase's existing test style in that same file:
- A fixture shaped like a real multi-colour product (mirror the two-colour shape already used elsewhere in this session's investigation: two `imageGroups` entries at `viewType: 'medium'`, one tagged `variationAttributes: [{id: 'color', values: [{value: 'BLK'}]}]` with more images, one tagged `TAN` with fewer) — assert the gallery only ever contains the colour matching `resolveRepresentativeColour`'s result, not just "whichever has more images." Make sure this test would have failed against the OLD "most images" logic (i.e., rig the wrong-colour group to have MORE images than the right one) — that's what proves the fix is real, not coincidental.
- `hoverImage` populates correctly from the scoped array.
- `primaryImageFallbacks` populates correctly from the scoped array (excluding nothing — it's independent of `hit.image`).
- Single-colour / no-variants-match fixture: confirms graceful `viewType`-only fallback, not a crash, not the old unscoped behaviour.
- Empty/undersized scoped array (0 or 1 images): `hoverImage` and `primaryImageFallbacks` both come back empty/undefined, not throwing.

Follow this repo's existing conventions exactly (see `.claude/rules/conventions.md`, `.claude/rules/typescript.md`): no `any`, real SDK types where they exist, JSDoc on any new exported function, no magic strings. Do not touch any other file. Do not run `npm run lint` with any extra arguments. Do not stage or commit anything — report back what you built and where.

This is a real should-fix gap, not purely theoretical: SFCC master products can have master-level `variants[]` where duplicate `productId` entries are plausible artefacts of certain variation-attribute configurations or index sync issues (unlike `representedProduct.id`→variants matching itself, which the docblock calls deterministic/server-decided, the *shape* of the `variants` array feeding that lookup is not something this mapper controls or validates). 1	import type { ShopperSearchTypes } from 'commerce-sdk-isomorphic';
2	import { getPriceData } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils';
3	import { productUrlBuilder } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/url';
4	import type {
5	  ZimmProductCardBaseProps,
6	  ZimmProductCardPlpVariation,
7	  ZimmProductCardImage,
8	} from '../../components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard';
9	import type { ZimmSizeChipValue } from '../../components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSizeChipGroup';
10	
11	// This mapper is PLP-only by design, so it returns the narrowed shape directly rather than the
12	// full `ZimmProductCardProps` union — letting a caller pass the result straight to a
13	// PLP-typed component (like this page's own `ProductListCard`) with no re-narrowing needed.
14	type ProductListCardResult = ZimmProductCardBaseProps & ZimmProductCardPlpVariation;
15	
16	/**
17	 * `c_productBadges` is a custom SFCC attribute (SFCC-225's own already-merged SCAPI hook) with no
18	 * typed field on the base SDK's `ProductSearchHit` — it only reaches this shape via that type's
19	 * own `{[key: string]: any}` index signature. Narrowed here to the one shape this mapper reads,
20	 * rather than trusting `any` at every call site.
21	 */
22	export type ProductListSearchHit = ShopperSearchTypes.ProductSearchHit & {
23	  c_productBadges?: Array<{ productBadge?: string }>;
24	};
25	
26	type RawImage = { alt?: string; disBaseLink?: string; link?: string };
27	
28	const toCardImage = (image: RawImage | undefined): ZimmProductCardImage | undefined => {
29	  const src = image?.disBaseLink ?? image?.link;
30	  if (!src) return undefined;
31	  return { src, alt: image?.alt ?? '' };
32	};
33	
34	/**
35	 * Picks the image group with the most images as this hit's gallery. Viewpoint-agnostic on
36	 * purpose — this catalog's real `viewType` naming (e.g. `large` vs `pdp`) was not confirmed for
37	 * this quick test integration, so "most images" is used as a simple, real-data-driven proxy for
38	 * "the full gallery" rather than guessing a specific viewType string. Returns `undefined` for 0
39	 * or 1 resulting images, matching `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own "no gallery" contract for that
40	 * case — this function doesn't duplicate that check, it just never returns a 1-length array.
41	 */
42	export const selectGalleryImages = (hit: ProductListSearchHit): ZimmProductCardImage[] | undefined => {
43	  const groups = hit.imageGroups ?? [];
44	  if (groups.length === 0) return undefined;
45	
46	  const largest = groups.reduce((best, group) =>
47	    (group.images?.length ?? 0) > (best.images?.length ?? 0) ? group : best,
48	  );
49	  const images = (largest.images ?? []).map(toCardImage).filter((img): img is ZimmProductCardImage => Boolean(img));
50	
51	  return images.length > 1 ? images : undefined;

content.text:
Here's the concrete before/after — what a shopper actually sees, plus what stays exactly the same.

## What changes

**1. Multi-colour products stop leaking the wrong colour's photos.**
Before: a card's swipeable gallery could show a mix of colours — e.g., the card representing the Black variant could have Tan photos mixed into its carousel. After: the gallery only ever shows that same product's Black photos, matching whatever SFCC already decided to represent.

**2. A broken primary photo now recovers instead of showing broken.**
Before: if the "official" photo 404s, the card just shows a broken image, permanently. After: it automatically falls back to the next real photo of the same colour — same recovery behaviour already proven on the Rail and Full History.

**3. Hovering a card with 2+ photos now does two things at once, not zero.**
Before: hover did nothing to the image at all (no swap — the data for it never existed — and no gallery interaction beyond whatever was already there). After: the main photo crossfades to a second/model shot **and** the paging arrows appear simultaneously, letting the shopper browse the rest.

**4. This lands differently depending on how many real photos a product has** (checked live, so these aren't guesses):
   - **Most products (5 of 7 checked — exactly 2 photos once correctly sorted by colour):** hover reveals the model shot, arrows let you toggle back and forth between the two.
   - **A few richer products (6–9 photos):** hover immediately previews the second photo while arrows let you page through the full set — a genuinely richer interaction than today, where hovering did nothing at all in this case.
   - **Single-photo products, or ones where colour can't be resolved:** no visible change — nothing to swap to, nothing to page through, same as today.

## What stays exactly the same

- The **primary/"official" photo itself** — still whatever SFCC's search config decides, untouched. This plan only adds a safety net around it, never changes the pick itself.
- **Add to Bag, size chips, Notify Me, was/now pricing** — already fixed in earlier work, unaffected here.
- **Full History's cards** — deliberately out of scope, no change.
- Anything about routes, translations, or other pages — this is scoped entirely to the PLP mapper and the shared image component.

## At the code level

- `productListCardMapper.ts` gains real colour-resolution logic and new test coverage for it.
- `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s hover-gating logic changes from "gallery always wins" to "both can be true" — with its own new tests proving the combined state.
- No new files, no new routes, no new dependencies — this is entirely a correctness fix to existing, already-shipped code.
