import React from 'react';
import type { ReactNode } from 'react';
import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
import { ZimmProductCard } from '../zimmProductCard';
import type { ZimmProductCardProps } from '../zimmProductCard';

export type ZimmRecentlyViewedGridProps = {
  /**
   * Typed as `ReactNode`, not `string` — this component owns no copy/intl, the same discipline
   * `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`'s own `title` prop documents for itself (build plan §A5/§B1). Styled
   * with `textStyle="heading3"` directly below, applied from the start rather than left for a
   * caller to pre-style — the rail's own `title` shipped once *without* this and had to be fixed
   * after live Storybook testing caught it rendering in the ambient body weight instead of the
   * intended one (see `zimmRecentlyViewedRail/index.tsx`'s own docblock, "Styling resolved
   * 2026-09-08"). That token is independently confirmed correct for THIS component's own title
   * bar too, not just carried over from the rail: build plan §B1's `get_variable_defs` read on
   * Figma node `3332:37131` ("PLP Bar desktop") returns "Default/Heading 3" — Futura Round
   * Medium, size 16 / line-height 18 / letterSpacing -1 — cross-checked against
   * `theme/foundation/typography.ts`'s own registered `heading3` (`fontSizes.xs` 16px /
   * `lineHeights['2xs']` 18px / `letterSpacings.xs` -0.12px, the same documented sub-pixel
   * rounding `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`'s Units section already carries elsewhere /
   * `textTransform: uppercase` already baked in) and found to match exactly.
   */
  title: ReactNode;
  /**
   * A pre-formatted, already-pluralized node (e.g. "16 Items" / "1 Item") — this component does
   * not own copy/intl, matching `title` above and `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`'s own container/
   * presentational split (`.claude/rules/components.md`). Build plan §B1: the item count is
   * mechanical ICU-plural-selector copy ("go for it" — Marcel, 2026-09-08), which is the calling
   * container's job (SFCC-84's Full History page container, not built by this step), not this
   * organism's. **Rendered exactly as received — never recomputed from `cards.length` here.** A
   * caller is expected to derive this from the same `cards` array it passes below; see this
   * component's own stories/tests for the "the two stay in sync when a real caller wires them
   * together correctly" proof this step's brief asked for — that proof lives at the call site
   * (story/test), not as internal recomputation, precisely so a future divergence between what a
   * caller *says* the count is and what actually rendered stays visible instead of being silently
   * papered over by this component re-deriving its own "correct" answer.
   *
   * Same `textStyle="heading3"` / colour treatment as `title` above — confirmed via the same
   * `3332:37131` screenshot, which renders "RECENTLY VIEWED" (left) and "16 ITEMS" (right) in the
   * same text style.
   */
  itemCountLabel: ReactNode;
  /**
   * Rendered in the exact order received — no sorting or reordering happens here, and (unlike
   * `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`) no cap/slice either: SFCC-84's Full History page has no ordering AC
   * of its own, but per build plan §B1 "the page is the rail's overflow — same order or it reads
   * as broken", and the page container (not this component) is already responsible for capping
   * its fetch at `RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED` (24, `app/constants/index.ts`) before this
   * component ever sees `cards` — see the build plan's B2 step. Typed as the full
   * `ZimmProductCardProps` union, matching `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`'s own contract verbatim
   * (build plan §A5) rather than a variation-narrowed type, so this component spreads each entry
   * straight into `ZimmProductCard` rather than forcing a variation onto every card itself. In
   * real usage every entry already carries `variation: 'plp'` by construction — SFCC-84 AC 2 /
   * SFCC-236's own "Recently Viewed Full History variation (same behavior as PLP card)" AC block,
   * corroborated 2026-09-07/08 against the `feature/zimmproductcard-live-demo` branch's own
   * "Recently Viewed (Full History)" section, which renders `variation: 'plp'` cards with zero
   * different props from its own PLP demo cards (see this component's own recipe file for the
   * full citation). Nothing new was needed on `ZimmProductCard` itself for this — see that
   * component's own module docblock: *"'Recently Viewed Full History' is not a fourth
   * variation... callers pass `variation: 'plp'` for it."*
   */
  cards: readonly ZimmProductCardProps[];
};

const ZIMM_RECENTLY_VIEWED_GRID_RECIPE = 'ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid';

/**
 * SFCC-84 — the Recently Viewed Full History grid organism (build plan section B1). Purely
 * presentational: data arrives as props, no data-fetching, no `useEinstein`, no `useIntl` — the
 * same container/presentational split `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` (SFCC-83, build plan §A5) already
 * establishes, adapted here from a horizontally-scrolling rail to a 4-up desktop grid. The
 * container (build plan §B2, not built by this step) is responsible for reading the shopper's
 * tracked view history, fetching real product data for it, mapping the result to `plp`-shaped
 * `ZimmProductCardProps` (a new mapper, `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts` — NOT
 * `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`'s own `recentlyViewedCard.ts`, whose narrower image-only output cannot
 * feed this grid's fuller `plp` card), and supplying `title`/`itemCountLabel` copy.
 *
 * **Design source, stated plainly per build plan §B1: this grid's layout comes from a
 * PROVISIONAL design source** (`Zimmermann_Designs` file, node `3332:35655` — not a PDP/Recently
 * Viewed node in the authoritative `Zimmermann_Design_System_2026` file the rail sibling uses;
 * see Marcel's 2026-09-04 precedence rule, restated verbatim in the build plan). That ranking is
 * unchanged by anything below. What DID change, this session (2026-09-07/08): the specific
 * geometry/typography/variation values actually used here were independently verified, not taken
 * on the provisional source's word alone —
 *   - **Layout** confirmed via live Figma metadata AND a real screenshot of `3332:37131` ("PLP
 *     Bar desktop", 1440×75), which renders "RECENTLY VIEWED" (left) / "16 ITEMS" (right) —
 *     confirming both the title-left/count-right layout and the title bar's own content in one
 *     node, not inferred from layer names alone (which the build plan notes were misleading here).
 *   - **The `Sidebar` (`3332:35664`) child holds four stacked `Products Module Desktop` instances**
 *     (`35665`/`35666`/`35668`/`35669`, each 1440×606) — two of which were checked directly and are
 *     structurally identical (four `Products S Desktop` instances each, 288×542, at
 *     x=0/384/768/1152): confirmed as 4 repeated example rows of real content, not 4 different
 *     states to design against.
 *   - **The `variation: 'plp'` decision** (see `cards`' own JSDoc above) is independently
 *     corroborated by a real, interactive prior-art branch, not just an AC-text reading — see this
 *     recipe file's own docblock for the full citation.
 *   - **The 96px horizontal card gap** (this recipe's own `GRID_CARD_GAP_DESKTOP`, Desktop only)
 *     was checked at two independent Figma sources specifically because it does NOT resolve to any
 *     bound variable — see this recipe's own docblock for the full "RESOLVED... checked twice,
 *     genuinely un-tokenised" citation. Tablet (80px) and Mobile (40px) each have their own,
 *     different, real-token values — corrected 2026-09-10, see that same docblock's "HORIZONTAL
 *     GAP" section for the full per-breakpoint story.
 * So: provisional design *source*, independently confirmed design *values* — both things are true
 * at once, and this docblock states both rather than letting the provisional-source caveat imply
 * the specific numbers below are unverified guesses, or letting the confirmed-values framing imply
 * the source ranking has changed.
 *
 * **This grid does NOT share its title row with `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`'s own `title-and-link`**
 * (a deliberate build-plan call, not an oversight): the rail's header is Figma node
 * `40000538:20306` (h96/h56); this grid's is `3332:37131` (h75, one Desktop reading only, no
 * separate Tablet/Mobile node). Different components in Figma, so sharing would be a wrong DRY
 * call — see this recipe's own docblock for why no fixed header height is set here at all (unlike
 * the rail's own two-tier `HEADER_HEIGHT_MOBILE`/`DESKTOP`).
 *
 * Renders `null` for an empty `cards` array — the same defensive-leaf-component default
 * `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` uses (its own container owns the actual "should this exist at all"
 * decision; SFCC-84's Full History page has its own separate empty-state design, per build plan
 * §B2, which does not involve mounting this component with zero cards at all).
 */
export const ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid = ({ title, itemCountLabel, cards }: ZimmRecentlyViewedGridProps) => {
  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_RECENTLY_VIEWED_GRID_RECIPE, {});

  if (cards.length === 0) {
    return null;
  }

  return (
    <chakra.div __css={styles.container} data-testid="recently-viewed-grid">
      <chakra.div __css={styles.header}>
        <chakra.span textStyle="heading3" color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)">
          {title}
        </chakra.span>
        <chakra.span
          textStyle="heading3"
          color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)"
          data-testid="recently-viewed-grid-count"
        >
          {itemCountLabel}
        </chakra.span>
      </chakra.div>
      <chakra.div __css={styles.grid} data-testid="recently-viewed-grid-group">
        {cards.map((card) => (
          <ZimmProductCard key={card.id} {...card} />
        ))}
      </chakra.div>
    </chakra.div>
  );
};

content.text:
No — confirmed via Figma, currently **not** flush. Here's the exact gap.

Figma's own structure shows the same "flush outer box, inset-via-padding content" pattern the Rail uses: the frame itself has zero outer margin (title-and-link, Product Card Group, everything spans the full 1440px frame edge-to-edge), with each part's own internal padding creating the visual inset — header's `p-40px`, card content's `px-40px`. Confirmed directly on the Product Card Group node (`9551:78222`): no left/right padding on the outer wrapper at all, first card sits flush at x=0.

But `recentlyViewed/index.tsx` (the actual page component) has **no bleed mechanism whatsoever** — no `PageContainer`, no `layerStyle="page"`, no `mx={PAGE_CONTENT_BLEED_MX}`, nothing. It's just a bare `<Box data-testid="recently-viewed-page">` wrapping `ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid` directly. That means the Grid sits inside `#app-main`'s own normal sitewide padding (32px mobile/tablet, 40px desktop) with nothing cancelling it — the exact same shape of bug I found and fixed for the Rail on PDP/PLP, except here it was never wired up at all, not wired up wrong.

The Grid's own recipe (`container`/`grid` parts) is already flush-ready — `width: 100%`, no padding of its own — so this isn't a rail-style multi-layer bug, it's purely the missing page-level piece. The natural fix is the same one already proven for PDP/PLP: apply `mx={PAGE_CONTENT_BLEED_MX}` (or equivalent) to this page's own outer wrapper.

Want me to wire that up?

content.text:
Yes — should be flush, and currently isn't. Checked both sides directly rather than assume.

**Figma confirms flush is the intent.** All three page frames (`9551:78221` Desktop 1440px, `9560:137688` Tablet 834px, `9560:138459` Mobile 402px) show both `title-and-link` and every `Product Card Group` instance at `x=0`, full frame width — same edge-to-edge composition pattern that justified the Rail's bleed. The header's own 40px/32px/20px padding (already fixed, `b4326db`) is *internal* content padding within that full-width box, not a page-level margin — same relationship the Rail has between its own internal padding and its outer flush edge.

**The code currently applies no bleed mechanism at all.** `recentlyViewed/index.tsx` renders:
```tsx
<Box data-testid="recently-viewed-page">
  <ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid title={title} itemCountLabel={...} cards={cards} />
</Box>
```
No `PageContainer`, no `layerStyle="page"`, no `mx={PAGE_CONTENT_BLEED_MX}` — nothing. That means `#app-main`'s own sitewide padding (32px/40px) is the *only* thing in effect, and it's never cancelled. The whole grid — header, item count, cards — sits inset by that padding on every breakpoint.

**Also worth noting:** `ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid`'s own prop type has no passthrough/`mx` slot at all (unlike `RecommendedProducts`, which forwards `{...props}` to its wrapping `Box` for exactly this reason) — so the fix is a wrapping `<Box mx={PAGE_CONTENT_BLEED_MX}>` at the page level, same mechanism already used for the Rail on PDP/PLP, not a change to the Grid component itself.

Want me to make that fix?

content.text:
Checked all three breakpoints directly against the real page frames (not the docblock's own past claims). Good news: the grid mechanics are up to spec.

| | Code (current) | Figma (fresh check) |
|---|---|---|
| Desktop columns | 4 | 4 — confirmed, fixed 288px cards |
| Desktop gap | 96px | 96px — derived: (1440 − 4×288) ÷ 3 = 96 |
| Desktop max-width | 1440px | 1440px, matches the frame width |
| Tablet columns | 3 | 3 — directly confirmed this time |
| Tablet gap | 80px | 80px — confirmed |
| Mobile columns | 2 | 2 — confirmed |
| Mobile gap (horizontal) | 40px | 40px — confirmed |
| Row gap (vertical, all breakpoints) | 64px | 64px — confirmed at all three |

Two things worth flagging, neither a visible bug:

**1. Documentation nit.** The recipe's own docblock claims Tablet's 3-column figure has "no corroborating Figma node — Marcel's own figure." That's now wrong: node `9560:137692` (already cited for the *gap* value) directly shows 3 fluid-width cards — the column count was corroborated all along, the comment just never connected the two. Worth a quick correction so the sourcing trail stays accurate, not a functional issue.

**2. A structural difference that happens to net out identically today.** Figma's Desktop mechanism is genuinely different from the code's: Figma uses *fixed* 288px cards with `justify-content: space-between` distributing whatever's left as gaps; the code uses CSS grid `1fr` columns with a *fixed* 96px gap. These only produce the same result because the container is capped at exactly 1440px — at any desktop width between 1280px (where 4-up starts) and 1439px (the cap), the two approaches would diverge: Figma's cards would stay 288px with a shrinking gap, the code's cards would shrink with the gap held at 96px. Figma has no frame for that narrow range to check against, so I can't confirm which behavior is actually intended there — flagging it as a known, low-impact gap (real desktop monitors are overwhelmingly ≥1440px) rather than chasing it without a spec to check against.

Want me to fix the doc nit, or leave both as noted?

9	export const CUSTOM_HOME_TITLE = '🎉 Hello Zimmermann!';
10	
11	// SFCC-83 — interim history-storage cap for `useRecentlyViewedHistory` (build plan §2, "Interim
12	// data source"). Set to 24, matching the Shopper Products `getProducts` endpoint's own hard
13	// per-request ID limit that `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts` must cap to (confirmed directly in
14	// the SDK's own doc comment — see that file): storing more IDs than a single fetch can ever
15	// resolve would never produce a displayable card. Confirmed with Marcel (2026-09-08): 500 was
16	// this constant's original value, superseded once the 24-ID fetch limit was discovered — `24` is
17	// the final value, not a pending question.
18	export const RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED = 24;
19	
20	// SFCC-84 — the Recently Viewed Full History page's own route path (build plan §B2). Named here,
21	// not just inlined in routes.tsx, so the "See Full History" link (RecommendedProducts' own
22	// `seeAllHref`) has one canonical value to import rather than a second hand-typed copy of this
23	// same string.
24	export const RECENTLY_VIEWED_ROUTE = '/recently-viewed';
25	
26	// SFCC-83/84 — the single source of truth for "how many Recently Viewed cards exist at once,
27	// per breakpoint." Serves two consumers that both need the same number for different reasons:
28	// (1) `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` (index.tsx) — the rail's own actual render cap. **Confirmed with
29	// Marcel (2026-09-08): a real hard cap, not a "visible before scrolling" soft limit** — the rail
30	// renders at most this many cards for the current real breakpoint and no more, full stop; a
31	// shopper cannot scroll a mobile rail to reach a 3rd or later card. This superseded the original
32	// flat `RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_MAX_ITEMS = 5` (removed) — that constant only ever capped at the
33	// single Desktop figure regardless of breakpoint, relying on the horizontal-scroll container to
34	// visually crop the rest at narrower viewports, which is the exact soft-limit behaviour Marcel's
35	// decision replaced.
36	// (2) `RecommendedProducts` — the See-Full-History link's own trigger: link
37	// shows whenever the shopper's tracked history exceeds what the rail will display at the current
38	// breakpoint. This consumer is unaffected by the cap becoming hard rather than soft — it was
39	// always asking "does more history exist than the rail shows," which reads identically either
40	// way.
41	// Values match zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts's own confirmed per-breakpoint card-width table
42	// (Mobile 201px cards × 2 = 402px full-bleed, Tablet 256px × 3 = 768px, Desktop 288px × 5 =
43	// 1440px) — restated here as counts, not re-measured. Keyed on Chakra's own breakpoint names for
44	// direct use with `useBreakpointValue`, matching the same `md`/`xl` steps the rail's own recipe
45	// uses (`breakpoints.md`/`breakpoints.xl`), not a separate breakpoint set.
46	export const RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS = { base: 2, md: 3, xl: 5 } as const;
47	
48	// Fixed 2026-09-10 (first pass), closing a real, live-confirmed bug (Figma-vs-build audit,
49	// Marcel): the negative-margin trick that lets a `RecommendedProducts` rail bleed edge-to-edge
50	// inside a `layerStyle="page"` container (PDP's Complete-the-Set/Might-Also-Like/Recently-Viewed,
51	// PLP's Recently-Viewed) previously used plain Chakra numeric spacing (`{base: -4, md: -8, lg:
52	// 0}`, i.e. -16px/-32px/0) with no relationship at all to this site's own real page padding. That
53	// real padding lives in exactly one place, `theme/foundation/gridSystem.ts`'s own
54	// `grid.containerPadding` (32px through just under 1280px, 40px from 1280px up) — the previous
55	// value cancelled only half of it on mobile (-16px against a real 32px, leaving the rail visibly
56	// inset by 16px instead of flush) and dropped to zero 288px too early (Chakra's `lg` step, 992px,
57	// a full 288px before this site's own real desktop breakpoint at 1280px). Derived directly from

Different numbers for each, and worth flagging that they don't match.

**Rail: flush up to 1560px.** The Rail's own internal `container` part is genuinely unbounded at Desktop (`maxWidth: 'none'`, confirmed via Figma) — so the Rail itself never caps. But it's nested inside PDP's `<PageContainer boxed={true}>` / PLP's `<Box layerStyle="page">`, and *both* of those set `maxWidth: 'container.xxxl'` — the base SFCC theme's own token, **1560px** (`sizes.js:16`, not something Zimmermann redefines). That outer wrapper is what actually stops growing past 1560px and centers itself; the Rail's bleed can only reach that wrapper's edge from there, not the true screen edge.

**Full History: flush up to 1440px.** This page has no `PageContainer`/`layerStyle` at all — I confirmed that directly when fixing its bleed. The only cap in the whole chain is `ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid`'s own `container` part: `GRID_CONTENT_MAX_WIDTH_DESKTOP = 1440px`, active from `breakpoints.xl` (1280px) up. That's the same 1440px the 4-column card grid's own math derives from (4×288px cards + 3×96px gaps), so it's a real, Figma-grounded value — just a *different* cap than the Rail's, sourced from a different place (the Rail's 1560px is incidental to whatever page it's embedded in; Full History's 1440px is intrinsic to its own grid).

So: **these two thresholds genuinely don't match — 1560px vs 1440px, a real 120px gap.** Below 1440px both are identically flush; between 1440px and 1560px, the Rail would still be edge-to-edge while Full History's grid has already stopped growing and centered. Given you framed Full History as "flush just like the rail," this divergence is worth a decision: leave it (each capped by what actually governs it), or make Full History's cap match the Rail's 1560px so the two behave identically at every width?

65	 *      this project's own installed Stylis (v4.2.0 — the same engine Emotion/Chakra invoke at
66	 *      runtime, confirmed by direct compilation) that a comma-separated list DOES distribute this
67	 *      recipe's generated class across every branch correctly, but four plain keys need no such
68	 *      verification to trust at a glance and are each individually addressable from a test. Only
69	 *      ONE of the four (`content` buttons) also adds `position: relative` — that element is
70	 *      `position: static` by default in its own component recipe, so a positioned ancestor is
71	 *      needed for z-index to apply at all. `close`, `carousel`, and `media` are the three

74	 *      top: 50%, ...`; `media` — its own root — via `position: relative`), so each needs (and

76	 *        - `close` — a competing `position` value previously declared alongside it had HIGHER
77	 *          specificity than Media's own rule (this rule is a class+attribute descendant selector;
78	 *          Media's is a single class) and silently won the cascade, knocking the remove button out
79	 *          of its pinned top-right corner into normal document flow (Fix 1). See the inline
80	 *          comment at that key below and index.test.tsx's "Fix 1" describe block for the proof.
81	 *        - `carousel` — Fix 3 (found during the manual real-browser check performed after the

83	 *          any automated pass). The lift rule used to target

88	 *          sets `transform: translateY(-50%)` (to vertically centre the arrow row against `slide`),
89	 *          and `transform` unconditionally creates a NEW stacking context on that element,
90	 *          regardless of its `position`/`z-index`. That traps each arrow button's `zIndex: 1`
91	 *          *inside* the carousel wrapper's own stacking context — it only wins ordering battles
92	 *          against the *other* arrow button, never against anything outside `carousel` (like the
93	 *          content overlay), because the whole `carousel` box is itself just an ordinary
94	 *          z-index:auto participant one level up — and, being earlier in DOM order than
95	 *          `[data-card-slot="content"]`, it lost. Moving the lift to the `carousel` WRAPPER itself
96	 *          (already `position: absolute` from Media's own recipe, so only `zIndex: 1` is needed
97	 *          here, same as `close`) fixes this: the wrapper's own stacking context — not one buried

461	          // focus landing on ANY descendant control (name link, bag button, size chip) triggers
462	          // the reveal — mirroring zimmSearchInput.css.ts's container/zimmFormRow's own
463	          // `_focusWithin` sibling to `_hover`.
464	          // Fix H (live-browser check after the arrow reveal shipped): plain `:focus-within`
465	          // does not distinguish a real Tab-focused descendant from one that only has focus
466	          // because the user *clicked* it with a mouse — most browsers give a `<button>` real
467	          // DOM focus on click, so clicking any interactive control inside the card (an arrow,
468	          // a size chip, notify-me) left `:focus-within` true, and therefore every reveal below
469	          // stuck open, until focus moved elsewhere entirely (e.g. a click outside the card) —
470	          // moving the mouse back out was not enough. `:has(:focus-visible)` fixes this: it only
471	          // matches when the browser's own focus-visible heuristic says a *keyboard* focus ring
472	          // is warranted, which excludes a mouse-click-focused `<button>` in every evergreen
473	          // engine but still matches genuine Tab navigation — so the keyboard case Fix 2 exists
474	          // for keeps working, and the mouse-click case that produced the stuck-open bug does
475	          // not. `:has()` is not used anywhere else in this codebase yet; it is fully covered by
476	          // this project's own browserslist (`iOS >= 17`, `Android >= 14`, `last 4 ChromeAndroid
477	          // versions`), all far past `:has()`'s 2022/2023 shipping baseline. Expressed as a
478	          // separate string key (not a comma-joined `'&:hover, &:has(:focus-visible) ...'`
479	          // selector) to match this file's own established idiom; raw selector strings are used
480	          // throughout rather than a Chakra shorthand prop because the descendant-combinator
481	          // path has to be baked into the selector itself, and Chakra has no `:has()` shorthand.
482	          // Fix J: was `display: 'block'` — converted alongside the `&:hover` entry above; see
483	          // docblock point 3/6 for why `display` no longer expresses this at all.
484	          [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {
485	            position: 'static',
486	            clipPath: 'none',
487	          },
488	        }),
489	        ...(hoverHidesPrice && {
490	          // PLP/Wishlist: price is visible by default (no unconditional rule needed above) and
491	          // hides only here, in favour of the size-selector reveal alongside it. Fix J: both
492	          // entries below were `display: 'none'` — see docblock point 3/6.
493	          [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {
494	            position: 'absolute',
495	            clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
496	          },
497	          // Fix 2 / Fix H — see the hoverRevealsPrice block above for the full rationale.
498	          // Keyboard focus anywhere in the card must hide price in favour of the size-selector
499	          // exactly as hover does, so a keyboard user sees the identical revealed state, not a
500	          // different partial one; `:has(:focus-visible)` keeps that true while no longer
501	          // sticking open after a mouse click.
502	          [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {
503	            position: 'absolute',
504	            clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
505	          },
506	        }),
507	        ...(hoverRevealsSizeSelector && {
508	          // Fix K (see the unconditional block above for the full narrative): a hover-capable
509	          // pointer overrides the `display: 'none'` above with the Fix J clip-path technique —
510	          // this pointer type genuinely CAN reveal the content below, so it needs to stay in the
511	          // DOM/tab order while merely not-yet-revealed, for the same VoiceOver/AT reason Fix J
512	          // exists at all. `display: 'flex'` matches ZimmSizeChipGroup's own natural root display
513	          // (zimmSizeChipGroup.css.ts's `radiogroup`/`oneSize` parts) — `position`/`clipPath` are
514	          // the only properties the reveal pair below needs to toggle.
515	          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: {
516	            display: 'flex',
517	            position: 'absolute',
518	            clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
519	          },
520	          // ...and is only revealed here, matching the price swap alongside it. Fix J: both
521	          // entries below were `display: 'block'` — see docblock point 3/6.
522	          [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: {
523	            position: 'static',
524	            clipPath: 'none',
525	          },
526	          // Fix 2 / Fix H — see the hoverRevealsPrice block above for the full rationale.
527	          [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: {
528	            position: 'static',
529	            clipPath: 'none',
530	          },
531	        }),
532	        // Fix C — see docblock point 4. Both the "hidden by default" declaration AND its reveal
533	        // live inside this same media-query block (unlike price/the size-selector above, whose
534	        // "hidden by default" half is unconditional): a touch pointer never matches this query at
535	        // all, so it never sees the hidden rule below either, leaving notify-me at its natural
536	        // (visible) default — exactly the unconditional visibility every Mobile Unavailable
537	        // reference confirms. Fix J: all three declarations below were `display: 'none'`/
538	        // `'block'` — converted together, same reasoning as the price/size-selector pair above.
539	        ...(hoverRevealsNotifyMe && {
540	          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.notifyMe}"]`]: {
541	            position: 'absolute',
542	            clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
543	          },
544	          [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.notifyMe}"]`]: {
545	            position: 'static',
546	            clipPath: 'none',
547	          },
548	          // Fix 2 / Fix H — see the hoverRevealsPrice block above for the full rationale.
549	          [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.notifyMe}"]`]: {
550	            position: 'static',
551	            clipPath: 'none',
552	          },
553	        }),
554	
555	        // 6. Carousel arrow reveal — see docblock point 6. Unconditional (no
556	        // `ZimmProductCardStyleProps` flag gates it): desktop prev/next arrows behave identically
557	        // across every variation whenever a card has more than one image. Confirmed against the
558	        // Jira AC ("when on desktop and the user hovers, then the arrows appear") and live Figma:
559	        // the Carousel element is `hidden="true"` on every Default-state instance checked, visible
560	        // only on the matching Hover-state instance, for both PLP and Wishlist.
561	        // `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s own `[HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]: { display: 'flex' }` used to
562	        // reveal this permanently on any hover-capable device (a device-capability check, not an
563	        // actual-hover one) — removed entirely there; this pair is now the only reveal path left,
564	        // the same `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)` shape as the price/size-selector swap above.
565	        // Fix J: `display: 'flex'` stays here (unlike the other four sites' reveal rules, which
566	        // drop `display` entirely) — `clipPath: 'none'` is ADDED alongside it, not instead of it.
567	        // See docblock point 6's own Fix J note for why: this part needs `display: flex` for its
568	        // own `justifyContent`/`alignItems` layout, and nothing else asserts that once
569	        // `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s own unconditional `display: 'none'` is replaced by
570	        // `clipPath`. `position` is deliberately absent from both entries below, also unlike the
571	        // other four sites: this part is `position: 'absolute'` unconditionally already (Media's
572	        // own vertical-centring rule), and toggling it to `'static'` here would break that
573	        // centring the instant the arrows are revealed.
574	        //
575	        // Fix K (CodeRabbit finding on PR #85, verified correct before fixing): a hover-capable
576	        // pointer needs its OWN not-yet-revealed base state here — `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s
577	        // own `carousel` part reverted to an unconditional `display: 'none'` (Fix K there), which a
578	        // hover-capable pointer must override to `flex`/clipped before `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)`
579	        // below can reveal it at all; without this, the arrows never render even on desktop. Touch
580	        // pointers never enter this media query, so they correctly keep the unconditional
581	        // `display: 'none'` and never become tab stops for a control they can never reveal.
582	        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
583	          display: 'flex',
584	          clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
585	        },
586	        [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
587	          display: 'flex',
588	          clipPath: 'none',
589	        },
590	        // Fix J belt-and-braces (see docblock point 6 and the new lift-adjacent rule in point 2
591	        // above): re-enables the arrow buttons' hit-testing only once genuinely revealed.
592	        [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"] button`]: {
593	          pointerEvents: 'auto',
594	        },
595	        [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
596	          display: 'flex',
597	          clipPath: 'none',
598	        },
599	        [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"] button`]: {
600	          pointerEvents: 'auto',
601	        },
602	      },
603	
604	      // 5. PLP-only bag-icon mobile hide — see docblock point 5. A separate, sibling media-query
605	      // key from HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY above (a viewport-width gate, not a pointer-capability one).
606	      // Mobile-first: hidden by default, shown again from the shared [DESKTOP_QUERY] block below.
607	      ...(hideBagOnMobile && {
608	        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.bag}"]`]: { display: 'none' },
609	      }),
610	
611	      // Fix F+D's shared desktop-reveal block — deliberately ONE `[DESKTOP_QUERY]` object key,
612	      // not two. A first version of this recipe gave `sizeSelectorUnavailable` and
613	      // `hideBagOnMobile` each their OWN separate `...(condition && { [DESKTOP_QUERY]: {...} })`
614	      // spread (mirroring how every other flag in this file gets its own independent spread) —
615	      // which silently broke, because both spreads produce a property with the exact same
616	      // *computed key string* (`'@media (min-width: 48em)'`) on the same `root` object. Object
617	      // spread is a SHALLOW merge: it does not deep-merge two spreads that happen to share a key,
618	      // it just lets whichever spread comes LAST overwrite the earlier one's value entirely. With
619	      // `hideBagOnMobile`'s spread positioned after `sizeSelectorUnavailable`'s in this file, its
620	      // `[DESKTOP_QUERY]` object silently replaced the other's, and the price-reveal-on-desktop
621	      // rule vanished from the actual emitted CSS — confirmed for real via
622	      // `document.styleSheets` in a live browser (price stayed `display: none` at 1280px width
623	      // despite `window.matchMedia('(min-width: 48em)').matches` correctly reporting `true`);
624	      // every jsdom test still passed, because each one only ever sets ONE of the two colliding
625	      // flags at a time, never the realistic combination a genuine unavailable PLP card produces.
626	      // `[HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]` above never had this problem because it was always written as a
627	      // single key with every contributing condition spread INSIDE it — this block now follows
628	      // that same shape.
629	      [DESKTOP_QUERY]: {
630	        ...(sizeSelectorUnavailable && {
631	          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: { display: 'block' },
632	        }),
633	        ...(hideBagOnMobile && {
634	          // 'flex', not 'block': ZimmProductCardContent's own `bagWrapper` part sets
635	          // `display: 'flex'` (it centres the icon inside via alignItems/justifyContent) — this
636	          // organism's `[data-card-slot="content"] [data-card-slot="bag"]` selector has higher
637	          // specificity (a class + two attribute selectors vs. Content's own single class) and
638	          // would win the cascade either way, so restoring the actual display type Content uses
639	          // matters here, not just "anything visible" — 'block' would silently flatten that
640	          // wrapper's centering.
641	          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.bag}"]`]: { display: 'flex' },
642	        }),
643	      },
644	    },
645	  }),
646	};

import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';
import { CARD_SLOT, HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY, DESKTOP_QUERY } from '../../zimmProductCardShared';

/**
 * Same hover-capable-pointer gate `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts` already establishes for its own
 * arrows/indicator split — now a shared import from `zimmProductCardShared.ts` rather than each
 * file's own module-private copy, so the two can't silently drift. Governs the price <->
 * size-selector swap below, so both composed children's hover treatments engage together off the
 * exact same media feature, on this shared root.
 */

/**
 * A viewport-width gate, unrelated to `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` above — governs the PLP-only bag-icon
 * mobile hide (Fix D, SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit) below. Also a shared import from
 * `zimmProductCardShared.ts`, same reasoning as `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` above: this and
 * `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`'s own `root` padding step both need the identical `min-width`
 * gate, and a module-private copy in each file was exactly the drift risk this extraction removes.
 */

type ZimmProductCardStyleProps = {
  /** Home only — see VARIATION_CONFIG in index.tsx. Price is hidden at every breakpoint/pointer
   *  type by default and only appears once a hover-capable pointer actually hovers the card. */
  hoverRevealsPrice?: boolean;
  /** PLP + Wishlist — price is visible by default (Content's own natural rendering; no override
   *  needed for that half) and hides only once a hover-capable pointer hovers the card. */
  hoverHidesPrice?: boolean;
  /** PLP + Wishlist — the size-chip picker is hidden at every breakpoint/pointer type by default
   *  and only appears once a hover-capable pointer actually hovers the card, in the same
   *  media-query gate as the price swap above so both engage together. */
  hoverRevealsSizeSelector?: boolean;
  /** Fix C — true whenever ZimmProductCardContent actually mounted a notify-me button
   *  (`isUnavailable && onNotifyMe`, computed once in index.tsx as `showNotifyMe`). Unlike the two
   *  flags above, the "hidden by default" half lives INSIDE `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`, not outside it
   *  — see docblock point 4: a touch pointer must see notify-me unconditionally (confirmed via
   *  every Mobile Unavailable Figma reference), where price/the size-selector do the opposite. */
  hoverRevealsNotifyMe?: boolean;
  /** Fix C — true for a PLP/Wishlist card that would normally hover-swap to the size-selector
   *  (`config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector`) but is out of stock. Unlike every other flag here, this
   *  is not a pointer-type concern at all: the size-chip wrapper stays hidden permanently, in
   *  every state, on every device — see docblock point 4. */
  sizeSelectorUnavailable?: boolean;
  /** Fix D — PLP only (`VARIATION_CONFIG.plp.hideBagOnMobile` in index.tsx). A viewport-width
   *  concern, not a pointer-type one: hidden below `breakpoints.md`, visible from it up — see
   *  docblock point 5. */
  hideBagOnMobile?: boolean;
};

/**
 * Recipe for the product-card organism (ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard) — composes
 * ZimmProductCardMedia (Step 4) and ZimmProductCardContent (Step 5) with no styling of its own
 * for either child. This recipe's entire job is the cross-component concerns neither child can
 * own by itself:
 *
 *   1. THE STRETCHED-LINK OVERLAY. ZimmProductCardContent's `nameLink` renders the one real `<a>`
 *      in the whole composed tree. Its `::after` is stretched to `inset: 0` against THIS
 *      component's own `root` — the nearest positioned ancestor. Confirmed by reading
 *      `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts` directly: neither its `root` nor `nameRow`, `nameLink`, or
 *      any other part sets `position` anywhere in that file, so nothing between the `<a>` and
 *      this `root` intercepts the containing-block chain. (`ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `root`
 *      IS `position: relative`, but Media is a *sibling* of Content under this organism's root,
 *      never an ancestor of Content's `<a>`, so it has no bearing on this chain.)
 *   2. LIFTING EVERY OTHER INTERACTIVE CONTROL above that overlay — a z-index higher than the
 *      overlay's own (left unset), or the invisible overlay would intercept their clicks first.
 *      Four separate, single-selector keys rather than one comma-joined selector: verified via
 *      this project's own installed Stylis (v4.2.0 — the same engine Emotion/Chakra invoke at
 *      runtime, confirmed by direct compilation) that a comma-separated list DOES distribute this
 *      recipe's generated class across every branch correctly, but four plain keys need no such
 *      verification to trust at a glance and are each individually addressable from a test. Only
 *      ONE of the four (`content` buttons) also adds `position: relative` — that element is
 *      `position: static` by default in its own component recipe, so a positioned ancestor is
 *      needed for z-index to apply at all. `close`, `carousel`, and `media` are the three
 *      exceptions: `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own recipe already positions each of them directly
 *      (`close` via `position: absolute, top: 0, right: 0`; `carousel` via `position: absolute,
 *      top: 50%, ...`; `media` — its own root — via `position: relative`), so each needs (and
 *      gets) only the z-index bump here:
 *        - `close` — a competing `position` value previously declared alongside it had HIGHER
 *          specificity than Media's own rule (this rule is a class+attribute descendant selector;
 *          Media's is a single class) and silently won the cascade, knocking the remove button out
 *          of its pinned top-right corner into normal document flow (Fix 1). See the inline
 *          comment at that key below and index.test.tsx's "Fix 1" describe block for the proof.
 *        - `carousel` — Fix 3 (found during the manual real-browser check performed after the
 *          round-2 Scorer PASS, which explicitly flagged that check as still outstanding, not by
 *          any automated pass). The lift rule used to target
 *          `'[data-card-slot="carousel"] button'` — the two arrow BUTTONS individually, each given
 *          its own `position: relative, zIndex: 1` — identical in shape to the `content button`
 *          rule above, and every jsdom test passed. A real click in a real browser still landed on
 *          the overlay, not the arrow. Root cause: `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `carousel` part
 *          sets `transform: translateY(-50%)` (to vertically centre the arrow row against `slide`),
 *          and `transform` unconditionally creates a NEW stacking context on that element,
 *          regardless of its `position`/`z-index`. That traps each arrow button's `zIndex: 1`
 *          *inside* the carousel wrapper's own stacking context — it only wins ordering battles
 *          against the *other* arrow button, never against anything outside `carousel` (like the
 *          content overlay), because the whole `carousel` box is itself just an ordinary
 *          z-index:auto participant one level up — and, being earlier in DOM order than
 *          `[data-card-slot="content"]`, it lost. Moving the lift to the `carousel` WRAPPER itself
 *          (already `position: absolute` from Media's own recipe, so only `zIndex: 1` is needed
 *          here, same as `close`) fixes this: the wrapper's own stacking context — not one buried
 *          inside it — is what gets compared against the overlay, and it wins outright, carrying
 *          both arrow buttons above the overlay with it. This is exactly the gap
 *          index.test.tsx's own "KNOWN LIMITATION" docblock warns about — jsdom resolves no
 *          stacking contexts at all, so this shipped past every automated check and was only
 *          found by a real click in a real browser. See index.test.tsx's "Fix 3" describe block.
 *        - `media` — Fix I (SFCC-236, found via a real mobile-device touch-swipe check performed
 *          after this branch's own live testing round, not by any automated pass). The media/
 *          gallery scroll region itself was never added to this lift list, even though it is
 *          exactly as interactive as the controls nested inside it: with no z-index of its own,
 *          `[data-card-slot="media"]` sat at the same default/auto stacking layer the overlay
 *          itself occupies, so a touch swipe starting on the image landed on the invisible
 *          overlay `<a>` first and the real scroll container underneath never received the
 *          gesture — the slide indicator still rendered correctly (proving the image data/gallery
 *          logic was fine), but nothing paged. Missed earlier because `close`/`carousel`/content-
 *          buttons were each checked with a real CLICK (Fix 1, Fix 3 above) — and a click on the
 *          image happened to "work" by accident either way, since it also landed on the overlay
 *          `<a>` and still navigated to the PDP — so nothing about a plain tap ever surfaced this;
 *          only a real SWIPE (which needs the scroll container itself, not the overlay, to be the
 *          hit target) exposed the gap. `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own root is already `position:
 *          relative` (its own recipe), so, same as `close`/`carousel`, only the z-index bump is
 *          needed here — plus `cursor: 'pointer'`, since this element is no longer inside the
 *          `<a>` that used to convey that affordance via the browser's default link cursor. Fixing
 *          this the same way used to fix `close`/`carousel` necessarily breaks the accidental
 *          click-still-navigates behaviour described above (media no longer lets the click reach
 *          the overlay at all) — restored deliberately via a real `onClick` on
 *          `ZimmProductCardMedia` instead of relying on the overlay by accident: see index.tsx's
 *          own docblock for the click-passthrough narrative, and its `handleMediaClick`, which
 *          guards the two arrow buttons and the remove/close button (all real `<button>`
 *          descendants of `media`) so they keep doing only their own thing.
 *   3. THE HOVER-REVEAL SWAP between price and the PLP/Wishlist size-selector (and Home's
 *      hidden-by-default price), gated by the same `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` query
 *      `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts` already uses for its own arrows/indicator split. Each reveal
 *      rule fires on `:hover` OR `:has(:focus-visible)` on this same root (Fix 2 rework below,
 *      superseded by Fix H — see point 6) — `:hover` alone would leave every reveal permanently
 *      unreachable by keyboard on a hover-capable device.
 *
 *      Fix J (SFCC-236, this fix — full defect + fix write-up lives at the end of point 6):
 *      "hidden" and "revealed" are expressed via `position`/`clipPath`, not `display`, at every
 *      site in this block. `display: 'none'` used to mean "hidden" here, but `display: none`
 *      unconditionally strips an element from the accessibility tree, not just from paint — see
 *      point 6's own Fix J note for the full defect this caused. Hidden is now `position:
 *      'absolute', clipPath: 'inset(50%)'` (out of flow, paints nothing — identical visual/layout
 *      footprint to `display: none` — but stays in the DOM, tab order, and accessibility tree);
 *      revealed is `position: 'static', clipPath: 'none'` (back in normal flow, painted again) —
 *      the exact technique `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx` already ships for its own off-page
 *      swatches. The trigger selectors themselves (`:hover`, `:has(:focus-visible)`) are
 *      byte-for-byte unchanged by Fix J — only the property values inside these blocks changed.
 *   4. NOTIFY-ME'S HOVER GATE (Fix C, found during the SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit against the
 *      real Figma Default+Hover Unavailable instances for all three variations, desktop AND
 *      mobile). Three behaviours confirmed together, all different from point 3 above:
 *        - `isUnavailable` suppresses the PLP/Wishlist size-selector swap entirely (index.tsx
 *          AND-s `hoverHidesPrice`/`hoverRevealsSizeSelector` with `!isUnavailable` before they
 *          ever reach this recipe) — there is nothing to pick for an out-of-stock item, so price
 *          stays visible on hover instead of being replaced. Home's own `hoverRevealsPrice` is
 *          untouched by this — its Unavailable Hover reference still reveals price normally.
 *        - Suppressing that swap is not, by itself, enough to reproduce the reference: with no
 *          hide/reveal pair of its own, the size-chip wrapper falls back to Content's natural
 *          (visible) default and would show permanently — briefly shipped exactly that way mid-fix
 *          and caught by re-checking the real render against Figma, which shows size chips hidden
 *          in BOTH states when unavailable, not merely "not swapped in on hover". `sizeSelectorUnavailable`
 *          (index.tsx: `config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector && isUnavailable`) carries that permanent
 *          hide as its own unconditional rule below — deliberately outside `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`
 *          entirely, since unlike everything else here this isn't a pointer-type distinction at
 *          all: every device sees it hidden, full stop.
 *        - Notify-me itself is hover-gated the OPPOSITE way round from price/the size-selector:
 *          hidden by default and revealed on hover **only inside `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`**, not
 *          unconditionally. Every Desktop Unavailable+Hover reference shows it appearing only on
 *          hover; every Mobile Unavailable reference (Mobile has no Hover variant at all, so
 *          whatever it shows is the only state a touch pointer ever sees) shows it plainly with no
 *          reveal needed. Putting the "hidden by default" half outside the media query — matching
 *          point 3's own structure literally — would have made notify-me permanently invisible on
 *          touch, since a touch pointer never matches `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` and so could never
 *          trigger the `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)` half either.
 *   5. THE BAG ICON'S PLP-ONLY MOBILE HIDE (Fix D, same SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit). A genuinely
 *      different axis from points 3-4 above: `DESKTOP_QUERY` is a **viewport-width** media query
 *      (`min-width`), not `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`'s pointer-capability one — a large touch tablet and
 *      a small hover-capable laptop window need to agree with Figma's own Desktop/Mobile split by
 *      width, not by input method. Figma's PLP/PDP Mobile Card-content instance
 *      (`40002163:41479`) has the bag icon's `Icons` frame `hidden="true"`; Desktop's own PLP
 *      instance and Wishlist's Mobile instance (`40002187:58472`) both leave it visible — so this
 *      is `hideBagOnMobile`, one boolean `index.tsx` derives from TWO separate per-variation
 *      config fields (`hideBagOnMobile` proper, PLP's own unconditional rule; and

        // below can reveal it at all; without this, the arrows never render even on desktop. Touch

        // `display: 'none'` and never become tab stops for a control they can never reveal.

          display: 'flex',
          clipPath: 'inset(50%)',

      // spread (mirroring how every other flag in this file gets its own independent spread) —

      // single key with every contributing condition spread INSIDE it — this block now follows

          // `display: 'flex'` (it centres the icon inside via alignItems/justifyContent) — this

          // wrapper's centering.
          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.bag}"]`]: { display: 'flex' },
        }),
      },
    },
  }),

content.text:
Yes — both are genuinely fluid within each breakpoint tier, not just snapping between fixed sizes.

**Rail:** cards are percentage-width (`50%`/`33.33%`/`20%`, computed as `100% ÷ cap`), so as the viewport resizes *within* a tier, each card's actual pixel width scales continuously and proportionally with it — not discrete steps. The width share itself, and the visible-card cap (2/3/5), only jump at the three confirmed breakpoints (768px, 1024px). There's one floor: `min-width: 200px` on Mobile/Tablet, so below roughly 400px container width (200px × 2 cards) the row stops shrinking further and will overflow instead — the one already-flagged, accepted edge case from earlier.

**Full History:** same principle, different mechanism — CSS Grid `1fr` columns, which are inherently fluid; each card's width falls out of whatever's left after the fixed per-breakpoint gap (40/80/96px) is subtracted, continuously as the viewport changes. Column count (2/3/4) jumps at the confirmed breakpoints (768px, 1280px).

Same "push past the frame" trick as before, but this time I grabbed the wrong recipe for it.

Picture two rooms. Room A (PDP/PLP) has a picture hanging inside a frame, and that frame sits on top of a second, bigger mounting board — two layers between the picture and the wall. Room B (Full History) just has the picture pinned straight to the wall — only one layer, no mounting board at all.

Earlier, I built a "push the picture out past everything" instruction sized specifically for Room A's two layers (frame + board). Then, when I fixed Full History, I grabbed that *same* two-layer instruction and used it in Room B — which only ever had one layer to push past. So the picture got shoved exactly as far as it needed to clear two layers, in a room that only had one — and since there was nothing there to stop it, it kept going right past the wall's own edge and hung off the side. That's the "wider than the screen" you saw in the screenshots.

The fix was just building a *second*, smaller "push past one layer only" instruction and using that one in Room B instead — same trick, correctly sized to the room it's actually being used in.

content.text:
Dev servers use hot-reloading — pushing code changes into the already-running page without a full reload, to save time. That works reliably for a component's own render logic, but is less consistent for a shared constants file (like `app/constants/index.ts`) that other files import a value from. The dev server can correctly rebuild the file, but the browser tab already has an older copy of that module loaded in memory, and the hot-swap doesn't always correctly propagate through every file that imported a value from it — so the page kept running on the old, cached `PAGE_CONTENT_BLEED_MX`-shaped behavior even though the source had already changed to `APP_MAIN_BLEED_MX`.

A hard refresh throws away that in-memory state and the browser's HTTP cache entirely, and loads everything fresh from the dev server — which is why it started working immediately once you did that.

Good takeaway for the rest of this build: whenever a fix touches a shared constants/token file rather than just a component's own recipe, a hard refresh before concluding pass/fail is worth doing first — this is the second time in this session a "not working" report turned out to be a stale build rather than the actual fix.

169	  const match = /^(\d+)\./.exec(filename);
170	  return match ? Number(match[1]) : undefined;
171	};
172	
173	/** Stable sort by `extractImageSequenceNumber` (guaranteed stable since ES2019) — images with no
174	 *  numeric filename compare equal and keep their original relative order. */
175	const sortByImageSequence = (images: ZimmProductCardImage[]): ZimmProductCardImage[] =>
176	  [...images].sort((a, b) => {
177	    const numA = extractImageSequenceNumber(a.src);
178	    const numB = extractImageSequenceNumber(b.src);
179	    if (numA === undefined || numB === undefined) return 0;
180	    return numA - numB;
181	  });

184	 * `getPriceData`'s own return shape (base SFCC, `product-utils.js:123-170`, confirmed by reading
185	 * it directly), narrowed to the three fields this mapper reads. `@salesforce/retail-react-app`

193	 * assigning `any` to any narrower type with no check, so the real correctness proof is the test
194	 * file's own direct comparison against a real `getPriceData` call, not this annotation alone.
195	 */
196	type SfccPriceData = {
197	  /** `findLowestPrice()`'s own `minPrice` — never `product.price` directly. This is the field
198	   *  `productListCardMapper.ts` does not use for its own `currentPrice` (it reads the flat
199	   *  `hit.price` field instead) — see this module's own docblock for why that risks disagreeing
200	   *  with a `getPriceData`-derived `originalPrice` on a multi-variant product. */
201	  currentPrice: number;
202	  /** The highest tiered price found — "was" price. `undefined` when the product has no
203	   *  `tieredPrices` at all (there is then no maximum to compute). */
204	  listPrice: number | undefined;
205	  /** `currentPrice < listPrice` — always `false`, never `true`, when `listPrice` is `undefined`
206	   *  (a numeric comparison against `undefined` evaluates to `false` in JS, never throws). */

208	};
209	
210	/** The real `imageGroups[].images[]` element shape (`commerce-sdk-isomorphic`'s own
211	 *  `ShopperProductsTypes.Image`) — named `RawImage` to match `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own
212	 *  local name for the equivalent concept, but pointed at the real SDK type rather than that
213	 *  file's hand-rolled shape (AGENTS.md > Type Definitions: don't re-declare a type the SDK
214	 *  already exports). */
215	type RawImage = ShopperProductsTypes.Image;
216	
217	const toCardImage = (image: RawImage | undefined): ZimmProductCardImage | undefined => {
218	  const src = image?.disBaseLink ?? image?.link;
219	  if (!src) return undefined;
220	  return { src, alt: image?.alt ?? '' };
221	};
222	
223	/**
224	 * The colour + `medium`-viewtype-scoped image list this product's card uses — one lookup feeding
225	 * four separate things below (`primaryImage`, the gallery, the hover-swap image, and the
226	 * broken-image fallback candidates), so none of them can ever disagree with each other or with the
227	 * resolved colour. Ported near-verbatim from `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own
228	 * `selectColourScopedImages`, re-pointed at `product.imageGroups` (the plain `getProducts` shape)
229	 * in place of a `ProductSearchHit`'s own same-named field — the underlying `ImageGroup`/`Image`
230	 * types are identical either way (confirmed directly against
231	 * `node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts`).
232	 *
233	 * **Two-pass, not one** — same real bug as `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own version closes: a
234	 * strict colour-scoped `filterImageGroups` match requires the group to explicitly declare a
235	 * matching `variationAttributes` entry, but a single-colour product's medium group commonly
236	 * carries no `variationAttributes` at all (nothing to disambiguate), which would make a
237	 * colour-scoped-only lookup exclude the group and return nothing. Falls back to a viewtype-only
238	 * match in that case. Never the reverse — a real colour-scoped match never falls back further, to
239	 * avoid re-mixing colours.
240	 */
241	const selectColourScopedImages = (
242	  product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct,
243	  colour: string | undefined,
244	): ZimmProductCardImage[] => {
245	  const colourScopedGroups = colour
246	    ? (filterImageGroups(product.imageGroups ?? [], {
247	        viewType: MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE,
248	        variationValues: { [COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID]: colour },
249	      }) as ShopperProductsTypes.ImageGroup[])
250	    : [];
251	
252	  const groups =
253	    colourScopedGroups.length > 0
254	      ? colourScopedGroups
255	      : (filterImageGroups(product.imageGroups ?? [], {
256	          viewType: MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE,
257	        }) as ShopperProductsTypes.ImageGroup[]);
258	
259	  const images = (groups[0]?.images ?? [])
260	    .map(toCardImage)
261	    .filter((image): image is ZimmProductCardImage => Boolean(image));
262	
263	  return sortByImageSequence(images);
264	};
265	
266	/**
267	 * Picks this product's gallery from the colour-scoped image list above — matches
268	 * `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own "no gallery" contract for 0 or 1 images (returns `undefined`, never
269	 * a 1-length array). Kept exported and independently tested, same as
270	 * `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `selectGalleryImages` — `selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard`

272	 * `primaryImage`/`primaryImageFallbacks`/`hoverImage`/`images` at once), matching that file's own
273	 * documented, deliberate minor redundancy rather than introducing a new one.
274	 */
275	export const selectGalleryImages = (product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct): ZimmProductCardImage[] | undefined => {
276	  const images = selectColourScopedImages(product, resolveViewedColour(product));
277	  return images.length > 1 ? images : undefined;
278	};
279	
280	/**
281	 * Reads the "size" variation attribute (if this product has one) into the shape
282	 * `ZimmSizeChipGroup` expects. Ported near-verbatim from `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own
283	 * `selectSizeChipValues`, re-pointed at `product.variationAttributes` directly — `orderable` on
284	 * each value already reflects real stock for that specific size, so it maps directly to
285	 * `isDisabled` with no extra lookup needed.
286	 */
287	export const selectSizeChipValues = (product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct): ZimmSizeChipValue[] => {
288	  const sizeAttribute = product.variationAttributes?.find((attr) => attr.id === SIZE_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID);

290	    value: value.value,
291	    label: value.name ?? value.value,
292	    isDisabled: value.orderable === false,
293	  }));
294	};
295	
296	/** What `resolveOrderableVariant` resolves a selected size chip value to — same shape, same
297	 *  reasoning, as `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `ResolvedVariant`: the real, orderable SKU for
298	 *  that specific size, not the master id this product otherwise defaults to. */
299	export type ResolvedVariant = {
300	  productId: string;
301	  price: number | undefined;
302	  orderable: boolean;
303	};
304	
305	/**
306	 * Resolves a selected size CHIP VALUE to its real orderable variant — ported near-verbatim from
307	 * `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `resolveOrderableVariant`, re-pointed at this input's own
308	 * `variants` field (identical shape either way — both are `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` `Variant`
309	 * types). Returns `null` when there is no matching variant at all — callers fall back to this
310	 * product's own default id/price in that case, the same default that already existed before
311	 * size-aware Add to Bag was ever selectable.
312	 */
313	export const resolveOrderableVariant = (
314	  product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct,
315	  sizeValue: string,
316	): ResolvedVariant | null => {
317	  const variant = product.variants?.find((candidate) => candidate.variationValues?.size === sizeValue);
318	  if (!variant) return null;
319	
320	  return {
321	    productId: variant.productId,
322	    price: variant.price,
323	    orderable: variant.orderable !== false,
324	  };
325	};
326	
327	/**
328	 * Derives `currentPrice`/`originalPrice` from a single `getPriceData(product)` call — see this
329	 * module's own docblock for why both must come from the same call rather than mixing a flat
330	 * `product.price` field for one and `getPriceData` for the other. No `opts` passed — the default
331	 * `quantity: 1` is correct for a single-unit card display (matches `variantScopedPrice.ts`'s own
332	 * no-opts calls for the same reason). No hardcoded fallback currency — if either the price or the
333	 * currency is absent, formatting is skipped rather than guessed, matching `productInfo.ts`'s and
334	 * `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s own "no hardcoded fallback currency" rule.
335	 */
336	const selectPriceFields = (
337	  product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct,
338	  formatPrice: FormatPrice,
339	): Pick<RecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard, 'currentPrice' | 'originalPrice'> => {
340	  const priceData: SfccPriceData = getPriceData(product);
341	
342	  const currentPrice =
343	    typeof priceData.currentPrice === 'number' && product.currency
344	      ? formatPrice(priceData.currentPrice, product.currency)
345	      : undefined;
346	
347	  // Only set when isOnSale is true -- a not-on-sale product must not render a crossed-out price
348	  // identical to its current one.
349	  const originalPrice =
350	    priceData.isOnSale && typeof priceData.listPrice === 'number' && product.currency
351	      ? formatPrice(priceData.listPrice, product.currency)
352	      : undefined;
353	
354	  return { currentPrice, originalPrice };
355	};
356	
357	/**
358	 * @param product - A plain Commerce API product from `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts`'s own
359	 *   `getProducts` call, or `undefined`/`null` while that data is not yet available.
360	 * @param formatPrice - Currency formatter, normally `intl.formatNumber`.
361	 * @returns Props for the `plp`-variation `ZimmProductCard`, or `null` when the product has no
362	 *   usable name or no usable image — never a broken card, never a throw. Same hard-gate contract
363	 *   as `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s own `selectRecentlyViewedCard`. `onAddToBag`/`selectedSizeChipValue`/
364	 *   `onSizeChipSelect` are deliberately not populated here — same split
365	 *   `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `ProductListCardResult` documents: this mapper is a pure data
366	 *   function with no per-card selection state of its own, so the page container wires those three
367	 *   (see `overrides/app/pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx`'s own per-card size-chip state).
368	 */
369	export const selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard = (
370	  product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct | undefined | null,
371	  formatPrice: FormatPrice,
372	): RecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard | null => {
373	  if (!product?.name) return null;
374	
375	  // One resolution feeds primaryImage, the gallery, the hover-swap image, and the broken-image
376	  // fallback candidates below — see selectColourScopedImages's own docblock for why.
377	  const scopedImages = selectColourScopedImages(product, resolveViewedColour(product));
378	  const [firstImage] = scopedImages;
379	  if (!firstImage) return null;
380	
381	  // Required-non-empty alt for the primary position only — mirrors this mapper's own established
382	  // fallback (and recentlyViewedCard.ts's identical one) exactly. The rest of scopedImages keeps
383	  // toCardImage's plain alt (matching productListCardMapper.ts's own gallery images, which get no
384	  // such treatment either) since only the primary slot ever carried this extra safeguard.
385	  const primaryImage: ZimmProductCardImage = { ...firstImage, alt: firstImage.alt || product.name };
386	
387	  const { currentPrice, originalPrice } = selectPriceFields(product, formatPrice);
388	
389	  return {
390	    id: product.id,
391	    href: productUrlBuilder({ id: product.id }),
392	    name: product.name,
393	    headingLevel: 'h3',
394	    primaryImage,
395	    // Ordered backup candidates if primaryImage itself fails to load — same real, live defect
396	    // productListCardMapper.ts's own primaryImageFallbacks closes.
397	    primaryImageFallbacks: scopedImages,
398	    // The second image in the same colour-scoped sequence — revealed on hover. undefined when
399	    // there is no second image, which ZimmProductCardMedia already treats as "no swap".
400	    hoverImage: scopedImages[1],
401	    images: scopedImages.length > 1 ? scopedImages : undefined,
402	    currentPrice,
403	    originalPrice,
404	    // product.master is this master product's own overall orderability (ShopperProductsTypes.Master
405	    // — confirmed via the SDK's own type) — the equivalent of productListCardMapper.ts's flat
406	    // hit.orderable for this input shape, which has no such flat field of its own.
407	    isUnavailable: product.master?.orderable === false,
408	    // Single highest-priority badge -- confirmed live, 2026-09-09 (see this module's own docblock's
409	    // "Badge" section). SFCC-225's own hook already sorts c_productBadges by badgePriorityOrder
410	    // before this ever reaches the frontend, matching productListCardMapper.ts's own identical read.
411	    badge: product.c_productBadges?.[0]?.productBadge,

413	    sizeChipValues: selectSizeChipValues(product),

content.text:
Read through both mappers (`productListCardMapper.ts` for PLP, `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts` for Full History) plus both pages' own consuming/wiring code. They're clearly built as deliberate mirrors of each other — most of what I'd normally flag as a discrepancy is already explicitly documented as a known, accepted difference in their own docblocks. Here's the real picture.

**Confirmed identical / equivalent behavior:**
- Both use `variation: 'plp'` on the shared `ZimmProductCard` — same hover reveals, bag-icon placement, carousel arrows, price display.
- Both derive `currentPrice`/`originalPrice` from one `getPriceData()` call each — no risk of the two price fields disagreeing internally.
- Image resolution (colour-scoped, `medium` viewtype, sequence-number sort for a mis-ordered API response) is ported near-verbatim between the two mappers.
- Add-to-bag: byte-for-byte identical basket mutation (`addItemToNewOrExistingBasket([{productId, price, quantity:1}])`) and identical success/error toast pattern — just separate i18n keys per page (deliberate, both default to "Added to bag").
- Badge: both read `c_productBadges?.[0]?.productBadge` — single highest-priority badge, same rule.
- Size chips: identical `variationAttributes` → `ZimmSizeChipValue` mapping.

**Two shared, pre-existing gaps (not a PLP-vs-Full-History difference — both are equally incomplete):**
- No wishlist/favourite heart control on either surface — PLP's own comment calls its `plp` card usage a "quick test integration," not full parity yet.
- No real notify-me handler wired on either surface — `onNotifyMe` is never supplied by either mapper, so that button is currently dead code on both.

**Real differences, worth your attention:**

1. **Same product, potentially different photo.** PLP resolves which colour's images to show via `representedProduct` (the store's own merchandised pick) when available, falling back to "first orderable variant" only when it isn't. Full History's data source (`getProducts`, not the Search index) has no `representedProduct` field at all — it can *only* use the fallback strategy. For a multi-colour product, this means the same item could legitimately show a different colour photo on Full History than it does on PLP. This is explicitly documented as an unavoidable data-source limitation in the mapper's own comments, not a bug to fix — but it's a real, visible thing a shopper could notice.

2. **Different state architecture for size selection**, same end result. PLP uses a per-card component (`ProductListCard`) with its own local `useState`. Full History uses one shared `Record<productId, sizeValue>` at the page container. Functionally equivalent — but selecting a size on Full History re-renders the *entire* page's card list, where PLP only re-renders the one card. Likely immaterial at the current 24-card cap, but a genuine asymmetry, not just a stylistic one.

3. **Orderability read from two different endpoints.** PLP's `isUnavailable` comes from the Search hit (`hit.orderable`); Full History's comes from the Products/hydration endpoint (`product.master?.orderable`). The Full History mapper's own docblock already documents a *confirmed* case of these two endpoints disagreeing on a different field (badges, due to search-index lag) — I haven't independently confirmed it happens for orderability too, but the same lag risk plausibly applies: a product that just sold out could show as available on one surface and not the other for a window of time.

None of these three are wrong code — they're consequences of genuinely different data sources feeding two mappers built to be as close to identical as those sources allow. Want me to chase any of them further (e.g., actually try to reproduce #3 with a real product), or file them as known/accepted?

message.content: #2 seems like a geniune gap? why the difference?

content.text:
Because the two pages have fundamentally different amounts of control over how their cards render — this is already documented in `recentlyViewed/index.tsx`'s own docblock, not something I'm newly inferring, so let me give you the actual reasoning rather than restate my own guess.

PLP builds its own grid inline, directly in `product-list/index.tsx` — so it has full freedom to insert `ProductListCard`, a per-card wrapper component, between the raw data and `ZimmProductCard`. That wrapper is where the local `useState` lives; each card gets its own component instance, so each gets its own isolated state for free.

Full History doesn't have that option: it renders through `ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid`, a shared, already-shipped organism whose own contract is `cards.map(card => <ZimmProductCard key={card.id} {...card} />)` — no slot for a container to inject a custom per-card wrapper. To get PLP's exact pattern, `ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid`'s own prop contract would need to change (something like a `renderCard` prop) — a change to a shared component used elsewhere, for the sake of one caller's size-chip state. The recorded decision was that this is a bigger, more cross-cutting change than "make add-to-bag size-aware" called for, so a single id-keyed map at the container was used instead, trading isolated re-renders for not touching the shared organism's contract at all.

Is that trade-off still right? I think so, practically: the cap on this page is 24 cards (`RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED`), so a size-chip click re-running the map function for, worst case, 24 lightweight prop objects is not something a real user would perceive — React's own reconciliation still only touches the DOM node that actually changed. The real cost of the alternative is touching a shared organism's contract (more surface area, more tests, more risk) for a performance difference that's very unlikely to be measurable at this scale.

So: a genuine architectural difference, yes — but a deliberate, reasoned one, not an accidental gap. I wouldn't fix it unless you're anticipating `ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid` needing per-card customization for some *other* reason down the line, in which case it'd be worth solving once for both.

input.command:
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(recently-viewed): bleed Full History past #app-main padding, reserve footer spacing

Two fixes to the Full History page container:

- The page rendered inset within #app-main's own sitewide padding
  with no bleed mechanism at all — no PageContainer, no
  layerStyle="page", nothing cancelling it. Confirmed against this
  page's own three Figma frames, which show the header and every
  Product Card Group spanning the full frame width. Fixed by wrapping
  ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid in a Box using a new APP_MAIN_BLEED_MX
  constant.

  APP_MAIN_BLEED_MX, not the existing PAGE_CONTENT_BLEED_MX — that
  constant cancels two stacked layers (#app-main + PDP/PLP's own
  PageContainer/layerStyle second layer), which this page doesn't
  have. Using it here over-cancelled by exactly the second layer's
  amount at every breakpoint, rendering the page wider than the
  viewport (confirmed live: 1504px at a 1440px viewport, margin
  -72px instead of the correct -40px). APP_MAIN_BLEED_MX cancels only
  the one universal layer, at #app-main's own two real breakpoints.

- Figma's page frames show "Footer Primary" (a Load More button,
  deferred separately) filling 112px of padding + a 52px button
  between the last card row and the real Footer. With no button
  rendered, that space disappeared entirely. Reserved the padding
  portion (112px) as bottom padding on the same Box, to grow by the
  button's 52px once Load More is actually built.
EOF
)" -- overrides/app/constants/index.ts overrides/app/pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx
