content.text: Critical finding already: Figma shows **zero gap** between rail cards at every breakpoint — 288×5=1440 (Desktop), 256×3=768 (Tablet), 201×2=402 (Mobile), all edge-to-edge with no gutter. Let me check what our CSS actually does.

content.content:
1	import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';
2	import { breakpoints } from 'app/theme/foundation';
3	import { RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS } from 'app/constants';
4	
5	/**
6	 * Recipe for the Recently Viewed rail organism (SFCC-83), build plan section A5. Figma component
7	 * set `40000587:38471` — Desktop `40000307:12444` (1440x528), Tablet `40000730:13363`
8	 * (768x437.85), Mobile `40000538:25030` (402x355.82). The Figma decomposition confirmed by the
9	 * build plan is exactly two children — `title-and-link` and `group`, no arrow layer (a rail-level
10	 * carousel would collide with ZimmProductCardMedia's own intra-card arrows) — mapped onto `header`
11	 * and `group` below. Two more parts exist that have no Figma layer of their own: `seeAllLink`
12	 * (the See-Full-History link's colour/hover/focus states) and `card` (each card's own
13	 * per-breakpoint fixed width — ZimmProductCard's own root has no width opinion, see index.tsx).
14	 * `container` is the outermost wrapper, deliberately not named `root`: this recipe's own outer
15	 * part and the composed ZimmProductCard's own `root` part (zimmProductCard.css.ts) are unrelated
16	 * recipes that would otherwise both want the same name.
17	 *
18	 * CARD SIZING — fluid, not fixed (corrected 2026-09-10, closing a real, live-confirmed bug —
19	 * Figma-vs-code audit requested by Marcel, the same pass that found and fixed the header padding
20	 * below). The previous revision set each card to an explicit, non-growing, non-shrinking pixel
21	 * width per breakpoint (201px / 256px / 288px), derived by dividing a Figma reference frame's own
22	 * fixed canvas width by its visible-card count — a correct read of that frame's own dimensions,
23	 * but the frame's own layout rule was never "fixed width." A fresh `get_design_context` pull
24	 * (not just metadata, which only ever shows a resolved snapshot, not the underlying rule) on every
25	 * real "Product-card" instance — Mobile `40000538:25030`, Tablet `40000730:13363`, Desktop
26	 * `40000307:12444` — confirms `flex: 1 0 0` (grow, no shrink, zero basis) with a `min-width` floor:
27	 * 200px on Mobile/Tablet, negligible on Desktop. Fixed-width cards were the single root cause of
28	 * two real, reported symptoms at once: on any real device narrower than the old fixed total
29	 * (201x2=402px — nearly every real phone), the row overflowed its own container, cutting off
30	 * cards and forcing horizontal scroll; on any device wider than that total, the row left an
31	 * unwanted gap instead of reaching the edge. Fluid cards fix both — they always evenly divide
32	 * whatever width the row's own container actually provides.
33	 *
34	 * The rail's own hard per-breakpoint visible-card cap (`RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS`,
35	 * `app/constants/index.ts` — 2/3/5, confirmed with Marcel as a genuine hard cap, not a
36	 * scroll-to-see-more soft limit) means the row is *at most* that many cards, never more — but can
37	 * genuinely be fewer (a shopper with only 1 tracked product). `group`'s own scroll/scroll-snap CSS
38	 * is removed below for the same reason (Marcel, 2026-09-10: horizontal scrolling "is not a
39	 * prescribed behavior for the recently viewed rail") — see "GROUP" below for the one narrow edge
40	 * case this leaves unhandled, flagged rather than silently ignored.
41	 *
42	 * **Under-populated rows — corrected 2026-09-10 (third pass, same day).** `flex: 1 0 0` divides
43	 * whatever space is available among however many cards actually exist — correct, and Figma-
44	 * confirmed, for a fully-populated row, but Figma's own component set (`40000587:38471`) has
45	 * exactly three variants (`Size=Desktop`/`Mobile`/`Tablet`) and no "fewer items" state at all, so
46	 * there was no Figma ground truth for what a partially-filled row should do. Left as `flex: 1 0 0`,
47	 * a lone card on Desktop would grow to consume the *entire* row — confirmed with Marcel as not the
48	 * intended behaviour, and a real user-facing case (any shopper with fewer tracked products than
49	 * the current breakpoint's cap). Fixed by sizing each card to its share of the row *as if the cap
50	 * were fully met* (`100 / RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS.<tier>`, computed below rather than
51	 * hand-typed so the two can never drift apart), left-aligned (Marcel's own choice, 2026-09-10,
52	 * between left-aligned-with-trailing-gap vs. centered) — `flex: 0 0 auto` (no grow, no shrink,
53	 * matching Figma's own no-shrink rule) with an explicit `width` instead of `flex: 1 0 0`'s
54	 * zero-basis growth. A fully-populated row is unaffected: N cards at `100/N%` each still sum to
55	 * exactly 100%, identical to the old behaviour in that case.
56	 *
57	 * `CARD_MIN_WIDTH_MOBILE_TABLET` (200px) has no existing --zimm-scale-* equivalent — checked
58	 * against every numeric alias in zimmTokens.ts, the scale runs ...64, 140, 180... with nothing at
59	 * 200 — same pending-token treatment as the header heights below. Desktop has no floor constant
60	 * of its own: its real Figma value is a negligible ~1px anti-overflow default, not a meaningful
61	 * design floor, and the visible-card cap already guarantees Desktop's 5 cards never need to shrink
62	 * anywhere near even the Mobile/Tablet floor (1280px / 5 = 256px at the narrowest real Desktop
63	 * viewport) — so the one floor is applied uniformly at every breakpoint rather than adding a
64	 * second, functionally-inert constant purely to mirror Figma's "no floor" reading literally.
65	 *
66	 * Card height is still never set anywhere in this recipe, unaffected by this correction —
67	 * ZimmProductCardMedia's own `slide` part already carries `aspectRatio: '2 / 3'` at `width: '100%'`
68	 * (zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts), and ZimmProductCard's own root has no height opinion of its own
69	 * (zimmProductCard.css.ts) — so height still falls out of that aspect-ratio math for free.
70	 *
71	 * GROUP HAS ZERO GAP / ZERO HORIZONTAL PADDING — confirmed directly (2026-09-10): the real
72	 * `group` node's own Figma export carries no `gap`/padding class of any kind, at any breakpoint.
73	 * This is `group`-only — `header` does NOT share this zero-inset treatment; see "HEADER PADDING"
74	 * below. GROUP'S SCROLL/SCROLL-SNAP CSS IS REMOVED (2026-09-10) for the same reason cards became
75	 * fluid — Marcel confirmed scrolling is not prescribed behaviour for this rail at all, and once
76	 * cards are fluid against a hard-capped visible count, there is structurally nothing to scroll to
77	 * in the normal case. **One accepted, narrow edge case this leaves open, flagged rather than
78	 * silently handled:** a real device narrower than `min-width x visible-count` (e.g. under 400px on
79	 * Mobile) would still overflow — `flex: 1 0 0` has shrink explicitly disabled, matching Figma, so
80	 * the row cannot shrink below that floor — with no scroll affordance left to reach the clipped
81	 * remainder. Not chased further without a product decision on whether that's an acceptable target-
82	 * device floor or needs its own fallback.
83	 *
84	 * HEADER HEIGHT — two states, not three: 56px at base (covers Mobile and Tablet — the build
85	 * plan's own brief gives exactly one Mobile header node and one Desktop header node, no separate
86	 * Tablet one), stepping to 96px from Desktop up — `RAIL_DESKTOP_BREAKPOINT` (1024px), this
87	 * component's own real Figma threshold, not this site's shared `breakpoints.xl` (1280px); see that
88	 * constant's own comment. Same rem-with-pending-comment treatment as the card widths above —
89	 * neither 56px nor 96px has an existing --zimm-scale-* equivalent either.
90	 *
91	 * HEADER PADDING — corrected 2026-09-10, closing a real, live-confirmed bug (Figma-vs-code audit
92	 * requested by Marcel). Previously zero horizontal padding and a flex `alignItems: 'center'`
93	 * vertical treatment — the earlier revision of this docblock called that a "judgment call, not a
94	 * confirmed Figma reading," flagged for confirmation once the rail sat inside a real page. Now
95	 * confirmed directly against Figma metadata: horizontal inset is `var(--zimm-scale-3xl)` (40px) on
96	 * Desktop (node `40000538:20306`) and `var(--zimm-scale-2xl)` (32px) on Tablet/Mobile (nodes
97	 * `40000730:13364` / `40000538:25031`) — all four exact matches on the existing named spacing
98	 * scale (`spacing.ts`), no pending-token gap here unlike the card widths/header heights above.
99	 * Vertical split is NOT centered by box height either — it's top-heavy: Desktop is `pt-3xl` (40px)
100	 * / `pb-2xl` (32px) around the 24px content (40+24+32=96, matching HEADER_HEIGHT_DESKTOP exactly);
101	 * Tablet/Mobile is `pt-l` (20px) / `pb-s` (12px) around the same 24px content (20+24+12=56,
102	 * matching HEADER_HEIGHT_MOBILE).
103	 *
104	 * **`alignItems` corrected again 2026-09-10 (second pass, same day) — reverted to `center`.** The
105	 * first pass (immediately above) replaced Figma's own literal `alignItems: 'center'` with
106	 * `'flex-start'`, reasoning that the asymmetric padding alone should position the content. That
107	 * reasoning produces identical pixels to `center` — but only because the padding above is authored
108	 * as an exact content-box fit at every breakpoint (72px padding + 24px content = 96px; 32px padding
109	 * + 24px content = 56px — zero slack either way), not because `flex-start` is what Figma actually
110	 * says. A fresh `get_design_context` pull on all three header nodes (`40000538:20306` Desktop,
111	 * `40000538:25031` Mobile, `40000730:13364` Tablet) confirms `items-center`, literally, on every
112	 * one. Reverted to match the literal declared rule — design spec is source of truth over a
113	 * derived-but-numerically-coincidental value (Marcel, 2026-09-10). Functionally a no-op for
114	 * today's single-line title copy, but `flex-start` would have silently diverged from `center` the
115	 * moment the title ever wraps to a second line (a longer translated string, most likely) — this
116	 * closes that latent risk, not just a cosmetic one.
117	 *
118	 * TITLE/LINK SPACING — corrected 2026-09-10 (second pass, same day). Figma nests the title and
119	 * Link inside an intermediate "Content" wrapper (`flex: 1 0 0`, `gap`: `var(--zimm-scale-3xl)`
120	 * 40px Desktop / `var(--zimm-scale-2xl)` 32px Mobile+Tablet), with the title itself also
121	 * `flex: 1 0 0` — it grows to fill whatever the gap and the Link's own width don't claim,
122	 * guaranteeing a fixed minimum gap between them no matter how long the title text gets. The
123	 * previous revision flattened this into `header` with two plain children and
124	 * `justifyContent: 'space-between'` (no intermediate wrapper — a reasonable simplification, since
125	 * Content's own rendered width always equals header's, being header's only Figma child) but that
126	 * dropped the gap floor entirely: `space-between` just uses whatever space happens to be left
127	 * over, with nothing stopping title and Link from touching if the title ever got close to the
128	 * Link's own edge. For today's actual copy ("RECENTLY VIEWED" / "SEE FULL HISTORY") both
129	 * approaches land the Link in the same place — there is no visible difference — purely because
130	 * there's ample slack today. Fixed by giving `header` itself the gap directly (the intermediate
131	 * wrapper is still correctly omitted — only the `gap` itself was missing, not the wrapper) and
132	 * setting the title span to `flex: '1 0 0'` / `minWidth: 0` directly in index.tsx (a Chakra prop,
133	 * not a new recipe part — the title has no other recipe-driven styling of its own, matching
134	 * overrideStyling.md's "Chakra UI props first" ordering for a plain structural, non-token value).
135	 * `seeAllLink` gets `flexShrink: 0` alongside its existing rules, matching Figma's Link box's own
136	 * `shrink-0` exactly.
137	 *
138	 * SEE-ALL LINK — colour/hover/focus-visible states only. Typography (uppercase, underline, size,
139	 * weight) comes from the `textStyle="linkLg"` prop applied directly in index.tsx
140	 * (typography.ts:152), not duplicated here as a recipe value — see
141	 * .claude/rules/overrideStyling.md hierarchy point 1 (textStyle before var(--zimm-*)). Colours
142	 * resolved from the registry, not re-derived: default var(--zimm-color-link-default), hover
143	 * var(--zimm-color-link-hover), focus ring var(--zimm-focus-ring) /
144	 * var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default) (zimmTokens.ts:68-69).
145	 *
146	 * No Figma hover/focus/active variant exists for this link — only a single "State=default" node
147	 * was supplied (see index.tsx's own comment on the same point for the full caveat). `active`
148	 * deliberately has no rule of its own below and simply inherits whatever `_hover` establishes —
149	 * see that key's own inline comment for why that is intentional, not a missed state.
150	 *
151	 * Parts: `container`, `header`, `seeAllLink`, `group`, `card` — reconciled against index.tsx's own
152	 * `useMultiStyleConfig` reads by `ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts`.
153	 */
154	
155	// Card min-width floor, Mobile/Tablet (also applied at Desktop — see docblock for why one
156	// uniform floor is correct there too) — see docblock's "CARD SIZING" section. rem, not px,
157	// matching footer.css.ts's SIZE_COL_SUB/SIZE_COL_MAP precedent for a sizing (non-hairline)
158	// dimension with no foundation token yet.
159	const CARD_MIN_WIDTH_MOBILE_TABLET = '12.5rem'; // 200px — confirmed Figma value (flex: 1 0 0, min-width: 200px on the real Mobile 40000538:25030 and Tablet 40000730:13363 Product-card instances, via get_design_context). No --zimm-scale-* equivalent (nearest neighbours: 1600=64px, 3500=140px) — pending promotion to foundation/spacing.ts or sizes.ts by the UI designer.
160	
161	// Each card's share of the row, sized against the per-breakpoint *cap* (RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS)
162	// rather than however many cards actually render — see docblock's "Under-populated rows" section.
163	// Derived, not hand-typed, so this can never silently drift from the cap it depends on.
164	const CARD_ROW_SHARE_MOBILE = `${(100 / RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS.base).toFixed(4)}%`; // 2 cards -> 50%
165	const CARD_ROW_SHARE_TABLET = `${(100 / RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS.md).toFixed(4)}%`; // 3 cards -> 33.3333%
166	const CARD_ROW_SHARE_DESKTOP = `${(100 / RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS.xl).toFixed(4)}%`; // 5 cards -> 20%

169	// widths above; neither value exists anywhere in zimmTokens.ts's numeric scale.
170	const HEADER_HEIGHT_MOBILE = '3.5rem'; // 56px — confirmed Figma value (node 40000538:25031, Mobile — also covers Tablet, see docblock). Pending promotion.

174	// wrong by the same Figma-vs-code audit that fixed CARD_MIN_WIDTH_MOBILE_TABLET above). Without a
175	// cap, `container`'s bare `width: '100%'` stretches to whatever width the page actually provides —
176	// this site's own grid foundation is deliberately uncapped (gridSystem.ts's `grid.maxWidth:
177	// 'none'`), so nothing above this component was ever going to constrain it on its own.
178	//
179	// The 2026-09-08 values (402px/768px/1440px) were derived from the same now-corrected card-width x
180	// visible-count arithmetic the card fix above closes (201x2=402, 256x3=768, 288x5=1440) — a real
181	// bug in its own right, now fixed here too: checked directly against each breakpoint's own master
182	// component (`get_design_context`, not just a page instance, which can be resized/overridden by
183	// its own parent frame and so doesn't reveal the component's real intrinsic rule):
184	//   - Mobile (`40000538:25030`): fluid, capped at 767px (not hard-set to 402px).
185	//   - Tablet (`40000730:13363`): fluid, capped at 1023px (not 768px) — also confirms Tablet's own
186	//     real ceiling is 1023px, not this site's shared `breakpoints.xl` (1280px); see
187	//     RAIL_DESKTOP_BREAKPOINT below for the direct consequence.
188	//   - Desktop (`40000307:12444`): fluid, genuinely UNBOUNDED — no max-width at all. Safe to leave
189	//     uncapped now (unlike before): the old cap existed specifically to stop `header` (width:100%)
190	//     drifting wider than `group` (self-limited to its own then-fixed-width children) on an
191	//     ultra-wide viewport — with cards now fluid too, `group` always tracks `container`'s own
192	//     width exactly like `header` does, so that divergence can no longer happen regardless of cap.
193	// audit-allow: derived composite, not itself a value with any promotable foundation-token
194	// equivalent — a "content max-width" isn't a spacing/sizing scale concept on its own.
195	const RAIL_CONTENT_MAX_WIDTH_MOBILE = '47.9375rem'; // 767px
196	const RAIL_CONTENT_MAX_WIDTH_TABLET = '63.9375rem'; // 1023px

202	const TABLET_UP_QUERY = `@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`; // 768px — matches this component's own real Figma Tablet start exactly (confirmed via its master component, see RAIL_CONTENT_MAX_WIDTH_TABLET's own comment above) — this site's shared breakpoints.md is the correct value here, not a coincidence.

206	// variants — NOT this site's shared `breakpoints.xl` (1280px), which the header height/padding
207	// fix and the container max-width fix above previously (and wrongly) keyed off. A genuine,

209	// hardcoded here rather than added to gridSystem.ts's own shared `breakpoints` object, which is a
210	// Tier 1, site-wide foundation value this one component's own deviation has no business changing.
211	// audit-allow: a real, deliberate, Figma-confirmed component-specific breakpoint, not a value with
212	// any site-wide token equivalent to promote to.
213	const RAIL_DESKTOP_BREAKPOINT = '64em'; // 1024px
214	const DESKTOP_UP_QUERY = `@media (min-width: ${RAIL_DESKTOP_BREAKPOINT})`; // 1024px — the "Desktop" tier for header height/padding and container max-width; card sizing no longer steps here at all, see "CARD SIZING" docblock section.

217	  parts: ['container', 'header', 'seeAllLink', 'group', 'card'],

226	      marginInline: 'auto',
227	      [TABLET_UP_QUERY]: {

229	      },

241	      // "alignItems corrected again" note for why the previous flex-start revision was wrong

245	      // Replaces the previous justifyContent: 'space-between' (no gap floor of its own); the

247	      // and the link's own width don't claim.

249	      height: HEADER_HEIGHT_MOBILE,
250	      paddingInline: 'var(--zimm-scale-2xl)',
251	      paddingTop: 'var(--zimm-scale-l)',
252	      paddingBottom: 'var(--zimm-scale-s)',
253	      [DESKTOP_UP_QUERY]: {
254	        gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-3xl)',
255	        height: HEADER_HEIGHT_DESKTOP,
256	        paddingInline: 'var(--zimm-scale-3xl)',
257	        paddingTop: 'var(--zimm-scale-3xl)',
258	        paddingBottom: 'var(--zimm-scale-2xl)',
259	      },
260	    },
261	
262	    seeAllLink: {

265	      // line-height (16px) is under the threshold on its own. Same fix, same token, as
266	      // zimmLink.css.ts's own baseStyle for the identical concern.
267	      display: 'inline-block',
268	      // Matches Figma's Link box (`shrink-0`) — never shrinks, so a long title's own flex-grow
269	      // (index.tsx) is what yields room, not this. See docblock's "TITLE/LINK SPACING" section.
270	      flexShrink: 0,
271	      paddingBlock: 'var(--zimm-scale-2xs)',
272	      color: 'var(--zimm-color-link-default)',
273	      _hover: {

275	      },

281	      _focusVisible: {

283	        outlineOffset: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)',

291	      // No overflow/scroll-snap CSS here any more — see the same docblock's own note on why

308	      [TABLET_UP_QUERY]: {

import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';
import { breakpoints } from 'app/theme/foundation';
import { RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS } from 'app/constants';

/**
 * Recipe for the Recently Viewed rail organism (SFCC-83), build plan section A5. Figma component
 * set `40000587:38471` — Desktop `40000307:12444` (1440x528), Tablet `40000730:13363`
 * (768x437.85), Mobile `40000538:25030` (402x355.82). The Figma decomposition confirmed by the
 * build plan is exactly two children — `title-and-link` and `group`, no arrow layer (a rail-level
 * carousel would collide with ZimmProductCardMedia's own intra-card arrows) — mapped onto `header`
 * and `group` below. Two more parts exist that have no Figma layer of their own: `seeAllLink`
 * (the See-Full-History link's colour/hover/focus states) and `card` (each card's own
 * per-breakpoint fixed width — ZimmProductCard's own root has no width opinion, see index.tsx).
 * `container` is the outermost wrapper, deliberately not named `root`: this recipe's own outer
 * part and the composed ZimmProductCard's own `root` part (zimmProductCard.css.ts) are unrelated
 * recipes that would otherwise both want the same name.
 *
 * CARD SIZING — fluid, not fixed (corrected 2026-09-10, closing a real, live-confirmed bug —
 * Figma-vs-code audit requested by Marcel, the same pass that found and fixed the header padding
 * below). The previous revision set each card to an explicit, non-growing, non-shrinking pixel
 * width per breakpoint (201px / 256px / 288px), derived by dividing a Figma reference frame's own
 * fixed canvas width by its visible-card count — a correct read of that frame's own dimensions,
 * but the frame's own layout rule was never "fixed width." A fresh `get_design_context` pull
 * (not just metadata, which only ever shows a resolved snapshot, not the underlying rule) on every
 * real "Product-card" instance — Mobile `40000538:25030`, Tablet `40000730:13363`, Desktop
 * `40000307:12444` — confirms `flex: 1 0 0` (grow, no shrink, zero basis) with a `min-width` floor:
 * 200px on Mobile/Tablet, negligible on Desktop. Fixed-width cards were the single root cause of
 * two real, reported symptoms at once: on any real device narrower than the old fixed total
 * (201x2=402px — nearly every real phone), the row overflowed its own container, cutting off
 * cards and forcing horizontal scroll; on any device wider than that total, the row left an
 * unwanted gap instead of reaching the edge. Fluid cards fix both — they always evenly divide
 * whatever width the row's own container actually provides.
 *
 * The rail's own hard per-breakpoint visible-card cap (`RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS`,
 * `app/constants/index.ts` — 2/3/5, confirmed with Marcel as a genuine hard cap, not a
 * scroll-to-see-more soft limit) means the row is *at most* that many cards, never more — but can
 * genuinely be fewer (a shopper with only 1 tracked product). `group`'s own scroll/scroll-snap CSS
 * is removed below for the same reason (Marcel, 2026-09-10: horizontal scrolling "is not a
 * prescribed behavior for the recently viewed rail") — see "GROUP" below for the one narrow edge
 * case this leaves unhandled, flagged rather than silently ignored.
 *
 * **Under-populated rows — corrected 2026-09-10 (third pass, same day).** `flex: 1 0 0` divides
 * whatever space is available among however many cards actually exist — correct, and Figma-
 * confirmed, for a fully-populated row, but Figma's own component set (`40000587:38471`) has
 * exactly three variants (`Size=Desktop`/`Mobile`/`Tablet`) and no "fewer items" state at all, so
 * there was no Figma ground truth for what a partially-filled row should do. Left as `flex: 1 0 0`,
 * a lone card on Desktop would grow to consume the *entire* row — confirmed with Marcel as not the
 * intended behaviour, and a real user-facing case (any shopper with fewer tracked products than
 * the current breakpoint's cap). Fixed by sizing each card to its share of the row *as if the cap
 * were fully met* (`100 / RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS.<tier>`, computed below rather than
 * hand-typed so the two can never drift apart), left-aligned (Marcel's own choice, 2026-09-10,
 * between left-aligned-with-trailing-gap vs. centered) — `flex: 0 0 auto` (no grow, no shrink,
 * matching Figma's own no-shrink rule) with an explicit `width` instead of `flex: 1 0 0`'s
 * zero-basis growth. A fully-populated row is unaffected: N cards at `100/N%` each still sum to
 * exactly 100%, identical to the old behaviour in that case.
 *
 * `CARD_MIN_WIDTH_MOBILE_TABLET` (200px) has no existing --zimm-scale-* equivalent — checked
 * against every numeric alias in zimmTokens.ts, the scale runs ...64, 140, 180... with nothing at
 * 200 — same pending-token treatment as the header heights below. Desktop has no floor constant
 * of its own: its real Figma value is a negligible ~1px anti-overflow default, not a meaningful
 * design floor, and the visible-card cap already guarantees Desktop's 5 cards never need to shrink
 * anywhere near even the Mobile/Tablet floor (1280px / 5 = 256px at the narrowest real Desktop
 * viewport) — so the one floor is applied uniformly at every breakpoint rather than adding a
 * second, functionally-inert constant purely to mirror Figma's "no floor" reading literally.
 *
 * Card height is still never set anywhere in this recipe, unaffected by this correction —
 * ZimmProductCardMedia's own `slide` part already carries `aspectRatio: '2 / 3'` at `width: '100%'`
 * (zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts), and ZimmProductCard's own root has no height opinion of its own
 * (zimmProductCard.css.ts) — so height still falls out of that aspect-ratio math for free.
 *
 * GROUP HAS ZERO GAP / ZERO HORIZONTAL PADDING — confirmed directly (2026-09-10): the real
 * `group` node's own Figma export carries no `gap`/padding class of any kind, at any breakpoint.
 * This is `group`-only — `header` does NOT share this zero-inset treatment; see "HEADER PADDING"
 * below. GROUP'S SCROLL/SCROLL-SNAP CSS IS REMOVED (2026-09-10) for the same reason cards became
 * fluid — Marcel confirmed scrolling is not prescribed behaviour for this rail at all, and once
 * cards are fluid against a hard-capped visible count, there is structurally nothing to scroll to
 * in the normal case. **One accepted, narrow edge case this leaves open, flagged rather than
 * silently handled:** a real device narrower than `min-width x visible-count` (e.g. under 400px on
 * Mobile) would still overflow — `flex: 1 0 0` has shrink explicitly disabled, matching Figma, so
 * the row cannot shrink below that floor — with no scroll affordance left to reach the clipped
 * remainder. Not chased further without a product decision on whether that's an acceptable target-
 * device floor or needs its own fallback.
 *
 * HEADER HEIGHT — two states, not three: 56px at base (covers Mobile and Tablet — the build
 * plan's own brief gives exactly one Mobile header node and one Desktop header node, no separate
 * Tablet one), stepping to 96px from Desktop up — `RAIL_DESKTOP_BREAKPOINT` (1024px), this
 * component's own real Figma threshold, not this site's shared `breakpoints.xl` (1280px); see that
 * constant's own comment. Same rem-with-pending-comment treatment as the card widths above —
 * neither 56px nor 96px has an existing --zimm-scale-* equivalent either.
 *
 * HEADER PADDING — corrected 2026-09-10, closing a real, live-confirmed bug (Figma-vs-code audit
 * requested by Marcel). Previously zero horizontal padding and a flex `alignItems: 'center'`
 * vertical treatment — the earlier revision of this docblock called that a "judgment call, not a
 * confirmed Figma reading," flagged for confirmation once the rail sat inside a real page. Now
 * confirmed directly against Figma metadata: horizontal inset is `var(--zimm-scale-3xl)` (40px) on
 * Desktop (node `40000538:20306`) and `var(--zimm-scale-2xl)` (32px) on Tablet/Mobile (nodes
 * `40000730:13364` / `40000538:25031`) — all four exact matches on the existing named spacing
 * scale (`spacing.ts`), no pending-token gap here unlike the card widths/header heights above.
 * Vertical split is NOT centered by box height either — it's top-heavy: Desktop is `pt-3xl` (40px)
 * / `pb-2xl` (32px) around the 24px content (40+24+32=96, matching HEADER_HEIGHT_DESKTOP exactly);
 * Tablet/Mobile is `pt-l` (20px) / `pb-s` (12px) around the same 24px content (20+24+12=56,
 * matching HEADER_HEIGHT_MOBILE).
 *
 * **`alignItems` corrected again 2026-09-10 (second pass, same day) — reverted to `center`.** The
 * first pass (immediately above) replaced Figma's own literal `alignItems: 'center'` with
 * `'flex-start'`, reasoning that the asymmetric padding alone should position the content. That
 * reasoning produces identical pixels to `center` — but only because the padding above is authored
 * as an exact content-box fit at every breakpoint (72px padding + 24px content = 96px; 32px padding
 * + 24px content = 56px — zero slack either way), not because `flex-start` is what Figma actually
 * says. A fresh `get_design_context` pull on all three header nodes (`40000538:20306` Desktop,
 * `40000538:25031` Mobile, `40000730:13364` Tablet) confirms `items-center`, literally, on every
 * one. Reverted to match the literal declared rule — design spec is source of truth over a
 * derived-but-numerically-coincidental value (Marcel, 2026-09-10). Functionally a no-op for
 * today's single-line title copy, but `flex-start` would have silently diverged from `center` the
 * moment the title ever wraps to a second line (a longer translated string, most likely) — this
 * closes that latent risk, not just a cosmetic one.
 *
 * TITLE/LINK SPACING — corrected 2026-09-10 (second pass, same day). Figma nests the title and
 * Link inside an intermediate "Content" wrapper (`flex: 1 0 0`, `gap`: `var(--zimm-scale-3xl)`
 * 40px Desktop / `var(--zimm-scale-2xl)` 32px Mobile+Tablet), with the title itself also
 * `flex: 1 0 0` — it grows to fill whatever the gap and the Link's own width don't claim,
 * guaranteeing a fixed minimum gap between them no matter how long the title text gets. The
 * previous revision flattened this into `header` with two plain children and
 * `justifyContent: 'space-between'` (no intermediate wrapper — a reasonable simplification, since
 * Content's own rendered width always equals header's, being header's only Figma child) but that
 * dropped the gap floor entirely: `space-between` just uses whatever space happens to be left
 * over, with nothing stopping title and Link from touching if the title ever got close to the
 * Link's own edge. For today's actual copy ("RECENTLY VIEWED" / "SEE FULL HISTORY") both
 * approaches land the Link in the same place — there is no visible difference — purely because
 * there's ample slack today. Fixed by giving `header` itself the gap directly (the intermediate
 * wrapper is still correctly omitted — only the `gap` itself was missing, not the wrapper) and
 * setting the title span to `flex: '1 0 0'` / `minWidth: 0` directly in index.tsx (a Chakra prop,
 * not a new recipe part — the title has no other recipe-driven styling of its own, matching
 * overrideStyling.md's "Chakra UI props first" ordering for a plain structural, non-token value).
 * `seeAllLink` gets `flexShrink: 0` alongside its existing rules, matching Figma's Link box's own
 * `shrink-0` exactly.
 *
 * SEE-ALL LINK — colour/hover/focus-visible states only. Typography (uppercase, underline, size,
 * weight) comes from the `textStyle="linkLg"` prop applied directly in index.tsx
 * (typography.ts:152), not duplicated here as a recipe value — see
 * .claude/rules/overrideStyling.md hierarchy point 1 (textStyle before var(--zimm-*)). Colours
 * resolved from the registry, not re-derived: default var(--zimm-color-link-default), hover
 * var(--zimm-color-link-hover), focus ring var(--zimm-focus-ring) /
 * var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default) (zimmTokens.ts:68-69).
 *
 * No Figma hover/focus/active variant exists for this link — only a single "State=default" node
 * was supplied (see index.tsx's own comment on the same point for the full caveat). `active`
 * deliberately has no rule of its own below and simply inherits whatever `_hover` establishes —
 * see that key's own inline comment for why that is intentional, not a missed state.
 *
 * Parts: `container`, `header`, `seeAllLink`, `group`, `card` — reconciled against index.tsx's own
 * `useMultiStyleConfig` reads by `ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts`.
 */

// Card min-width floor, Mobile/Tablet (also applied at Desktop — see docblock for why one
// uniform floor is correct there too) — see docblock's "CARD SIZING" section. rem, not px,
// matching footer.css.ts's SIZE_COL_SUB/SIZE_COL_MAP precedent for a sizing (non-hairline)
// dimension with no foundation token yet.
const CARD_MIN_WIDTH_MOBILE_TABLET = '12.5rem'; // 200px — confirmed Figma value (flex: 1 0 0, min-width: 200px on the real Mobile 40000538:25030 and Tablet 40000730:13363 Product-card instances, via get_design_context). No --zimm-scale-* equivalent (nearest neighbours: 1600=64px, 3500=140px) — pending promotion to foundation/spacing.ts or sizes.ts by the UI designer.

// Each card's share of the row, sized against the per-breakpoint *cap* (RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS)
// rather than however many cards actually render — see docblock's "Under-populated rows" section.
// Derived, not hand-typed, so this can never silently drift from the cap it depends on.
const CARD_ROW_SHARE_MOBILE = `${(100 / RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS.base).toFixed(4)}%`; // 2 cards -> 50%
const CARD_ROW_SHARE_TABLET = `${(100 / RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS.md).toFixed(4)}%`; // 3 cards -> 33.3333%
const CARD_ROW_SHARE_DESKTOP = `${(100 / RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS.xl).toFixed(4)}%`; // 5 cards -> 20%

// Header (title-and-link row) height — see docblock. Same pending-token treatment as the card
// widths above; neither value exists anywhere in zimmTokens.ts's numeric scale.
const HEADER_HEIGHT_MOBILE = '3.5rem'; // 56px — confirmed Figma value (node 40000538:25031, Mobile — also covers Tablet, see docblock). Pending promotion.
const HEADER_HEIGHT_DESKTOP = '6rem'; // 96px — confirmed Figma value (node 40000538:20306, Desktop). Pending promotion.

// Rail content max-width, per breakpoint — corrected 2026-09-10 (was fixed 2026-09-08, then found
// wrong by the same Figma-vs-code audit that fixed CARD_MIN_WIDTH_MOBILE_TABLET above). Without a
// cap, `container`'s bare `width: '100%'` stretches to whatever width the page actually provides —
// this site's own grid foundation is deliberately uncapped (gridSystem.ts's `grid.maxWidth:
// 'none'`), so nothing above this component was ever going to constrain it on its own.
//
// The 2026-09-08 values (402px/768px/1440px) were derived from the same now-corrected card-width x
// visible-count arithmetic the card fix above closes (201x2=402, 256x3=768, 288x5=1440) — a real
// bug in its own right, now fixed here too: checked directly against each breakpoint's own master
// component (`get_design_context`, not just a page instance, which can be resized/overridden by
// its own parent frame and so doesn't reveal the component's real intrinsic rule):
//   - Mobile (`40000538:25030`): fluid, capped at 767px (not hard-set to 402px).
//   - Tablet (`40000730:13363`): fluid, capped at 1023px (not 768px) — also confirms Tablet's own
//     real ceiling is 1023px, not this site's shared `breakpoints.xl` (1280px); see
//     RAIL_DESKTOP_BREAKPOINT below for the direct consequence.
//   - Desktop (`40000307:12444`): fluid, genuinely UNBOUNDED — no max-width at all. Safe to leave
//     uncapped now (unlike before): the old cap existed specifically to stop `header` (width:100%)
//     drifting wider than `group` (self-limited to its own then-fixed-width children) on an
//     ultra-wide viewport — with cards now fluid too, `group` always tracks `container`'s own
//     width exactly like `header` does, so that divergence can no longer happen regardless of cap.
// audit-allow: derived composite, not itself a value with any promotable foundation-token
// equivalent — a "content max-width" isn't a spacing/sizing scale concept on its own.
const RAIL_CONTENT_MAX_WIDTH_MOBILE = '47.9375rem'; // 767px
const RAIL_CONTENT_MAX_WIDTH_TABLET = '63.9375rem'; // 1023px

// Deliberately NOT named DESKTOP_QUERY / sharing zimmProductCardShared.ts's constant of that
// name: that one gates at breakpoints.md (768px, the product-card family's own "show the bag icon
// again" threshold) — a different breakpoint for a different concern. Reusing the name here would
// read as the same threshold when it isn't.
const TABLET_UP_QUERY = `@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`; // 768px — matches this component's own real Figma Tablet start exactly (confirmed via its master component, see RAIL_CONTENT_MAX_WIDTH_TABLET's own comment above) — this site's shared breakpoints.md is the correct value here, not a coincidence.

// This component's own real Figma "Desktop" threshold is 1024px, confirmed directly (2026-09-10)
// via its master component's own Tablet (max-width 1023px) and Desktop (min-width 1024px)
// variants — NOT this site's shared `breakpoints.xl` (1280px), which the header height/padding
// fix and the container max-width fix above previously (and wrongly) keyed off. A genuine,
// deliberate mismatch with the site-wide breakpoint scale for this one component, not a typo —
// hardcoded here rather than added to gridSystem.ts's own shared `breakpoints` object, which is a
// Tier 1, site-wide foundation value this one component's own deviation has no business changing.
// audit-allow: a real, deliberate, Figma-confirmed component-specific breakpoint, not a value with
// any site-wide token equivalent to promote to.
const RAIL_DESKTOP_BREAKPOINT = '64em'; // 1024px
const DESKTOP_UP_QUERY = `@media (min-width: ${RAIL_DESKTOP_BREAKPOINT})`; // 1024px — the "Desktop" tier for header height/padding and container max-width; card sizing no longer steps here at all, see "CARD SIZING" docblock section.

export const ZimmRecentlyViewedRail = {
  parts: ['container', 'header', 'seeAllLink', 'group', 'card'],

  baseStyle: (): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => ({
    container: {
      width: '100%',
      maxWidth: RAIL_CONTENT_MAX_WIDTH_MOBILE,
      // Centres the rail once the viewport exceeds this breakpoint's own content width — matches
      // the Figma frame's own edge-to-edge composition at exactly this width, not a component
      // left flush to one side with the excess space unused.
      marginInline: 'auto',
      [TABLET_UP_QUERY]: {
        maxWidth: RAIL_CONTENT_MAX_WIDTH_TABLET,
      },
      [DESKTOP_UP_QUERY]: {
        // Genuinely unbounded on Desktop per Figma — see RAIL_CONTENT_MAX_WIDTH_MOBILE/TABLET's
        // own comment above for why this is now safe (cards are fluid, so header/group can no
        // longer diverge regardless of cap).
        maxWidth: 'none',
      },
    },

    header: {
      display: 'flex',
      // Matches Figma's literal rule at all three breakpoints — see module docblock's
      // "alignItems corrected again" note for why the previous flex-start revision was wrong
      // despite producing identical pixels today.
      alignItems: 'center',
      // Guaranteed minimum title/link spacing — see docblock's "TITLE/LINK SPACING" section.
      // Replaces the previous justifyContent: 'space-between' (no gap floor of its own); the
      // title span itself is set to flex: '1 0 0' in index.tsx so it grows into whatever this gap
      // and the link's own width don't claim.
      gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-2xl)',
      height: HEADER_HEIGHT_MOBILE,
      paddingInline: 'var(--zimm-scale-2xl)',
      paddingTop: 'var(--zimm-scale-l)',
      paddingBottom: 'var(--zimm-scale-s)',
      [DESKTOP_UP_QUERY]: {
        gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-3xl)',
        height: HEADER_HEIGHT_DESKTOP,
        paddingInline: 'var(--zimm-scale-3xl)',
        paddingTop: 'var(--zimm-scale-3xl)',
        paddingBottom: 'var(--zimm-scale-2xl)',
      },
    },

    seeAllLink: {
      // WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.5.8 — 24px minimum target. This link sits alone in its own row (not
      // inline within a sentence), so the inline-text exemption doesn't apply, and `linkLg`'s
      // line-height (16px) is under the threshold on its own. Same fix, same token, as
      // zimmLink.css.ts's own baseStyle for the identical concern.
      display: 'inline-block',
      // Matches Figma's Link box (`shrink-0`) — never shrinks, so a long title's own flex-grow
      // (index.tsx) is what yields room, not this. See docblock's "TITLE/LINK SPACING" section.
      flexShrink: 0,
      paddingBlock: 'var(--zimm-scale-2xs)',
      color: 'var(--zimm-color-link-default)',
      _hover: {
        color: 'var(--zimm-color-link-hover)',
      },
      // No distinct `active` token exists anywhere in the design system for this link (see the
      // module docblock) — deliberately no `_active` rule here. A pointer is already over the
      // link while pressing it in the normal (non-keyboard) case, so `_hover` above keeps
      // matching through the press and "active" ends up the same colour as hover by inheritance.
      // This is intentional, not a missed state.
      _focusVisible: {
        outline: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring)',
        outlineOffset: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)',
      },
    },

    group: {
      display: 'flex',
      width: '100%',
      // Zero gap, zero horizontal padding — see module docblock's "GROUP HAS ZERO GAP" note.
      // No overflow/scroll-snap CSS here any more — see the same docblock's own note on why
      // scrolling was removed (not prescribed behaviour) and the one accepted edge case that
      // leaves open.
      gap: 0,
      // Explicit, not relying on the flex initial value — left-aligned is a deliberate choice
      // (Marcel, 2026-09-10) for the under-populated-row case below, not an incidental default.
      justifyContent: 'flex-start',
    },

    card: {
      // Each card claims a fixed share of the row (see docblock's "Under-populated rows" section)
      // rather than growing to fill whatever space is left — flex: 0 0 auto defers sizing entirely
      // to `width` below instead of `flex: 1 0 0`'s zero-basis growth. No grow, no shrink (matching
      // Figma's own confirmed no-shrink rule, unchanged from the previous revision).
      flex: '0 0 auto',
      width: CARD_ROW_SHARE_MOBILE,
      minWidth: CARD_MIN_WIDTH_MOBILE_TABLET,
      [TABLET_UP_QUERY]: {
        width: CARD_ROW_SHARE_TABLET,
      },
      [DESKTOP_UP_QUERY]: {
        width: CARD_ROW_SHARE_DESKTOP,
      },
    },
  }),
};

1	import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';
2	import { breakpoints } from 'app/theme/foundation';
3	
4	/**
5	 * Recipe for the Recently Viewed Full History grid organism (SFCC-84), build plan section B1.
6	 * Design source: `Zimmermann_Designs` file, `3332:35655` → `Container` → `PLP Bar desktop`
7	 * (`3332:37131`, 1440×75, title left / item-count right) + `Sidebar` (`3332:35664`, four stacked
8	 * `Products Module Desktop` instances, each 1440×606, containing `Products S Desktop` cards at
9	 * 288×542, x = 0/384/768/1152 — a `plp`-shaped `ZimmProductCard`, not a new card; see index.tsx's
10	 * own `cards` JSDoc for the `variation: 'plp'` citation). **This source is provisional per
11	 * Marcel's 2026-09-04 precedence rule** (it is not a PDP/Recently Viewed node in the authoritative
12	 * `Zimmermann_Design_System_2026` file `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`'s own recipe uses) — that ranking
13	 * is unaffected by the "confirmed" values below; see index.tsx's own module docblock for why both
14	 * things are true at once.
15	 *
16	 * Parts: `container`, `header`, `grid` — reconciled against index.tsx's own `useMultiStyleConfig`
17	 * reads by `ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts`. No `card` part (contrast
18	 * `zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts`'s own `card` part): the rail fixes a per-breakpoint PIXEL width
19	 * on each item because it lays out a horizontally-scrolling flex row with no requirement to fill
20	 * the viewport exactly. This is a real grid, not a scroller — `grid` below uses fractional
21	 * (`1fr`) column tracks instead, so each card's rendered width falls out of the container width
22	 * divided across the current column count with nothing extra to style per card; `ZimmProductCard`
23	 * itself still has no width/height opinion of its own (`zimmProductCard.css.ts`), same precedent
24	 * the rail's own docblock already establishes.
25	 *
26	 * HORIZONTAL GAP — three tiers, NOT a single uniform value (corrected 2026-09-10, closing a real
27	 * bug: a fuller page-node audit found the previous single 96px-everywhere value was only ever
28	 * confirmed for Desktop; Tablet and Mobile each have their own, different, real Figma value that
29	 * was never actually checked before this correction). Checked directly against the real page
30	 * frames' own card-group children:
31	 *   - Desktop (unchanged, still confirmed via the two independent sources this paragraph already
32	 *     cited): 96px, GENUINELY UN-TOKENISED — see `GRID_CARD_GAP_DESKTOP`'s own comment below for
33	 *     the full pending-token reasoning, unaffected by this correction.
34	 *   - Tablet (`9560:137692`, 3-card row, 834px wide): 80px, bound to a real Figma variable
35	 *     (`alias/space/2000`) — and unlike Desktop's 96px, this one DOES have a real registered
36	 *     equivalent: `--zimm-scale-5xl` (`spacing['5xl']`, `foundation/spacing.ts`), confirmed
37	 *     directly, no pending-token gap here.
38	 *   - Mobile (`9560:138463`, 2×2 grid): 40px, bound to a real Figma variable
39	 *     (`alias/space/gap/1000`) — also a real registered equivalent, `--zimm-scale-1000`
40	 *     (`spacing['3xl']`), same as this file's own `HEADER_PADDING_DESKTOP` constant below.
41	 * `columnGap` below is now set per-breakpoint instead of once at the base level.
42	 *
43	 * VERTICAL (ROW) GAP — 64px, and UNLIKE the horizontal gap above, this one has a real registered
44	 * token: `--zimm-scale-1600` (`zimmTokens.ts`), which resolves to `spacing['4xl']` —
45	 * independently verified directly against `foundation/spacing.ts` (`'4xl': '4rem'`, i.e. 64px),
46	 * not assumed from the build plan's own citation of it. Matches the real bound Figma variable
47	 * `section/4xl` (Designs file) / `alias/space/1600` (System file) per build plan §B1. Per this
48	 * step's own instruction, a REAL token is referenced directly (`var(--zimm-scale-1600)`) rather
49	 * than re-declared as a named constant — there is nothing to name here that isn't already named.
50	 *
51	 * COLUMN COUNT PER BREAKPOINT — three tiers: 2 (Mobile, below `breakpoints.md`), 3 (Tablet,
52	 * `breakpoints.md` up), 4 (Desktop, `breakpoints.xl` up).
53	 *   - `GRID_COLUMNS_BASE = 2` (Mobile only — matches the "2-up on the smallest breakpoint"
54	 *     convention `overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx`'s own `SimpleGrid columns={[2, 2,
55	 *     4, 5]}` already establishes elsewhere in this codebase).
56	 *   - `GRID_COLUMNS_TABLET = 3` — originally Marcel's own direct figure (2026-09-08), not a
57	 *     re-derived Figma reading, since this grid's provisional design source (cited above) has no
58	 *     Tablet-specific node of its own. Corrected 2026-09-10: a fuller page-node audit (the same
59	 *     pass that fixed this file's own HORIZONTAL GAP section) checked the real Tablet page frame
60	 *     directly (`9560:137692`, cited above for its gap value) and found it also shows exactly 3
61	 *     fluid-width cards per row — the figure was already corroborated, this comment just never
62	 *     connected the two. Confirmed, not merely instructed, as of this correction.
63	 *   - `GRID_COLUMNS_DESKTOP = 4` — unchanged, the one confirmed-via-Figma value (cited above).
64	 *
65	 * HEADER HEIGHT — deliberately UNSET (contrast `zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts`'s own
66	 * `HEADER_HEIGHT_MOBILE`/`DESKTOP`). The one Figma reading available (`3332:37131`, 75px,
67	 * Desktop-only) has no corroborating Mobile/Tablet reading to pair it with, and neither this
68	 * step's brief nor the build plan's own B1 pass criteria asks for a fixed header height at all —
69	 * unlike the rail, where two independent node heights (Mobile+Tablet-covering 56px, Desktop 96px)
70	 * were both explicitly supplied. Setting one anyway from a single, viewport-unconfirmed number
71	 * would be inventing a cross-viewport claim this session has no evidence for. `header` below sizes
72	 * itself from its own content instead (`display: flex`, vertically centred) — the same
73	 * "leave it simple, comment why" instruction this docblock's COLUMN COUNT section above follows
74	 * for the same underlying reason (one Desktop-only reading, no Tablet/Mobile counterpart).
75	 *
76	 * TITLE ROW PADDING — corrected 2026-09-10, closing a real, live-confirmed bug (Figma-vs-code
77	 * audit requested by Marcel, same pass that found and fixed the sibling Rail's own header padding
78	 * bug). The paragraph this replaces called the horizontal inset "deliberately zero... flagged for
79	 * confirmation" pending a real page context — that page context now exists
80	 * (`overrides/app/pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx`), and checking the header row directly against
81	 * the three real page-composition frames (`9551:110758` Desktop, `9560:137691` Tablet,
82	 * `9560:138462` Mobile, same `Zimmermann_Designs` file) found the actual values are neither zero
83	 * nor the asymmetric split the previous revision derived from a single provisional bar node
84	 * (`3332:37131`) — see "Header padding" below, which replaces both the old "Header vertical
85	 * padding" and "Header horizontal insets" sections entirely.
86	 */
87	
88	// Horizontal card-to-card gap, Desktop only now — see this file's own "HORIZONTAL GAP" docblock
89	// section above for the full per-breakpoint correction. rem, not px, matching
90	// zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts's CARD_WIDTH_MOBILE/TABLET/DESKTOP precedent for a sizing
91	// (non-hairline) dimension with no foundation token yet.
92	const GRID_CARD_GAP_DESKTOP = '6rem'; // 96px — confirmed Figma value, checked at two independent sources (40000301:11694 "Product Card Group" master, Size=Desktop/Display=4, node 40000307:12446; and the page-level instance 3332:35655). No --zimm-scale-* equivalent (nearest neighbours: named scale 5xl=80px / 6xl=128px; numeric alias 1600=64px jumps straight to 3500=140px) — pending promotion to foundation/spacing.ts or sizes.ts by the UI designer.
93	
94	// Column counts per breakpoint — see this file's own "COLUMN COUNT PER BREAKPOINT" docblock
95	// section above for the full reasoning and sourcing (Desktop is a confirmed Figma reading; Mobile
96	// and Tablet are Marcel's own direct figures, 2026-09-08, not re-derived design-asset readings).
97	const GRID_COLUMNS_BASE = 2; // Mobile only (below breakpoints.md) — Marcel, 2026-09-08.
98	const GRID_COLUMNS_TABLET = 3; // breakpoints.md up, below breakpoints.xl — Marcel, 2026-09-08.
99	const GRID_COLUMNS_DESKTOP = 4; // breakpoints.xl and up — confirmed (Figma nodes cited in the docblock above).
100	
101	// Same Tablet/Desktop query convention (name and breakpoint) as zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts's
102	// own identically-named constants.
103	const TABLET_UP_QUERY = `@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`; // 768px
104	const DESKTOP_UP_QUERY = `@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.xl})`; // 1280px — the confirmed 4-up/288px reading itself comes from a 1440px Figma frame, inside this tier.
105	
106	// Content max-width — fixed 2026-09-08, same root cause and same fix shape as
107	// zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts's own identical bug found via live testing the same day: with no
108	// cap, `container`'s `width: '100%'` (and `grid`'s own, below) stretch to whatever width the page
109	// actually provides — confirmed via Storybook screenshot that this genuinely oversizes every card
110	// beyond the confirmed 288px reading, not just a cosmetic nit. 1440px is the same confirmed value
111	// `GRID_CARD_GAP_DESKTOP`'s own docblock derives from (4 x 288px cards + 3 x 96px gaps) — restated here as
112	// a width cap rather than a per-card value. Desktop-only, matching the fact that the 4-column
113	// layout itself only applies from this breakpoint up; neither the Mobile (2-column) nor Tablet
114	// (3-column) tier has a confirmed reference *width* to cap against — Marcel's own figures above
115	// are column counts, not card widths or a max-width reading — so both stay fluid, same "don't
116	// guess" reasoning as the column counts' own docblock section.
117	// audit-allow: derived composite (already-pending card width x confirmed column/gap counts),
118	// not itself a value with any promotable foundation-token equivalent.
119	const GRID_CONTENT_MAX_WIDTH_DESKTOP = '90rem'; // 1440px = (288px x 4 cards) + (96px x 3 gaps)
120	
121	// Header padding — corrected 2026-09-10, replacing both the old "Header vertical padding" and
122	// "Header horizontal insets" sections (see the module docblock's own "TITLE ROW PADDING" note for
123	// the full correction narrative). Checked directly against the three real page-composition frames
124	// rather than the single provisional bar node the previous revision relied on:
125	//   - Desktop (`9551:110758`): 40px padding on all four sides, symmetric -- not the previous
126	//     asymmetric 40px-start/180px-end split, which was derived from that bar's own inner content
127	//     box being narrower than the frame for unrelated layout reasons, not a real padding reading.
128	//   - Tablet (`9560:137691`) / Mobile (`9560:138462`), identical: 32px horizontal, 20px vertical,
129	//     symmetric -- not the previous zero horizontal / 32px vertical (the 32px vertical value was
130	//     real but only for Desktop; Tablet/Mobile's own real vertical figure is smaller, 20px).
131	// All three real values map onto already-registered tokens: `--zimm-scale-1000` (40px),
132	// `--zimm-scale-800` (32px), `--zimm-scale-500` (20px, spacing['l']) -- confirmed directly against
133	// zimmTokens.ts, not assumed.
134	const HEADER_PADDING_INLINE = 'var(--zimm-scale-800)'; // 32px -- Tablet/Mobile
135	const HEADER_PADDING_BLOCK = 'var(--zimm-scale-500)'; // 20px -- Tablet/Mobile
136	const HEADER_PADDING_DESKTOP = 'var(--zimm-scale-1000)'; // 40px -- Desktop, all four sides
137	
138	export const ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid = {
139	  parts: ['container', 'header', 'grid'],
140	
141	  baseStyle: (): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => ({
142	    container: {
143	      width: '100%',
144	      marginInline: 'auto',
145	      [DESKTOP_UP_QUERY]: {
146	        maxWidth: GRID_CONTENT_MAX_WIDTH_DESKTOP,
147	      },
148	    },
149	
150	    header: {
151	      display: 'flex',
152	      alignItems: 'center',
153	      justifyContent: 'space-between',
154	      paddingInline: HEADER_PADDING_INLINE,
155	      paddingBlock: HEADER_PADDING_BLOCK,
156	      [DESKTOP_UP_QUERY]: {
157	        paddingInline: HEADER_PADDING_DESKTOP,
158	        paddingBlock: HEADER_PADDING_DESKTOP,
159	      },
160	    },
161	
162	    grid: {
163	      display: 'grid',
164	      width: '100%',
165	      gridTemplateColumns: `repeat(${GRID_COLUMNS_BASE}, 1fr)`,
166	      // Per-breakpoint now — see this file's own "HORIZONTAL GAP" docblock section above for the
167	      // correction. Mobile/Tablet use real registered tokens directly; only Desktop's 96px is a
168	      // pending-token named constant.
169	      columnGap: 'var(--zimm-scale-1000)', // 40px — Mobile
170	      // Real registered token, referenced directly — see this file's own "VERTICAL (ROW) GAP"
171	      // docblock section above for why this one is NOT a named constant, unlike GRID_CARD_GAP_DESKTOP.
172	      rowGap: 'var(--zimm-scale-1600)', // 64px
173	      [TABLET_UP_QUERY]: {
174	        gridTemplateColumns: `repeat(${GRID_COLUMNS_TABLET}, 1fr)`,
175	        columnGap: 'var(--zimm-scale-5xl)', // 80px
176	      },
177	      [DESKTOP_UP_QUERY]: {
178	        gridTemplateColumns: `repeat(${GRID_COLUMNS_DESKTOP}, 1fr)`,
179	        columnGap: GRID_CARD_GAP_DESKTOP,
180	      },
181	    },
182	  }),
183	};

content.text:
Here's the real re-audit, done properly this time — fresh Figma pulls, fresh code reads, actual math cross-checked against actual numbers, not old citations.

## What I could and couldn't do

I don't have a browser tool in this environment, so I can't screenshot localhost or Storybook directly — both render their actual content via JavaScript, and a plain fetch only gets me the empty loading shell, not the real picture. What I *could* confirm: both servers are up, and the live page correctly shows the empty state for a fresh visit with no browsing history (which is the right behavior, not a bug). For the actual pixel-level design comparison, I leaned on something just as rigorous: pulling exact numbers from Figma (positions, widths, gaps) and exact numbers from the current CSS, then checking the math matches — which is how I caught real bugs earlier this session too.

## Rail — fully confirmed, no new issues

Pulled the real component set fresh. The numbers came back exact:
- **Zero gap between cards at every screen size** — 288×5=1440 (Desktop), 256×3=768 (Tablet), 201×2=402 (Mobile), cards sitting perfectly edge to edge. Our code already does exactly this (`gap: 0`).
- **Header heights**: 96px Desktop, 56px Tablet/Mobile — exact match to what's coded.
- **Bleed**: checked the rail sitting inside a real PDP mockup at all 3 sizes — it spans the full page width with zero inset (x=0, full frame width) at every breakpoint. Matches our bleed fix exactly.

## Full History page — fully confirmed, no new issues

Every number checked out:
- Card gaps: 96px Desktop, 80px Tablet, 40px Mobile — all exact matches, computed directly from real card positions, not assumed.
- Row gap (vertical): 64px, matches.
- Column counts: 4/3/2 — matches.
- Header height math (padding + content): 104px Desktop, 64px Tablet/Mobile — both land exactly right.
- **Footer spacing** — this one's satisfying: the reserved 164px block (32px + 52px button + 80px padding) sits flush against the last card row and flush against the real footer, with zero extra gap, at all three screen sizes, independently confirmed with real coordinates. Exactly matches what's already built.

## Card behavior (default / hover / out-of-stock) — confirmed, with one thing I chased down and ruled out

Pulled fresh screenshots of all three states. Default and out-of-stock both matched what I found last time. Hover (in-stock) also matched — size selector appears, price hides, bag icon stays — but I spotted something that looked like a real miss at first: the hover screenshot showed literal text reading "SELECT SIZE & ADD TO BAG" next to the bag icon, and our code never renders any visible text there, only an icon.

I dug into it before flagging it as a bug, and it turned out to be a false alarm: that text is sitting in the exact same layer that shows "PRODUCT NAME" in the default-state screenshot — it's the product-name placeholder slot, and whoever built this one specific mockup instance just typed instructional text into it instead of a real name, most likely as a note to themselves about what the state does. It's not a separate, real UI element we're missing. Worth mentioning since I did seriously consider it, but it's not a gap.

## Size chip spacing — still a real, confirmed bug, now with harder evidence

Re-pulled the master component fresh: 6 chips, each exactly 28×28px, with an exact 8px gap between them (168px of chips + 40px of gaps = 208px total) — completely fixed, independent of container width. Our code still uses `justifyContent: space-between` instead, which stretches the gaps to fill whatever width is available. I also found something worth noting: the current code's own comment cites checking a real page instance (not the master component) that happens to have exactly 6 chips filling exactly 208px — which looks identical to a fixed 8px gap in that one specific case, but isn't the same rule. That's the exact "checked the instance, not the master" mistake this project already caught itself making once before this session (with the rail's header alignment). This is still open, unfixed, ready to go whenever you want it done.

## Bottom line

Rail and Full History page are both genuinely 1:1 with Figma now — not just "looks right," independently verified with matching numbers on both sides. The one real, unresolved item is still the size chip spacing. Want me to fix that now?

12	 *     real interactive chips, just non-interactive — confirmed via `get_design_context` on
13	 *     node 40003066:34866 ("Type=One Size").

18	    radiogroup: {
19	      display: 'flex',

21	      // Fixed 8px gap, not `justifyContent: 'space-between'` (corrected 2026-09-10, closing a
22	      // real bug found by a fresh Figma-vs-code audit). The previous value was confirmed against

24	      // chips filling exactly 208px — 6×28px chips + 5×8px gaps = 208px, so `space-between`
25	      // produces pixel-identical spacing to a fixed 8px gap in that one specific case, but the two
26	      // rules diverge the moment a product has fewer than 6 sizes: `space-between` spreads fewer
27	      // same-size chips across the same 208px width (wider gaps), while the real rule keeps the
28	      // gap fixed and lets the row itself be narrower. The real master component
29	      // (`40003066:34867`, "Type=Default") settles it directly: 6 `.base-size-selector` instances
30	      // at x = 0/36/72/108/144/180, each 28px wide — a fixed 8px gap

So the source code is right. What I think happened: **your dev server hasn't actually picked up the change.**

Here's the plain-language version of why this is different from a normal file edit. Most of the files I've touched all session are React components — when I save one, your dev server's hot-reload notices and swaps it in live. But a `.css.ts` file like this one isn't a component — it's a "recipe" that Chakra (the UI library) reads *once*, when the whole page first boots, to build one big combined style object for every component in the app. If the dev server's hot-reload doesn't realize that this deeply-nested recipe object needs rebuilding (which is a known soft spot — we've hit this same "change didn't take effect until a hard refresh" issue twice already this session with other shared files), you can end up looking at the *old* spaced-out version even though the file on disk is already fixed.

Can you fully restart the dev server (stop `npm start` and start it again — not just refresh the browser tab)? A theme-level change like this is more likely to need a real restart than just a hard refresh, since the whole theme object gets built once at startup. If it still looks wrong after a full restart, tell me and I'll dig further — but at that point it'd mean something I haven't found yet, not what I can currently see in the code.

Found it — and it's genuinely not a code problem. I fetched the real page straight from the server (bypassing your browser entirely) and inspected the exact CSS it's sending:

**The radiogroup row:** `display:flex; align-items:center; gap:var(--zimm-scale-200)` — no `justify-content` at all. That's my fix, byte for byte.

**Each individual chip:** `width:var(--zimm-scale-700); height:var(--zimm-scale-700)` — the fixed 28×28px box, unchanged, correct.

**The token itself:** `--zimm-scale-200: 0.5rem` — that's 8px, exactly right.

So the server is 100% sending the correct, fixed code. Every layer I could check is right. That means what you're looking at in the browser isn't coming from the dev server at all anymore — it's a leftover in your browser itself.

This app is a PWA, which means it registers a **service worker** — a background script Chrome keeps running that's specifically designed to serve cached pages even when the real server has something newer. Restarting the dev server doesn't touch that cache at all; it lives entirely in the browser, independent of the server. That's almost certainly what's still showing you the old version.

Try one of these:
1. Open DevTools → **Application** tab → **Service Workers** → click **Unregister**, then reload the page.
2. Or, with DevTools open, right-click the browser's reload button and choose **Empty Cache and Hard Reload**.
3. Or fastest gut-check: open the same PLP page in an **incognito/private window** — that has no service worker registered yet, so it'll show you the true current state immediately.

Try #3 first since it's the quickest way to confirm — if the chips look right there, we've found it, and you can clear the service worker in your normal window after.

You were right — I should've taken that more seriously the first time. Let me show you the math, since I can actually calculate it from numbers I already know.

**PLP's placeholder grid genuinely doesn't give each card enough room, and no amount of gap-tweaking could fix that.**

Here's the arithmetic, using PLP's actual current layout code:
- Page content area at a typical desktop width (~1440px), minus page padding, minus the 280px filter sidebar, minus the gap between sidebar and grid ≈ **1072px** left for the product grid.
- At that width, PLP's placeholder grid shows 5 columns (`columns={[2, 2, 4, 5]}`), with 16px gaps between them (4 gaps total = 64px).
- `(1072 - 64) / 5` ≈ **~202px per card.**

content.text:
Yes, I understand it now — and I should say clearly: you were right from the moment you first raised it, and I was too slow to accept it. Here's the point in one sentence: **six chips need at least 168px just to sit touching, and PLP's placeholder card only has about 122px of room for them** — no spacing fix, mine or otherwise, was ever going to close a 46px+ gap. That's not a chip bug, it's a "the card itself is the wrong size" situation, and it only shows up on PLP because PLP is the one surface still running the old placeholder grid instead of the real one.

Saved that reasoning to memory so it doesn't need re-deriving next time this symptom shows up on PLP specifically. Everything's left exactly where you want it: size-chip fix stays as-is (correct, and already proven correct via the served CSS), PLP's grid stays untouched until the real one gets built. Nothing else pending from this thread.

content.text:
Found it, and traced the exact mechanism — this one's a real interaction between two things: my earlier fix, and a separate, pre-existing gap in the Grid's own code that was just never triggered before.

**The short version:** when you hover a card, the size-selector row goes from "invisible and not taking up space" to "visible and part of the layout." Before my fix, that row could always squeeze itself down to fit whatever room it was given. After my fix, it has a genuine, non-negotiable minimum width (six 28px chips + five fixed 8px gaps = ~208px) — which is exactly what Figma actually wants, but it means the row can no longer shrink past that point.

Separately — and this part has nothing to do with my fix, it's just been sitting there — the Full History grid's own column code doesn't tell the browser "these columns are allowed to be smaller than their content." So when that now-208px-wide row suddenly needs more room than a narrow column currently has, instead of just clipping or overflowing quietly, the browser does what it's told to do by default: **it widens the whole column to make room.** And because one column's width is shared by every row underneath it, that stretch applies to every card in that column, not just the one you're hovering — which is exactly why you saw the whole column grow, not just one card. The taller-looking image is a side effect of that: the image is set to keep a fixed proportion (2:3), so a wider box means a taller image, automatically.

Why only at the narrow end of each size tier: there's just enough slack at wider tablet/desktop/mobile widths for a column to already be wider than 208px, so nothing needs to stretch. At the narrow end of each tier, the column's natural share is closer to (or under) that 208px line, so hovering tips it over.

**The fix is small, and it's a pattern this codebase already uses elsewhere** (there are already a couple of spots doing the equivalent thing for text/price elements): tell the grid's columns explicitly "you're allowed to shrink to zero, don't grow to fit a child's content" — a one-line change per breakpoint in the Full History grid's own file, nothing touched in the card or the size chips themselves.

Want me to make that fix?

Good — I went and checked the actual image-swap code directly, and it rules out the swap as an independent cause. Both images (the default and the "model" hover shot) are stacked with `position: absolute; inset: 0`, each sized via `width:100%; height:100%; object-fit: cover` to exactly fill the same box — the swap is a pure opacity crossfade. Neither image can ever change that box's size; the box's shape is locked entirely by its own `aspect-ratio`, driven only by *its own width*. So the box growing has to come from the width changing upstream — which is exactly the grid-column mechanism I traced. The "image looks bigger when it swaps to the model shot" is the same event happening at the same time (hover), not a second, separate cause — the image is just filling whatever box it's handed, and that box got wider.

content.text:
Here's the mechanism, in plain terms.

**`1fr` isn't quite what it sounds like.** You'd think "1fr" means "exactly one fair share, no more, no less." But CSS secretly reads it as "at least as much room as whatever's inside needs, AND ALSO try to give it one fair share." There's a hidden safety-net minimum baked in.

Think of splitting a pizza four ways. `1fr` columns are like a rule that says: "everyone gets an equal slice — but if someone's fork needs extra clearance to fit on the table, widen the *whole table* to make room for that one fork." Nobody asked for that, but that's the default behavior.

That's exactly what was happening: each product card normally just takes its fair, equal slice of the row. But the moment you hover a card, the size-selector row (now correctly holding a fixed minimum width thanks to the earlier fix) suddenly says "I need at least ~208px, no less." The column had no rule telling it "you're not allowed to grow past your fair share for this" — so the browser did what `1fr`'s hidden default says: widen the column to fit that demand. And because one column's width applies to *every card sitting in it*, not just the one you're hovering, the whole column — and every image in it, since images keep a fixed shape — stretched along with it.

`minmax(0, 1fr)` removes that hidden safety net. It says: "this column's minimum is zero — split the row evenly regardless of what's inside, full stop." Back to the pizza analogy: now the rule is "equal slices, and if your fork doesn't fit in your slice, that's on your fork, we're not resizing the table." So now, even when the size-chip row wants more room than its column has, the column holds its ground — it just lets that content sit within its own card rather than dragging the whole column wider.

One honest caveat: this stops the *column* from stretching, but it doesn't magically create extra room out of nowhere. If a card's column were ever genuinely too narrow for its hover content, that content could clip slightly at the very edge instead of growing the column. Full History uses the real, Figma-confirmed 288px-card grid though (unlike PLP's placeholder one), so it isn't sitting anywhere near that edge — this fix should be clean there, not just clipping the symptom out of view.

So the same shopper with, say, 4 tracked items would see the link on mobile (4 > 2) and tablet (4 > 3), but not on desktop (4 is not > 5) — because on desktop, all 4 of their items already fit in the rail with no need to click through to see more.

content.text:
Found it — and it's a genuinely interesting one: **two different parts of the Rail are using two different definitions of "Desktop," and they don't agree.**

Here are the two numbers:

1. **How many cards to show** (`RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS` in `constants/index.ts`) switches from 3 to 5 at **1280px** — that's Chakra's standard, shared "xl" breakpoint, used sitewide.
2. **How wide each card should be styled** (in the Rail's own CSS) switches to "Desktop" sizing at **1024px** — a different, narrower number, deliberately chosen earlier this session because that's what the Rail's actual Figma design specifies as its real Desktop threshold, confirmed directly against the design file.

Those two numbers used to not matter much independently, but they now disagree with each other — and 1277px sits squarely in the 256px-wide gap between them (1024px–1280px). In that gap:

- The **card-width CSS** already thinks it's in Desktop mode (≥1024px), so it styles the row as five 20%-wide slots.
- The **item-count logic** still thinks it's in the previous tier (<1280px), so it still only allows 3 cards to render, and still triggers the link at "more than 3."

Put together: a row visually laid out for 5 cards, with only 3 actually placed in it — which is exactly the "4th one vanished, empty space where it should be, and the link shows anyway" you're seeing.

This isn't a typo-level fix — it's two different pieces of logic (one in the shared constants file, one in the Rail's own recipe) that need to agree on the same threshold. Want me to make them both key off the same 1024px number, or do you want to look at anything else first?

content.text:
Fixed and fully verified — `tsc` clean, all 1298 tests pass (85 files), lint and token-audit both unchanged from baseline.

**What changed, and why each piece was needed:**
- **`constants/index.ts`** — added `RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_DESKTOP_BREAKPOINT` (1024px) as the one shared source of truth, and corrected the stale comment that had been quietly asserting a no-longer-true fact (that the rail's CSS still used 1280px) — that comment is genuinely why nobody caught the drift.
- **New hook, `useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount.ts`** — replaces the plain `useBreakpointValue` call with two real `min-width` checks (768px and 1024px), matching exactly what the CSS already does, instead of Chakra's shared breakpoint shorthand which can't express 1024px at all.
- **`zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts`** — now imports that same shared constant instead of keeping its own local copy, so the two literally cannot retype the same number differently again.
- **`recommended-products/index.tsx`** and **`zimmRecentlyViewedRail/index.tsx`** — both switched to the new hook, so the "how many cards fit" and "when does the link show" logic and the "how wide is each card" styling are now driven by the exact same threshold.
- Added a dedicated test for the new hook (the old two component test files needed no changes — they pass unchanged, since jsdom's test polyfill happens to make both old and new mechanisms resolve to the same fallback value).

Nothing committed — this sits alongside the other two fixes from this session (size-chip spacing, grid track growth), all in the working tree, ready whenever you want them in.

content.text:
Because the bug itself lived in three places at once — this wasn't scope creep, it's just what "make three things agree on one number" actually touches. Breaking it down:

**One new fact, one new file:**
- `constants/index.ts` — added the single number (1024px) everything else now points at.

**One new mechanism to read that fact correctly, two files:**
- `useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount.ts` — the new hook itself.
- `useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount.test.ts` — every hook in this codebase gets its own test file; this one's no exception.

**Three places that were already using the *old, broken* way of getting this number, all needed to switch to the new one:**
- `zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts` — used to have its own private copy of "1024px"; now imports the shared one instead of retyping it (which is exactly how this bug happened in the first place — two copies of the same number, nobody keeping them in sync).
- `recommended-products/index.tsx` — the "should the link show" check.
- `zimmRecentlyViewedRail/index.tsx` — the "how many cards to render" check.

So really it's 1 fact + 1 mechanism (+its test) + 3 call sites that had to stop doing their own thing and start reading from the same place. Nothing unrelated got touched — every file is either the new source of truth or a consumer that was part of the actual disagreement.

content.text:
Found a real, concrete discrepancy — and I think it's exactly what you're seeing. Here's the full picture.

## The Rail itself: zero self-spacing, confirmed correct

I checked the Rail's own recipe first. It adds **no top or bottom spacing of its own at all** — only horizontal centering and a max-width. That's deliberate and matches Figma: I'd already confirmed (from the PDP page mockups) that Recently Viewed sits with **zero gap** against whatever's directly above and below it in the design — the spacing between sections isn't the rail's job, it's whoever places it.

## PDP: the rail gets a 64px gap above it that Figma doesn't show

On PDP, Recently Viewed is the last of three recommendation rails (Complete the Set, Might Also Like, Recently Viewed), and all three sit inside a `<Stack spacing={16}>` — Chakra's stacking helper that inserts a uniform 64px gap between every child. Since Recently Viewed is always last in that list, it always gets a 64px gap pushed in above it, no matter what.

That doesn't match the Figma reference I checked earlier — Product Card Group → Product Card Group with Lookbook → Recently Viewed → Footer, sitting with **zero gap** between every one of them. So PDP's 64px gap looks like a real, unexamined side effect of using a generic "stack everything with equal spacing" pattern for all three rails, not a deliberate call made specifically for Recently Viewed.

## PLP: zero gap, above and below

PLP places the rail as a plain sibling right after the product grid — no `Stack`, no margin, nothing. So it gets **zero gap above and below**, which matches the zero-gap principle the Figma evidence points to.

**One honest caveat:** the specific Figma frames I checked earlier were labelled "PDP Template" — I don't have a PLP-specific mockup in hand to point to directly. So I'm reasoning by extension (no known reason PLP should behave differently from PDP), not from a frame that literally shows PLP. Worth keeping in mind, though everything else lines up.

## Full History page: top is correct, bottom is deliberate, not a bug

Top: zero gap, matching Figma exactly (page content starts immediately below the site header, no extra margin).
Bottom: 112px of reserved padding — but that one's intentional, from earlier this session (space held for the not-yet-built "Load More" button).

## Bottom line

The "varying behavior" you're seeing is almost certainly real, and it's specifically a **PDP-only problem**: the same Recently Viewed rail gets a 64px gap above it on PDP but zero gap on PLP, purely because of how each page happens to wrap it — not because of any actual design difference between the two surfaces. PLP and Full History both already look correct.

Want me to fix PDP's spacing to match?
