# Build Plan — Real Einstein wiring for Recently Viewed (SFCC-83 Rail, SFCC-84 Full History)

**Produced:** 2026-09-15 · **Planner:** zm-planner (Opus, high effort)
**Branch:** `feature/SFCC-83-84_recently-viewed-einstein` (already created, forked from
`feature/SFCC-83-84_recently-viewed` = the interim mechanism shipping as draft PR #107)
**Gate:** `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-83+84-einstein/findings.md` (no open blocker; #3 resolved)
**Feature spec:** `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-83+84-einstein/feature-spec.md`

> **Read this first — the scope in the feature-spec is undercounted, corrected here after a direct
> code read.** The feature-spec says "3 files modified, 2 deleted, don't touch the recentlyViewed
> page." That is **not buildable as written**: the SFCC-84 Full History page and the PDP write-path
> both consume the two files marked for deletion, so deleting them while leaving those files alone
> breaks `tsc`. The real change is **~6 files modified + 4 files deleted** (see §3). It is still one
> contained, single-branch, single-PR piece of work — just bigger than the brief stated. Two other
> feature-spec instructions are corrected below (the mapper needs no change; the page + PDP + its
> tests must change). This plan is written against the corrected scope.

---

## 1. Goal statement

Swap the data source for Recently Viewed from the interim browser-tracked mechanism to real Einstein,
delivering **SFCC-83** (rail on PDP + PLP) and **SFCC-84** (Full History page) as already prescribed
by their unchanged ACs and unchanged Figma designs (audited in `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-83+84/`),
by matching the exact `useEinstein()` → `getRecommendations` → `recommendations.recs` pattern the
**four already-working recommenders in the same file** (`ADD_TO_CART_MODAL`, `CART_MAY_ALSO_LIKE`,
`PDP_COMPLETE_SET`, `PDP_MIGHT_ALSO_LIKE`) run live every day, and the shape the **original
`b5f4a45` Einstein mapper** established — reusing every presentational component, every mapper, and
every card decision the interim build already shipped unchanged (the container/presentational split
paying off exactly as designed). This is a **restore-and-merge onto a data seam**, not a
new-from-scratch build.

---

## 2. Scale call

### One branch, one PR, four commits. Justified.

One coherent feature (one data source swapped in two consumers), one reviewer conversation, one CI
run. The only protected file is `recommended-products/` (Tier 2, Squad B). No Tier 1 file is
touched anywhere. `use-einstein.js` is base SFCC — we only ever *call* it, never edit it (it is not
even in `overrides/`). So a single branch / single PR is correct; splitting would add a stacked-PR
tax for no isolation benefit.

**Four commits, sequenced so every commit is `tsc`-green** (consumers rewired before the modules
they depend on are deleted):

> E1 (rail) → E2 (page) → E3 (PDP write-path) → E4 (delete + cleanup)

### How much loop — scaled down deliberately

This is a mid-small change with a **hard ceiling on what can be proven**: Einstein is deployed
nowhere reachable (not dev, not SIT, none of the 8 storefronts, none of the 3 sandboxes). So there
is **no live render, no Storybook-against-Einstein, no browser check, no Playwright** possible for
the one behaviour that actually changed. Say this out loud rather than asking for a
visual-checkpoint step that cannot happen. Every pass criterion below therefore leans entirely on
**code-level correctness**: `npx tsc --noEmit`, the existing + rewritten Vitest suites (which prove
the wiring is structurally right *and* that the 6 other rails sharing the file do not regress),
lint, `audit:tokens`, `npm run build`, and the mandatory local CodeRabbit pass.

- **Full implementer → tester → scorer** on **E1** and **E2** only — these are where a silent
  wrong answer ships (an empty-state gate that never fires or fires always; a dead-check ordering
  that swallows the rail; regressing one of the 6 sibling rails; a flash-of-empty on the page).
- **Implementer + scorer only** on **E3** (a 3-line deletion) and **E4** (deletions + grep-gated
  cleanup) — their gate is mechanical (`tsc`, `npm run test`, `grep`, a diff read). A tester
  round-trip adds latency without adding a check.

**Deliberately dropped, with reasons — not oversights:**
- **No new stories, no story edits.** The presentational organisms (`zimmRecentlyViewedRail`,
  `zimmRecentlyViewedGrid`) and the cards take data as props and do not change. `recommended-products`
  is a hook-driven container with no story. Nothing to add.
- **No new interactive elements → no new state matrix.** The See-Full-History link, the rail, the
  cards and their hover/focus/active/disabled states all already exist and ship unchanged; only the
  data feeding them changes. The interactive-state pass-criteria rule adds nothing new here.
- **No copy-first, no render-pause.** `recommended-products/index.tsx` already exists as an override
  — this modifies it, it does not create it. The copy-first render-pause is both inapplicable and
  impossible (Einstein unreachable).
- **No Playwright / E2E.** These paths resolve to `e2e_scope: skip`; adding an allow-list group is
  Tier 1 CI config, out of scope. State this in the PR body rather than implying coverage exists.

---

## 3. File manifest

Tiers are from `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` and `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md` only (never the
registry). **No Tier 1 file is touched. Nothing is BLOCKED.**

### Modify

| File | Action | Tier | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| `overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.tsx` | Rewire the RV branch to Einstein (E1) | **Tier 2** — Shared Product Components (`protectedFiles.md`) | CODEOWNERS → `@ZimmermannAU/pwa-squad-b` (notify Squad A per Tier 2). Needs a non-author Squad B review. |
| `overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.test.tsx` | Rewrite RV test cases (E1) | **Tier 2** (same dir) | as above |
| `overrides/app/pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx` | Rewire the Full History container to Einstein (E2) — **feature-spec missed this** | Untiered (no `protectedFiles`/`frozenFiles` entry) | CODEOWNERS → Squad B by page association |
| `overrides/app/pages/recentlyViewed/index.test.tsx` | Rewire mocks from interim hooks to `useEinstein` (E2) — **feature-spec missed this** | Untiered | as above |
| `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` | Remove the interim `markProductViewed` write-path (E3) — **feature-spec missed this** | Untiered (page; not in frozen/protected) | CODEOWNERS → `@ZimmermannAU/pwa-squad-b` |
| `overrides/app/constants/index.ts` | Remove the now-dead interim constants, grep-gated (E4) | Untiered | — |

### Delete (explicitly authorised by the task prompt; AGENTS.md Hard Rule #9 satisfied)

| File | Why | Tier |
|---|---|---|
| `overrides/app/hooks/useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts` | Decision #3 — local tracking removed entirely, no gating crutch kept | Untiered — **not** on either protected-hook list |
| `overrides/app/hooks/useRecentlyViewedHistory.test.ts` | with its module | Untiered |
| `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts` | Superseded by Einstein's own internal `fetchRecProductDetails` (finding #11) | Untiered |
| `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedProductFetch.test.ts` | with its module | Untiered |

### Explicitly NOT changed — verify unchanged, do not touch

- `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedCard.ts` — **no functional change.** The feature-spec's
  "restore the 2 Einstein-only fields (`productId`, flat `image`)" instruction is **wrong** and must
  not be followed. The Einstein rec is `{...rec, ...fullProduct, productId, image}` — a strict
  **superset** of the plain `ShopperProductsTypes.Product` this mapper already reads, so the current
  file reads `id`/`imageGroups`/`variants`/`price` straight off the rec unchanged. Restoring
  `productId`/flat-`image` would re-introduce two hand-rolled fields (that the current docblock
  explicitly explains it removed) *and* would be strictly worse than the current colour-scoped,
  two-pass, sequence-sorted image selection those fields predate. This is the exact superset logic
  finding #11 already applied to the full-history mapper — it applies identically here. A
  **docblock-only** note that the input is again the Einstein rec is optional (E4).
- `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedCard.test.ts` — no fixture change needed (a `Product`-shaped
  fixture is a valid Einstein rec by superset; existing behavioural assertions still hold).
- `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts` + `.test.ts` — no change (finding #11,
  confirmed: no import from the deleted fetch, superset input).
- `overrides/app/utils/productCardMappingHelpers.ts` — shared primitives, untouched.
- `overrides/app/hooks/useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount.ts` + `.test.ts` — presentation-layer
  breakpoint logic, independent of data source. Feeds the See-Full-History threshold. **Keep.**
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedRail/**` — presentational, props-only.
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedGrid/**` — presentational, props-only.
  (Note it still imports `RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED` — see E4 and Open Question 4.)
- `overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx` (PLP) — its `<RecommendedProducts recommender=...>`
  call is unchanged; the data swap lives entirely inside `recommended-products`. PLP has no
  view-write path. **No change.**
- `overrides/app/routes.tsx`, `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` — the route and recipes are
  already registered from the interim build. **Not touched** (both are Tier 2; leaving them alone
  keeps this PR's protected surface to one file).

**One protection tier (Tier 2) is touched** — `recommended-products/`. AGENTS.md Hard Rule #10
("more than one protection tier") does **not** trip; a single confirmation at plan approval covers it.

---

## 4. Steps

One commit per step. `conventions.md` no-magic-strings throughout: the recommender is only ever
`EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED`, never the literal `'viewed-recently-einstein'`.

### E1 — Rail: `recommended-products/index.tsx` + `index.test.tsx` (Tier 2)

**Consequence if wrong:** the PDP/PLP rail either never renders, always renders (even for a
zero-history shopper — the opposite of AC 8), or one of the 6 sibling rails on the same page breaks
silently. This is the load-bearing commit.

**What changes (four coupled edits, one commit — they are meaningless apart):**
1. **Remove the fetch-effect early-return** (currently lines ~300-302: `if (recommender ===
   PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED) return;`) so `getRecommendations(recommender, _products)` fires for this
   recommender again — exactly as it does for the other four. (Finding #9a.) The seed-products arg
   `_products` stays as-is; RV supplies none, Einstein derives from `cookieId`/`userId` (finding #7,
   carried assumption).
2. **Switch the RV render branch's data source** from `useRecentlyViewedProductFetch(recentlyViewedIds)`
   → `recentlyViewedProducts` to **`recommendations.recs`**. The existing
   `.map(selectRecentlyViewedCard) → .filter(non-null) → .map(add headingLevel+variation)` chain and
   the `selectRecentlyViewedCard` import stay; only the source array changes. (Finding #9b.)
3. **Empty-state gate becomes `recommendations?.recs?.length` directly** (decision #3): replace
   `if (!hasRecentlyViewed) return null;` with `if (!recommendations?.recs?.length) return null;`.
   Keep the branch **ahead of** the base dead-check (`if (!isLoading && (!recommendations ||
   recommendations.length < 1)) return null;`) — with Einstein populating `recommendations` as an
   object, the branch's own recs-gate now owns loading (recs undefined → null) and empty (recs
   empty → null, AC 8); the base dead-check is designed for the ProductScroller path and must not
   swallow the RV rail. **Delete the local-tracking crutch entirely** — remove the
   `useRecentlyViewedHistory`, `useRecentlyViewedProductFetch`, and `NO_RECENTLY_VIEWED_IDS` imports
   and calls, and the `hasRecentlyViewed`/`recentlyViewedIds` destructures.
4. **Preserve, unchanged:** the Cart exclusion (`isCartPage` → `return null`), the See-Full-History
   link (`cards.length > visibleCardCount` via the kept `useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount` +
   `buildUrl(RECENTLY_VIEWED_ROUTE)`), rendering `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` (not `ProductScroller`),
   the `<Box ref={ref} {...props}>` wrapper and its bleed passthrough.

**Named, intended behaviour change (not a regression):** the `isOnScreen && recommendations?.recs`
impression effect (lines ~333-350) currently no-ops for RV because `recommendations` stays `[]`.
Once real recs arrive, `sendViewReco` + `dataCloud.sendViewRecommendations` begin firing for the RV
rail. Finding #9c: this is the intended closing of a previously-accepted analytics gap. Name it in
the PR body; no code change needed for it.

**Cart wasted-call note:** removing the early-return means `getRecommendations` also fires on Cart
(same recommender string), where the branch returns null. One unread call on a descoped surface —
acceptable, matches "fire unconditionally like the other four." The implementer *may* keep a
Cart-only skip in the effect if trivial; not required.

**Test rewrite (`index.test.tsx`, ~455 lines, ~9 RV cases):** remove the
`vi.mock('../../hooks/useRecentlyViewedHistory')` and `vi.mock('../../utils/recentlyViewedProductFetch')`
blocks and their `mockUseRecentlyViewedHistory`/`mockUseRecentlyViewedProductFetch` handles; drive
every RV case through the already-present `mockUseEinstein` by setting `recommendations: {recs: [...]}`.
Follow the exact `mockUseEinstein` pattern this file already uses for the other four recommenders.

**Pass criteria:**
- `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0.
- `grep -n "useRecentlyViewedHistory\|useRecentlyViewedProductFetch\|hasRecentlyViewed\|recentlyViewedIds\|NO_RECENTLY_VIEWED_IDS" index.tsx` returns **zero** hits.
- The RV branch renders `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` when `recommendations.recs.length > 0`, and returns
  `null` when `recs` is empty/undefined (AC 8) and when on the Cart route. Each of these three
  assertions **must be made to fail on purpose first** (memory: prove-don't-assert) before it counts.
- **The 6 sibling rails are unaffected:** a test proves a non-RV recommender still calls
  `getRecommendations` and renders via `ProductScroller` (not the rail) — flip the recommender to a
  non-RV value and watch the rail assertion fail, proving the branch is recommender-gated.
- See-Full-History link appears iff `cards.length > visibleCardCount` and points at
  `buildUrl(RECENTLY_VIEWED_ROUTE)`.
- `npm run test` green.

**Skill:** no scaffolding skill (this is hand-editing an existing override). Run `/code-quality` as
the pre-commit audit.

### E2 — Full History page: `recentlyViewed/index.tsx` + `index.test.tsx` (untiered)

**Consequence if wrong:** the Full History page either won't compile (its two data imports are
being deleted), or flashes "you haven't viewed anything" at a real returning shopper mid-fetch, or
loses its Add-to-Bag/size behaviour.

**What changes:**
- Replace the two interim data hooks (`useRecentlyViewedHistory` + `useRecentlyViewedProductFetch`,
  lines 217-218) with a direct Einstein read: call `useEinstein()`, fire
  `getRecommendations(EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED)` in a `useEffect([])`, and read
  `recommendations.recs` + `isLoading`. Map `recs` through the **unchanged**
  `selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard` (superset input, finding #11). The Add-to-Bag /
  size-selection map (`selectedSizeChipValues`, `resolveOrderableVariant`, `handleResolvedAddToBag`)
  is unchanged — it reads `product.id`/`product.price`/`product.variants`, all present on the rec.
- **Empty gate (decision #3, race-safe):** show the grid when `recs.length > 0`; show
  `EmptyRecentlyViewed` only when `!isLoading && recs.length === 0`; render nothing while
  `isLoading`. This preserves the page's own existing anti-flash reasoning (its docblock already
  argues against gating on `cards.length` mid-fetch) — just re-expressed against Einstein's
  `isLoading` instead of the deleted hook's ID list.
- Keep unchanged: SEO (`noindex, nofollow` child), the `<Heading as="h1" srOnly>`, the
  `APP_MAIN_BLEED_MX` wrapper + 112px footer reservation, the item-count label.
- Rewrite `index.test.tsx` mocks from the two interim hooks to `useEinstein` (same pattern as E1).

**Pass criteria:**
- `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0.
- `grep -n "useRecentlyViewedHistory\|useRecentlyViewedProductFetch" recentlyViewed/index.tsx` → zero hits.
- Grid renders when `recs.length > 0`; empty state renders only when `!isLoading && recs.length === 0`;
  **prove the no-flash contract fails on purpose first** (assert the empty state does NOT render
  while `isLoading` true with empty recs).
- Add-to-Bag with and without a size selection still resolves to the right variant (existing
  assertions kept, passing unchanged).
- `npm run test` green.

**Skill:** hand-edit; `/code-quality` pre-commit.

### E3 — PDP write-path removal: `product-detail/index.tsx` (untiered)

**Consequence if wrong / why it's needed:** the interim `markProductViewed(product.id)` writes to
browser storage that nothing reads after E1/E2; leaving it keeps `useRecentlyViewedHistory` alive
and un-deletable, and ships dead code. Einstein's own write path (`einstein.sendViewProduct`,
already called unconditionally at lines ~812/817/829 — finding #5) **stays untouched** — it *is* the
real write path.

**What changes (exactly three lines, no more — AGENTS.md Hard Rule #5, no refactoring upward):**
- Remove the import `import { useRecentlyViewedHistory } from '../../hooks/useRecentlyViewedHistory';`
  (line ~63).
- Remove `const { markProductViewed } = useRecentlyViewedHistory();` (line ~807).
- Remove `if (product) markProductViewed(product.id);` (line ~839).

**Pass criteria:**
- `git diff` shows only those three removals; no other line in the file moved.
- `grep -n "markProductViewed\|useRecentlyViewedHistory" product-detail/index.tsx` → zero hits.
- `einstein.sendViewProduct` / `dataCloud.sendViewProduct` calls are byte-identical to before.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` + `npm run test` green.

**Skill:** hand-edit; implementer + scorer only.

### E4 — Delete interim modules + grep-gated cleanup

**Consequence if wrong:** a dangling import breaks the build, or a live constant gets deleted and
takes the grid with it.

**What changes:**
- Delete the four files in §3 (both hooks-modules-with-tests). Do this **last**, after E1-E3, so no
  intermediate `tsc` is ever broken.
- **Constants cleanup — grep-driven, not blind.** After E1-E3 land: remove
  `RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_STORAGE_KEY`, `GET_PRODUCTS_MAX_IDS_PER_REQUEST`, **and
  `RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED`** — all three now have zero live code consumers (verified:
  `zimmRecentlyViewedGrid` was re-checked directly and never imported the third one at all, only
  referenced it in a stale comment — see Open Questions 4/5, resolved 2026-09-15, Marcel: delete
  outright, no client-side cap to preserve).

/**
 * Maps one Recently Viewed product to the FULL `ZimmProductCard` props Recently Viewed's Full
 * History page (SFCC-84) renders — badge, size chips, was/now pricing and a multi-image gallery,
 * i.e. the `plp` variation's already-shipped shape, not `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s narrower
 * image-only rail shape (SFCC-83's `recentlyViewed` variation). Both mappers read the same
 * underlying input — a plain Commerce API `Product` from `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts`'s own
 * `getProducts` call — but produce deliberately different output shapes for two deliberately
 * different surfaces; see that mapper's own docblock for the rail's narrower contract and why it
 * stops at image-only.
 *
 * Added per the build plan's B2 discussion (finding 41b): "reuse the rail's mapper" was the
 * original, incorrect assumption for this page — `recentlyViewedCard.ts` cannot produce this
 * shape by its own design (image-only, no price, no gallery), so a second, separate mapper is
 * required. Per Jasmijn's SFCC-84 comment, the Full History card's default state is "image, name,
 * badge, price (incl. was/now), and cart icon" — exactly the `plp` variation's shape, which is why
 * this mapper's output includes `headingLevel: 'h3'` and `variation: 'plp'` directly (unlike
 * `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s `RecentlyViewedCard`, which deliberately excludes both as its rail
 * container's job) — mirroring `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `ProductListCardResult`, which
 * bakes in the same two fields for the same reason: its output is meant to be spread straight
 * into `<ZimmProductCard>` with nothing left for a caller to add.

# Handoff — SFCC-83+84-einstein
Branch: `feature/SFCC-83-84_recently-viewed-einstein`   Base: `c14ee9f` (tip of `feature/SFCC-83-84_recently-viewed`)   Head: (in progress)

## Steps
| # | What | Commit | Scorer verdict | Rework rounds |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | Rail: wire `recommended-products/index.tsx` + `.test.tsx` to real `useEinstein()` | `0f7de14` | PASS | 0 (round 1) |
| E2 | Full History page: wire `recentlyViewed/index.tsx` + `.test.tsx` to real `useEinstein()` | `07be6c5` | PASS | 0 (round 1) |
| E3 | PDP write-path removal: delete `markProductViewed`/`useRecentlyViewedHistory` usage from `product-detail/index.tsx` | `01f4dc3` | PASS | 0 (round 1) |

## Gates (real numbers, not claims)
| Gate | Result | Baseline |
|---|---|---|
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | 0 (clean) | 0 (clean) |
| `npm run test` | 1324/1324, 87 files | 1324/1324, 87 files |
| `npm run lint` | 8 errors / 44 warnings | 8 errors / 44 warnings (identical) |
| `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` | 3 unacknowledged | 3 unacknowledged (identical) |

Re-confirmed identical, zero drift, at E1, E2, and E3.

## UNIFORM findings
- **Stale recommendations on a failed re-fetch, no error signal.** Base SFCC's own `use-einstein.js`
  `getRecommendations`'s `catch` block only logs — never calls `setRecommendations` — so if a
  fetch succeeds once and a later re-fetch on the same mounted instance fails, the component keeps
  silently showing the old, now-stale data with nothing telling the shopper. CONFIRMED (traced to
  source by the E1 scorer, upgraded from the tester's PLAUSIBLE). Pre-existing in unmodified vendor
  code, applies to every recommender sharing this hook (not introduced by, or fixable within, this
  branch). Now applies to Recently-Viewed for the first time, since it never called this function
  before. Recommend naming in the PR body's "stated external dependencies" list.
- **Base SFCC's own Einstein hydration path doesn't cap at 24 before hydrating** (`fetchRecProductDetails`,
  found during Phase 1 planning, not step-specific — carried here for completeness). Same treatment:
  name in the PR body, do not attempt to fix in this branch.
- **First-paint flash: the empty state can briefly paint for a shopper who does have history.**
  `use-einstein.js:462-463`'s `isLoading`/`recommendations` both start `false`/`[]` on every render,
  before the mount effect has run — CONFIRMED, deterministic, traced to source (E2 tester, via an
  actual mutation test on the surrounding gate logic, not just a read). Same root cause at E1, but
  invisible there (E1's gate returns `null` for both "loading" and "empty" — nothing wrong ever
  paints). E2 is the first place this becomes visible, because it has two differently-worded states
  and briefly shows "you haven't viewed anything yet" to everyone, including shoppers with real
  history, until the fetch resolves. **Marcel's explicit decision (2026-09-15): name it, ship as
  is — no code fix.** Same treatment as the two findings above: record as a known, pre-existing
  limitation in the PR body, do not expand E2's scope to add a local "has fetched" flag.
- **The E4 forward-reference phrasing bug exists in two places, only one fixed so far.** E2's own
  docblock originally stated E4's file deletions as already-done ("both deleted in build plan step
  E4") when E4 hasn't run yet — caught by the E2 orchestrator, fixed directly (now: "scheduled for
  deletion in build plan step E4, not yet run as of this commit..."), confirmed by the E2 scorer.
  The **E2 scorer then found the identical construction still sitting, unfixed, in E1's own
  already-committed docblock** — `recommended-products/index.tsx:49-50`, "...both deleted in build
  plan step E4...". Not fixed as part of E2 (outside its manifest, would be scope creep on an
  already-committed step) — **E4's own planned stale-comment sweep of this exact file must catch
  this specific line**, not just the `:402` comment already named in the plan's file manifest.

## Could not verify
- Any live/visual rendering of the rail — Einstein is undeployed everywhere reachable (not dev, SIT,
  any of the 8 real storefronts, or the 3 sandboxes). Every check this step ran was code-level
  (tsc, mutation-tested Vitest, direct reads of the real vendor hook) — there is no live render to
  check against, and the plan itself states this ceiling rather than asking for an impossible
  visual checkpoint.
- Whether the real Business-Manager-configured `viewed-recently-einstein` recommender, once it
  exists, actually matches the shape assumed here — the *code* that merges Einstein's rec with a

**Fix 1 — `overrides/app/pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx` (untiered): gate on mapped cards, not raw recs.**

Currently (around line 281-324): `cards` is computed by `.map(selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard).filter(non-null)` over `recs`, but the render gate at line 324 checks `recs.length > 0` (and the empty-state branch checks `recs.length === 0`), not `cards.length`. If Einstein returns recs but every single one fails to map to a card (e.g. every product is now offline/deleted, so `selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard` returns `null` for each), `recs.length > 0` is still true, so the page takes the grid branch and renders `<ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid cards={[]} />` — which (per this page's own docblock, confirming `ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid`'s documented contract) renders `null` for an empty `cards` array. The empty-state branch never fires either, since it's gated on `recs.length === 0`, which is false. **The fix:** change both the grid-branch condition and the empty-state-branch condition to check `cards.length` instead of `recs.length`. Do NOT change how `isLoading` is used, and do NOT change how `recs` itself is computed or used to build `cards` — `cards` is already a synchronous, same-render derivation of `recs` (no separate state, no separate effect), so switching the gate's own condition to `cards.length` does not reintroduce any async race — it only fixes the specific degenerate case where recs exist but none of them successfully map. not fixed here.

recentlyViewed/index.tsx: the render gate checked recs.length (raw
Einstein count) instead of cards.length (count after
selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard's null-filtering map). If every
rec fails to map to a card -- e.g. every product now offline or
deleted -- recs.length stayed truthy, so the grid branch rendered
ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid with an empty cards array (which renders
null by its own contract), and the empty-state branch never got a
chance to fire either, since it checked the same recs.length. A
shopper with real but entirely stale history saw a blank page. Both
branch conditions now check cards.length instead. cards is a plain
synchronous map/filter over recs in the same render with no
separate state or effect, so this closes the gap without
reintroducing any async race. New test proves it, mutation-tested:
reverted the fix, confirmed the new test fails for the claimed
reason, restored, confirmed green. A pre-existing test was already
sitting on this exact edge case (returning null from the card mapper
for every product) but only asserted "does an h1 render" -- true
regardless of branch -- so it never caught the bug; corrected to
assert the actual branch rendered.

recommended-products/index.tsx: the fetch effect fired
getRecommendations unconditionally on the Cart route for the
Recently-Viewed recommender, even though the render branch always
returns null there and never reads the result. Named as an accepted,
optional cleanup in the original build plan ("may keep a Cart-only
skip if trivial; not required") -- now skipped outright. One
existing test asserted the old wasted-call behaviour as accepted;
updated to assert the call no longer happens.

returned are on code neither this fix nor the branch's own E1-E4

introduced.

# Handoff — SFCC-83+84-einstein
Branch: `feature/SFCC-83-84_recently-viewed-einstein`   Base: `c14ee9f` (tip of `feature/SFCC-83-84_recently-viewed`)   Head: (in progress)

E4's drop from 1324→1305 tests and 87→85 files is expected, not a regression: the two deleted
modules' own `.test.ts` files (19 tests, 2 files) went with them. Lint's 44→43 warnings is also
expected, not a regression: one warning lived in a now-deleted file. Both confirmed by the E4
scorer independently, not just asserted.

`npm run build` regenerates `translations/*.json` + `overrides/app/static/translations/compiled/*`
as a documented side effect (memory: `feedback_build_regenerates_translations.md`) — discarded via
`git checkout --` after inspecting the diff both times (once after the implementer's `npm run
test` run, once after my own `npm run build` run), confirmed unrelated both times (pre-existing
`recently_viewed.*` keys from E1/E2's own earlier commits, not new copy from E4).

## UNIFORM findings
- **Stale recommendations on a failed re-fetch, no error signal.** Base SFCC's own `use-einstein.js`
  `getRecommendations`'s `catch` block only logs — never calls `setRecommendations` — so if a
  fetch succeeds once and a later re-fetch on the same mounted instance fails, the component keeps
  silently showing the old, now-stale data with nothing telling the shopper. CONFIRMED (traced to
  source by the E1 scorer, upgraded from the tester's PLAUSIBLE). Pre-existing in unmodified vendor
  code, applies to every recommender sharing this hook (not introduced by, or fixable within, this
  branch). Now applies to Recently-Viewed for the first time, since it never called this function
  before. Recommend naming in the PR body's "stated external dependencies" list.
- **Base SFCC's own Einstein hydration path doesn't cap at 24 before hydrating** (`fetchRecProductDetails`,
  found during Phase 1 planning, not step-specific — carried here for completeness). Same treatment:
  name in the PR body, do not attempt to fix in this branch.
- **First-paint flash: the empty state can briefly paint for a shopper who does have history.**
  `use-einstein.js:462-463`'s `isLoading`/`recommendations` both start `false`/`[]` on every render,
  before the mount effect has run — CONFIRMED, deterministic, traced to source (E2 tester, via an
  actual mutation test on the surrounding gate logic, not just a read). Same root cause at E1, but
  invisible there (E1's gate returns `null` for both "loading" and "empty" — nothing wrong ever
  paints). E2 is the first place this becomes visible, because it has two differently-worded states
  and briefly shows "you haven't viewed anything yet" to everyone, including shoppers with real
  history, until the fetch resolves. **Marcel's explicit decision (2026-09-15): name it, ship as
  is — no code fix.** Same treatment as the two findings above: record as a known, pre-existing
  limitation in the PR body, do not expand E2's scope to add a local "has fetched" flag.
- **The E4 forward-reference phrasing bug existed in two places — both now fixed.** E2's own
  docblock originally stated E4's file deletions as already-done ("both deleted in build plan step
  E4") when E4 hadn't run yet — caught by the E2 orchestrator, fixed directly during E2 (worded to
  "scheduled for deletion..., not yet run as of this commit"), confirmed by the E2 scorer. The E2
  scorer then found the identical construction still sitting, unfixed, in E1's own already-committed
  docblock (`recommended-products/index.tsx:49-50`). Named as a required catch for E4's own sweep
  rather than fixed out-of-turn during E2 — **confirmed fixed as part of E4** (now correctly reads
  "both removed in build plan step E4", past tense, since E4 has actually run).

## Could not verify
- Any live/visual rendering of the rail — Einstein is undeployed everywhere reachable (not dev, SIT,
  any of the 8 real storefronts, or the 3 sandboxes). Every check this step ran was code-level
  (tsc, mutation-tested Vitest, direct reads of the real vendor hook) — there is no live render to
  check against, and the plan itself states this ceiling rather than asking for an impossible
  visual checkpoint.
- Whether the real Business-Manager-configured `viewed-recently-einstein` recommender, once it
  exists, actually matches the shape assumed here — the *code* that merges Einstein's rec with a
  real Commerce Product is confirmed real (`use-einstein.js:465-520`), but its real-world output
  isn't observable pre-deployment.
- The "impression analytics now fire for Recently-Viewed" behaviour change is real in the code
  (unchanged code path, now reachable for real) but genuinely untested — the test file mocks
  `useIntersectionObserver` to always return `false`, so nothing in this step's suite exercises
  `sendViewReco`/`dataCloud.sendViewRecommendations` actually firing for this branch.

- PR body must also name, plainly, as known/accepted limitations rather than silently shipped: all

Traced each one back through actual git history rather than just confirming they predate this branch. All of them are part of the SFCC-83/84 effort itself — none are from `develop` or an unrelated story — spanning from the very first commit that created these files (2026-09-07) through the later fix-batch work (2026-09-09), all landing on `feature/SFCC-83-84_recently-viewed` before this branch forked from it at `c14ee9f`.

**One important correction to how I characterized these to you:** the two "dead button" findings aren't actually an oversight — they're a documented, deliberate decision. The exact line CodeRabbit flags (`zimmProductCard/index.tsx:508`) sits right under a comment from commit `d752252` (2026-09-09) that reads: *"this deliberately ships the button inert (visible, clicking does nothing) rather than waiting for that story to land."* Someone already decided to ship it this way, on purpose, pending a separate Notify-Me/back-in-stock feature that hasn't been built yet. CodeRabbit is flagging a known, intentional placeholder as if it were a bug.

Here's where each of the 7 actually comes from:

| # | Finding | Introduced by | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `productListCardMapper.ts` — $0.00 renders for a hit with no price | `d752252` "resolve colour-blind images and complete card interactions" | 2026-09-09 |
| 2/3 | Notify Me button ships inert | `d752252`, same commit — **documented, deliberate**, waiting on a separate not-yet-built story | 2026-09-09 |
| 4 | Rail story's breakpoint docs went stale | Doc written in `93adcd2`, went stale when a later commit swapped the underlying hook | 2026-09-09 (doc), drifted since |
| 5 | Alt-text not normalized for every image candidate | `24a491e` "full-history card parity with PLP's product card" | 2026-09-09 |
| 6 | RV card links missing site/locale prefix | `b5f4a45` — the very first Einstein mapper commit, ever | 2026-09-07 |
| 7 | `.claude/registry/routes.md` stale | `3917fb4`, this session's own fix-batch, didn't trigger a routes-specific regen | this engagement |
| — | Rail overflows below 400px viewport | Rail's own CSS build/refinement commits | 2026-09-08/09 |
| — | Rail's `cards` prop accepts the wrong card-variation type | `ab26ee6` — the very first ZimmRecentlyViewedRail commit, ever | 2026-09-07 |

So: 6 of 8 are real, unintentional gaps from the original build (ranging from the very first commit to the later fix-batch). One (the Notify Me pair) is a documented placeholder, not a bug — that one's arguably not yours to fix at all right now, since fixing it for real means building the Notify-Me feature it's waiting on, not a quick patch.

Looks like a plain miss. On a non-AU storefront, clicking a Recently Viewed card would land you on the wrong site/locale.
2. **Stale breakpoint doc comment** in the rail's story file — genuinely just out of date; the doc still describes an old hook/breakpoint that got replaced later. Harmless, purely cosmetic.
3. **`.claude/registry/routes.md` stale** — auto-generated file that missed a regen. Zero functional impact, tooling metadata only.
4. **Rail's `cards` prop type is wider than it needs to be** (accepts any card variation, not just the recently-viewed one) — real type-safety gap, but nothing today actually passes the wrong variation in, so it's hardening, not a live bug.

**Not real bugs — already deliberate, and in one case already escalated to exactly this kind of decision:**

5. **"Notify Me" button ships inert.** The line CodeRabbit flags sits directly under a comment from 2026-09-09: *"this deliberately ships the button inert (visible, clicking does nothing) rather than waiting for that story to land."* Someone already decided this on purpose, pending a separate Notify-Me feature that hasn't been built yet. Not an oversight.
6. **$0.00 price render for a no-price hit.** There's a permanent regression test locking this in as correct, with a comment explaining exactly why: base SFCC's own `findLowestPrice` deliberately resolves "no price" to `0`, with its own source comment saying it does this "to be able to use this value on UI." Someone already read the vendor source directly and confirmed this is real, intended base-SFCC behavior — not a bug to route around.

CodeRabbit re-found something already flagged and already waiting on you specifically.

content.text:
**Consequence:** nothing wrong is happening today. This is about closing a door that's currently unlocked, not fixing something broken.

**Mechanism:** `ZimmProductCard` has four "variations" — PLP (full card: price, badge, size chips, add-to-bag), Home, Wishlist, and Recently-Viewed (image-only, nothing else). The Rail component's `cards` prop is typed to accept *any* of those four shapes, when it should only ever accept the Recently-Viewed one — that's the only kind it's built to render. Because the prop type is too loose, TypeScript won't stop someone from handing the Rail a PLP-shaped card by mistake — say, a future edit that copy-pastes card-building code from the PLP page without noticing it built the wrong variation. Nothing in the codebase does this today; every real caller already builds the correct `recentlyViewed`-shaped card before handing it to the Rail.

**Fix:** narrow the Rail's prop type from "any card variation" down to "only the recently-viewed one." Purely a type declaration change — no runtime behavior changes at all. The payoff is that if anyone ever *does* make that mistake in the future, TypeScript catches it immediately at compile time instead of silently letting the wrong shape through.

**Fix A — Recently Viewed card links are missing their site/locale URL prefix, in BOTH places this occurs.**

`overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedCard.ts:213` and `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts:392` both build `href: productUrlBuilder({ id: product.id })` — a bare `/product/:id` path with no site/locale prefix. `ZimmProductCard` renders this href via `react-router-dom`'s own `RouteLink` directly (not the base SFCC `Link`, which is the thing that normally applies a site/locale prefix internally) — so nothing downstream rescues this. On a non-default storefront (e.g. `/en-GB/...`), clicking a Recently Viewed card sends the shopper to the default site/locale instead of staying on the one they're actually browsing.

**The fix, matching this codebase's own established pattern:** both mappers already take `formatPrice` as an injected parameter specifically so the mapper itself stays free of any hook dependency (see either mapper's own docblock for why). Apply the identical pattern for `buildUrl`: add a `buildUrl: (path: string) => string` parameter to `selectRecentlyViewedCard` (in `recentlyViewedCard.ts`) and to `selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard` (in `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts`), and wrap the `href` value with it inside each mapper, instead of leaving callers to wrap the mapper's output afterward.

Update both call sites to pass it:
- `overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.tsx` already calls `useMultiSite()` and has `buildUrl` in scope (used elsewhere in the same file for `RECENTLY_VIEWED_ROUTE`) — pass it into `selectRecentlyViewedCard`.
- `overrides/app/pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx` does **not** currently call `useMultiSite()` at all — add the hook call and pass `buildUrl` into `selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard`.

Update all four affected test files (`recentlyViewedCard.test.ts`, `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.test.ts`, `recommended-products/index.test.tsx`, `recentlyViewed/index.test.tsx`) to pass a `buildUrl` argument/mock wherever these functions are called directly or `useMultiSite` needs mocking — follow whatever mocking pattern each test file already uses for its other injected dependencies (e.g. how `formatPrice` is already mocked/passed). Add or update at least one assertion per mapper proving the returned `href` actually has the prefix applied (e.g. mock `buildUrl` to prepend a distinguishable string like `/en-GB` and assert the returned card's `href` contains it) — prove this works, don't just assume passing the parameter through is enough.

**Fix B — `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`'s `cards` prop is typed too wide.**

`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedRail/index.tsx` (around line 38) declares `cards: readonly ZimmProductCardProps[]` — the full union across all four `ZimmProductCard` variations (`plp`/`home`/`wishlist`/`recentlyViewed`), when this component only ever renders the `recentlyViewed` variation. Narrow it: declare a local type `ZimmRecentlyViewedCardProps = ZimmProductCardBaseProps & ZimmProductCardRecentlyViewedVariation` (both real, confirmed exports from `../zimmProductCard`), and change the `cards` prop to `readonly ZimmRecentlyViewedCardProps[]`. This is a type-only change — no runtime behavior changes. Verify nothing currently passing cards into this component breaks (`recommended-products/index.tsx` already builds `variation: 'recentlyViewed'` cards for this exact rail, so it should type-check cleanly against the narrower type with no changes needed there).

**Do not touch:** the routes registry, any story file's breakpoint documentation, `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts`'s alt-text handling, the Notify Me button logic, or the $0.00 price rendering — none of those are part of this fix. Do not touch the mobile-overflow-below-400px CSS in `zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts` — that one is a documented, already-escalated product decision, not something to silently patch.

Run `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run test -- --run` after both fixes and report the full numbers. Report exactly which files changed and confirm nothing outside this list was touched.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/skills/zimmerMANNPostBuild

Marcel's own senior dev. Nothing built here — this skill judges what was built, writes what goes
public, and holds the conversation with CodeRabbit and the reviewer.

**Intended model: Sonnet 5 at maximum effort.**

**Input:** `` — a Jira key. Reads three files under
`~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/`:

- **`handoff.md`** — Build's record: steps, commits, Scorer verdicts, rework rounds, gate numbers,
  UNIFORM findings, what went unverified
- **`plan.md`** — what was meant to be built
- **`findings.md`** — the gate table, with its 🟡 CLARIFY assumptions

If `handoff.md` is missing, Build either did not finish or ran before this was written. Say so and
reconstruct what you can from the branch's commits — but flag the audit as partial, because the
Scorer verdicts and UNIFORM findings are not recoverable from git.

**Scale to the work.** A two-point story does not get a five-agent sweep. Honour the scale the
plan chose. Nothing too crazy, no overthinking.

---

## Phase 1 — audit against both artefacts

Two documents, two different questions. Neither is covered by the loop that just ran.

### `findings.md` — did the gate hold?

Walk every row. For each:

- **🔴 BLOCKED** — was it resolved before Build started, and by what?
- **🟡 CLARIFY** — this is the one that matters. Each of these carried a **stated assumption** into
  the plan. **Did that assumption actually hold once the code existed?** Nothing else in the chain
  revisits them. An assumption that turned out wrong mid-build, that nobody went back to, is the
  most likely thing to reach the PR unnoticed.
- **🔵 NOTE** — still true? A note that has become a defect is a finding.

### `plan.md` — did the build deliver?

- Every step shipped what it promised, with its Scorer verdict.
- The diff matches the file manifest. Anything in the diff that isn't in the manifest is a scope
  finding — even if it looks correct.
- Every file's tier is what the plan said it was.
- **Registry churn under `.claude/registry/*.md` is automatic and expected.** Never a finding.

Use `zm-orchestrator` for the manifest-versus-diff conformance pass. It already does exactly this
judgement at step scope.

---

## Phase 2 — the whole-feature sweep

Per-step scoring is **structurally blind** to a pattern applied consistently but wrongly: it
passes every individual review. On this project a systematic spacing error survived five commits
and every score, and was only found afterwards. This phase exists for that.

Run it in two directions, internal first.

### Internal — does the feature agree with itself?

No external rubric. One question: is this internally consistent?

- Every recipe the same shape — same `parts` convention, same registration, same naming
- Every component the same structure — export, props type, story, test
- Every token used the same way for the same purpose
- The same value not typed twice in two places

A divergence here is a finding even when both variants are individually defensible.

### External — does that shared shape conform?

Only once you know what the feature's own pattern *is*:

- **The exemplar PR** — does the feature match what it established? Where the exemplar is itself
  inconsistent, say which variant this work followed and whether that was the better choice. Do
  not report a divergence from an unstable pattern as a defect.
- **`.claude/rules/*`** — do the rules hold across the whole feature, not just per file?
- **Figma, end to end** — the rendered feature against the named nodes, every variant and state.
  Remember the node-type discriminator and never cross-compare the two Figma files.

Use `zm-tester` for this, fanning out across the feature rather than one step. Every finding
carries **UNIFORM** or **ONE-OFF** — at this scope, UNIFORM is what you are hunting.

---

## Phase 3 — if the audit fails

**Hand back to `zimmerMANNBuild`. Do not fix it here.**

The auditor becoming the author is exactly the independence that makes this phase worth running,
and Build has a Scorer and a rework cap that this skill does not.

Report the defect with its evidence, return the work, and **re-audit when it comes back.** A
re-audit is a fresh pass, not a check that the named item changed.

---

## Phase 4 — the PR

Write the body yourself. Do not call `/pr-checklist` — its output is the team's format, and this
one is yours.

**The body describes the diff that actually shipped, not the plan.** If the two differ, the diff
wins and the difference is worth a line.

Include: what changed and why · the tier of every touched file, with any Tier 2 approver named ·
what was tested and the real numbers · anything deliberately deferred, with the owning ticket ·
anything left unverified.

**Never in a PR title, body, commit message or code comment:**
- Claude attribution of any kind — no `Co-Authored-By`, no mention
- CodeRabbit mentions
- A citation of any local-only doc. `~/Dev/fed-handbook.md` and its predecessors are Marcel's
  personal files. Where the same rule exists in `AGENTS.md` or `.claude/rules/*`, cite that.
- Draft or pending disclaimers

inferring a format. Verify authorship before copying one as a template — a PR merged in this repo
is not automatically his; check `gh pr view <N> --json author` or an explicit self-identifying
line in the body (e.g. "Authenticated as X") before treating its structure as house style. This
matters most exactly when a PR was found by keyword search rather than by number from a memory
note that already named the right one.

---

## Phase 5 — write it down, then present

**First write `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/postbuild.md`:**

```
# PostBuild — <TICKET>
Branch: <branch>   Head: <sha>   Audited: <date>

## Audit — findings.md
| # | Gate item | Severity | Held? | Evidence |
<one row per row of findings.md. For every 🟡 CLARIFY: did the assumption hold?>

## Audit — plan.md
| Step | Delivered? | Commit | Notes |
<plus: files in the diff that were not in the manifest>

## Sweep — internal consistency
<does the feature agree with itself — recipes, structure, token use>

## Sweep — external conformance
<exemplar PR · .claude/rules/* · Figma end to end>

## UNIFORM findings
<the ones a per-step review structurally cannot catch>

## PR body as written
<the exact text>

## Could not verify
<named, with why>
```

**Then append a block per review round**, as the loop runs:

```
## Round <n> — <date>
Findings received: <n> (CodeRabbit <n>, reviewer <n>)
| # | Finding | Verdict | Fixed in | Reply posted? |
<VALID / INVALID / OUT OF SCOPE / DEFER, with the evidence for each decline>
```

This file is read by **`zimmerMANNBuild rework`** — so it knows what was already declined and why,
rather than re-litigating it — and by **`zimmerMANNDevImprover`**. Write it even when the audit is
clean; a clean audit that left no record is indistinguishable from one that never ran.

## Then present

Give him, in **"ELI5BITFEDLOTP"** (Explain Like I'm 5, But I'm The FED Lead Of The Project) register:

1. The diff summary — files, tiers, commits
2. The audit result — every gate item and plan step, with anything that failed
3. The sweep result — **UNIFORM findings first**, they are the point of this skill
4. The proposed PR title and body
5. What could not be verified

Then **stop.**

**On his go: push and open the PR.** Not before. Push is the first irreversible, outward-facing
step in the chain, and it is his to authorise.

---

## Phase 6 — the review loop

When CodeRabbit or a reviewer requests changes:

1. **Hand the findings to `zimmerMANNBuild rework`.** It verifies each finding is real before
   anything is touched — CodeRabbit has run as low as 1-in-6 correct on this repo — then fixes and
   commits the valid ones.

2. **Draft a reply for every finding when it comes back.** Every thread gets a written answer:
   - **Fixed** — what changed, and the commit
   - **Declined** — the specific quotable repo rule, doc, or empirical result that makes it wrong.
     Not an opinion.
   - **Deferred** — the owning ticket or the person who decides

   **A fix commit with no in-thread reply does not count.** A prior PR here carried 18 threads with
   zero human replies; the process was being followed on the PR before it and was dropped entirely.

3. **Show him the full batch, then post on his go.** One approval covers the set.

4. Repeat until approved. If CodeRabbit raises the same objection a third time, stop re-running it
   and answer the threads instead — it has nothing to learn from unanswered comments.

manifest-versus-diff audit is a snapshot, not a standing guarantee. Any fix round in this phase
(a CodeRabbit rework, a reviewer's requested change, or a gap Marcel spots and Build fixes
directly) can add a file outside the original manifest — including a legitimate, individually-
authorized Tier 1/2 exception. If it does, that file belongs in the plan's manifest and in
postbuild.md's own audit paragraph, not left for the audit to silently go stale. Before presenting
the final state for merge, confirm the manifest audit's claim still matches `git diff
<base>..HEAD --numstat` exactly — if it doesn't, append a dated correction (same pattern as
plan.md's own "Open questions" section) rather than leaving the original claim uncorrected.

---

## The owner rule — everywhere outward-facing

The audit report, the PR body, and every reply.

Every finding names **who resolves it**: Marcel, Tim, a designer, a BA, QA. A blocker owned by the
designer and one owned by Marcel need different actions.

**Where the owner is senior or lateral, phrase it as a question to them — never a directive.**
"Should this route via X, or have I misread it?" not "change this to X." Ask confirmatorily.

Before anything posts, count the asks. A review that mentions one person eight times reads as
hiding behind their authority.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never write code.** Every fix goes back to Build. This skill audits, writes, and posts.
- **Never push or post without an explicit go.** Both are outward-facing and irreversible in
  practice.
- **Never write to the repo's config** — `.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CODEOWNERS`,
  `.docs/memory/**`, `.docs/prd/**`. Tier 1 Governance.
- **Never re-litigate a settled decision.** If the plan decided it and the build honoured it, it
  is not a finding — report a *mechanical consequence* of a decision, never the decision.
- **Say what you could not verify.** An audit that finds nothing has not been shown to be capable
  of finding anything.

---

## What Marcel is missing

Close every report with this section. Always, even when it is one line.

This is **not** "what I could not verify" — that is your own blind spot and it has its own home.
This is his: something he has not thought to ask about, a decision he is about to make on a stale
premise, a risk sitting just outside this task that you can see from where you are standing, or a
call that genuinely needs him rather than you. Name it, say why it needs him, and say what you
will do if he says nothing.

Write "nothing this pass" only when you have actually gone looking. This is the one section where
a blank is itself a claim.

input.prompt:
This is a PostBuild-phase, whole-feature sweep for ticket SFCC-83+84-einstein, branch `feature/SFCC-83-84_recently-viewed-einstein` — different from a per-step test pass. The build is done (six commits: `0f7de14`, `07be6c5`, `01f4dc3`, `eccbb68`, `5660869`, `aedbc58`, all already individually scored PASS during the build). Your job now is a step-blind sweep across the WHOLE feature, looking for a pattern that was applied consistently but wrongly — something no single per-step review could have caught because each step looked fine in isolation.

**Context, so you don't have to re-derive it:** this build swapped Recently Viewed's data source from a local-storage-based interim mechanism to real Einstein recommendations, across two consumers (a PDP/PLP/Cart rail, and a standalone Full History page), then deleted the interim mechanism entirely and fixed several small bugs a local CodeRabbit review caught along the way (a missing site/locale URL prefix on card links, a rail prop-type narrowing, a blank-page gate bug on the Full History page, a wasted network call on Cart). No new component, recipe, or Storybook story was created anywhere in this build — every touched component/mapper/page already existed; only data sources and a handful of bugs changed. Read `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-83+84-einstein/plan.md` and `handoff.md` for full detail.

**Scale this appropriately — this is not a "5 new components" build.** Given nothing new was authored, the internal-consistency question is narrower than usual: did the SAME kind of fix/pattern get applied consistently everywhere it needed to, not "do all the new recipes share one shape" (there are no new recipes).

**Internal — does the feature agree with itself? Specifically check:**
1. **The `buildUrl` site/locale-prefix fix** was applied to both `recentlyViewedCard.ts` (Rail) and `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts` (Full History page) — confirm both use the *identical* injected-parameter pattern (matching the codebase's own `formatPrice` precedent), not two different approaches to the same fix. Also confirm both container components (`recommended-products/index.tsx`, `recentlyViewed/index.tsx`) call `useMultiSite()` and pass `buildUrl` the same way.
2. **The Einstein-wiring pattern itself** — `recommended-products/index.tsx`'s Recently-Viewed branch and `recentlyViewed/index.tsx`'s own container both call `useEinstein()`/`getRecommendations(EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED)` and read `recommendations.recs` — confirm both actually do this the same way, not two subtly different implementations of what's supposed to be the same integration pattern.
3. **The empty/loading gate logic** — E1's rail gate (`!recommendations?.recs?.length → return null`) and E2's page gate (`cards.length > 0 / !isLoading && cards.length === 0 / else null`) are deliberately different shapes for a stated reason (the page has a distinct empty-state UI, the rail doesn't) — confirm this difference is still the ONLY difference, i.e. nothing else about how the two consume Einstein's response diverges without a reason.
4. Whether any leftover reference, dead code, or stale comment about the deleted interim mechanism survived anywhere in the final diff — do a fresh, independent repo-wide grep yourself for `useRecentlyViewedHistory|recentlyViewedProductFetch|RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_STORAGE_KEY|GET_PRODUCTS_MAX_IDS_PER_REQUEST|RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED` across all of `overrides/` — don't trust the build's own claim of zero hits, re-derive it.

**External — does this conform to established patterns?**
1. **The exemplar pattern**: `recommended-products/index.tsx` already had four other, pre-existing recommenders (`ADD_TO_CART_MODAL`, `CART_MAY_ALSO_LIKE`, `PDP_COMPLETE_SET`, `PDP_MIGHT_ALSO_LIKE`) using the identical `useEinstein()`/`getRecommendations`/`recommendations.recs` chain before this build touched anything. Confirm the Recently-Viewed branch, post-build, genuinely matches that existing pattern rather than diverging from it in some way that happens to also work.
2. **`.claude/rules/*` conformance across the whole diff** — spot check: no bare Chakra token keys where `var(--zimm-*)` is required (`overrideStyling.md`); TypeScript-only inside `overrides/` (no `.js`/`.jsx`); no magic strings/numbers introduced (`conventions.md`); Australian spelling in any new Zimmermann-authored comment. Since no theme/recipe file was touched anywhere in this build, the CSS/token rules should be trivially satisfied — confirm that's actually true rather than assumed.
3. **Figma** — explicitly out of scope for live/visual comparison, since Einstein is undeployed everywhere reachable and the plan itself states this ceiling. Do not attempt a live render check. Do confirm no component's static, already-Figma-matched CSS/recipe was touched by this build at all (it shouldn't have been — this was a data-source swap, not a visual change).

Report every finding as **UNIFORM** (a pattern issue reaching across the whole feature) or **ONE-OFF** (isolated to one file) — UNIFORM is what this pass exists to catch. State what you tried to falsify and what you could not verify, per your own standard practice.

This surfaces one genuinely important, previously-uncaught issue — exactly the kind of thing this whole audit phase exists to catch. Let me lay out the mechanism precisely before bringing it to you, since it's the headline finding.

**The bug:** the CodeRabbit-response fix (`5660869`) correctly fixed the Full History page's blank-page bug — it was gating render on the *raw* Einstein rec count instead of the count *after* filtering out recs that fail to map to cards. That fix only touched the page. The Rail's own consumer (`recommended-products/index.tsx`) has the exact same map→filter→render shape, and its render gate is still checking the raw count, unchanged.

**Why nothing visibly broke:** the Rail component itself has its own internal "nothing to show → render nothing" guard, so an empty mapped-cards array still correctly shows nothing on screen. That's exactly why no per-step review caught it — the visible behavior is fine.

**What's actually wrong:** the Rail's *impression-tracking* call (the one that tells Einstein "the shopper saw this recommendation") checks that same raw, unmapped rec count — not the mapped, actually-rendered count. So in the narrow case where every one of a shopper's recently-viewed products has gone offline (all recs fail to map), the Rail renders correctly (nothing), but still tells Einstein the shopper *viewed* recommendations that were never actually shown — silently feeding Einstein's own recommendation-quality signal false data.

The tester also found two smaller things riding along: a stale comment in `recentlyViewed/index.tsx`'s own docblock that now incorrectly claims the rail follows "the same principle" (no longer true after the asymmetric fix), and no test exists for this exact scenario on the rail's side. Plus two unrelated, trivial misses (two paraphrased stale comments about the deleted hook in the Rail component that a literal-name grep couldn't catch, and one "Normalized" that should be "Normalised").

input.prompt:
A real bug found during PostBuild's whole-feature sweep on branch `feature/SFCC-83-84_recently-viewed-einstein`, sent back from that audit for a fix round (not part of the original E1-E4 plan). Five small, independently-verified fixes — implement precisely, don't re-litigate whether they're real.

**Fix 1 (the important one) — `overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.tsx`: impression-tracking reports recommendations that were never actually rendered.**

The impression-tracking effect (around line 308-325) is shared across all 5 recommenders on this file and fires `sendViewReco`/`dataCloud.sendViewRecommendations` with the full, raw `recommendations.recs` array whenever `isOnScreen && recommendations?.recs` — this is correct today for the other 4 recommenders (`ADD_TO_CART_MODAL`, `CART_MAY_ALSO_LIKE`, `PDP_COMPLETE_SET`, `PDP_MIGHT_ALSO_LIKE`), which don't have any null-filtering step between the raw recs and what renders. **Do not change anything about how this effect behaves for those 4 recommenders — their behavior must stay byte-identical.**

The Recently-Viewed branch is different: further down (around line 363), it builds `cards` by mapping `recommendations.recs` through `selectRecentlyViewedCard`, which can return `null` for a given product (e.g. no usable name or image — see that mapper's own hard-gate contract), then filters those nulls out. So `cards` can legitimately be a strict subset of `recommendations.recs`. The impression-tracking effect runs *before* this filtering happens and has no visibility into it — it reports every id in the raw `recommendations.recs`, including ones that got filtered out and never actually rendered. Consequence: if every one of a shopper's recently-viewed products fails to map (e.g. all now offline/deleted — a real, if narrow, scenario), the rail correctly renders nothing, but still tells Einstein/DataCloud that the shopper *viewed* those recommendations. That's false signal into Einstein's own recommendation-quality feedback loop, and it's silent — nothing on screen indicates it happened.

**The fix, for the Recently-Viewed recommender only:** the impression-tracking effect should only report the ids that actually survived `selectRecentlyViewedCard`'s null-filtering — the same set `cards` represents — not the full raw `recommendations.recs`. You have judgment on the exact shape: either (a) branch inside the existing effect so that for `recommender === EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` specifically, the reported id list is filtered through the same `selectRecentlyViewedCard(product, formatPrice, buildUrl) !== null` check the render path already applies (accept the minor duplicate computation — this effect only fires once per mount, since `isOnScreen` is `useOnce: true`), or (b) restructure so the RV branch's own `cards`-derived id list is what the effect reports for that recommender. Whichever shape you choose: **the other 4 recommenders' reported payload and firing condition must not change in any way** — verify this explicitly, don't just assume it. If the successfully-mapped set for RV is empty (every rec failed to map), no impression should be reported at all for that fire (matching the intent: nothing rendered, nothing to report as viewed).

**Fix 2 — same file, module docblock:** `recentlyViewed/index.tsx`'s own docblock (around line 190-211, the "Empty-state gate, race-safe" section) claims the rail's own gate follows "the same principle" as the page's `cards.length`-based gate. That was true when it was written, but the page's render gate was later fixed (2026-09-15, CodeRabbit finding) to check `cards.length` specifically to close the exact bug Fix 1 above addresses — while the rail's own *render* gate (line ~346, `if (!recommendations?.recs?.length) return null;`) intentionally still checks the raw count, because the rail has its own downstream `visibleCards.length === 0 → null` guard inside `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` that makes the render outcome safe either way (only the *impression tracking*, not the render, needed Fix 1). Correct this docblock claim so it no longer asserts the two gates work "the same" — say plainly that the render gates differ in shape for a stated reason (the page has no equivalent downstream guard the rail has), and that impression-tracking parity is what Fix 1 (above) specifically closes.

**Fix 3 — `overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.test.tsx`:** add a test proving Fix 1, mirroring the mutation-tested pattern `recentlyViewed/index.test.tsx` already established for its own equivalent case: a fixture where `recommendations.recs` is non-empty but every product fails `selectRecentlyViewedCard`'s null-gate (e.g. missing name/image), `isOnScreen` true — assert `sendViewReco`/`dataCloud.sendViewRecommendations` are NOT called (or called with an empty id list, matching whatever Fix 1's exact shape produces). Prove this test would have failed against the old code first (temporarily revert Fix 1, confirm this new test fails for the claimed reason, restore, confirm it passes) — this codebase's own prove-don't-assert discipline. Also confirm the 4 other recommenders' existing impression-tracking tests in this same file still pass completely unchanged.

**Fix 4 — `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedRail/index.tsx`:** two stale comments (around lines 69 and 125) still describe the deleted `useRecentlyViewedHistory` hook's `hasRecentlyViewed` return value as the *current* visibility-gating mechanism ("A4's own visibility gate"), in present tense. The real gate now lives entirely in the container (`recommended-products/index.tsx`'s `!recommendations?.recs?.length` check, build plan step E1) — this component has never gated its own visibility, it just renders whatever `cards` it's given (or nothing, if `visibleCards.length === 0`). Correct both comments to reflect this — comment-only, no functional change.

**Fix 5 — `overrides/app/pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx:293`:** "Normalized" should be "Normalised" — Australian spelling, matching the other 6 correctly-spelled "colour" instances already in this same diff (`.claude/rules/conventions.md`'s spelling rule). One-word comment fix.

**Do not touch:** anything else in any of these files, the mobile-overflow CSS, the Notify Me logic, the $0.00 price rendering, or the alt-text handling — none of those are part of this fix round.

Run `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run test -- --run` after all 5 fixes and report the full numbers. Report exactly what changed per fix, with before/after for Fix 1 specifically since it's the substantive one, and confirm the other 4 recommenders' impression-tracking behavior is verified unchanged, not just assumed.

Correct this docblock claim so it no longer asserts the two gates work "the same" — say plainly that the render gates differ in shape for a stated reason (the page has no equivalent downstream guard the rail has), and that impression-tracking parity is what Fix 1 (above) specifically closes.

**Fix 3 — `overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.test.tsx`:** add a test proving Fix 1, mirroring the mutation-tested pattern `recentlyViewed/index.test.tsx` already established for its own equivalent case: a fixture where `recommendations.recs` is non-empty but every product fails `selectRecentlyViewedCard`'s null-gate (e.g. missing name/image), `isOnScreen` true — assert `sendViewReco`/`dataCloud.sendViewRecommendations` are NOT called (or called with an empty id list, matching whatever Fix 1's exact shape produces). Prove this test would have failed against the old code first (temporarily revert Fix 1, confirm this new test fails for the claimed reason, restore, confirm it passes) — this codebase's own prove-don't-assert discipline. Also confirm the 4 other recommenders' existing impression-tracking tests in this same file still pass completely unchanged.

**Fix 4 — `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedRail/index.tsx`:** two stale comments (around lines 69 and 125) still describe the deleted `useRecentlyViewedHistory` hook's `hasRecentlyViewed` return value as the *current* visibility-gating mechanism ("A4's own visibility gate"), in present tense. The real gate now lives entirely in the container (`recommended-products/index.tsx`'s `!recommendations?.recs?.length` check, build plan step E1) — this component has never gated its own visibility, it just renders whatever `cards` it's given (or nothing, if `visibleCards.length === 0`). Correct both comments to reflect this — comment-only, no functional change.

**Fix 5 — `overrides/app/pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx:293`:** "Normalized" should be "Normalised" — Australian spelling, matching the other 6 correctly-spelled "colour" instances already in this same diff (`.claude/rules/conventions.md`'s spelling rule). One-word comment fix.

**Do not touch:** anything else in any of these files, the mobile-overflow CSS, the Notify Me logic, the $0.00 price rendering, or the alt-text handling — none of those are part of this fix round.

Run `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run test -- --run` after all 5 fixes and report the full numbers. content.text:
The one-line goal: swap Recently Viewed's data source from a temporary browser-local stand-in to the real Einstein engine, so the feature is fully wired and ready to work the instant Einstein actually deploys, with zero further code changes needed.

But here's the part that matters most for what you'll actually *observe*:

**The moment this PR merges and reaches any real environment, Recently Viewed goes blank for everyone — not because anything is broken, but because Einstein genuinely isn't deployed anywhere yet.** The rail won't render on PDP/PLP (its empty-state gate correctly returns nothing when there's no real Einstein response), and the Full History page will show "you haven't viewed anything yet" for every single shopper, permanently, until Einstein is actually live. That's a real, expected behavior change versus PR #107's demo branch, which does show fake-but-real-looking recently-viewed content today via the browser-tracking stand-in. This PR trades that away on purpose — the whole point was to stop faking it and wire the real thing.

**The moment Einstein does go live**, this code should start working with no further changes: the rail appears on PDP/PLP (not Cart) showing up to 2/3/5 recently-viewed products depending on viewport, each linking to the correct product on whatever regional storefront the shopper is actually browsing (one of the bugs this build fixed), with a "see full history" link when there's more than fits; the Full History page shows the complete list with full pricing/size/add-to-bag; a shopper with genuinely no history sees the clean empty state instead.

**Two things beyond this code have to also be true before any of that actually happens, even after Einstein deploys** — both already flagged, neither fixable in this branch:
- DNT (Do Not Track) defaults ON across Zimmermann's sites today, and every Einstein call silently no-ops when DNT is true.
- No consent gate exists yet for Einstein calls — needs to land before this can go to production for real, per the project's own consent rules.

And the first thing anyone should check the day Einstein actually goes live: open a genuinely fresh, zero-history session and confirm the empty state renders correctly — that's the one thing this build couldn't verify itself and deliberately left as a named follow-up rather than assume.

content.text:
Confirmed — zero GitHub Environments (checked all 7 relevant ones as both secrets and variables) have `EINSTEIN_API_SITE_ID` set at all. Let me give you the precise answer to all four parts.

**1. Do we have a demo key?** Not quite a "key" in the credential sense — Einstein authenticates via two values: `einsteinId` (a fixed identifier, hardcoded directly in `config/default.js`: `1ea06c6e-c936-4324-bcf0-fada93f83bb1`, same everywhere, not a secret) and `siteId` (meant to vary per environment). The `siteId`'s sample value in `.env.sample` is `aaij-MobileFirst` — a Salesforce **demo org's** site ID, not a real Zimmermann one, because Einstein has never actually been provisioned for any of Zimmermann's real storefronts.

**2. Is it local-only?** Yes. I checked every one of the 7 relevant GitHub Environments (dev, test, sit, uat, staging, prod, shared) for both secrets and variables — `EINSTEIN_API_SITE_ID` doesn't exist in any of them. The only place this value exists anywhere is `.env.sample`'s own shown default, which only reaches a machine when a developer runs `npm run env -- init` locally.

**3. Is it in GitHub / used by the envs?** No, and this is the important, previously-unconfirmed part: it's not just that the demo value hasn't been swapped for a real one — **nothing has been pushed at all.** On dev, test, sit, uat, staging, and prod right now, `process.env.EINSTEIN_API_SITE_ID` is simply `undefined`. Nobody has ever run `npm run env -- push tier` for this variable.

**4. Does it affect what we build once deployed?** It confirms a third, distinct blocker beyond the two I already mentioned (Einstein not provisioned on the Salesforce side, and DNT defaulting on) — even setting both of those aside, Einstein's client-side call would currently go out with an empty `siteId` on every real environment, which would fail regardless. This doesn't change anything about the code this build wired — the code correctly reads whatever's in the env var — but it's one more piece that has to be set up before Einstein can work anywhere, and it's a `scope:tier` variable (needs a real value per environment, tier-1-approver to push it), not something fixable in this PR.

This is precise enough to be worth recording — let me update the existing Einstein memory with it.
