name: project-einstein-siteid-investigation
description: "EINSTEIN_API_SITE_ID / aaij-MobileFirst is unmodified Salesforce SDK demo boilerplate, not a real Zimmermann value — real setup is JIRA SFCC-112, still In Refinement. Never enable Einstein on SIT."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 8a3c90dc-1e73-41af-8c87-71e6db7e2556
  modified: 2026-09-08T02:44:11.105Z
---

**`aaij-MobileFirst` (+ einsteinId `1ea06c6e-c936-4324-bcf0-fada93f83bb1`) is NOT a Zimmermann value — it's unmodified Salesforce retail-react-app SDK demo boilerplate.** Verified byte-identical to `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/config/default.js:82,84` (Salesforce's own reference-architecture demo storefront credentials). `git log -S` confirms both values entered `config/default.js` in the very first commit (`cd60b7a` "Initial commit during Detailed Design phase", Hardi, 12 Jun) and have never been touched since — nobody at Zimmermann ever configured this.

**Live-tested and confirmed working** (curl replicating the exact SDK request): `aaij-MobileFirst` → `200 OK` with real `{uuid, requestId}`. Any other siteId (e.g. `ZimmermannAU`, `undefined`) → `400 {"error":{"code":"InvalidClientId","message":"The Client ID in the request does not have access to the site ID in the request"}}`. So it "works" only because it's Salesforce's own demo tenant that the shared einsteinId happens to be authorized for — not because Zimmermann has a real Einstein site.

**Real setup is tracked and NOT done:** JIRA **SFCC-112** "Recommendations – Einstein Configuration & Zone Setup" (labels SPR-59/SPR-63, Squad-B) — status **In Refinement**, description: "Einstein Recommendations provisioned and recommendation zones configured in Business Manager... before any PWA carousel work begins." Related: SFCC-7 (Search & Recommendations epic), SFCC-647 (updated 2026-08-10), SFCC-642 (Einstein AI Sort BM config), SFCC-118 (carousel UI), SFCC-106 (consent-gating for tracking). Confluence "8.1 Technical Files (Zimm Provided)" (253362177-adjacent, id 264765445) has an EMPTY row for "Salesforce Einstein" — no credentials ever handed over by the client. A "Search & Recommendations Workshop part 2" was scheduled 2026-08-10–14 (active as of this finding).

**⚠️ CRITICAL — Never enable Einstein on SIT.** Confluence "05.6 - Environment Details" (id 285540356) explicitly: *"Never enable Einstein, Global-e, or Narvar on SIT — see config/sit.js."* SIT is a dedicated isolated env for NewStore order-management integration testing. BUT `config/sit.js` has NO actual code enforcing this (only overrides SCAPI/OCAPI proxy hosts) — enforcement today is purely "leave the env var blank," not a code gate. I had filled `EINSTEIN_API_SITE_ID` into local `.env.sit` during a fix-verification pass (2026-08-10) — reverted to blank same session per user instruction ("revert and hold-off") once this policy was found. `.env.dev`/`.env.test`/`.env.uat` still have the value locally (not policy-restricted) but were NEVER pushed to GitHub Environments (confirmed 404 on the var across all environments) — holding off on any push pending SFCC-112 resolution, per user decision.

**Recommendation given (accepted):** don't push this demo credential to any GitHub Environment — it's a throwaway fix for a story (SFCC-112) already in progress; real Einstein provisioning should replace it. Raise with whoever owns SFCC-112 (Squad B) rather than quietly wiring the demo value into shared config.

**Confirmed by full codebase/git-history sweep (2026-08-10, Explore agent, 126 tool uses):**
- Byte-for-byte match to `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/config/default.js:80-86` (pinned SDK v10.0.0) — Salesforce's own "RefArchGlobal" demo config (org `f_ecom_zzrf_001`, shortCode `8o7m175y`). The SDK's own comment (`// This differs from the siteId in commerceAPIConfig for testing purposes`) was DROPPED when copied into config/default.js — only the unrelated isProduction comment survived.
- `.env.sample` scope:tier comparison: of 13 tier-scoped SFCC-adjacent credentials, EINSTEIN_API_SITE_ID is the ONLY one with a real-looking non-blank/non-TODO default — every sibling (COMMERCE_API_*, CONTENTFUL_*, GLOBALE_*, ADYEN_*) is blank or `TODO`.
- Only live runtime use anywhere in overrides/: `einstein.sendViewPage(pathname)` in home/index.tsx:152 (page-view beacon only). `RecommendedProducts` component (actual recs rendering) has ZERO consumers per the registry — Einstein isn't even rendering anything yet, just firing tracking pings.
- **SIT-disable was documented as "done" but was NEVER implemented.** A deleted doc (`docs/environments/sit.md`, removed in migrate-to-Confluence commit) + `.docs/prompts/omsIntClaudeCodePrompt.md:326-333` (marked "Status — done... already implemented") both describe an aspirational `config/sit.js` snippet: `einsteinAPI: { enabled: false }` with comment "avoid polluting recommendation data." Checked config/sit.js's full history (3 commits total) — this was NEVER added; sit.js only ever overrode SCAPI/OCAPI proxy hosts. ALSO: even if it had been added, the base `useEinstein()` hook has no `enabled` flag check at all (only destructures host/einsteinId/siteId/isProduction) — the killswitch wouldn't have worked anyway. So the team knew/worried about this and documented a fix that was never real.
- No `.docs/integration/` doc exists for Einstein specifically — folded into 01-sfcc.md as 3 minor bullets (recs are consent-gated, Didomi purpose TBC, falls back to static merchandising group on no-consent or 5xx). No "credentials" section anywhere, unlike every other integration doc.
- PRD sign-off (`.docs/prd/search.md`): SPR-63 "confirmed and signed off 2026-05-08" is about the PLATFORM CHOICE (Einstein vs Athos Commerce) only — never about this specific credential. CAI-005 cross-sheet contradiction (RJ: "99% likely we will move away from Athos") still open in cart.md.
- Residual honest caveat from the agent: cannot see actual GitHub Environment/MRT secret values from a static repo scan — can't 100% rule out a different real value was set out-of-band without ever being reflected in .env.sample. Worth closing out directly with the Integration Lead / whoever owns CQuotient BM for the bkzk realm.

**Unrelated bug SOLVED using the same methodology (2026-08-10) — Shopper Context 412 on test/sit/uat.** Root cause is NOT a code bug — it's an SFCC org-level feature toggle. Direct SCAPI probe (fresh random usids, multiple sites, reading full JSON error body via `scripts/sfcc/_shared.mjs`'s getSlasToken, hitting shopper-context v1 directly) returned the literal SFCC error on ALL of test(bkzk_005)/sit(bkzk_003)/uat(bkzk_dev), 7/7 requests each, zero variance across usid or site: `{"title":"Shopper Context Pre Condition Not Met","detail":"...Pre-condition: The feature toggle ShopperContextEnabled is not enabled."}`. Dev (bkzk_002) has this toggle ON (inferred from Jesse's original real-browser 404 = genuinely-not-found, not precondition-failed; my own direct test of dev returned a DIFFERENT error — `400 usid-token-mismatch` — because my test script's usid didn't match the SLAS token's internal usid, an artifact of not passing a matching usid to getSlasToken, NOT evidence about dev's toggle state). **Actionable ask for BM/Integration:** enable `ShopperContextEnabled` for the SFCC orgs backing test/sit/uat to match dev. Not fixable in code — pure BM/Account Manager config.

Cross-cutting lesson: same pattern as [[env-topology-doc-conflicts]] — docs (Confluence AND a since-deleted local doc) describe safeguards/rules the code never actually implements; always grep the referenced config file before trusting a "see config/X.js" citation, and check git history to see if an aspirational snippet in a prompt/doc actually landed.

---

## DNT gate — Einstein is OFF by default in this app (added 2026-09-07, code-verified)

**Every Einstein call in the storefront returns `{}` unless a `dw_dnt=0` cookie exists.** Verified chain,
each link read directly:

1. `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/constants.js:216` → `DEFAULT_DNT_STATE = true`
2. `overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx:196` → `defaultDnt={DEFAULT_DNT_STATE}`
3. `node_modules/@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react/auth/index.js:337-339` → `getDnt({includeDefaults:true})`:
   no `dw_dnt` cookie → `effectiveDnt = defaultDnt` (= `true`)
4. `node_modules/@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react/hooks/useDNT.js:34` → `effectiveDnt` comes from that call
5. `use-einstein.js:458` → `dnt: effectiveDnt` into `EinsteinAPI`
6. `use-einstein.js:156` → `einsteinFetch`: `if (this.dnt !== false) return {}`

**`updateDnt` (useDNT.js:39) is the ONLY thing in the entire SDK that calls `setDnt`, and nothing in
`overrides/` calls `updateDnt`.** Zero hits for `dw_dnt`/`updateDnt`/`useDNT`/`Didomi` anywhere under
`overrides/app`. So no shopper ever gets the cookie.

This is *correct* fail-closed consent behaviour per AGENTS.md — but the consequence is that **SFCC-106
(consent gating, Blocked) is a hard dependency of SFCC-83, not the "relates to" link Jira records.**

**Status: code-verified, NOT browser-verified.** Decisive test is to set `document.cookie = 'dw_dnt=0;
path=/'` and reload — if the rail populates, confirmed. Marcel took this to verify live 2026-09-07.
Tension to resolve: he previously reported seeing an unbrowsed product in the rail, which implies data
was flowing at some point.

## Recently Viewed — vendor behaviour, now documented (2026-09-07)

- **Cross-device for logged-in shoppers is documented**, closing the residual left open 2026-09-04:
  Salesforce defines `userId` as *"Unique identifier of a logged-in shopper that enables Einstein to
  link the same logged-in user across multiple devices."* The SDK sends it on both write and read.
  SFCC-83 AC 7 is satisfiable by the mechanism already wired.
- **`Recently Viewed` is a single-strategy recommender — it CANNOT backfill.** Salesforce: *"The
  Recently Viewed and Complete the Set recommender types use only one strategy."* So the two-product
  prefix seen against the demo org is a *configuration* artefact (pinned/included products on that
  org's recommender), not intrinsic recommender behaviour. Turns the parked Bianca question into a
  one-line ask: don't pin/include any products on Zimmermann's Recently Viewed recommender.
- **The recommender NAME is an unverified string contract.** `viewed-recently-einstein` is hardcoded in
  base `constants.js:154-163` (both `PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` and `CART_RECENTLY_VIEWED` = same string).
  BM recommender names are user-defined, and **no Confluence page anywhere maps Einstein recommender
  names to UI surfaces** — "recommendation zone" appears nowhere in the space. Wrong name = silently
  empty rail.

## Jira/Confluence deltas re-verified 2026-09-07

- **SFCC-112 is now `Blocked`** (was In Refinement). Its zones cover Recommended-for-You and
  More-from-Category — still **no Recently Viewed zone**. RV is a *recommender*, not a zone, so it
  likely needs Einstein merely enabled, not SFCC-112's zone work.
- **SFCC-647 "Review Einstein Recommendation Capabilities" is CANCELLED** — this is why no Einstein
  capability findings are documented anywhere.
- **No TSD exists for Einstein or recommendations** (19 TSDs exist; none covers it). Three Search &
  Recommendations workshops are marked Complete with **zero artefacts** — Open Questions cells still
  read "TBD", page has no children.
- Einstein still has **no credentials row** on 7.1b and an **empty** documentation cell on 8.1 (page
  touched 2026-09-03, so current). No Didomi purpose ID assigned for Einstein or Recently Viewed.
- `EINSTEIN_API_SITE_ID` is **empty in `.env.staging` and `.env.prod`** (as well as `.env.sit`, which
  is deliberate). Staging/prod blanks are a go-live gap, not policy.
- `.docs/integration/01-sfcc.md:78` is wrong twice: says GET (it's POST), and promises a "static SFCC
  merchandising group" fallback that **does not exist in code** — `einsteinFetch` returns `{}` and the
  rail renders nothing.
- Doc conflict: SPR-61 says Recently Viewed on **PDP and Cart**; Confluence 04.7 Component Inventory
  says **PDP only**. The SFCC-83 build wires both.

See [[prove-dont-assert]] — the DNT chain was read link-by-link rather than inferred from the top constant.

## 🔴 Einstein is "Not Deployed" for every real Zimmermann site — the foundational layer (2026-09-07, Marcel/BM screenshots)

**The deepest of three independent, stacking blockers, now fully mapped.** Marcel checked the
Einstein Status Dashboard (BM: Administration > Operations > Einstein Status Dashboard) on three
separate sandboxes — BKZK_002, BKZK_003, BKZK_005 — and got an identical result on all three: **all
8 sites** (AU, EU, EUIntl, HK, ME, UK, US, USIntl) show **Einstein Status: Not Deployed**, **Data
Quality: Not Available**, and **Catalog Runs / Order Runs both `—` (never run, ever)**. He also
checked Global Preferences > Einstein Search Dictionaries Opt-In on the same three sandboxes: the
"I accept these terms and conditions" checkbox is unticked and Save is disabled on all three, with
the page's own note that *"the state of the agreement can only be changed on a Staging instance"* —
so this can't even be self-served from a sandbox.

**Why this is the root layer, not just a third data point:** "Not Deployed" + zero catalog/order
runs means there is no trained recommendation model behind any Zimmermann site at all — a gap that
sits *before* either of the other two documented issues:
- Even with [[project-einstein-siteid-investigation|`EINSTEIN_API_SITE_ID` corrected]] to a real
  Zimmermann site, there would be no deployed engine on the other end to answer it.
- Even with the DNT gate (above) fixed/bypassed, a request that actually reaches Einstein would hit
  an undeployed engine with no catalog/order history to recommend from.
- The only Einstein responses anyone has ever actually observed (the `200 OK` demo-siteId curl test,
  the "single-strategy recommender, two-product baseline" analysis, Marcel's live "stuck on one
  product" report) were **all against Salesforce's own `aaij-MobileFirst` demo tenant** — a
  pre-existing Salesforce demo instance unrelated to Zimmermann's own catalog — not against any real
  Zimmermann deployment, because no real Zimmermann deployment has ever existed to test against.

**Blast radius: not specific to Recently Viewed (SFCC-83/84).** Every Einstein-powered surface —
PDP Complete-the-Set, PDP/Cart Might-Also-Like, the add-to-cart-modal recs, PLP empty-search
top-sellers/most-viewed, and the new Recently Viewed rail — depends on the same undeployed
platform-level engine. None of them can return real, personalized data on any real Zimmermann site
in any environment today, independent of any frontend code.

**Consistent with, not contradicting, the existing SFCC-112 finding above:** SFCC-112
("Recommendations – Einstein Configuration & Zone Setup") being **Blocked** now reads as blocked on
exactly this — platform-level Einstein activation plus initial catalog/order feed export — which is
very plausibly Salesforce/Account-Rep-level provisioning work, not something self-serviceable from
BM by Zimmermann or the SI partner (consistent with the opt-in being locked to Staging-only).

**Not yet done, deliberately left to Marcel:** escalating this (owner is already tagged as Bianca on
the related finding-28/backfill question above) and any sprint/Definition-of-Done consequence for
the wider personalization epic — this is a cross-team platform-provisioning decision, not something
to action unilaterally from a build session.

## Full round-trip live-confirmed (2026-09-08) — plumbing works, data is foreign

Marcel asked "how do we use that key, what APIs are available" as a sidequest. Direct curl,
bypassing `useEinstein()`'s DNT gate entirely, confirms both endpoint families genuinely work
against the demo tenant:

- **`getRecommenders`** (`GET /v3/personalization/recommenders/aaij-MobileFirst`) → `200 OK`, 20
  recommenders configured, including `{"name":"viewed-recently-einstein",
  "recommenderType":"recently-viewed"}` — byte-identical to our own hardcoded
  `EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED`/`CART_RECENTLY_VIEWED` string. Confirms *why* the SDK
  example uses that exact string: the base retail-react-app was built/tested against this same
  Salesforce demo tenant, which happens to ship a recommender with that name already configured.
- **`getRecommendations`** (`POST /v3/personalization/recs/aaij-MobileFirst/viewed-recently-einstein`,
  body `{"products":[],"realm":"aaij","instanceType":"sbx"}`) → `200 OK`, returned 2 real products
  (`11736753M` "Summer Bomber Jacket", `12416789M` "Straight Leg Trousers") with working image/product
  URLs on `zzcu-007.sandbox.us01.dx.commercecloud.salesforce.com` — Salesforce's own men's-apparel
  demo storefront. This is the concrete evidence behind the "two-product baseline" line above —
  previously inferred from docs, now directly observed with real response data.

**Confirms, doesn't change, the existing three-layer-blocker conclusion.** Auth (static
`x-cq-client-id` header, no OAuth) and both endpoint families work correctly end-to-end — but the
returned product IDs belong to Salesforce's demo catalog, not Zimmermann's, so a follow-up
`getProducts` against Zimmermann's real SFCC instance would find nothing. Independently, none of
this is reachable through the live storefront anyway (DNT gate above), and even a corrected siteId
would hit an undeployed engine (Einstein Status Dashboard section above). All three blockers are
separate and each independently sufficient — fixing only one doesn't unblock Recently Viewed via
Einstein.

## Real per-visitor personalization CONFIRMED live (2026-09-08) — mutation-tested, not asserted

Marcel asked directly: "does it return any products under recently viewed?" Rather than infer from
the static 2-product response above, ran an actual before/after mutation test against a
never-before-used `cookieId`:

1. Fresh `cookieId` (`sfcc83-verify-<timestamp>`, never used before) → `getRecommendations` on
   `viewed-recently-einstein`, empty `products` → same 2 fixed products as always
   (`11736753M`, `12416789M`).
2. `sendViewProduct` (`POST /v3/activities/aaij-MobileFirst/viewProduct`) for that **same
   cookieId**, product `25519318M` (a genuinely different, freshly-harvested real catalog ID,
   confirmed via a `products-in-all-categories` call first — not a guess) → `200 OK`.
2. Immediately re-queried `viewed-recently-einstein` with the **same cookieId** → now returned
   **3 products**: the same 2 fixed ones **plus `25519318M` appended** — no batching delay, no
   cache lag.
3. Also tried the *other* same-typed recommender found in the full 20-recommender list,
   `recently-viewed` ("Shopper, Recently-Viewed") → returned **only `25519318M`**, no pinned
   filler at all.

**This settles two things conclusively:**
- **Real per-visitor Einstein view tracking genuinely works, live, immediately** — this is not a
  static/fallback-only mechanism. If DNT + platform-deployment were both resolved and pointed at a
  real Zimmermann site, this exact mechanism would produce real personalized recently-viewed data.
- **The "two-product baseline" (memory above, "single-strategy recommender... configuration
  artefact") is now proven, not inferred** — `viewed-recently-einstein` specifically has 2
  products pinned/included in its BM config on this demo tenant, added on top of genuine per-visitor
  history. A same-type sibling recommender (`recently-viewed`) has zero pinning and reflects only
  real tracked views. This is a **per-recommender BM configuration choice**, not an inherent
  limitation of the `recently-viewed` recommender type — so Zimmermann's own recommender (once
  Einstein is actually deployed) should be built with no pinned/included products, matching
  `recently-viewed`'s behaviour here, not `viewed-recently-einstein`'s.

Net effect on the standing conclusion: unchanged — still blocked by DNT (not reachable from the
live app) and by platform non-deployment (Einstein Status Dashboard, "Not Deployed" on all 8 real
sites) — but this closes out any residual doubt that the *mechanism itself* is sound. The blockers
are entirely about reachability/deployment, not about whether Einstein's recently-viewed feature
actually does what it claims.

```tsx
const ids: { id?: string }[] =

    ? recommendations.recs

sendViewReco({...}, ids);
dataCloud.sendViewRecommendations({...}, ids);
```
The `else` branch is byte-identical to the original expression — a non-RV recommender never enters the `recommender === PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` branch, so nothing changes for it.

@@ -8,6 +8,127 @@
 
 export const CUSTOM_HOME_TITLE = '🎉 Hello Zimmermann!';
 
+// SFCC-84 — the Recently Viewed Full History page's own route path (build plan §B2). Named here,
+// not just inlined in routes.tsx, so the "See Full History" link (RecommendedProducts' own
+// `seeAllHref`) has one canonical value to import rather than a second hand-typed copy of this
+// same string.
+export const RECENTLY_VIEWED_ROUTE = '/recently-viewed';
+
+// SFCC-83/84 — the single source of truth for "how many Recently Viewed cards exist at once,
+// per breakpoint." Serves two consumers that both need the same number for different reasons:
+// (1) `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` (index.tsx) — the rail's own actual render cap. **Confirmed with
+// Marcel (2026-09-08): a real hard cap, not a "visible before scrolling" soft limit** — the rail
+// renders at most this many cards for the current real breakpoint and no more, full stop; a
+// shopper cannot scroll a mobile rail to reach a 3rd or later card. This superseded the original
+// flat `RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_MAX_ITEMS = 5` (removed) — that constant only ever capped at the
+// single Desktop figure regardless of breakpoint, relying on the horizontal-scroll container to
+// visually crop the rest at narrower viewports, which is the exact soft-limit behaviour Marcel's
+// decision replaced.
+// (2) `RecommendedProducts` — the See-Full-History link's own trigger: link
+// shows whenever the shopper's tracked history exceeds what the rail will display at the current
+// breakpoint. This consumer is unaffected by the cap becoming hard rather than soft — it was
+// always asking "does more history exist than the rail shows," which reads identically either
+// way.
+// Values match zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts's own confirmed per-breakpoint card-width table
+// (Mobile 201px cards × 2 = 402px full-bleed, Tablet 256px × 3 = 768px, Desktop 288px × 5 =
+// 1440px) — restated here as counts, not re-measured.
+//
+// **Correction, 2026-09-10 (later same day as the card-width fixes above): the `md`/`xl` key
+// names below no longer mean "switches at breakpoints.md/breakpoints.xl."** That claim was true
+// when this constant was first written, but went stale the moment
+// zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts's own `DESKTOP_UP_QUERY` was corrected (same day, earlier pass)
+// to switch card width to Desktop sizing at 1024px — this component's own real Figma Desktop
+// threshold — rather than this site's shared `breakpoints.xl` (1280px). Nobody updated this
+// comment or this constant's own consumers to match, so between 1024px and 1280px the two
+// disagreed: card width already said "Desktop" (5 slots styled), while `useBreakpointValue`
+// (which can only switch at this site's own registered breakpoint names) still said "previous
+// tier" (3 cards) — confirmed live (Marcel, 2026-09-10: a ~1277px screenshot showing the rail
+// styled for 5 cards, only 3 actually rendered, and the See-Full-History link showing as if
+// capped at 3). The `md` key is still correct (768px matches both this site's `breakpoints.md`
+// AND the rail's own Tablet start — confirmed independently, no drift there). Only `xl`'s
+// *meaning* changed: it is now "the rail's own Desktop tier," resolved against
+// `RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_DESKTOP_BREAKPOINT` below, not against `breakpoints.xl` — see
+// `useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount.ts` (`overrides/app/hooks/`) for the real resolution logic
+// this now requires, since `useBreakpointValue`'s Chakra-breakpoint-name shorthand cannot express
+// a threshold with no registered breakpoint of its own. Both consumers named in this constant's
+// own original docblock above (`ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`, `RecommendedProducts`) now go through
+// that hook instead of calling `useBreakpointValue` on this object directly.
+export const RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS = { base: 2, md: 3, xl: 5 } as const;
+
+// The Recently Viewed Rail's own real Figma "Desktop" breakpoint — 1024px, not this site's shared
+// `breakpoints.xl` (1280px). Confirmed directly against the rail's own master component
+// (2026-09-10) — see zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts's own "CARD SIZING"/`RAIL_DESKTOP_BREAKPOINT`
+// docblock section for the original derivation. Exported here, and imported by both that CSS
+// file and `useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount.ts`, so the two can never retype this value

## Round 1 fix — landed and independently re-scored PASS

`recommended-products/index.tsx`'s impression-tracking effect now re-derives its reported id list
through the same `selectRecentlyViewedCard` null-filter the render path uses, for the RV
recommender only — the other 4 recommenders' behaviour is untouched (confirmed via a byte-diff
against the prior commit, not assumed). Plus the 4 riders (stale docblock claim, 2 stale comments,
1 spelling fix). Committed `7994360`. Scorer independently re-verified: re-ran the mutation test
itself, read both vendor implementations to rule out an array-reference-mutation risk, traced the
Cart/PDP string-collision non-issue to its real mechanism (route-based guard fires first, `ref`
never attaches on Cart) rather than accepting the implementer's own self-assessment. PASS, no
defects.

## Branch sync with develop — a real, separate issue found and resolved

This branch's fork point (`3cec638`, tip of PR #105) was 16 commits behind `origin/develop` — 3
merged PRs landed since (Adyen webpack chunk-split fix #115, dynamic bag icon #114, PDP badges
#108). Opening this PR as-is would have shown all of that as reverted. Checked both sides of every
real conflict file before merging — all purely additive, zero semantic overlap. Merged via `git
merge origin/develop --no-edit` (Marcel's explicit choice over rebase), resolved 1 real conflict
(`constants/index.ts` — kept both sides' additions) plus regenerated the 5 registry files fresh
rather than hand-resolving generated content. `routes.tsx` and `theme/components/index.ts` (both
Tier 2) auto-merged cleanly with no conflict. Merge commit: `a4b2fe7`.

**A mistake happened and was fixed during this investigation, recorded for the audit trail:**
while checking whether a post-merge lint-count spike (8→827 errors) was caused by the merge or
already present on `develop`, `git checkout origin/develop -- .` was run — this overwrites the
*entire* working tree from the given ref, not a scoped inspection command. Working tree and index
were both silently replaced with `develop`'s content for every tracked file. No data was actually
lost — the merge commit `a4b2fe7` already held everything safely, confirmed via `git status`
showing "no local changes to save" from a preceding `git stash` immediately before the mistake — so
`git reset --hard HEAD` restored the correct state exactly, verified by content spot-checks
(`RECENTLY_VIEWED_ROUTE`/`SHIPPING_COUNTRY_CODES` both present, zero remaining references to the
deleted interim mechanism) and a full gate re-run (tsc clean, 90/1342 tests). The actual
investigation was then redone safely via an isolated `git worktree`, which never touches the main
working tree at all.

**The lint spike itself, fully resolved:** `develop` itself, independently, already has 827
errors/53 warnings (confirmed by running the identical lint command inside a `git worktree` of
`origin/develop` alone) — entirely pre-existing, unrelated to anything in this branch. This
branch's own 828/54 is that same baseline plus exactly one warning, diffed line-by-line: a
pre-existing `no-floating-promises` warning in `zimmRecentlyViewedRail/index.stories.tsx`'s
`OverCap` story (from PR #107's original CI-fix work, well before any of this session's commits) —
invisible in the develop-only comparison only because that file doesn't exist on `develop` at all
(the whole SFCC-83/84 feature never merged there). **Net: this merge and this whole session's work
introduced zero new lint issues.**

| Gate | Result | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | 0 (clean) | Unchanged from every prior check. |
| `npm run test` | 90 files / 1342 tests, all passing | Up from 85/1310 pre-merge — the increase is `develop`'s own new tests (badges, checkout-error/redirect) landing via the merge, not anything this branch added. |
| `npm run lint` | 828 errors / 54 warnings | `develop`'s own current baseline (827/53) + 1 pre-existing, unrelated warning already explained above. Zero new from this branch's own work. |
| `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` | 3 unacknowledged | Identical to the baseline tracked throughout the whole build — all 3 in files this branch never touched. |

See the message to Marcel for the full text — written directly in this turn, covering the complete
SFCC-83/84 feature (both original build and Einstein-wiring), since this PR is the sole vehicle
that will ever bring any of it to `develop`.

{"author":{"id":"U_kgDOEbS5lQ","is_bot":false,"login":"marcelannavarro","name":""},"body":"# Description

Builds the global footer per SFCC-55 — shell, layout, and component structure across
all eight storefronts and both breakpoints. Content is Contentful-shaped but
fixture-backed: the CMS integration, link destinations, and Omneo sign-up are
separate stories, so `FooterContainer` supplies `FOOTER_FIXTURE` and `Footer` itself
takes its content as a required prop and fetches nothing.

Six ui-kit atoms/molecules were built or completed alongside it — logo, icon,
nav-item, button, text-input, and the input-action molecule — all six consumed by
the footer.

Three points worth surfacing before review:

- **Fonts are now self-hosted**, reversing the position stated in #53. Futura Round
  renders in-app and in Storybook from one shared `@font-face` module. The fallback
  stack measures ~13% wider, so several sizing decisions made against it were wrong
  and were redone once real metrics were in play. Licence files are deliberately
  excluded from the repository.
- **This branch was taken over from Jersey.** Their three CodeRabbit-fix commits are
  in the history; the parts worth keeping were adopted deliberately as separate
  commits (`fix(button)`, `feat(footer)`, `test(ui-kit)`) rather than folded into
  conflict resolution, so what came from upstream and why stays visible.
- **9 of the 16 new commits carry `.claude/registry/` churn.** The `pre-commit` hook
  regenerates it on any `components/`/`hooks/`/`utils/` change and `git add`s it.
  Mechanical — skip those hunks.

`header/index.tsx` carries a pre-existing `fontSize="l"` (invalid token) and a
`useCurrentBasket` call from the original copy-first import. Both predate this PR —
our diff there is comments only — but they surface in the changed-files view.

# Linked

- Ticket: **SFCC-55** (Global Footer UI). Design: Figma *Zimmermann_Design_System_2026*;
  footer frames signed off with Dani & Vicky (2026-07-07). Test cases SFCC-T116 – SFCC-T122
- Sprint: SFCC — Sprint 3

# Squad ownership

- [x] Squad B

# Types of Changes

- [x] **New feature** (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

# Changes

- `components/footer/` — footer assembly, subscribe section + modal, contact icon row,
  bottom bar; Contentful-shaped fixture and schema placeholder
- `theme/components/footer.ts` — the `ZimmFooter` multipart recipe. Named `ZimmFooter`,
  not `Footer`: `extendTheme` deep-merges, so a recipe sharing a base SFCC recipe's name
  inherits it rather than replacing it
- `components/ui-kits/` — six atoms/molecules; `cssVars` indirection removed in favour of
  the `--zimm-*` custom properties directly, and `utils/cssVars.ts` deleted
- `theme/fontFace.tsx` + `static/fonts/` — self-hosted Futura Round, mounted in both the
  app and Storybook from one module so the two cannot drift
- `components/icons/` — the four Zimmermann chevrons, replacing base-template
  substitutions that rendered a filled glyph where the design is a 1px stroke
- `theme/components/zimmTextInput.ts` — colour derivation moved out of the hook into the
  recipe, so the recipe is the single styling surface
- `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` — prop extraction scoped to `<ComponentName>Props`,
  Markdown table cells escaped, comma-containing types no longer silently dropped

- `npm run env -- dev && npm start` → `/`, scroll to the footer. Nav columns hug their
  content with even gaps; hovering a link underlines it

  it at every width
- Type a valid email → `>` opens the Join Us modal; empty or malformed is blocked inline
  with no modal
- `npm run storybook` → `Layout/Footer` (4 states incl. modal-open), `Elements/ZimmNavItem`
  (unsafe-href fallback), `Forms/ZimmInputAction` (validation)

> owned by **both squads** — Squad A notified.

- [x] `npm run test` (Vitest) — 168/168
- [x] Storybook interaction — 15 `play` functions across 7 stories
- [x] Runtime behaviour — 20/20 (hover, focus-visible, validation, modal focus trap + Escape + focus restore, overlay z-index above the sticky header)
- [x] Figma geometry — structural paddings exact at 64/48, 48/48, 24/24
- [x] Box model — 112 footer elements × 6 viewports, 0 off-token paddings/margins/gaps/borders
- [x] Accessibility — axe 0 violations / 17 passes (wcag2a → 2.2aa)
- [x] Local CodeRabbit — no new findings

# Proposed PR

**Title:** `feat(recently-viewed): SFCC-83, SFCC-84 Recently Viewed rail and Full History page`

**Base:** `develop`

**Body:**

```markdown
# Description

Delivers SFCC-83 (Recently Viewed rail on PDP/PLP/Cart) and SFCC-84 (Full History
page), wired to real Einstein recommendations from the start — not a stub needing
follow-up rewiring once Einstein deploys. The rail's Recently-Viewed branch and the
Full History page both call `useEinstein()`/`getRecommendations`, matching the exact
pattern the four other recommenders already sharing `recommended-products/index.tsx`
use today.

**Relationship to #107.** That PR is a demo/QA-only vehicle for the live MRT Preview
— it will never merge. It shipped an interim, browser-tracked stand-in for Recently
Viewed's data source because Einstein wasn't reachable to build against directly.
This PR is the branch that was always meant to actually merge: same rail, same Full
History page, same presentational components, but wired to Einstein for real, with
the interim mechanism (`useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts`, `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts`)
deleted outright rather than kept as a fallback.

**The one thing every reviewer needs to know going in:** Einstein is not deployed
anywhere reachable — not dev, not SIT, none of the 8 real Zimmermann storefronts, none
of the 3 sandboxes (Business Manager–verified, Einstein Status Dashboard shows "Not
Deployed" on all 8 sites). So there is no live or visual way to verify this PR's actual
behaviour pre-merge. Every check behind this PR is code-level: `tsc`, Vitest (including
several mutation-tested proofs — reverting a fix on purpose, confirming the right test
fails, restoring, confirming it passes again), and direct reads of the real vendor
`use-einstein.js` source rather than assumptions about its behaviour.

**The consequence once this merges:** Recently Viewed will render as empty everywhere
— no rail, no Full History content, for every shopper — until Einstein actually goes
live. That's deliberate, not a bug: showing nothing is correct when there's nothing
real to show, and it's a better trade than leaving a demo-org-shaped stand-in live in
production.

**Three external dependencies, none fixable in this PR, all already named:**
- **DNT defaults to `true`** across this app (base SDK behaviour) — every Einstein
  call silently no-ops until this is addressed. Code-verified, not yet browser-verified.
- **`EINSTEIN_API_SITE_ID` has never been pushed to any GitHub Environment** — checked
  directly, absent from all of dev/test/sit/uat/staging/prod as both variable and
  secret. Even once Einstein is provisioned, this `scope:tier` value needs a real,
  per-environment Zimmermann site ID pushed by a tier-1-approver — today it would
  resolve to `undefined` everywhere.
- **No consent gate exists yet for Einstein calls** — a pre-existing, platform-wide
  gap (SFCC-106/107 own it), not something this PR was asked to build. Must land
  before this can go to production for real.

**Mandatory follow-up, the day Einstein actually deploys:** open a genuinely fresh,
zero-history session and confirm the empty state renders correctly (no rail, Full
History page shows its own empty state) — the one thing this round couldn't verify
itself, named rather than assumed.

# Linked

- Tickets: **SFCC-83** (Recently Viewed rail), **SFCC-84** (Full History page)
- Design: Zimmermann_Designs Figma file — Recently Viewed frames (Rail + Full History,
  Desktop/Tablet/Mobile)
- Not linked: SFCC-647 — confirmed with Marcel this branch is deliberately standalone

# Squad ownership

- [x] Squad B

# Types of Changes

- [x] **New feature** (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
```

entries.name: ExitWorktree
entries.description:
Exit a worktree session created by EnterWorktree and return the session to the original working directory.

## Scope

This tool ONLY operates on worktrees created by EnterWorktree in this session. It will NOT touch:
- Worktrees you created manually with `git worktree add`
- Worktrees from a previous session (even if created by EnterWorktree then)
- The directory you're in if EnterWorktree was never called

If called outside an EnterWorktree session, the tool is a **no-op**: it reports that no worktree session is active and takes no action. Filesystem state is unchanged.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly asks to "exit the worktree", "leave the worktree", "go back", or otherwise end the worktree session
- Do NOT call this proactively — only when the user asks

## Parameters

- `action` (required): `"keep"` or `"remove"`
  - `"keep"` — leave the worktree directory and branch intact on disk. Use this if the user wants to come back to the work later, or if there are changes to preserve.
  - `"remove"` — delete the worktree directory and its branch. Use this for a clean exit when the work is done or abandoned.
- `discard_changes` (optional, default false): only meaningful with `action: "remove"`. If the worktree has uncommitted files or commits not on the original branch, the tool will REFUSE to remove it unless this is set to `true`. If the tool returns an error listing changes, confirm with the user before re-invoking with `discard_changes: true`.

## Behavior

- Restores the session's working directory to where it was before EnterWorktree
- Clears CWD-dependent caches (system prompt sections, memory files, plans directory) so the session state reflects the original directory
- If a tmux session was attached to the worktree: killed on `remove`, left running on `keep` (its name is returned so the user can reattach)
- Once exited, EnterWorktree can be called again to create a fresh worktree

action.description: "keep" leaves the worktree and branch on disk; "remove" deletes both.

discard_changes.description: Required true when action is "remove" and the worktree has uncommitted files or unmerged commits. The tool will refuse and list them otherwise.

entries.name: mcp__plugin_figma_figma__add_code_connect_map
entries.description: Map a Figma node to a code component in your codebase using Code Connect. Use the nodeId parameter to specify a node id. Use the fileKey parameter to specify the file key. If a URL is provided, extract the node id and file key from the URL, for example, if given the URL https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=1-2, the extracted nodeId would be `1:2` and the fileKey would be `:fileKey`. If the URL does not include `node-id`, ask the user for a node-specific URL. Do not pass an empty or guessed nodeId.

nodeId.description: The ID of the node in the Figma document, eg. "123:456" or "123-456". This should be a valid node ID in the Figma document. Do not pass an empty string for node_id.

fileKey.description: The key of the Figma file to use. If the URL is provided, extract the file key from the URL. The given URL must be in the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:int1-:int2. The extracted fileKey would be `:fileKey`. Only design files are supported: the URL must be a /design/ URL. /slides/, /board/, and /make/ URLs are not allowed.

source.description: The location of the component in the source code

componentName.description: The name of the component to map to in the source code

label.description: The framework or language label for this Code Connect mapping. Valid values: React, Web Components, Vue, Svelte, Storybook, Javascript, Swift, Swift UIKit, Objective-C UIKit, SwiftUI, Compose, Java, Kotlin, Android XML Layout, Flutter, Markdown

template.description: The executable JS template code for a Code Connect template. When provided, creates a figmadoc-type record (full template) instead of a component_browser mapping (simple mapping).

templateDataJson.description: JSON string of template metadata. May include isParserless (boolean), imports, nestable, props fields. If omitted when template is provided, defaults to {}.

input.prompt:
Two verified, real findings from a CodeRabbit review round on PR #116 (`feature/SFCC-83-84_recently-viewed-einstein`), confirmed via direct code trace and a mutation test respectively. Implement precisely, don't re-litigate whether they're real.

**Fix 1 — the Rail's impression-tracking reports more "viewed" items than are actually rendered.**

`overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.tsx`: the container builds a full, unsliced `cards` array from Einstein's recs (via `.map(selectRecentlyViewedCard).filter(non-null)`) and passes the whole thing to `<ZimmRecentlyViewedRail cards={cards}>`. The Rail component itself (`zimmRecentlyViewedRail/index.tsx:128-129`) does its own internal `cards.slice(0, maxVisibleCards)` using `useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount()` — a hook called *inside* the Rail, whose result the container never sees. The impression-tracking effect (around lines 334-340, the one that calls `sendViewReco`/`dataCloud.sendViewRecommendations`) reports ids built from the full, unsliced set — so whenever a shopper has more recently-viewed history than fits one row at the current breakpoint (the exact condition that triggers the "See Full History" link), Einstein is told about more "viewed" recommendations than were actually shown on screen.

**The fix:** the container should also call `useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount()` itself (the same hook — it's a pure read of a media-query breakpoint via `useMediaQuery`, no side effects, safe to call from more than one component simultaneously), and use it to slice the `cards` array down to the same count the Rail will independently slice to, specifically for the impression-tracking effect's own id list. **Do not change what's passed to `<ZimmRecentlyViewedRail cards={cards}>`** — keep passing the full, unsliced list there; the Rail's own presentational contract (untouched throughout this whole build, deliberately) already handles its own slice correctly for rendering. Only the impression effect's own reported id list needs to be limited to the visible-count slice.

One CodeRabbit claim was checked and found NOT accurate, so don't build for it: it also suggested this effect could retrigger on a breakpoint/media-query resize. Checked directly — the effect's dependency array is `[isOnScreen, recommendations]`, with no visible-count value in it, so a pure resize can't retrigger this specific effect as currently structured. If your fix adds the visible count as a new value the effect reads, think carefully about whether it needs to go in the dependency array too (correctness) without accidentally making the effect newly re-fire on every resize (which would reintroduce exactly the problem CodeRabbit incorrectly claimed already existed) — the effect should still fire once per mount/impression, not on every breakpoint change.

Add or update a test in `overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.test.tsx` proving this: a fixture where more recs exist than the current visible-count breakpoint would show, asserting the reported `sendViewReco`/`dataCloud.sendViewRecommendations` id list length matches the visible count, not the full mapped count. Prove it the way this whole build has proven every fix so far: revert the fix, confirm the new test fails for the claimed reason, restore, confirm it passes again.

**Fix 2 — a no-op test assertion.**

`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardContent/index.test.tsx:254` uses a pattern equivalent to `await expect(user.click(button)).resolves.not.toThrow()` (or similar) around a `user.click(button)` call — confirmed via mutation testing that this assertion cannot fail even when the click handler genuinely throws (the thrown error surfaces as an unhandled error separately from the test's own pass/fail result, not as an assertion failure). Fix this to a pattern that actually verifies what the test's own name/intent describes (the click completing without throwing) — e.g. simply `await user.click(button)` and let a real rejection fail the test naturally, or `await expect(user.click(button)).resolves.toBeUndefined()` matching `userEvent`'s actual real resolved value. Re-verify with the same mutation-test discipline: make the handler throw on purpose, confirm the corrected test now genuinely fails, restore, confirm it passes.

**Do not touch:** the Notify Me button logic, the mobile-overflow CSS, the duplicate-slide-image behavior in `zimmProductCardMedia`, the first-paint-flash gate, or the registry generator — all five are separately confirmed as deliberate, already-documented, or already-escalated decisions, not part of this fix round.

Run `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run test -- --run` after both fixes and report the full numbers. Report exactly what changed, file:line, and confirm nothing outside the necessary files was touched.

content.text:
Fix work is running. Here are the 5 replies for the findings we're not changing:

---

**#1 — `.claude/registry/routes.md` (generator can't resolve constant-based routes)**

> Confirmed — `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs`'s route-parsing regex only matches a route declared as a literal string (`path: '/some-route'`), not a named constant like `RECENTLY_VIEWED_ROUTE`, so this entry is structurally invisible to it. Real, but deliberately left as-is: fixing it means changing shared dev tooling every developer relies on, which is a different, bigger scope than this PR. Zero functional impact on the shipped app — this registry is internal reference tooling only, never read by the running application. Tracked as a known, named gap.

---

**#4 — `zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx` (duplicate gallery image in one fallback case)**

> Confirmed real and reproducible — but this is an explicitly documented, accepted tradeoff from 2026-09-09 (see this file's own comment at the point of the decision), not something this PR introduced or is silently overlooking. Left as-is per that existing decision; worth revisiting on its own if this becomes a priority, not folded into this PR.

---

**#5 — `zimmProductCard/index.tsx:508` (Notify Me renders enabled with no handler)**

> This is deliberate, not an oversight — the comment directly above this line (2026-09-08) states it ships the button visible-but-inert on purpose, pending a separate Notify-Me feature that hasn't been built yet (PRD-018–021). Fixing the visibility condition now would just hide the button instead of making it work, which isn't an improvement over the current placeholder. Deferred to whenever that feature actually lands.

---

**#6 — `zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts` (mobile overflow below ~400px)**

> Already known and already flagged in-code for exactly this — see this file's own comment: "Not chased further without a product decision on whether that's an acceptable target-device floor or needs its own fallback." That decision hasn't been made yet, so there's nothing to fix here until it is. Flagging this again is appreciated, but it's the same open item, not a new one.

---

**#7 — `recentlyViewed/index.tsx` (first-paint flash, `hasRequested` flag suggestion)**

> Confirmed and already decided: this is the same first-paint-flash behavior already found and named during this feature's own build (Einstein's hook starts in an empty state before its mount effect runs, so the empty-state message can flash briefly even for a shopper with real history). We deliberately chose not to add a local flag to paper over it, since Einstein isn't deployed anywhere yet and this is recorded as a known, accepted limitation in the PR description rather than something to design around blind. Not being fixed in this PR.

{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/pulls/comments/4012526537","pull_request_review_id":5206194043,"id":4012526537,"node_id":"PRRC_kwDOTJJNGs7vKkvJ","diff_hunk":"@@ -0,0 +1,325 @@
+import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';
+import { breakpoints } from 'app/theme/foundation';
+import { RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS, RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_DESKTOP_BREAKPOINT } from 'app/constants';
+
+/**
+ * Recipe for the Recently Viewed rail organism (SFCC-83), build plan section A5. Figma component
+ * set `40000587:38471` — Desktop `40000307:12444` (1440x528), Tablet `40000730:13363`
+ * (768x437.85), Mobile `40000538:25030` (402x355.82). The Figma decomposition confirmed by the
+ * build plan is exactly two children — `title-and-link` and `group`, no arrow layer (a rail-level
+ * carousel would collide with ZimmProductCardMedia's own intra-card arrows) — mapped onto `header`
+ * and `group` below. Two more parts exist that have no Figma layer of their own: `seeAllLink`
+ * (the See-Full-History link's colour/hover/focus states) and `card` (each card's own
+ * per-breakpoint fixed width — ZimmProductCard's own root has no width opinion, see index.tsx).
+ * `container` is the outermost wrapper, deliberately not named `root`: this recipe's own outer
+ * part and the composed ZimmProductCard's own `root` part (zimmProductCard.css.ts) are unrelated
+ * recipes that would otherwise both want the same name.
+ *
+ * CARD SIZING — fluid, not fixed (corrected 2026-09-10, closing a real, live-confirmed bug —
+ * Figma-vs-code audit requested by Marcel, the same pass that found and fixed the header padding
+ * below). The previous revision set each card to an explicit, non-growing, non-shrinking pixel
+ * width per breakpoint (201px / 256px / 288px), derived by dividing a Figma reference frame's own
+ * fixed canvas width by its visible-card count — a correct read of that frame's own dimensions,
+ * but the frame's own layout rule was never "fixed width." A fresh `get_design_context` pull
+ * (not just metadata, which only ever shows a resolved snapshot, not the underlying rule) on every
+ * real "Product-card" instance — Mobile `40000538:25030`, Tablet `40000730:13363`, Desktop
+ * `40000307:12444` — confirms `flex: 1 0 0` (grow, no shrink, zero basis) with a `min-width` floor:
+ * 200px on Mobile/Tablet, negligible on Desktop. Fixed-width cards were the single root cause of
+ * two real, reported symptoms at once: on any real device narrower than the old fixed total
+ * (201x2=402px — nearly every real phone), the row overflowed its own container, cutting off
+ * cards and forcing horizontal scroll; on any device wider than that total, the row left an
+ * unwanted gap instead of reaching the edge. Fluid cards fix both — they always evenly divide
+ * whatever width the row's own container actually provides.
+ *
+ * The rail's own hard per-breakpoint visible-card cap (`RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS`,
+ * `app/constants/index.ts` — 2/3/5, confirmed with Marcel as a genuine hard cap, not a
+ * scroll-to-see-more soft limit) means the row is *at most* that many cards, never more — but can
+ * genuinely be fewer (a shopper with only 1 tracked product). `group`'s own scroll/scroll-snap CSS
+ * is removed below for the same reason (Marcel, 2026-09-10: horizontal scrolling "is not a
+ * prescribed behavior for the recently viewed rail") — see "GROUP" below for the one narrow edge
+ * case this leaves unhandled, flagged rather than silently ignored.
+ *
+ * **Under-populated rows — corrected 2026-09-10 (third pass, same day).** `flex: 1 0 0` divides
+ * whatever space is available among however many cards actually exist — correct, and Figma-
+ * confirmed, for a fully-populated row, but Figma's own component set (`40000587:38471`) has
+ * exactly three variants (`Size=Desktop`/`Mobile`/`Tablet`) and no "fewer items" state at all, so
+ * there was no Figma ground truth for what a partially-filled row should do. Left as `flex: 1 0 0`,
+ * a lone card on Desktop would grow to consume the *entire* row — confirmed with Marcel as not the
+ * intended behaviour, and a real user-facing case (any shopper with fewer tracked products than
+ * the current breakpoint's cap). Fixed by sizing each card to its share of the row *as if the cap
+ * were fully met* (`100 / RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS.<tier>`, computed below rather than
+ * hand-typed so the two can never drift apart), left-aligned (Marcel's own choice, 2026-09-10,
+ * between left-aligned-with-trailing-gap vs. centered) — `flex: 0 0 auto` (no grow, no shrink,
+ * matching Figma's own no-shrink rule) with an explicit `width` instead of `flex: 1 0 0`'s
+ * zero-basis growth. A fully-populated row is unaffected: N cards at `100/N%` each still sum to
+ * exactly 100%, identical to the old behaviour in that case.
+ *
+ * `CARD_MIN_WIDTH_MOBILE_TABLET` (200px) has no existing --zimm-scale-* equivalent — checked
+ * against every numeric alias in zimmTokens.ts, the scale runs ...64, 140, 180... with nothing at
+ * 200 — same pending-token treatment as the header heights below. Desktop has no floor constant
+ * of its own: its real Figma value is a negligible ~1px anti-overflow default, not a meaningful
+ * design floor, and the visible-card cap already guarantees Desktop's 5 cards never need to shrink
+ * anywhere near even the Mobile/Tablet floor (1280px / 5 = 256px at the narrowest real Desktop
+ * viewport) — so the one floor is applied uniformly at every breakpoint rather than adding a
+ * second, functionally-inert constant purely to mirror Figma's "no floor" reading literally.
+ *
+ * Card height is still never set anywhere in this recipe, unaffected by this correction —
+ * ZimmProductCardMedia's own `slide` part already carries `aspectRatio: '2 / 3'` at `width: '100%'`
+ * (zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts), and ZimmProductCard's own root has no height opinion of its own
+ * (zimmProductCard.css.ts) — so height still falls out of that aspect-ratio math for free.
+ *
+ * GROUP HAS ZERO GAP / ZERO HORIZONTAL PADDING — confirmed directly (2026-09-10): the real
+ * `group` node's own Figma export carries no `gap`/padding class of any kind, at any breakpoint.
+ * This is `group`-only — `header` does NOT share this zero-inset treatment; see "HEADER PADDING"
+ * below. GROUP'S SCROLL/SCROLL-SNAP CSS IS REMOVED (2026-09-10) for the same reason cards became
+ * fluid — Marcel confirmed scrolling is not prescribed behaviour for this rail at all, and once
+ * cards are fluid against a hard-capped visible count, there is structurally nothing to scroll to
+ * in the normal case. **One accepted, narrow edge case this leaves open, flagged rather than
+ * silently handled:** a real device narrower than `min-width x visible-count` (e.g. under 400px on
+ * Mobile) would still overflow — `flex: 1 0 0` has shrink explicitly disabled, matching Figma, so
+ * the row cannot shrink below that floor — with no scroll affordance left to reach the clipped
+ * remainder. Not chased further without a product decision on whether that's an acceptable target-
+ * device floor or needs its own fallback.
+ *
+ * HEADER HEIGHT — two states, not three: 56px at base (covers Mobile and Tablet — the build
+ * plan's own brief gives exactly one Mobile header node and one Desktop header node, no separate
+ * Tablet one), stepping to 96px from Desktop up — `RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_DESKTOP_BREAKPOINT`
+ * (1024px, app/constants), this component's own real Figma threshold, not this site's shared
+ * `breakpoints.xl` (1280px); see that constant's own comment. Same rem-with-pending-comment
+ * treatment as the card widths above —
+ * neither 56px nor 96px has an existing --zimm-scale-* equivalent either.
+ *
+ * HEADER PADDING — corrected 2026-09-10, closing a real, live-confirmed bug (Figma-vs-code audit
+ * requested by Marcel). Previously zero horizontal padding and a flex `alignItems: 'center'`
+ * vertical treatment — the earlier revision of this docblock called that a "judgment call, not a
+ * confirmed Figma reading," flagged for confirmation once the rail sat inside a real page. Now
+ * confirmed directly against Figma metadata: horizontal inset is `var(--zimm-scale-3xl)` (40px) on
+ * Desktop (node `40000538:20306`) and `var(--zimm-scale-2xl)` (32px) on Tablet/Mobile (nodes
+ * `40000730:13364` / `40000538:25031`) — all four exact matches on the existing named spacing
+ * scale (`spacing.ts`), no pending-token gap here unlike the card widths/header heights above.
+ * Vertical split is NOT centered by box height either — it's top-heavy: Desktop is `pt-3xl` (40px)
+ * / `pb-2xl` (32px) around the 24px content (40+24+32=96, matching HEADER_HEIGHT_DESKTOP exactly);
+ * Tablet/Mobile is `pt-l` (20px) / `pb-s` (12px) around the same 24px content (20+24+12=56,
+ * matching HEADER_HEIGHT_MOBILE).
+ *
+ * **`alignItems` corrected again 2026-09-10 (second pass, same day) — reverted to `center`.** The
+ * first pass (immediately above) replaced Figma's own literal `alignItems: 'center'` with

+ * revision of this paragraph wrongly claimed it did.** That gate stays on the raw, pre-mapping

+ * (`ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`) has its own downstream `visibleCards.length === 0 -> null` guard

+ * counterpart comment in `recommended-products/index.tsx`), whether that's because there was no

+ * `recommended-products/index.tsx`'s own `sendViewReco`/`dataCloud.sendViewRecommendations` call

+          paddingBottom="calc(var(--zimm-scale-800) + var(--zimm-scale-5xl))" // 32px + 80px = 112px

git add overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.test.tsx overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.tsx overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardContent/index.test.tsx && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(recently-viewed): cap the rail's impression report to what actually renders

Two real CodeRabbit findings on PR #116, both independently verified
before this commit -- not fixed on faith.

recommended-products/index.tsx: the impression-tracking effect
reported every card that survived selectRecentlyViewedCard's
null-filter to Einstein/DataCloud as "viewed", but never applied the
same visible-count cap ZimmRecentlyViewedRail applies internally at
render time. Whenever a shopper had more recently-viewed history than
fits one row -- the same condition that triggers the See-Full-History
link -- Einstein was told about more "viewed" items than were
actually shown. Fixed by reusing the container's own already-computed
visibleCardCount (previously only used for the link's own threshold)
to slice the effect's reported id list. visibleCardCount is
deliberately not added to the effect's dependency array -- a
breakpoint resize after the impression already fired must not refire
this once-per-mount effect with a different count. What's passed to
ZimmRecentlyViewedRail itself is untouched.

zimmProductCardContent/index.test.tsx: a test asserting a Notify Me
click doesn't throw used an assertion that could never fail even if
the handler genuinely threw. CodeRabbit's own suggested fix
(a bare awaited click, no special assertion) was tested directly and
found to be equally incapable of catching it -- confirmed against
real DOM-dispatch semantics: a handler that throws synchronously
during dispatchEvent() never propagates to reject the click's
returned promise, in a real browser as much as here. Fixed by
spying on console.error around the click instead, since that's
where jsdom's virtual console actually surfaces an uncaught error --
same technique already used elsewhere in this suite
(resolveByRegion.test.ts). No production code changed for this one.

Both mutation-tested: the impression fix by removing it and
confirming the new test fails with the over-reported id present; the
test fix by forcing the real handler to throw and confirming the new
assertion catches it, where the old one and CodeRabbit's own
suggestion both did not.

Verified: tsc clean; test 93 files/1371 tests (up from 1370 -- the
one new impression-cap proof test).
EOF
)"

gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/pulls/116/comments/4012275064/replies -f body="$(cat <<'EOF'
Confirmed real and fixed in 522980b. The impression-tracking effect reported every card that survived selectRecentlyViewedCard's null-filter, but never applied the same visible-count cap ZimmRecentlyViewedRail applies internally at render time — so whenever a shopper had more recently-viewed history than fits one row, Einstein was told about more "viewed" items than were actually shown. Fixed by reusing the container's own already-computed visibleCardCount to slice the reported id list. One correction to the finding as written: the suggested retrigger-on-breakpoint-change concern doesn't hold here — the effect's dependency array doesn't include the visible count, so a resize alone can't retrigger it, and that's deliberate (a resize after the impression already fired must not re-fire this once-per-mount effect with a different count).
EOF
)" 2>&1 | head -5

+ * file's own dead check (`recommendations.length < 1` on what is always an object) is ported

+ * recommendation-context product (reused for the `productTileProps` callback's own `product`

+ * param on the one nested callback that isn't contextually typed; and inline
+ * `{ productId?: string }` / `{ id?: string }` object-type-literal params on four
+ * `.find`/`.some`/`.map` callbacks whose containing expression is untyped (`any`) and therefore
+ * supplies no contextual parameter type — `noImplicitAny` flags these regardless of the `any`
+ * receiver (confirmed against `npx tsc --noEmit`, which is why these four are annotated despite
+ * this file's own initial plan expecting two of them not to need it). The `{ productId?: string
+ * }` shape and inline-annotation style mirrors the existing precedent at
+ * product-detail/index.tsx:437 and :735; the `{ id?: string }` shape matches the field the base
+ * hook itself reads, `use-einstein.js`'s own `reco.recs?.map((rec) => rec.id)` (line 466).
+ *
+ * A sixth adjustment, found by lint rather than tsc: the base file destructures `formatMessage`
+ * straight off `useIntl()`, but `@typescript-eslint/unbound-method` flags any destructured
+ * reference to it — `formatMessage` is declared with method-shorthand syntax in
+ * `@formatjs/intl/src/types.d.ts:64-65`, which this rule always flags regardless of whether the
+ * real implementation needs `this`. Fix: keep the whole object (`const intl = useIntl();`) and
+ * call `intl.formatMessage(...)` at each of its five call sites instead of destructuring — a
+ * property-access call sidesteps the rule entirely, with zero behavioural change. Same
+ * "toolchain requires a different access shape than the untyped base file used" reasoning as the
+ * annotations above.
+ *
+ * SFCC-83/84 — this branch renders `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` instead of `ProductScroller` when
+ * `recommender === EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` (`'viewed-recently-einstein'`, the
+ * same string `CART_RECENTLY_VIEWED` resolves to — confirmed identical in

+ * already-committed component (A5), keeps this fix entirely inside this file.
+ *
+ * `headingLevel`/`variation` are added here, not by the mapper: `selectRecentlyViewedCard`'s own

+ * container's decision to make. `headingLevel: 'h3'` is inert for this variation —

+ * PDP passes `mx={{base: -4, md: -8, lg: 0}}` and Cart passes `mx={{base: -4, sm: -6, lg: 0}}` to

+ * had none before this step) because nothing here owned any copy of its own until now — `title`

+ * this is the one piece of copy this container itself needs.

+const messages = defineMessages({
+  seeFullHistory: {

+    defaultMessage: 'See Full History',

+/**

+ * useEinstein/ProductScroller ship untyped (vendor.d.ts's wildcard), so this is narrowed

+ * Definitions: hand-roll only the genuinely unexported shape actually used).

+type RecommendedProduct = { productId?: string };
+
+export type RecommendedProductsProps = {
+  /* The title to appear above the product scroller */
+  title?: ReactNode;
+
+  /* The zone to request */
+  zone?: string;
+
+  /* The recommender to request */

+/**
+ * A component for fetching and rendering product recommendations from the Einstein API
+ * by a zone or a recommender name.

+  recommender,
+  products,
+  title,

+  ...props

+  // section: a real storefront path is locale/site-prefixed (e.g. `/en-GB/cart`), so an exact
+  // `=== '/cart'` would only ever match the default site.

+    // trivial"); it is.

+    }

+    // Check if the component should fetch results or not. This is useful

+    if (typeof shouldFetch === 'function' && !shouldFetch()) {

+    }

+      // this `ids` computation changes nothing for them.

**Both fixes are committed (`522980b`), pushed, and both threads closed with "fixed" replies.** All 7 CodeRabbit findings on PR #116 now have explicit in-thread replies — 5 declined with specific reasons, 2 fixed with the commit referenced.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/skills/zimmerMANNDevImprover

The look-back. It reads how build work actually went, works out what would have prevented each
failure, and proposes the specific edit that does it.

**Intended model: Sonnet 5 at maximum effort.**

**Report in "ELI5BITFEDLOTP" register** — Explain Like I'm 5, But I'm The FED Lead Of The
Project. Not dumbed down, but no jargon that gets in the way: lead with the consequence, then the
mechanism, then the fix. This is the default for everything you put in front of Marcel unless he
asks for a different level.

**Scale to the work.** A look-back over one small story does not need the full sweep. Say what
depth you are running and what it drops, then run that. Over-scaled effort is a defect, not
thoroughness — and re-reading a transcript you have already read, or re-deriving a finding already
in `.runs/_improver/`, is the specific waste to avoid.

**Input:** `` — one or more Jira keys. `devimprove SFCC-89 SFCC-194`.

**Nothing observes the loop while it runs.** An in-loop tracker role was considered and
deliberately dropped, so improvement is post-hoc and reconstructed. Everything below is evidence
you have to go and find — none of it was recorded for you.

---

## What you read

**1. The session transcripts.** A bare `grep -l` on the ticket key is useless — it returns every
session that ever mentioned it in passing. For `SFCC-89` that is 79 sessions, most of them
unrelated. **Rank instead, and read the top few:**

```bash
D=~/.claude/projects/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa
for f in "$D"/*.jsonl; do
  n=$(grep -o "SFCC-89" "$f" 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
  [ "$n" -gt 20 ] || continue
  b=$(basename "$f" .jsonl)
  a=$(find "$D/$b/subagents" -name '*.jsonl' 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
  echo "$n mentions, $a agents — $b"
done | sort -rn
```

Mention count separates the build session from a passing reference — on this project the real
SFCC-89 session had 992 mentions where the next had 62. **Agent-transcript count tells you where
the loop actually ran.** A session with high mentions and zero agents is discussion, not a build.

Read the top-ranked sessions and their `<session-uuid>/subagents/*.jsonl`. The `.meta.json` sidecar
beside each agent transcript gives `agentType` and `description`, so you can tell which loop role a
transcript belongs to without opening it — read the `zm-scorer` and `zm-tester` ones first, since
that is where verdicts and missed defects live.

If the top-ranked session is enormous, extract just the user turns and the agent `.meta.json`
descriptions first, and only open full transcripts where those point.

This is unstructured and you will have to infer the loop's shape from it. That is the cost of
having no tracker.

**2. The run artefacts.** `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/`:

- `plan.md` and `findings.md` — what PreBuild planned and gated on
- `handoff.md` — Build's record: Scorer verdicts, rework rounds, gate numbers, UNIFORM findings
- `postbuild.md` — the audit, the sweep, and every review round with its verdicts

These are structured and cheap to read. **Start here, and use the transcripts to explain what they
show** rather than to rediscover it.

**3. Your own previous findings.** `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/_improver/` — what earlier
look-backs observed. **This is how you know whether something has happened before.**

**4. The current skills and agents**, and the repo, for job B.

---

## Job A — how the loop performed

For each failure you can identify, name **whose gap it was.** Be precise; the whole value is in
attributing correctly.

| Gap | Means |
|---|---|
| **Plan** | The step was underspecified, or its pass criteria were unmeasurable |
| **Implementer** | The step was clear and was implemented wrong |
| **Tester** | A defect reached the Scorer that the Tester should have caught |
| **Scorer** | Something passed that shouldn't have, or was returned without a usable instruction |
| **Brief** | **The instruction itself was wrong.** Historically the most common class on this project — eight cross-corrections against the brief in a single commit's loop. Record it plainly. |
| **Rule** | The codebase rule is wrong, missing, or contradicts another rule |

### The bar

**Any genuine defect qualifies** — a single clear failure is enough if the fix is real.

But **recurrence is the strongest signal.** Check `.runs/_improver/` before proposing: has this
class appeared before? If so, say so and say when. A pattern across two stories is worth more than
five one-offs from one, and it changes how confidently you propose.

### What is not a finding

- A one-off typo that would not recur
- Anything that traces to a decision Marcel made deliberately — report the *mechanical consequence*
  of a decision, never the decision
- "Be more careful", "add more checks", "be more thorough". If you cannot name the line to change,
  you have an observation, not a proposal

---

## Job B — citation drift

The skills cite rules, files and line numbers. Those move.

The `var(--zimm-*)` boundary **reversed direction twice in a fortnight** on this project.
`tagging.md` still describes sprint tagging that has been dead since `scripts/sprint.txt` stopped
existing. This is exactly the failure mode that made the FED handbook stale.

For every `file:line`, rule name and repo path the skills and agents cite:

- Does the file still exist?
- Does the line still say what the skill claims?
- Has the rule changed direction, not just moved?

A moved line is a citation fix. **A rule that changed direction may mean the skill's advice is now
wrong, not just its reference** — say which you think it is, and let Marcel rule.

---

## What you may change

**In scope:** `zimmerMANNPreBuild` · `zimmerMANNBuild` · `zimmerMANNPostBuild` · and the five loop
agents — `zm-planner`, `zm-orchestrator`, `zm-implementer`, `zm-tester`, `zm-scorer`.

Most failures belong in an agent brief, not a skill. A defect that reached the Scorer is a Tester
gap, and the Tester's brief is the thing to change.

**Out of bounds — never propose an edit to these:**

- `zimmerMANNReview` — that is `zimmerMANNRevImprover`'s
- `zimmerMANNSprinter`, `zimmerMANNDevOps` — different work, different evidence
- **This skill.** You do not edit your own judgement criteria.
- Anything in `zimmermann-pwa/` — Tier 1 and not ours

---

## Output

Every proposal, in this shape:

```
PROPOSAL <n> — <file>
Gap:        <plan | implementer | tester | scorer | brief | rule | citation>
Recurrence: <first seen | also seen in <ticket>, <date>>
Evidence:   <transcript turn, agent report, or file:line — quoted>
Current:    <the exact text today>
Proposed:   <the exact replacement>
Why:        <what this would have prevented, concretely>
```

**Paste-ready or it is not a proposal.**

Present them **one at a time via AskUserQuestion**, most consequential first. Apply on his explicit
go, and only the ones he approves.

**If you are running as a fork or subagent:** output all proposals in the format above and write
the log, then stop. Do not apply anything. The parent session presents proposals and collects
approval — that step requires the interactive `AskUserQuestion` tool, which only the parent can
use. A subagent that applies without approval has bypassed the only gate this skill has.

---

## Always write the log

Append to `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/_improver/<YYYY-MM-DD>.md`, whether or not anything was
proposed:

```
## <date> — reviewed <tickets>
Sessions read: <n>   Agent transcripts read: <n>
Findings: <n proposed, n recorded-not-proposed>
- <gap> — <one line> — [PROPOSED / RECORDED] — <accepted / declined / pending>
Citation drift: <n checked, n stale>
Not examined: <what you could not reach>
```

**Record what you saw even when you propose nothing.** Nothing else remembers — the tracker that
would have is gone, and this log is the only way a later run can tell a second occurrence from a
first.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never edit a skill or agent without an explicit go**, one proposal at a time. This applies to forks and subagents too — write the log and output proposals, then stop. The approval gate requires the interactive parent session.

- **Never propose a rewrite where an edit will do.** Small, specific, traceable.
- **Never re-litigate a decision.** If it is in `.research/DECISIONS.md` as ruled, it is settled —

entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.
